text: /nMalfoy couldn't believe his eyes when he saw that/nHarry and Ron were still at Hogwarts the next day,/nlooking tired but perfectly cheerful. Indeed, by the/nnext morning Harry and Ron thought that meeting/nthe three-headed dog had been an excellent/nadventure, and they were quite keen to have another/none. In the meantime, Harry filled Ron in about the/npackage that seemed to have been moved from/nGringotts to Hogwarts, and they spent a lot of time/nwondering what could possibly need such heavy/nprotection./n/n"It's either really valuable or really dangerous," said/nRon./n/n"Or both," said Harry./n/nBut as all they knew for sure about the mysterious/nobject was that it was about two inches long, they/ndidn't have much chance of guessing what it was/nwithout further clues./n/n/n/n/nNeither Neville nor Hermione showed the slightest/ninterest in what lay underneath the dog and the/ntrapdoor. All Neville cared about was never going near/nthe dog again./n/nHermione was now refusing to speak to Harry and/nRon, but she was such a bossy know-it-all that they/nsaw this as an added bonus. All they really wanted/nnow was a way of getting back at Malfoy, and to their/ngreat delight, just such a thing arrived in the mail/nabout a week later./n/nAs the owls flooded into the Great Hall as usual,/neveryone's attention was caught at once by a long,/nthin package carried by six large screech owls. Harry/nwas just as interested as everyone else to see what/nwas in this large parcel, and was amazed when the/nowls soared down and dropped it right in front of him,/nknocking his bacon to the floor. They had hardly/nfluttered out of the way when another owl dropped a/nletter on top of the parcel./n/nHarry ripped open the letter first, which was lucky,/nbecause it said:/n/n/n/nDO NOT OPEN THE PARCEL AT THE TABLE./n/nIt contains your new Nimbus Two Thousand, but I/ndon't want everybody knowing you've got a/nbroomstick or they'll all want one. Oliver Wood will/nmeet you tonight on the Quidditch field at seven/no'clock for your first training session./n/nProfessor M. McGonagall/n/nHarry had difficulty hiding his glee as he handed the/nnote to Ron to read./n/n/n/n/n/n"A Nimbus Two Thousand!" Ron moaned enviously./n"I've never even touched one."/n/nThey left the hall quickly, wanting to unwrap the/nbroomstick in private before their first class, but/nhalfway across the entrance hall they found the way/nupstairs barred by Crabbe and Goyle. Malfoy seized/nthe package from Harry and felt it./n/n"That's a broomstick," he said, throwing it back to/nHarry with a mixture of jealousy and spite on his face./n"You'll be in for it this time, Potter, first years aren't/nallowed them."/n/nRon couldn't resist it./n/n"It's not any old broomstick," he said, "it's a Nimbus/nTwo Thousand. What did you say you've got at home,/nMalfoy, a Comet Two Sixty?" Ron grinned at Harry./n"Comets look flashy, but they're not in the same/nleague as the Nimbus."/n/n"What would you know about it, Weasley, you/ncouldn't afford half the handle," Malfoy snapped back./n"I suppose you and your brothers have to save up/ntwig by twig."/n/nBefore Ron could answer, Professor Flitwick appeared/nat Malfoy's elbow./n/n"Not arguing, I hope, boys?" he squeaked./n/n"Potters been sent a broomstick, Professor," said/nMalfoy quickly./n/n"Yes, yes, that's right," said Professor Flitwick,/nbeaming at Harry. "Professor McGonagall told me all/nabout the special circumstances, Potter. And what/nmodel is it?"/n/n/n/n/n/n"A Nimbus Two Thousand, sir," said Harry, fighting/nnot to laugh at the look of horror on Malfoy's face./n"And it's really thanks to Malfoy here that I've got it,"/nhe added./n/nHarry and Ron headed upstairs, smothering their/nlaughter at Malfoy's obvious rage and confusion./n/n"Well, it's true," Harry chortled as they reached the/ntop of the marble staircase, "If he hadn't stolen/nNeville's Remembrall I wouldn't be on the team. ..."/n/n"So I suppose you think that's a reward for breaking/nrules?" came an angry voice from just behind them./nHermione was stomping up the stairs, looking/ndisapprovingly at the package in Harry's hand./n/n"I thought you weren't speaking to us?" said Harry./n/n"Yes, don't stop now," said Ron, "it's doing us so/nmuch good."/n/nHermione marched away with her nose in the air./n/nHarry had a lot of trouble keeping his mind on his/nlessons that day. It kept wandering up to the/ndormitory where his new broomstick was lying under/nhis bed, or straying off to the Quidditch field where/nhe'd be learning to play that night. He bolted his/ndinner that evening without noticing what he was/neating, and then rushed upstairs with Ron to unwrap/nthe Nimbus Two Thousand at last./n/n"Wow," Ron sighed, as the broomstick rolled onto/nHarry's bedspread./n/nEven Harry, who knew nothing about the different/nbrooms, thought it looked wonderful. Sleek and/nshiny, with a mahogany handle, it had a long tail of/n/n/n/n/n/nneat, straight twigs and Nimbus Two Thousand/nwritten in gold near the top./n/nAs seven o'clock drew nearer, Harry left the castle and/nset off in the dusk toward the Quidditch field. He'd/nnever been inside the stadium before. Hundreds of/nseats were raised in stands around the field so that/nthe spectators were high enough to see what was/ngoing on. At either end of the field were three golden/npoles with hoops on the end. They reminded Harry of/nthe little plastic sticks Muggle children blew bubbles/nthrough, except that they were fifty feet high./n/nToo eager to fly again to wait for Wood, Harry/nmounted his broomstick and kicked off from the/nground. What a feeling — he swooped in and out of/nthe goal posts and then sped up and down the field./nThe Nimbus Two Thousand turned wherever he/nwanted at his lightest touch./n/n"Hey, Potter, come down!"/n/nOliver Wood had arrived. He was carrying a large/nwooden crate under his arm. Harry landed next to/nhim./n/n"Very nice," said Wood, his eyes glinting. "I see what/nMcGonagall meant ... you really are a natural. I'm/njust going to teach you the rules this evening, then/nyou'll be joining team practice three times a week."/n/nHe opened the crate. Inside were four different-sized/nballs./n/n"Right," said Wood. "Now, Quidditch is easy enough to/nunderstand, even if it's not too easy to play. There are/nseven players on each side. Three of them are called/nChasers."/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"Three Chasers," Harry repeated, as Wood took out a/nbright red ball about the size of a soccer ball./n/n"This ball's called the Quaffle," said Wood. "The/nChasers throw the Quaffle to each other and try and/nget it through one of the hoops to score a goal. Ten/npoints every time the Quaffle goes through one of the/nhoops. Follow me?"/n/n"The Chasers throw the Quaffle and put it through/nthe hoops to score," Harry recited. "So — that's sort of/nlike basketball on broomsticks with six hoops, isn't/nit?"/n/n/n/n"What's basketball?" said Wood curiously./n/n"Never mind," said Harry quickly./n/n"Now, there's another player on each side who's called/nthe Keeper — I'm Keeper for Gryffindor. I have to fly/naround our hoops and stop the other team from/nscoring."/n/n"Three Chasers, one Keeper," said Harry, who was/ndetermined to remember it all. "And they play with/nthe Quaffle. Okay, got that. So what are they for?" He/npointed at the three balls left inside the box./n/n"I'll show you now," said Wood. "Take this."/n/nHe handed Harry a small club, a bit like a short/nbaseball bat./n/n"I'm going to show you what the Bludgers do," Wood/nsaid. "These two are the Bludgers."/n/nHe showed Harry two identical balls, jet black and/nslightly smaller than the red Quaffle. Harry noticed/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nthat they seemed to be straining to escape the straps/nholding them inside the box./n/n"Stand back," Wood warned Harry. He bent down and/nfreed one of the Bludgers./n/nAt once, the black ball rose high in the air and then/npelted straight at Harry's face. Harry swung at it with/nthe bat to stop it from breaking his nose, and sent it/nzigzagging away into the air — it zoomed around their/nheads and then shot at Wood, who dived on top of it/nand managed to pin it to the ground./n/n"See?" Wood panted, forcing the struggling Bludger/nback into the crate and strapping it down safely. "The/nBludgers rocket around, trying to knock players off/ntheir brooms. That's why you have two Beaters on/neach team — the Weasley twins are ours — it's their/njob to protect their side from the Bludgers and try and/nknock them toward the other team. So — think you've/ngot all that?"/n/n"Three Chasers try and score with the Quaffle; the/nKeeper guards the goal posts; the Beaters keep the/nBludgers away from their team," Harry reeled off./n/n"Very good," said Wood./n/n"Er — have the Bludgers ever killed anyone?" Harry/nasked, hoping he sounded offhand./n/n"Never at Hogwarts. We've had a couple of broken/njaws but nothing worse than that. Now, the last/nmember of the team is the Seeker. That's you. And/nyou don't have to worry about the Quaffle or the/nBludgers — "/n/n" — unless they crack my head open."/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"Don't worry, the Weasleys are more than a match for/nthe Bludgers — I mean, they're like a pair of human/nBludgers themselves."/n/nWood reached into the crate and took out the fourth/nand last ball. Compared with the Quaffle and the/nBludgers, it was tiny, about the size of a large walnut./nIt was bright gold and had little fluttering silver/nwings./n/n"This," said Wood, "is the Golden Snitch, and it's the/nmost important ball of the lot. It's very hard to catch/nbecause it's so fast and difficult to see. It's the/nSeeker's job to catch it. You've got to weave in and out/nof the Chasers, Beaters, Bludgers, and Quaffle to get/nit before the other team's Seeker, because whichever/nSeeker catches the Snitch wins his team an extra/nhundred and fifty points, so they nearly always win./nThat's why Seekers get fouled so much. A game of/nQuidditch only ends when the Snitch is caught, so it/ncan go on for ages — I think the record is three/nmonths, they had to keep bringing on substitutes so/nthe players could get some sleep./n/n"Well, that's it — any questions?"/n/nHarry shook his head. He understood what he had to/ndo all right, it was doing it that was going to be the/nproblem./n/n"We won't practice with the Snitch yet," said Wood,/ncarefully shutting it back inside the crate, "it's too/ndark, we might lose it. Let's try you out with a few of/nthese."/n/nHe pulled a bag of ordinary golf balls out of his pocket/nand a few minutes later, he and Harry were up in the/nair, Wood throwing the golf balls as hard as he could/nin every direction for Harry to catch./n/n/n/n/n/nHarry didn't miss a single one, and Wood was/ndelighted. After half an hour, night had really fallen/nand they couldn't carry on./n/n"That Quidditch Cup'll have our name on it this year,"/nsaid Wood happily as they trudged back up to the/ncastle. "I wouldn't be surprised if you turn out better/nthan Charlie Weasley, and he could have played for/nEngland if he hadn't gone off chasing dragons."/n/nPerhaps it was because he was now so busy, what/nwith Quidditch practice three evenings a week on top/nof all his homework, but Harry could hardly believe it/nwhen he realized that he'd already been at Hogwarts/ntwo months. The castle felt more like home than/nPrivet Drive ever had. His lessons, too, were becoming/nmore and more interesting now that they had/nmastered the basics./n/nOn Halloween morning they woke to the delicious/nsmell of baking pumpkin wafting through the/ncorridors. Even better, Professor Flitwick announced/nin Charms that he thought they were ready to start/nmaking objects fly, something they had all been dying/nto try since they'd seen him make Neville's toad zoom/naround the classroom. Professor Flitwick put the/nclass into pairs to practice. Harry's partner was/nSeamus Finnigan (which was a relief, because Neville/nhad been trying to catch his eye). Ron, however, was/nto be working with Hermione Granger. It was hard to/ntell whether Ron or Hermione was angrier about this./nShe hadn't spoken to either of them since the day/nHarry's broomstick had arrived./n/n"Now, don't forget that nice wrist movement we've/nbeen practicing!" squeaked Professor Flitwick,/nperched on top of his pile of books as usual. "Swish/nand flick, remember, swish and flick. And saying the/nmagic words properly is very important, too — never/n/n/n/n/nforget Wizard Baruffio, who said 's' instead of 'f and/nfound himself on the floor with a buffalo on his/nchest."/n/nIt was very difficult. Harry and Seamus swished and/nflicked, but the feather they were supposed to be/nsending skyward just lay on the desktop. Seamus got/nso impatient that he prodded it with his wand and set/nfire to it — Harry had to put it out with his hat./n/nRon, at the next table, wasn't having much more/nluck./n/n"Wingardium Leviosal" he shouted, waving his long/narms like a windmill./n/n"You're saying it wrong," Harry heard Hermione snap./n"It's Wing-gar-dium Levi-o-sa, make the 'gar' nice and/nlong."/n/n"You do it, then, if you're so clever," Ron snarled./n/nHermione rolled up the sleeves of her gown, flicked/nher wand, and said, "Wingardium LeviosaV'/n/nTheir feather rose off the desk and hovered about four/nfeet above their heads./n/n"Oh, well done!" cried Professor Flitwick, clapping./n"Everyone see here, Miss Granger's done it!"/n/nRon was in a very bad mood by the end of the class./n/n"It's no wonder no one can stand her," he said to/nHarry as they pushed their way into the crowded/ncorridor, "she's a nightmare, honestly."/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nSomeone knocked into Harry as they hurried past/nhim. It was Hermione. Harry caught a glimpse of her/nface — and was startled to see that she was in tears./n/n"I think she heard you."/n/n"So?" said Ron, but he looked a bit uncomfortable./n"She must've noticed she's got no friends."/n/nHermione didn't turn up for the next class and wasn't/nseen all afternoon. On their way down to the Great/nHall for the Halloween feast, Harry and Ron overheard/nParvati Patil telling her friend Lavender that Hermione/nwas crying in the girls' bathroom and wanted to be/nleft alone. Ron looked still more awkward at this, but/na moment later they had entered the Great Hall,/nwhere the Halloween decorations put Hermione out of/ntheir minds./n/nA thousand live bats fluttered from the walls and/nceiling while a thousand more swooped over the/ntables in low black clouds, making the candles in the/npumpkins stutter. The feast appeared suddenly on/nthe golden plates, as it had at the start-of-term/nbanquet./n/nHarry was just helping himself to a baked potato/nwhen Professor Quirrell came sprinting into the hall,/nhis turban askew and terror on his face. Everyone/nstared as he reached Professor Dumbledore's chair,/nslumped against the table, and gasped, "Troll — in/nthe dungeons — thought you ought to know."/n/nHe then sank to the floor in a dead faint./n/nThere was an uproar. It took several purple/nfirecrackers exploding from the end of Professor/nDumbledore's wand to bring silence./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"Prefects," he rumbled, "lead your Houses back to the/ndormitories immediately!"/n/nPercy was in his element./n/n"Follow me! Stick together, first years! No need to fear/nthe troll if you follow my orders! Stay close behind/nme, now. Make way, first years coming through!/nExcuse me, I'm a prefect!"/n/n"How could a troll get in?" Harry asked as they/nclimbed the stairs./n/n"Don't ask me, they're supposed to be really stupid,"/nsaid Ron. "Maybe Peeves let it in for a Halloween/njoke."/n/nThey passed different groups of people hurrying in/ndifferent directions. As they jostled their way through/na crowd of confused Hufflepuffs, Harry suddenly/ngrabbed Ron's arm./n/n"I've just thought — Hermione."/n/n"What about her?"/n/n"She doesn't know about the troll."/n/nRon bit his lip./n/n"Oh, all right," he snapped. "But Percy'd better not/nsee us."/n/nDucking down, they joined the Hufflepuffs going the/nother way, slipped down a deserted side corridor, and/nhurried off toward the girls' bathroom. They had just/nturned the corner when they heard quick footsteps/nbehind them./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"Percy!" hissed Ron, pulling Harry behind a large/nstone griffin./n/nPeering around it, however, they saw not Percy but/nSnape. He crossed the corridor and disappeared from/nview./n/n"What's he doing?" Harry whispered. "Why isn't he/ndown in the dungeons with the rest of the teachers?"/n/n"Search me."/n/nQuietly as possible, they crept along the next corridor/nafter Snape 's fading footsteps./n/n"He's heading for the third floor," Harry said, but Ron/nheld up his hand./n/n"Can you smell something?"/n/nHarry sniffed and a foul stench reached his nostrils, a/nmixture of old socks and the kind of public toilet no/none seems to clean./n/nAnd then they heard it — a low grunting, and the/nshuffling footfalls of gigantic feet. Ron pointed — at/nthe end of a passage to the left, something huge was/nmoving toward them. They shrank into the shadows/nand watched as it emerged into a patch of moonlight./n/nIt was a horrible sight. Twelve feet tall, its skin was a/ndull, granite gray, its great lumpy body like a boulder/nwith its small bald head perched on top like a/ncoconut. It had short legs thick as tree trunks with/nflat, horny feet. The smell coming from it was/nincredible. It was holding a huge wooden club, which/ndragged along the floor because its arms were so long./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nThe troll stopped next to a doorway and peered inside./nIt waggled its long ears, making up its tiny mind, then/nslouched slowly into the room./n/n"The key's in the lock," Harry muttered. "We could/nlock it in."/n/n"Good idea," said Ron nervously./n/nThey edged toward the open door, mouths dry,/npraying the troll wasn't about to come out of it. With/none great leap, Harry managed to grab the key, slam/nthe door, and lock it./n/n"Yes!"/n/nFlushed with their victory, they started to run back/nup the passage, but as they reached the corner they/nheard something that made their hearts stop — a/nhigh, petrified scream — and it was coming from the/nchamber they'd just chained up./n/n"Oh, no," said Ron, pale as the Bloody Baron./n/n"It's the girls' bathroom!" Harry gasped./n/n" Hermionel" they said together./n/nIt was the last thing they wanted to do, but what/nchoice did they have? Wheeling around, they sprinted/nback to the door and turned the key, fumbling in their/npanic. Harry pulled the door open and they ran/ninside./n/nHermione Granger was shrinking against the wall/nopposite, looking as if she was about to faint. The troll/nwas advancing on her, knocking the sinks off the/nwalls as it went./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"Confuse it!" Harry said desperately to Ron, and,/nseizing a tap, he threw it as hard as he could against/nthe wall./n/nThe troll stopped a few feet from Hermione. It/nlumbered around, blinking stupidly, to see what had/nmade the noise. Its mean little eyes saw Harry. It/nhesitated, then made for him instead, lifting its club/nas it went./n/n"Oy, pea-brain!" yelled Ron from the other side of the/nchamber, and he threw a metal pipe at it. The troll/ndidn't even seem to notice the pipe hitting its/nshoulder, but it heard the yell and paused again,/nturning its ugly snout toward Ron instead, giving/nHarry time to run around it./n/n"Come on, run, run\" Harry yelled at Hermione, trying/nto pull her toward the door, but she couldn't move,/nshe was still flat against the wall, her mouth open/nwith terror./n/nThe shouting and the echoes seemed to be driving the/ntroll berserk. It roared again and started toward Ron,/nwho was nearest and had no way to escape./n/nHarry then did something that was both very brave/nand very stupid: He took a great running jump and/nmanaged to fasten his arms around the troll's neck/nfrom behind. The troll couldn't feel Harry hanging/nthere, but even a troll will notice if you stick a long bit/nof wood up its nose, and Harry's wand had still been/nin his hand when he'd jumped — it had gone straight/nup one of the troll's nostrils./n/nHowling with pain, the troll twisted and flailed its/nclub, with Harry clinging on for dear life; any second,/nthe troll was going to rip him off or catch him a/nterrible blow with the club./n/n/n/n/n/nHermione had sunk to the floor in fright; Ron pulled/nout his own wand — not knowing what he was going/nto do he heard himself cry the first spell that came/ninto his head: "Wingardium Leviosal"/n/nThe club flew suddenly out of the troll's hand, rose/nhigh, high up into the air, turned slowly over — and/ndropped, with a sickening crack, onto its owner's/nhead. The troll swayed on the spot and then fell flat/non its face, with a thud that made the whole room/ntremble./n/nHarry got to his feet. He was shaking and out of/nbreath. Ron was standing there with his wand still/nraised, staring at what he had done./n/nIt was Hermione who spoke first./n/n"Is it — dead?"/n/n"I don't think so," said Harry, "I think it's just been/nknocked out."/n/nHe bent down and pulled his wand out of the troll's/nnose. It was covered in what looked like lumpy gray/nglue./n/n"Urgh — troll boogers."/n/nHe wiped it on the troll's trousers./n/nA sudden slamming and loud footsteps made the/nthree of them look up. They hadn't realized what a/nracket they had been making, but of course, someone/ndownstairs must have heard the crashes and the/ntroll's roars. A moment later, Professor McGonagall/nhad come bursting into the room, closely followed by/nSnape, with Quirrell bringing up the rear. Quirrell/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/ntook one look at the troll, let out a faint whimper, and/nsat quickly down on a toilet, clutching his heart./n/nSnape bent over the troll. Professor McGonagall was/nlooking at Ron and Harry. Harry had never seen her/nlook so angry. Her lips were white. Hopes of winning/nfifty points for Gryffindor faded quickly from Harry's/nmind./n/n"What on earth were you thinking of?" said Professor/nMcGonagall, with cold fury in her voice. Harry looked/nat Ron, who was still standing with his wand in the/nair. "You're lucky you weren't killed. Why aren't you/nin your dormitory?"/n/nSnape gave Harry a swift, piercing look. Harry looked/nat the floor. He wished Ron would put his wand down./n/nThen a small voice came out of the shadows./n/n"Please, Professor McGonagall — they were looking for/nme."/n/n"Miss Granger!"/n/nHermione had managed to get to her feet at last./n/n"I went looking for the troll because I — I thought I/ncould deal with it on my own — you know, because/nI've read all about them."/n/nRon dropped his wand. Hermione Granger, telling a/ndownright lie to a teacher?/n/n"If they hadn't found me, I'd be dead now. Harry/nstuck his wand up its nose and Ron knocked it out/nwith its own club. They didn't have time to come and/nfetch anyone. It was about to finish me off when they/narrived."/n/n/n/n/n/nHarry and Ron tried to look as though this story/nwasn't new to them./n/n"Well — in that case ..." said Professor McGonagall,/nstaring at the three of them, "Miss Granger, you/nfoolish girl, how could you think of tackling a/nmountain troll on your own?"/n/nHermione hung her head. Harry was speechless./nHermione was the last person to do anything against/nthe rules, and here she was, pretending she had, to/nget them out of trouble. It was as if Snape had started/nhanding out sweets./n/n"Miss Granger, five points will be taken from/nGryffindor for this," said Professor McGonagall. "I'm/nvery disappointed in you. If you're not hurt at all,/nyou'd better get off to Gryffindor Tower. Students are/nfinishing the feast in their Houses."/n/nHermione left./n/nProfessor McGonagall turned to Harry and Ron./n/n"Well, I still say you were lucky, but not many first/nyears could have taken on a full-grown mountain/ntroll. You each win Gryffindor five points. Professor/nDumbledore will be informed of this. You may go."/n/nThey hurried out of the chamber and didn't speak at/nall until they had climbed two floors up. It was a relief/nto be away from the smell of the troll, quite apart from/nanything else./n/n"We should have gotten more than ten points," Ron/ngrumbled./n/n"Five, you mean, once she's taken off Hermione 's."/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"Good of her to get us out of trouble like that," Ron/nadmitted. "Mind you, we did save her."/n/n"She might not have needed saving if we hadn't/nlocked the thing in with her," Harry reminded him./n/nThey had reached the portrait of the Fat Lady./n/n"Pig snout," they said and entered./n/nThe common room was packed and noisy. Everyone/nwas eating the food that had been sent up. Hermione,/nhowever, stood alone by the door, waiting for them./nThere was a very embarrassed pause. Then, none of/nthem looking at each other, they all said "Thanks,"/nand hurried off to get plates./n/nBut from that moment on, Hermione Granger became/ntheir friend. There are some things you can't share/nwithout ending up liking each other, and knocking/nout a twelve-foot mountain troll is one of them./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n

title: Quidditch
text: /nAs they entered November, the weather turned very/ncold. The mountains around the school became icy/ngray and the lake like chilled steel. Every morning the/nground was covered in frost. Hagrid could be seen/nfrom the upstairs windows defrosting broomsticks on/nthe Quidditch field, bundled up in a long moleskin/novercoat, rabbit fur gloves, and enormous beaverskin/nboots./n/nThe Quidditch season had begun. On Saturday, Harry/nwould be playing in his first match after weeks of/ntraining: Gryffindor versus Slytherin. If Gryffindor/nwon, they would move up into second place in the/nHouse Championship./n/nHardly anyone had seen Harry play because Wood/nhad decided that, as their secret weapon, Harry/nshould be kept, well, secret. But the news that he was/nplaying Seeker had leaked out somehow, and Harry/ndidn't know which was worse — people telling him/nhe'd be brilliant or people telling him they'd be/nrunning around underneath him holding a mattress./n/n/n/nIt was really lucky that Harry now had Hermione as a/nfriend. He didn't know how he'd have gotten through/nall his homework without her, what with all the last-/nminute Quidditch practice Wood was making them/ndo. She had also lent him Quidditch Through the Ages,/nwhich turned out to be a very interesting read./n/nHarry learned that there were seven hundred ways of/ncommitting a Quidditch foul and that all of them had/nhappened during a World Cup match in 1473; that/nSeekers were usually the smallest and fastest players,/nand that most serious Quidditch accidents seemed to/nhappen to them; that although people rarely died/nplaying Quidditch, referees had been known to vanish/nand turn up months later in the Sahara Desert./n/nHermione had become a bit more relaxed about/nbreaking rules since Harry and Ron had saved her/nfrom the mountain troll, and she was much nicer for/nit. The day before Harry's first Quidditch match the/nthree of them were out in the freezing courtyard/nduring break, and she had conjured them up a bright/nblue fire that could be carried around in a jam jar./nThey were standing with their backs to it, getting/nwarm, when Snape crossed the yard. Harry noticed at/nonce that Snape was limping. Harry, Ron, and/nHermione moved closer together to block the fire from/nview; they were sure it wouldn't be allowed./nUnfortunately, something about their guilty faces/ncaught Snape's eye. He limped over. He hadn't seen/nthe fire, but he seemed to be looking for a reason to/ntell them off anyway./n/n"What's that you've got there, Potter?"/n/nIt was Quidditch Through the Ages. Harry showed him./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"Library books are not to be taken outside the/nschool," said Snape. "Give it to me. Five points from/nGryffindor."/n/n"He's just made that rule up," Harry muttered angrily/nas Snape limped away. "Wonder what's wrong with/nhis leg?"/n/n"Dunno, but I hope it's really hurting him," said Ron/nbitterly./n/nThe Gryffindor common room was very noisy that/nevening. Harry, Ron, and Hermione sat together next/nto a window. Hermione was checking Harry and Ron's/nCharms homework for them. She would never let/nthem copy ("How will you learn?"), but by asking her/nto read it through, they got the right answers anyway./n/nHarry felt restless. He wanted Quidditch Through the/nAges back, to take his mind off his nerves about/ntomorrow. Why should he be afraid of Snape? Getting/nup, he told Ron and Hermione he was going to ask/nSnape if he could have it./n/n"Better you than me," they said together, but Harry/nhad an idea that Snape wouldn't refuse if there were/nother teachers listening./n/nHe made his way down to the staffroom and knocked./nThere was no answer. He knocked again. Nothing./n/nPerhaps Snape had left the book in there? It was/nworth a try. He pushed the door ajar and peered/ninside — and a horrible scene met his eyes./n/nSnape and Filch were inside, alone. Snape was/nholding his robes above his knees. One of his legs was/nbloody and mangled. Filch was handing Snape/nbandages./n/n/n/n/n/n"Blasted thing," Snape was saying. "How are you/nsupposed to keep your eyes on all three heads at/nonce?"/n/nHarry tried to shut the door quietly, but —/n/n"POTTER!"/n/nSnape 's face was twisted with fury as he dropped his/nrobes quickly to hide his leg. Harry gulped./n/n"I just wondered if I could have my book back."/n/n"GET OUT! OUT!"/n/nHarry left, before Snape could take any more points/nfrom Gryffindor. He sprinted back upstairs./n/n"Did you get it?" Ron asked as Harry joined them./n"What's the matter?"/n/nIn a low whisper, Harry told them what he'd seen./n/n"You know what this means?" he finished/nbreathlessly. "He tried to get past that three-headed/ndog at Halloween! That's where he was going when we/nsaw him — he's after whatever it's guarding! And I'd/nbet my broomstick he let that troll in, to make a/ndiversion!"/n/nHermione's eyes were wide./n/n"No — he wouldn't," she said. "I know he's not very/nnice, but he wouldn't try and steal something/nDumbledore was keeping safe."/n/n"Honestly, Hermione, you think all teachers are saints/nor something," snapped Ron. "I'm with Harry. I/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nwouldn't put anything past Snape. But what's he/nafter? What's that dog guarding?"/n/nHarry went to bed with his head buzzing with the/nsame question. Neville was snoring loudly, but Harry/ncouldn't sleep. He tried to empty his mind — he/nneeded to sleep, he had to, he had his first Quidditch/nmatch in a few hours — but the expression on/nSnape's face when Harry had seen his leg wasn't easy/nto forget./n/nThe next morning dawned very bright and cold. The/nGreat Hall was full of the delicious smell of fried/nsausages and the cheerful chatter of everyone looking/nforward to a good Quidditch match./n/n"You've got to eat some breakfast."/n/n"I don't want anything."/n/n"Just a bit of toast," wheedled Hermione./n/n"I'm not hungry."/n/nHarry felt terrible. In an hour's time he'd be walking/nonto the field./n/n"Harry, you need your strength," said Seamus/nFinnigan. "Seekers are always the ones who get/nclobbered by the other team."/n/n"Thanks, Seamus," said Harry, watching Seamus pile/nketchup on his sausages./n/nBy eleven o'clock the whole school seemed to be out/nin the stands around the Quidditch pitch. Many/nstudents had binoculars. The seats might be raised/nhigh in the air, but it was still difficult to see what/nwas going on sometimes./n/n/n/n/n/nRon and Hermione joined Neville, Seamus, and Dean/nthe West Ham fan up in the top row. As a surprise for/nHarry, they had painted a large banner on one of the/nsheets Scabbers had ruined. It said Potter for/nPresident, and Dean, who was good at drawing, had/ndone a large Gryffindor lion underneath. Then/nHermione had performed a tricky little charm so that/nthe paint flashed different colors./n/nMeanwhile, in the locker room, Harry and the rest of/nthe team were changing into their scarlet Quidditch/nrobes (Slytherin would be playing in green) ./n/nWood cleared his throat for silence./n/n"Okay, men," he said./n/n"And women," said Chaser Angelina Johnson./n/n"And women," Wood agreed. "This is it."/n/n"The big one," said Fred Weasley./n/n"The one we've all been waiting for," said George./n/n"We know Oliver's speech by heart," Fred told Harry,/n"we were on the team last year."/n/n"Shut up, you two," said Wood. "This is the best team/nGryffindor's had in years. We're going to win. I know/nit."/n/nHe glared at them all as if to say, "Or else."/n/n"Right. It's time. Good luck, all of you."/n/nHarry followed Fred and George out of the locker/nroom and, hoping his knees weren't going to give way,/nwalked onto the field to loud cheers./n/n/n/n/n/nMadam Hooch was refereeing. She stood in the/nmiddle of the field waiting for the two teams, her/nbroom in her hand./n/n"Now, I want a nice fair game, all of you," she said,/nonce they were all gathered around her. Harry noticed/nthat she seemed to be speaking particularly to the/nSlytherin Captain, Marcus Flint, a fifth year. Harry/nthought Flint looked as if he had some troll blood in/nhim. Out of the corner of his eye he saw the fluttering/nbanner high above, flashing Potter for President over/nthe crowd. His heart skipped. He felt braver./n/n"Mount your brooms, please."/n/nHarry clambered onto his Nimbus Two Thousand./n/nMadam Hooch gave a loud blast on her silver whistle./n/nFifteen brooms rose up, high, high into the air. They/nwere off./n/n"And the Quaffle is taken immediately by Angelina/nJohnson of Gryffindor — what an excellent Chaser/nthat girl is, and rather attractive, too — "/n/n"JORDAN!"/n/n"Sorry, Professor."/n/nThe Weasley twins' friend, Lee Jordan, was doing the/ncommentary for the match, closely watched by/nProfessor McGonagall./n/n"And she's really belting along up there, a neat pass/nto Alicia Spinnet, a good find of Oliver Wood's, last/nyear only a reserve — back to Johnson and — no, the/nSlytherins have taken the Quaffle, Slytherin Captain/nMarcus Flint gains the Quaffle and off he goes — Flint/n/n/n/n/nflying like an eagle up there — he's going to sc- no,/nstopped by an excellent move by Gryffindor Keeper/nWood and the Gryffindors take the Quaffle — that's/nChaser Katie Bell of Gryffindor there, nice dive/naround Flint, off up the field and — OUCH — that/nmust have hurt, hit in the back of the head by a/nBludger — Quaffle taken by the Slytherins — that's/nAdrian Pucey speeding off toward the goal posts, but/nhe's blocked by a second Bludger — sent his way by/nFred or George Weasley, can't tell which — nice play/nby the Gryffindor Beater, anyway, and Johnson back/nin possession of the Quaffle, a clear field ahead and/noff she goes — she's really flying — dodges a speeding/nBludger — the goal posts are ahead — come on, now,/nAngelina — Keeper Bletchley dives — misses —/nGRYFFINDORS SCORE!"/n/nGryffindor cheers filled the cold air, with howls and/nmoans from the Slytherins./n/n"Budge up there, move along."/n/n"Hagrid!"/n/nRon and Hermione squeezed together to give Hagrid/nenough space to join them./n/n"Bin watchin' from me hut," said Hagrid, patting a/nlarge pair of binoculars around his neck, "But it isn't/nthe same as bein' in the crowd. No sign of the Snitch/nyet, eh?"/n/n"Nope," said Ron. "Harry hasn't had much to do yet."/n/n"Kept outta trouble, though, that's somethin'," said/nHagrid, raising his binoculars and peering skyward at/nthe speck that was Harry./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nWay up above them, Harry was gliding over the game,/nsquinting about for some sign of the Snitch. This was/npart of his and Wood's game plan./n/n"Keep out of the way until you catch sight of the/nSnitch," Wood had said. "We don't want you attacked/nbefore you have to be."/n/nWhen Angelina had scored, Harry had done a couple/nof loop-the-loops to let off his feelings. Now he was/nback to staring around for the Snitch. Once he caught/nsight of a flash of gold, but it was just a reflection/nfrom one of the Weasleys' wristwatches, and once a/nBludger decided to come pelting his way, more like a/ncannonball than anything, but Harry dodged it and/nFred Weasley came chasing after it./n/n"All right there, Harry?" he had time to yell, as he/nbeat the Bludger furiously toward Marcus Flint./n/n"Slytherin in possession," Lee Jordan was saying,/n"Chaser Pucey ducks two Bludgers, two Weasleys,/nand Chaser Bell, and speeds toward the — wait a/nmoment — was that the Snitch?"/n/nA murmur ran through the crowd as Adrian Pucey/ndropped the Quaffle, too busy looking over his/nshoulder at the flash of gold that had passed his left/near./n/nHarry saw it. In a great rush of excitement he dived/ndownward after the streak of gold. Slytherin Seeker/nTerence Higgs had seen it, too. Neck and neck they/nhurtled toward the Snitch — all the Chasers seemed/nto have forgotten what they were supposed to be/ndoing as they hung in midair to watch./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nHarry was faster than Higgs — he could see the little/nround ball, wings fluttering, darting up ahead — he/nput on an extra spurt of speed —/n/nWHAM! A roar of rage echoed from the Gryffindors/nbelow — Marcus Flint had blocked Harry on purpose,/nand Harry's broom spun off course, Harry holding on/nfor dear life./n/n"Foul!" screamed the Gryffindors./n/nMadam Hooch spoke angrily to Flint and then ordered/na free shot at the goal posts for Gryffindor. But in all/nthe confusion, of course, the Golden Snitch had/ndisappeared from sight again./n/nDown in the stands, Dean Thomas was yelling, "Send/nhim off, ref! Red card!"/n/n"What are you talking about, Dean?" said Ron./n/n"Red card!" said Dean furiously. "In soccer you get/nshown the red card and you're out of the game!"/n/n"But this isn't soccer, Dean," Ron reminded him./n/nHagrid, however, was on Dean's side./n/n"They oughta change the rules. Flint coulda knocked/nHarry outta the air."/n/nLee Jordan was finding it difficult not to take sides./n/n"So — after that obvious and disgusting bit of/ncheating — "/n/n"Jordan!" growled Professor McGonagall./n/n"I mean, after that open and revolting foul — "/n/n/n/n/n/n"Jordan, I'm warning you — "/n/n/n/n"All right, all right. Flint nearly kills the Gryffindor/nSeeker, which could happen to anyone, I'm sure, so a/npenalty to Gryffindor, taken by Spinnet, who puts it/naway, no trouble, and we continue play, Gryffindor/nstill in possession."/n/nIt was as Harry dodged another Bludger, which went/nspinning dangerously past his head, that it happened./nHis broom gave a sudden, frightening lurch. For a/nsplit second, he thought he was going to fall. He/ngripped the broom tightly with both his hands and/nknees. He'd never felt anything like that./n/nIt happened again. It was as though the broom was/ntrying to buck him off. But Nimbus Two Thousands/ndid not suddenly decide to buck their riders off. Harry/ntried to turn back toward the Gryffindor goal posts —/nhe had half a mind to ask Wood to call time-out —/nand then he realized that his broom was completely/nout of his control. He couldn't turn it. He couldn't/ndirect it at all. It was zigzagging through the air, and/nevery now and then making violent swishing/nmovements that almost unseated him./n/nLee was still commentating./n/n"Slytherin in possession — Flint with the Quaffle —/npasses Spinnet — passes Bell — hit hard in the face/nby a Bludger, hope it broke his nose — only joking,/nProfessor — Slytherins score — oh no ..."/n/nThe Slytherins were cheering. No one seemed to have/nnoticed that Harry's broom was behaving strangely It/nwas carrying him slowly higher, away from the game,/njerking and twitching as it went./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"Dunno what Harry thinks he's doing," Hagrid/nmumbled. He stared through his binoculars. "If I/ndidn' know better, I'd say he'd lost control of his/nbroom ... but he can't have. ..."/n/nSuddenly, people were pointing up at Harry all over/nthe stands. His broom had started to roll over and/nover, with him only just managing to hold on. Then/nthe whole crowd gasped. Harry's broom had given a/nwild jerk and Harry swung off it. He was now dangling/nfrom it, holding on with only one hand./n/n"Did something happen to it when Flint blocked him?"/nSeamus whispered./n/n"Can't have," Hagrid said, his voice shaking. "Can't/nnothing interfere with a broomstick except powerful/nDark magic — no kid could do that to a Nimbus Two/nThousand."/n/nAt these words, Hermione seized Hagrid 's binoculars,/nbut instead of looking up at Harry, she started/nlooking frantically at the crowd./n/n"What are you doing?" moaned Ron, gray-faced./n/n"I knew it," Hermione gasped, "Snape — look."/n/nRon grabbed the binoculars. Snape was in the middle/nof the stands opposite them. He had his eyes fixed on/nHarry and was muttering nonstop under his breath./n/n"He's doing something — jinxing the broom," said/nHermione./n/n"What should we do?"/n/n"Leave it to me."/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nBefore Ron could say another word, Hermione had/ndisappeared. Ron turned the binoculars back on/nHarry. His broom was vibrating so hard, it was almost/nimpossible for him to hang on much longer. The/nwhole crowd was on its feet, watching, terrified, as the/nWeasleys flew up to try and pull Harry safely onto one/nof their brooms, but it was no good — every time they/ngot near him, the broom would jump higher still. They/ndropped lower and circled beneath him, obviously/nhoping to catch him if he fell. Marcus Flint seized the/nQuaffle and scored five times without anyone/nnoticing./n/n"Come on, Hermione," Ron muttered desperately./n/nHermione had fought her way across to the stand/nwhere Snape stood, and was now racing along the row/nbehind him; she didn't even stop to say sorry as she/nknocked Professor Quirrell headfirst into the row in/nfront. Reaching Snape, she crouched down, pulled/nout her wand, and whispered a few, well-chosen/nwords. Bright blue flames shot from her wand onto/nthe hem of Snape 's robes./n/nIt took perhaps thirty seconds for Snape to realize/nthat he was on fire. A sudden yelp told her she had/ndone her job. Scooping the fire off him into a little jar/nin her pocket, she scrambled back along the row —/nSnape would never know what had happened./n/nIt was enough. Up in the air, Harry was suddenly able/nto clamber back on to his broom./n/n"Neville, you can look!" Ron said. Neville had been/nsobbing into Hagrid's jacket for the last five minutes./n/nHarry was speeding toward the ground when the/ncrowd saw him clap his hand to his mouth as though/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nhe was about to be sick — he hit the field on all fours/n— coughed — and something gold fell into his hand./n/n"I've got the Snitch!" he shouted, waving it above his/nhead, and the game ended in complete confusion./n/n"He didn't catch it, he nearly swallowed it," Flint was/nstill howling twenty minutes later, but it made no/ndifference — Harry hadn't broken any rules and Lee/nJordan was still happily shouting the results —/nGryffindor had won by one hundred and seventy/npoints to sixty. Harry heard none of this, though. He/nwas being made a cup of strong tea back in Hagrid's/nhut, with Ron and Hermione./n/n"It was Snape," Ron was explaining, "Hermione and I/nsaw him. He was cursing your broomstick, muttering,/nhe wouldn't take his eyes off you."/n/n"Rubbish," said Hagrid, who hadn't heard a word of/nwhat had gone on next to him in the stands. "Why/nwould Snape do somethin' like that?"/n/nHarry, Ron, and Hermione looked at one another,/nwondering what to tell him. Harry decided on the/ntruth./n/n"I found out something about him," he told Hagrid./n"He tried to get past that three-headed dog on/nHalloween. It bit him. We think he was trying to steal/nwhatever it's guarding."/n/nHagrid dropped the teapot./n/n"How do you know about Fluffy?" he said./n/n" Fluffy ?"/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"Yeah — he's mine — bought him off a Greek chappie/nI met in the pub las' year — I lent him to Dumbledore/nto guard the — "/n/n"Yes?" said Harry eagerly./n/n"Now, don't ask me anymore," said Hagrid gruffly./n"That's top secret, that is."/n/n"But Snape's trying to steal it."/n/n"Rubbish," said Hagrid again. "Snape's a Hogwarts/nteacher, he'd do nothin' of the sort."/n/n"So why did he just try and kill Harry?" cried/nHermione./n/nThe afternoon's events certainly seemed to have/nchanged her mind about Snape./n/n"I know a jinx when I see one, Hagrid, I've read all/nabout them! You've got to keep eye contact, and/nSnape wasn't blinking at all, I saw him!"/n/n"I'm tellin' yeh, yer wrong!" said Hagrid hotly. "I don'/nknow why Harry's broom acted like that, but Snape/nwouldn' try an' kill a student! Now, listen to me, all/nthree of yeh — yer meddlin' in things that don'/nconcern yeh. It's dangerous. You forget that dog, an'/nyou forget what it's guardin', that's between Professor/nDumbledore an' Nicolas Flamel — ■"/n/n"Aha!" said Harry, "so there's someone called Nicolas/nFlamel involved, is there?"/n/nHagrid looked furious with himself./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n

title: The Mirror Of Erised
text: /nChristmas was coming. One morning in mid-/nDecember, Hogwarts woke to find itself covered in/nseveral feet of snow.
