My mum ... trying to stop Voldemort/nkilling me ... and you did that ... you did it. ..."/n/nBefore either of them could say another word,/nsomething ginger streaked past Harry; Crookshanks/nleapt onto Black's chest and settled himself there,/nright over Black's heart. Black blinked and looked/ndown at the cat./n/n"Get off," he murmured, trying to push Crookshanks/noff him./n/nBut Crookshanks sank his claws into Black's robes/nand wouldn't shift. He turned his ugly, squashed face/nto Harry and looked up at him with those great yellow/neyes. To his right, Hermione gave a dry sob./n/n/n/n/n/nHarry stared down at Black and Crookshanks, his/ngrip tightening on the wand. So what if he had to kill/nthe cat too? It was in league with Black. ... If it was/nprepared to die, trying to protect Black, that wasn't/nHarry's business. ... If Black wanted to save it, that/nonly proved he cared more for Crookshanks than for/nHarry's parents. .../n/nHarry raised the wand. Now was the moment to do it./nNow was the moment to avenge his mother and/nfather. He was going to kill Black. He had to kill/nBlack. This was his chance. .../n/nThe seconds lengthened. And still Harry stood frozen/nthere, wand poised, Black staring up at him,/nCrookshanks on his chest. Ron's ragged breathing/ncame from near the bed; Hermione was quite silent./n/nAnd then came a new sound —/n/nMuffled footsteps were echoing up through the floor/n— someone was moving downstairs./n/n"WE'RE UP HERE!" Hermione screamed suddenly./n"WE'RE UP HERE — SIRIUS BLACK — QUICK!"/n/nBlack made a startled movement that almost/ndislodged Crookshanks; Harry gripped his wand/nconvulsively — Do it nouA said a voice in his head —/nbut the footsteps were thundering up the stairs and/nHarry still hadn't done it./n/nThe door of the room burst open in a shower of red/nsparks and Harry wheeled around as Professor Lupin/ncame hurtling into the room, his face bloodless, his/nwand raised and ready. His eyes flickered over Ron,/nlying on the floor, over Hermione, cowering next to the/ndoor, to Harry, standing there with his wand covering/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nBlack, and then to Black himself, crumpled and/nbleeding at Harry's feet./n/n" ExpelliarmusV' Lupin shouted./n/nHarry's wand flew once more out of his hand; so did/nthe two Hermione was holding. Lupin caught them all/ndeftly, then moved into the room, staring at Black,/nwho still had Crookshanks lying protectively across/nhis chest./n/nHarry stood there, feeling suddenly empty. He hadn't/ndone it. His nerve had failed him. Black was going to/nbe handed back to the dementors./n/nThen Lupin spoke, in a very tense voice./n/n"Where is he, Sirius?"/n/nHarry looked quickly at Lupin. He didn't understand/nwhat Lupin meant. Who was Lupin talking about? He/nturned to look at Black again./n/nBlack's face was quite expressionless. For a few/nseconds, he didn't move at all. Then, very slowly, he/nraised his empty hand and pointed straight at Ron./nMystified, Harry glanced around at Ron, who looked/nbewildered./n/n"But then ... ," Lupin muttered, staring at Black so/nintently it seemed he was trying to read his mind, ".../nwhy hasn't he shown himself before now? Unless" —/nLupin's eyes suddenly widened, as though he was/nseeing something beyond Black, something none of/nthe rest could see, " — unless he was the one .../nunless you switched . . . without telling me?"/n/nVery slowly, his sunken gaze never leaving Lupin's/nface, Black nodded./n/n/n/n/n/n"Professor," Harry interrupted loudly, "what's going/non — ?"/n/nBut he never finished the question, because what he/nsaw made his voice die in his throat. Lupin was/nlowering his wand, gazing fixedly at Black. The/nProfessor walked to Black's side, seized his hand,/npulled him to his feet so that Crookshanks fell to the/nfloor, and embraced Black like a brother./n/nHarry felt as though the bottom had dropped out of/nhis stomach./n/n"I DONT BELIEVE IT!" Hermione screamed./n/nLupin let go of Black and turned to her. She had/nraised herself off the floor and was pointing at Lupin,/nwild-eyed. "You — you — "/n/n"Hermione — "/n/n" — you and him!"/n/n"Hermione, calm down — "/n/n"I didn't tell anyone!" Hermione shrieked. "I've been/ncovering up for you — "/n/n"Hermione, listen to me, please!" Lupin shouted. "I/ncan explain — "/n/nHarry could feel himself shaking, not with fear, but/nwith a fresh wave of fury./n/n"I trusted you," he shouted at Lupin, his voice/nwavering out of control, "and all the time you've been/nhis friend!"/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"You're wrong," said Lupin. "I haven't been Sirius's/nfriend, but I am now — Let me explain. ..."/n/n"NO!" Hermione screamed. "Harry, don't trust him,/nhe's been helping Black get into the castle, he wants/nyou dead too — he's a werewolf."/n/nThere was a ringing silence. Everyone's eyes were now/non Lupin, who looked remarkably calm, though rather/npale./n/n"Not at all up to your usual standard, Hermione," he/nsaid. "Only one out of three, I'm afraid. I have not/nbeen helping Sirius get into the castle and I certainly/ndon't want Harry dead. ..." An odd shiver passed over/nhis face. "But I won't deny that I am a werewolf."/n/nRon made a valiant effort to get up again but fell back/nwith a whimper of pain. Lupin made toward him,/nlooking concerned, but Ron gasped,/n/n"Get away from me, werewolf"/n/nLupin stopped dead. Then, with an obvious effort, he/nturned to Hermione and said, "How long have you/nknown?"/n/n"Ages," Hermione whispered. "Since I did Professor/nSnape's essay. ..."/n/n"He'll be delighted," said Lupin coolly. "He assigned/nthat essay hoping someone would realize what my/nsymptoms meant. ... Did you check the lunar chart/nand realize that I was always ill at the full moon? Or/ndid you realize that the boggart changed into the/nmoon when it saw me?"/n/n"Both," Hermione said quietly./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nLupin forced a laugh./n/n"You're the cleverest witch of your age I've ever met,/nHermione."/n/n"I'm not," Hermione whispered. "If I'd been a bit/ncleverer, I'd have told everyone what you are!"/n/n"But they already know," said Lupin. "At least, the/nstaff do."/n/n"Dumbledore hired you when he knew you were a/nwerewolf?" Ron gasped. "Is he mad?"/n/n"Some of the staff thought so," said Lupin. "He had to/nwork very hard to convince certain teachers that I'm/ntrustworthy — "/n/n"AND HE WAS WRONG!" Harry yelled. "YOU VE BEEN/nHELPING HIM ALL THE TIME!" He was pointing at/nBlack, who suddenly crossed to the four-poster bed/nand sank onto it, his face hidden in one shaking/nhand. Crookshanks leapt up beside him and stepped/nonto his lap, purring. Ron edged away from both of/nthem, dragging his leg./n/n"I have not been helping Sirius," said Lupin. "If you'll/ngive me a chance, I'll explain. Look — "/n/nHe separated Harry's, Ron's and Hermione's wands/nand threw each back to its owner; Harry caught his,/nstunned./n/n"There," said Lupin, sticking his own wand back into/nhis belt. "You're armed, we're not. Now will you/nlisten?"/n/nHarry didn't know what to think. Was it a trick?/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"If you haven't been helping him," he said, with a/nfurious glance at Black, "how did you know he was/nhere?"/n/n/n/n"The map," said Lupin. "The Marauder's Map. I was in/nmy office examining it — "/n/n"You know how to work it?" Harry said suspiciously./n/n"Of course I know how to work it," said Lupin, waving/nhis hand impatiently. "I helped write it. I'm Moony —/nthat was my friends' nickname for me at school."/n/n"You wrote — ?"/n/n"The important thing is, I was watching it carefully/nthis evening, because I had an idea that you, Ron,/nand Hermione might try and sneak out of the castle to/nvisit Hagrid before his hippogriff was executed. And I/nwas right, wasn't I?"/n/nHe had started to pace up and down, looking at them./nLittle patches of dust rose at his feet./n/n"You might have been wearing your father's old cloak,/nHarry — "/n/n"How d'you know about the cloak?"/n/n"The number of times I saw James disappearing/nunder it... ," said Lupin, waving an impatient hand/nagain. "The point is, even if you're wearing an/nInvisibility Cloak, you still show up on the Marauder's/nMap. I watched you cross the grounds and enter/nHagrid's hut. Twenty minutes later, you left Hagrid,/nand set off back toward the castle. But you were now/naccompanied by somebody else."/n/n"What?" said Harry. "No, we weren't!"/n/n/n/n/n/n"I couldn't believe my eyes," said Lupin, still pacing,/nand ignoring Harry's interruption. "I thought the map/nmust be malfunctioning. How could he be with you?"/n/n"No one was with us!" said Harry./n/n"And then I saw another dot, moving fast toward you,/nlabeled Sirius Black. ... I saw him collide with you; I/nwatched as he pulled two of you into the Whomping/nWillow — "/n/n"One of us!" Ron said angrily./n/n"No, Ron," said Lupin. "Two of you."/n/nHe had stopped his pacing, his eyes moving over Ron./n/n"Do you think I could have a look at the rat?" he said/nevenly./n/n"What?" said Ron. "What's Scabbers got to do with/nit?"/n/n/n/n"Everything," said Lupin. "Could I see him, please?"/n/nRon hesitated, then put a hand inside his robes./nScabbers emerged, thrashing desperately; Ron had to/nseize his long bald tail to stop him escaping./nCrookshanks stood up on Black's leg and made a soft/nhissing noise./n/nLupin moved closer to Ron. He seemed to be holding/nhis breath as he gazed intently at Scabbers./n/n"What?" Ron said again, holding Scabbers close to/nhim, looking scared. "What's my rat got to do with/nanything?"/n/n"That's not a rat," croaked Sirius Black suddenly./n/n/n/n/n/n"What d'you mean — of course he's a rat — "/n/n"No, he's not," said Lupin quietly. "He's a wizard."/n/n"An Animagus," said Black, "by the name of Peter/nPettigrew."/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n

title: Moony, Wormtail, Padfoot, And
text: /nPRONGS/n/nIt took a few seconds for the absurdity of this/nstatement to sink in. Then Ron voiced what Harry/nwas thinking./n/n"You're both mental."/n/n"Ridiculous!" said Hermione faintly./n/n"Peter Pettigrew's dead!" said Harry. "He killed him/ntwelve years ago!" He pointed at Black, whose face/ntwitched convulsively./n/n"I meant to," he growled, his yellow teeth bared, "but/nlittle Peter got the better of me ... not this time,/nthough!"/n/nAnd Crookshanks was thrown to the floor as Black/nlunged at Scabbers; Ron yelled with pain as Black's/nweight fell on his broken leg./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"Sirius, NO!" Lupin yelled, launching himself forwards/nand dragging Black away from Ron again, "WAIT! You/ncan't do it just like that — they need to understand —/nwe've got to explain — "/n/n"We can explain afterwards!" snarled Black, trying to/nthrow Lupin off. One hand was still clawing the air as/nit tried to reach Scabbers, who was squealing like a/npiglet, scratching Ron's face and neck as he tried to/nescape./n/n"They've — got — a — right — to — know —/neverything!" Lupin panted, still trying to restrain/nBlack. "Ron's kept him as a pet! There are parts of it/neven I don't understand! And Harry — you owe Harry/nthe truth, Sirius!"/n/nBlack stopped struggling, though his hollowed eyes/nwere still fixed on Scabbers, who was clamped tightly/nunder Ron's bitten, scratched, and bleeding hands./n/n"All right, then," Black said, without taking his eyes/noff the rat. "Tell them whatever you like. But make it/nquick, Remus. I want to commit the murder I was/nimprisoned for. ..."/n/n"You're nutters, both of you," said Ron shakily,/nlooking round at Harry and Hermione for support./n/n"I've had enough of this. I'm off."/n/nHe tried to heave himself up on his good leg, but/nLupin raised his wand again, pointing it at Scabbers./n/n"You're going to hear me out, Ron," he said quietly./n"Just keep a tight hold on Peter while you listen."/n/n"HE'S NOT PETER, HE'S SCABBERS!" Ron yelled,/ntrying to force the rat back into his front pocket, but/nScabbers was fighting too hard; Ron swayed and/n/n/n/n/n/noverbalanced, and Harry caught him and pushed him/nback down to the bed. Then, ignoring Black, Harry/nturned to Lupin./n/n"There were witnesses who saw Pettigrew die," he/nsaid. "A whole street full of them ..."/n/n"They didn't see what they thought they saw!" said/nBlack savagely, still watching Scabbers struggling in/nRon's hands./n/n"Everyone thought Sirius killed Peter," said Lupin,/nnodding. "I believed it myself — until I saw the map/ntonight. Because the Marauder's map never lies .../nPeter's alive. Ron's holding him, Harry."/n/nHarry looked down at Ron, and as their eyes met,/nthey agreed, silently: Black and Lupin were both out/nof their minds. Their story made no sense whatsoever./nHow could Scabbers be Peter Pettigrew? Azkaban/nmust have unhinged Black after all — but why was/nLupin playing along with him?/n/nThen Hermione spoke, in a trembling, would-be calm/nsort of voice, as though trying to will Professor Lupin/nto talk sensibly./n/n"But Professor Lupin ... Scabbers can't be Pettigrew/n... it just can't be true, you know it can't ..."/n/n"Why can't it be true?" Lupin said calmly, as though/nthey were in class, and Hermione had simply spotted/na problem in an experiment with grindylows./n/n"Because . . . because people would know if Peter/nPettigrew had been an Animagus. We did Animagi in/nclass with Professor McGonagall. And I looked them/nup when I did my homework — the Ministry of Magic/nkeeps tabs on witches and wizards who can become/n/n/n/n/nanimals; there's a register showing what animal they/nbecome, and their markings and things ... and I went/nand looked Professor McGonagall up on the register,/nand there have been only seven Animagi this century,/nand Pettigrew's name wasn't on the list — "/n/nHarry had barely had time to marvel inwardly at the/neffort Hermione put into her homework, when Lupin/nstarted to laugh. "Right again, Hermione!" he said./n"But the Ministry never knew that there used to be/nthree unregistered Animagi running around/nHogwarts."/n/n"If you're going to tell them the story, get a move on,/nRemus," snarled Black, who was still watching/nScabbers's every desperate move. "I've waited twelve/nyears, I'm not going to wait much longer."/n/n"All right ... but you'll need to help me, Sirius," said/nLupin, "I only know how it began ..."/n/nLupin broke off. There had been a loud creak behind/nhim. The bedroom door had opened of its own accord./nAll five of them stared at it. Then Lupin strode toward/nit and looked out into the landing./n/n"No one there ..."/n/n"This place is haunted!" said Ron./n/n"It's not," said Lupin, still looking at the door in a/npuzzled way. "The Shrieking Shack was never/nhaunted. ... The screams and howls the villagers used/nto hear were made by me."/n/nHe pushed his graying hair out of his eyes, thought/nfor a moment, then said, "That's where all of this/nstarts — with my becoming a werewolf. None of this/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/ncould have happened if I hadn't been bitten ... and if I/nhadn't been so foolhardy. ..."/n/nHe looked sober and tired. Ron started to interrupt,/nbut Hermione said, "Shh!" She was watching Lupin/nvery intently./n/n"I was a very small boy when I received the bite. My/nparents tried everything, but in those days there was/nno cure. The potion that Professor Snape has been/nmaking for me is a very recent discovery. It makes me/nsafe, you see. As long as I take it in the week/npreceding the full moon, I keep my mind when I/ntransform. ... I am able to curl up in my office, a/nharmless wolf, and wait for the moon to wane again./n/n"Before the Wolfsbane Potion was discovered,/nhowever, I became a fully fledged monster once a/nmonth. It seemed impossible that I would be able to/ncome to Hogwarts. Other parents weren't likely to/nwant their children exposed to me./n/n"But then Dumbledore became Headmaster, and he/nwas sympathetic. He said that as long as we took/ncertain precautions, there was no reason I shouldn't/ncome to school. ..." Lupin sighed, and looked directly/nat Harry. "I told you, months ago, that the Whomping/nWillow was planted the year I came to Hogwarts. The/ntruth is that it was planted because I came to/nHogwarts. This house" — Lupin looked miserably/naround the room, — "the tunnel that leads to it —/nthey were built for my use. Once a month, I was/nsmuggled out of the castle, into this place, to/ntransform. The tree was placed at the tunnel mouth/nto stop anyone coming across me while I was/ndangerous."/n/nHarry couldn't see where this story was going, but he/nwas listening raptly all the same. The only sound/n/n/n/n/n/napart from Lupin's voice was Scabbers's frightened/nsqueaking./n/n/n/n"My transformations in those days were — were/nterrible. It is very painful to turn into a werewolf. I/nwas separated from humans to bite, so I bit and/nscratched myself instead. The villagers heard the/nnoise and the screaming and thought they were/nhearing particularly violent spirits. Dumbledore/nencouraged the rumor. . . . Even now, when the house/nhas been silent for years, the villagers don't dare/napproach it. .../n/n"But apart from my transformations, I was happier/nthan I had ever been in my life. For the first time ever,/nI had friends, three great friends. Sirius Black .../n/nPeter Pettigrew ... and, of course, your father, Harry/n— James Potter./n/n"Now, my three friends could hardly fail to notice that/nI disappeared once a month. I made up all sorts of/nstories. I told them my mother was ill, and that I had/nto go home to see her. ... I was terrified they would/ndesert me the moment they found out what I was. But/nof course, they, like you, Hermione, worked out the/ntruth. .../n/n"And they didn't desert me at all. Instead, they did/nsomething for me that would make my/ntransformations not only bearable, but the best times/nof my life. They became Animagi."/n/n"My dad too?" said Harry, astounded./n/n"Yes, indeed," said Lupin. "It took them the best part/nof three years to work out how to do it. Your father/nand Sirius here were the cleverest students in the/nschool, and lucky they were, because the Animagus/ntransformation can go horribly wrong — one reason/n/n/n/n/nthe Ministry keeps a close watch on those attempting/nto do it. Peter needed all the help he could get from/nJames and Sirius. Finally, in our fifth year, they/nmanaged it. They could each turn into a different/nanimal at will."/n/n"But how did that help you?" said Hermione,/nsounding puzzled./n/n"They couldn't keep me company as humans, so they/nkept me company as animals," said Lupin. "A/nwerewolf is only a danger to people. They sneaked out/nof the castle every month under James's Invisibility/nCloak. They transformed . . . Peter, as the smallest,/ncould slip beneath the Willow's attacking branches/nand touch the knot that freezes it. They would then/nslip down the tunnel and join me. Under their/ninfluence, I became less dangerous. My body was still/nwolfish, but my mind seemed to become less so while/nI was with them."/n/n"Hurry up, Remus," snarled Black, who was still/nwatching Scabbers with a horrible sort of hunger on/nhis face./n/n"I'm getting there, Sirius, I'm getting there ... well,/nhighly exciting possibilities were open to us now that/nwe could all transform. Soon we were leaving the/nShrieking Shack and roaming the school grounds and/nthe village by night. Sirius and James transformed/ninto such large animals, they were able to keep a/nwerewolf in check. I doubt whether any Hogwarts/nstudents ever found out more about the Hogwarts/ngrounds and Hogsmeade than we did. ... And that's/nhow we came to write the Marauder's Map, and sign it/nwith our nicknames. Sirius is Padfoot. Peter is/nWormtail. James was Prongs."/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"What sort of animal — ?" Harry began, but Hermione/ncut him off./n/n"That was still really dangerous! Running around in/nthe dark with a werewolf! What if you'd given the/nothers the slip, and bitten somebody?"/n/n"A thought that still haunts me," said Lupin heavily./n"And there were near misses, many of them. We/nlaughed about them afterwards. We were young,/nthoughtless — carried away with our own cleverness."/n/n"I sometimes felt guilty about betraying Dumbledore's/ntrust, of course ... he had admitted me to Hogwarts/nwhen no other headmaster would have done so, and/nhe had no idea I was breaking the rules he had set/ndown for my own and others' safety. He never knew I/nhad led three fellow students into becoming Animagi/nillegally. But I always managed to forget my guilty/nfeelings every time we sat down to plan our next/nmonth's adventure. And I haven't changed ..."/n/nLupin's face had hardened, and there was self-disgust/nin his voice. "All this year, I have been battling with/nmyself, wondering whether I should tell Dumbledore/nthat Sirius was an Animagus. But I didn't do it. Why?/nBecause I was too cowardly. It would have meant/nadmitting that I'd betrayed his trust while I was at/nschool, admitting that I'd led others along with me .../nand Dumbledore's trust has meant everything to me./nHe let me into Hogwarts as a boy, and he gave me a/njob when I have been shunned all my adult life,/nunable to find paid work because of what I am. And/nso I convinced myself that Sirius was getting into the/nschool using dark arts he learned from Voldemort,/nthat being an Animagus had nothing to do with it . . ./nso, in a way, Snape's been right about me all along."/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"Snape?" said Black harshly, taking his eyes off/nScabbers for the first time in minutes and looking up/nat Lupin. "What's Snape got to do with it?"/n/n"He's here, Sirius," said Lupin heavily. "He's teaching/nhere as well." He looked up at Harry, Ron, and/nHermione./n/n"Professor Snape was at school with us. He fought/nvery hard against my appointment to the Defense/nAgainst the Dark Arts job. He has been telling/nDumbledore all year that I am not to be trusted. He/nhas his reasons ... you see, Sirius here played a trick/non him which nearly killed him, a trick which/ninvolved me — "/n/nBlack made a derisive noise./n/n"It served him right," he sneered. "Sneaking around,/ntrying to find out what we were up to . . . hoping he/ncould get us expelled. ..."/n/n"Severus was very interested in where I went every/nmonth." Lupin told Harry, Ron, and Hermione. "We/nwere in the same year, you know, and we — er —/ndidn't like each other very much. He especially/ndisliked James. Jealous, I think, of James's talent on/nthe Quidditch field . . . anyway Snape had seen me/ncrossing the grounds with Madam Pomfrey one/nevening as she led me toward the Whomping Willow/nto transform. Sirius thought it would be — er —/namusing, to tell Snape all he had to do was prod the/nknot on the tree trunk with a long stick, and he'd be/nable to get in after me. Well, of course, Snape tried it/n— if he'd got as far as this house, he'd have met a/nfully grown werewolf — but your father, who'd heard/nwhat Sirius had done, went after Snape and pulled/nhim back, at great risk to his life . . . Snape glimpsed/nme, though, at the end of the tunnel. He was/n/n/n/n/nforbidden by Dumbledore to tell anybody, but from/nthat time on he knew what I was. ..."/n/n"So that's why Snape doesn't like you," said Harry/nslowly, "because he thought you were in on the joke?"/n/n"That's right," sneered a cold voice from the wall/nbehind Lupin./n/nSeverus Snape was pulling off the Invisibility Cloak,/nhis wand pointing directly at Lupin./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n

title: The Servant Of Lord Voldermort
text: /nHermione screamed. Black leapt to his feet. Harry felt/nas though he'd received a huge electric shock./n/n"I found this at the base of the Whomping Willow,"/nsaid Snape, throwing the cloak aside, careful to keep/nthis wand pointing directly at Lupin's chest. "Very/nuseful, Potter, I thank you. ..."/n/nSnape was slightly breathless, but his face was full of/nsuppressed triumph. "You're wondering, perhaps,/nhow I knew you were here?" he said, his eyes/nglittering. "I've just been to your office, Lupin. You/nforgot to take your potion tonight, so I took a gobletful/nalong. And very lucky I did ... lucky for me, I mean./nLying on your desk was a certain map. One glance at/nit told me all I needed to know. I saw you running/nalong this passageway and out of sight."/n/n"Severus — " Lupin began, but Snape overrode him./n/n/n/n/n/n/n"I've told the headmaster again and again that you're/nhelping your old friend Black into the castle, Lupin,/nand here's the proof. Not even I dreamed you would/nhave the nerve to use this old place as your hideout/n/n/n/n"Severus, you're making a mistake," said Lupin/nurgently. "You haven't heard everything — I can/nexplain — Sirius is not here to kill Harry — "/n/n"Two more for Azkaban tonight," said Snape, his eyes/nnow gleaming fanatically. "I shall be interested to see/nhow Dumbledore takes this. ... He was quite/nconvinced you were harmless, you know, Lupin ... a/ntame werewolf — "/n/n"You fool," said Lupin softly. "Is a schoolboy grudge/nworth putting an innocent man back inside/nAzkaban?"/n/nBANG! Thin, snakelike cords burst from the end of/nSnape's wand and twisted themselves around Lupin's/nmouth, wrists, and ankles; he overbalanced and fell/nto the floor, unable to move. With a roar of rage,/n/nBlack started toward Snape, but Snape pointed his/nwand straight between Black's eyes./n/n"Give me a reason," he whispered. "Give me a reason/nto do it, and I swear I will."/n/nBlack stopped dead. It would have been impossible to/nsay which face showed more hatred./n/nHarry stood there, paralyzed, not knowing what to do/nor whom to believe. He glanced around at Ron and/nHermione. Ron looked just as confused as he did, still/nfighting to keep hold on the struggling Scabbers./nHermione, however, took an uncertain step toward/nSnape and said, in a very breathless voice, "Professor/n/n/n/n/nSnape — it — it wouldn't hurt to hear what they've/ngot to say, w — would it?"/n/n"Miss Granger, you are already facing suspension/nfrom this school," Snape spat. "You, Potter, and/nWeasley are out-of-bounds, in the company of a/nconvicted murderer and a werewolf. For once in your/nlife, hold your tongue."/n/n"But if — if there was a mistake — "/n/n"KEEP QUIET, YOU STUPID GIRL!" Snape shouted,/nlooking suddenly quite deranged. "DONT TALK/nABOUT WHAT YOU DONT UNDERSTAND!" A few/nsparks shot out of the end of his wand, which was/nstill pointed at Black's face. Hermione fell silent./n/n"Vengeance is very sweet," Snape breathed at Black./n"How I hoped I would be the one to catch you. ..."/n/n"The joke's on you again, Severus," Black snarled. "As/nlong as this boy brings his rat up to the castle" — he/njerked his head at Ron — "I'll come quietly. ..."/n/n"Up to the castle?" said Snape silkily. "I don't think/nwe need to go that far. All I have to do is call the/ndementors once we get out of the Willow. They'll be/nvery pleased to see you, Black ... pleased enough to/ngive you a little kiss, I daresay. ..."/n/nWhat little color there was in Black's face left it./n/n"You — you've got to hear me out," he croaked. "The/nrat — look at the rat — "/n/nBut there was a mad glint in Snape 's eyes that Harry/nhad never seen before. He seemed beyond reason./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"Come on, all of you," he said. He clicked his fingers,/nand the ends of the cords that bound Lupin flew to/nhis hands. "Ill drag the werewolf. Perhaps the/ndementors will have a kiss for him too — "/n/nBefore he knew what he was doing, Harry had crossed/nthe room in three strides and blocked the door./n/n"Get out of the way, Potter, you're in enough trouble/nalready," snarled Snape. "If I hadn't been here to save/nyour skin — "/n/n"Professor Lupin could have killed me about a/nhundred times this year," Harry said. "I've been alone/nwith him loads of times, having defense lessons/nagainst the dementors. If he was helping Black, why/ndidn't he just finish me off then?"/n/n"Don't ask me to fathom the way a werewolf's mind/nworks," hissed Snape. "Get out of the way, Potter."/n/n"YOU'RE PATHETIC!" Harry yelled. "JUST BECAUSE/nTHEY MADE A FOOL OF YOU AT SCHOOL YOU/nWONT EVEN LISTEN — "/n/n"SILENCE! I WILL NOT BE SPOKEN TO LIKE THAT!"/nSnape shrieked, looking madder than ever. "Like/nfather, like son, Potter! I have just saved your neck;/nyou should be thanking me on bended knee! You/nwould have been well served if he'd killed you! You'd/nhave died like your father, too arrogant to believe you/nmight be mistaken in Black — now get out of the way,/nor I will make you. GET OUT OF THE WAY, POTTER!"/n/nHarry made up his mind in a split second. Before/nSnape could take even one step toward him, he had/nraised his wand./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n" Expelliarmus\" he yelled — except that his wasn't the/nonly voice that shouted. There was a blast that made/nthe door rattle on its hinges; Snape was lifted off his/nfeet and slammed into the wall, then slid down it to/nthe floor, a trickle of blood oozing from under his hair./nHe had been knocked out./n/nHarry looked around. Both Ron and Hermione had/ntried to disarm Snape at exactly the same moment./nSnape 's wand soared in a high arc and landed on the/nbed next to Crookshanks./n/n"You shouldn't have done that," said Black, looking at/nHarry. "You should have left him to me. ..."/n/nHarry avoided Black's eyes. He wasn't sure, even now,/nthat he'd done the right thing./n/n"We attacked a teacher. ... We attacked a teacher ... ,"/nHermione whimpered, staring at the lifeless Snape/nwith frightened eyes. "Oh, we're going to be in so/nmuch trouble — "/n/nLupin was struggling against his bonds. Black bent/ndown quickly and untied him. Lupin straightened up,/nrubbing his arms where the ropes had cut into them./n/n"Thank you, Harry," he said./n/n"I'm still not saying I believe you," he told Lupin./n/n"Then it's time we offered you some proof," said/nLupin. "You, boy — give me Peter, please. Now."/n/nRon clutched Scabbers closer to his chest./n/n"Come off it," he said weakly. "Are you trying to say/nhe broke out of Azkaban just to get his hands on/nScabbers ? I mean ..." He looked up at Harry and/n/n/n/n/n/nHermione for support, "Okay, say Pettigrew could/nturn into a rat — there are millions of rats — how's he/nsupposed to know which one he's after if he was/nlocked up in Azkaban?"/n/n"You know, Sirius, that's a fair question," said Lupin,/nturning to Black and frowning slightly. "How did you/nfind out where he was?"/n/nBlack put one of his clawlike hands inside his robes/nand took out a crumpled piece of paper, which he/nsmoothed flat and held out to show the others./n/nIt was the photograph of Ron and his family that had/nappeared in the Daily Prophet the previous summer,/nand there, on Ron's shoulder, was Scabbers./n/n"How did you get this?" Lupin asked Black,/nthunderstruck./n/n"Fudge," said Black. "When he came to inspect/nAzkaban last year, he gave me his paper. And there/nwas Peter, on the front page ... on this boy's shoulder./n... I knew him at once . . . how many times had I seen/nhim transform? And the caption said the boy would/nbe going back to Hogwarts ... to where Harry was. ..."/n/n"My God," said Lupin softly, staring from Scabbers to/nthe picture in the paper and back again. "His front/npaw ..."/n/n"What about it?" said Ron defiantly./n/n"He's got a toe missing," said Black./n/n"Of course," Lupin breathed. "So simple ... so brilliant/n... he cut it off himself?"/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"Just before he transformed," said Black. "When I/ncornered him, he yelled for the whole street to hear/nthat I'd betrayed Lily and James. Then, before I could/ncurse him, he blew apart the street with the wand/nbehind his back, killed everyone within twenty feet of/nhimself — and sped down into the sewer with the/nother rats. ..."/n/n"Didn't you ever hear, Ron?" said Lupin. "The biggest/nbit of Peter they found was his finger."/n/n"Look, Scabbers probably had a fight with another rat/nor something! He's been in my family for ages, right —/n/n/n/n"Twelve years, in fact," said Lupin. "Didn't you ever/nwonder why he was living so long?"/n/n"We — we've been taking good care of him!" said Ron./n/n"Not looking too good at the moment, though, is he?"/nsaid Lupin. "I'd guess he's been losing weight ever/nsince he heard Sirius was on the loose again. ..."/n/n"He's been scared of that mad cat!" said Ron, nodding/ntoward Crookshanks, who was still purring on the/nbed./n/nBut that wasn't right, Harry thought suddenly. .../nScabbers had been looking ill before he met/nCrookshanks . . . ever since Ron's return from Egypt . . ./nsince the time when Black had escaped. .../n/n"This cat isn't mad," said Black hoarsely. He reached/nout a bony hand and stroked Crookshanks 's fluffy/nhead. "He's the most intelligent of his kind I've ever/nmet. He recognized Peter for what he was right away./nAnd when he met me, he knew I was no dog. It was a/nwhile before he trusted me. ... Finally, I managed to/n/n/n/n/ncommunicate to him what I was after, and he's been/nhelping me. ..."/n/n/n/n"What do you mean?" breathed Hermione./n/n"He tried to bring Peter to me, but couldn't ... so he/nstole the passwords into Gryffindor Tower for me. .../n/nAs I understand it, he took them from a boy's bedside/ntable. ..."/n/nHarry's brain seemed to be sagging under the weight/nof what he was hearing. It was absurd . . . and yet . . ./n/n"But Peter got wind of what was going on and ran for/nit. ..." croaked Black. "This cat — Crookshanks, did/nyou call him? — told me Peter had left blood on the/nsheets. ... I supposed he bit himself. ... Well, faking/nhis own death had worked once. ..."/n/nThese words jolted Harry to his senses./n/n"And why did he fake his death?" he said furiously./n"Because he knew you were about to kill him like you/nkilled my parents!"/n/n"No," said Lupin, "Harry — "/n/n"And now you've come to finish him off!"/n/n"Yes, I have," said Black, with an evil look at/nScabbers./n/n"Then I should've let Snape take you!" Harry shouted./n/n"Harry," said Lupin hurriedly, "don't you see? All this/ntime we've thought Sirius betrayed your parents, and/nPeter tracked him down — but it was the other way/naround, don't you see? Peter betrayed your mother/nand father — Sirius tracked Peter down — "/n/n/n/n/n/n"THAT'S NOT TRUE!" Harry yelled. "HE WAS THEIR/nSECRET-KEEPER! HE SAID SO BEFORE YOU/nTURNED UP. HE SAID HE KILLED THEM!"/n/nHe was pointing at Black, who shook his head slowly;/nthe sunken eyes were suddenly overbright./n/n"Harry ... I as good as killed them," he croaked. "I/npersuaded Lily and James to change to Peter at the/nlast moment, persuaded them to use him as Secret-/nKeeper instead of me. ... I'm to blame, I know it. .../nThe night they died, I'd arranged to check on Peter,/nmake sure he was still safe, but when I arrived at his/nhiding place, he'd gone. Yet there was no sign of a/nstruggle. It didn't feel right. I was scared. I set out for/nyour parents' house straight away. And when I saw/ntheir house, destroyed, and their bodies ... I realized/nwhat Peter must've done ... what I'd done. ..."/n/nHis voice broke. He turned away./n/n"Enough of this," said Lupin, and there was a steely/nnote in his voice Harry had never heard before./n"There's one certain way to prove what really/nhappened. Ron, give me that rat"/n/n"What are you going to do with him if I give him to/nyou?" Ron asked Lupin tensely./n/n"Force him to show himself," said Lupin. "If he really/nis a rat, it won't hurt him."/n/nRon hesitated. Then at long last, he held out/nScabbers and Lupin took him. Scabbers began to/nsqueak without stopping, twisting and turning, his/ntiny black eyes bulging in his head./n/n"Ready, Sirius?" said Lupin./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nBlack had already retrieved Snape's wand from the/nbed. He approached Lupin and the struggling rat, and/nhis wet eyes suddenly seemed to be burning in his/nface./n/n"Together?" he said quietly./n/n"I think so," said Lupin, holding Scabbers tightly in/none hand and his wand in the other. "On the count of/nthree. One — two — THREE!"/n/nA flash of blue-white light erupted from both wands;/nfor a moment, Scabbers was frozen in midair, his/nsmall gray form twisting madly — Ron yelled — the/nrat fell and hit the floor. There was another blinding/nflash of light and then —/n/nIt was like watching a speeded-up film of a growing/ntree. A head was shooting upward from the ground;/nlimbs were sprouting; a moment later, a man was/nstanding where Scabbers had been, cringing and/nwringing his hands. Crookshanks was spitting and/nsnarling on the bed; the hair on his back was/nstanding up./n/nHe was a very short man, hardly taller than Harry/nand Hermione. His thin, colorless hair was unkempt/nand there was a large bald patch on top. He had the/nshrunken appearance of a plump man who has lost a/nlot of weight in a short time. His skin looked grubby,/nalmost like Scabbers 's fur, and something of the rat/nlingered around his pointed nose and his very small,/nwatery eyes. He looked around at them all, his/nbreathing fast and shallow. Harry saw his eyes dart to/nthe door and back again./n/n"Well, hello, Peter," said Lupin pleasantly, as though/nrats frequently erupted into old school friends around/nhim. "Long time, no see."/n/n/n/n/n/n"S — Sirius ... R — Remus ..." Even Pettigrew's voice/nwas squeaky. Again, his eyes darted toward the door./n"My friends ... my old friends ..."/n/nBlack's wand arm rose, but Lupin seized him around/nthe wrist, gave him a warning look, then turned again/nto Pettigrew, his voice light and casual./n/n"We've been having a little chat, Peter, about what/nhappened the night Lily and James died. You might/nhave missed the finer points while you were/nsqueaking around down there on the bed — "/n/n"Remus," gasped Pettigrew, and Harry could see/nbeads of sweat breaking out over his pasty face, "you/ndon't believe him, do you... ? He tried to kill me,/nRemus. ..."/n/n"So we've heard," said Lupin, more coldly. "I'd like to/nclear up one or two little matters with you, Peter, if/nyou'd be so — "/n/n"He's come to try and kill me again!" Pettigrew/nsqueaked suddenly, pointing at Black, and Harry saw/nthat he used his middle finger, because his index was/nmissing. "He killed Lily and James and now he's going/nto kill me too. ... You've got to help me, Remus. ..."/n/nBlack's face looked more skull-like than ever as he/nstared at Pettigrew with his fathomless eyes./n/n"No one's going to try and kill you until we've sorted a/nfew things out," said Lupin./n/n"Sorted things out?" squealed Pettigrew, looking/nwildly about him once more, eyes taking in the/nboarded windows and, again, the only door. "I knew/nhe'd come after me! I knew he'd be back for me! I've/nbeen waiting for this for twelve years!"/n/n/n/n/n/n"You knew Sirius was going to break out of Azkaban?"/nsaid Lupin, his brow furrowed. "When nobody has/never done it before?"/n/n"He's got dark powers the rest of us can only dream/nof!" Pettigrew shouted shrilly. "How else did he get out/nof there? I suppose He-Who-Must-Not-Be-Named/ntaught him a few tricks!"/n/nBlack started to laugh, a horrible, mirthless laugh/nthat filled the whole room./n/n"Voldemort, teach me tricks?" he said./n/nPettigrew flinched as though Black had brandished a/nwhip at him./n/n"What, scared to hear your old master's name?" said/nBlack. "I don't blame you, Peter. His lot aren't very/nhappy with you, are they?"/n/n"Don't know what you mean, Sirius — " muttered/nPettigrew, his breathing faster than ever. His whole/nface was shining with sweat now./n/n"You haven't been hiding from me for twelve years,"/nsaid Black. "You've been hiding from Voldemort's old/nsupporters. I heard things in Azkaban, Peter. ... They/nall think you're dead, or you'd have to answer to/nthem. ... I've heard them screaming all sorts of things/nin their sleep. Sounds like they think the double-/ncrosser double-crossed them. Voldemort went to the/nPotters' on your information ... and Voldemort met his/ndownfall there. And not all Voldemort's supporters/nended up in Azkaban, did they? There are still plenty/nout here, biding their time, pretending they've seen/nthe error of their ways. ... If they ever got wind that/nyou were still alive, Peter — "/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"Don't know ... what you're talking about... said/nPettigrew again, more shrilly than ever. He wiped his/nface on his sleeve and looked up at Lupin. "You don't/nbelieve this — this madness, Remus — "/n/n"I must admit, Peter, I have difficulty in/nunderstanding why an innocent man would want to/nspend twelve years as a rat," said Lupin evenly./n/n"Innocent, but scared!" squealed Pettigrew. "If/nVoldemort's supporters were after me, it was because/nI put one of their best men in Azkaban — the spy,/nSirius Black!"/n/nBlack's face contorted./n/n"How dare you," he growled, sounding suddenly like/nthe bear-sized dog he had been. "I, a spy for/nVoldemort? When did I ever sneak around people who/nwere stronger and more powerful than myself? But/nyou, Peter — I'll never understand why I didn't see/nyou were the spy from the start. You always liked big/nfriends who'd look after you, didn't you? It used to be/nus ... me and Remus ... and James. ..."/n/nPettigrew wiped his face again; he was almost panting/nfor breath./n/n"Me, a spy ... must be out of your mind ... never .../ndon't know how you can say such a — "/n/n"Lily and James only made you Secret-Keeper/nbecause I suggested it," Black hissed, so venomously/nthat Pettigrew took a step backward. "I thought it was/nthe perfect plan ... a bluff. ... Voldemort would be/nsure to come after me, would never dream they'd use/na weak, talentless thing like you. ... It must have been/nthe finest moment of your miserable life, telling/nVoldemort you could hand him the Potters."/n/n/n/n/n/nPettigrew was muttering distractedly; Harry caught/nwords like "far-fetched" and "lunacy," but he couldn't/nhelp paying more attention to the ashen color of/nPettigrew's face and the way his eyes continued to/ndart toward the windows and door./n/n"Professor Lupin?" said Hermione timidly. "Can — can/nI say something?"/n/n"Certainly, Hermione," said Lupin courteously./n/n"Well — Scabbers — I mean, this — this man — he's/nbeen sleeping in Harry's dormitory for three years. If/nhe's working for You-Know-Who, how come he never/ntried to hurt Harry before now?"/n/n"There!" said Pettigrew shrilly, pointing at Ron with/nhis maimed hand. "Thank you! You see, Remus? I/nhave never hurt a hair of Harry's head! Why should/nI?"/n/n"I'll tell you why," said Black. "Because you never did/nanything for anyone unless you could see what was in/nit for you. Voldemort's been in hiding for fifteen years,/nthey say he's half dead. You weren't about to commit/nmurder right under Albus Dumbledore's nose, for a/nwreck of a wizard who'd lost all of his power, were/nyou? You'd want to be quite sure he was the biggest/nbully in the playground before you went back to him,/nwouldn't you? Why else did you find a wizard family/nto take you in? Keeping an ear out for news, weren't/nyou, Peter? Just in case your old protector regained/nstrength, and it was safe to rejoin him. ..."/n/nPettigrew opened his mouth and closed it several/ntimes. He seemed to have lost the ability to talk./n/n"Er — Mr. Black — Sirius?" said Hermione./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nBlack jumped at being addressed like this and stared/nat Hermione as though he had never seen anything/nquite like her./n/n"If you don't mind me asking, how — how did you get/nout of Azkaban, if you didn't use Dark Magic?"/n/n"Thank you!" gasped Pettigrew, nodding frantically at/nher. "Exactly! Precisely what I — "/n/nBut Lupin silenced him with a look. Black was/nfrowning slightly at Hermione, but not as though he/nwere annoyed with her. He seemed to be pondering/nhis answer./n/n"I don't know how I did it," he said slowly. "I think the/nonly reason I never lost my mind is that I knew I was/ninnocent. That wasn't a happy thought, so the/ndementors couldn't suck it out of me ... but it kept me/nsane and knowing who I am . . . helped me keep my/npowers ... so when it all became . . . too much ... I/ncould transform in my cell . . . become a dog./nDementors can't see, you know. ..." He swallowed./n"They feel their way toward people by feeding off their/nemotions. ... They could tell that my feelings were less/n— less human, less complex when I was a dog ... but/nthey thought, of course, that I was losing my mind/nlike everyone else in there, so it didn't trouble them./nBut I was weak, very weak, and I had no hope of/ndriving them away from me without a wand. .../n/n"But then I saw Peter in that picture ... I realized he/nwas at Hogwarts with Harry . . . perfectly positioned to/nact, if one hint reached his ears that the Dark Side/nwas gathering strength again. ..."/n/nPettigrew was shaking his head, mouthing/nnoiselessly, but staring all the while at Black as/nthough hypnotized./n/n/n/n/n/n"... ready to strike at the moment he could be sure of/nallies ... and to deliver the last Potter to them. If he/ngave them Harry, who'd dare say he'd betrayed Lord/nVoldemort? He'd be welcomed back with honors. .../n/n"So you see, I had to do something. I was the only one/nwho knew Peter was still alive. ..."/n/nHarry remembered what Mr. Weasley had told Mrs./nWeasley. "The guards say he's been talking in his/nsleep ... always the same words ... 'He's at Hog warts.'/n/n/n/n"It was as if someone had lit a fire in my head, and/nthe dementors couldn't destroy it. ... It wasn't a/nhappy feeling ... it was an obsession . . . but it gave me/nstrength, it cleared my mind. So, one night when they/nopened my door to bring food, I slipped past them as/na dog. ... It's so much harder for them to sense/nanimal emotions that they were confused. ... I was/nthin, very thin . . . thin enough to slip through the/nbars. ... I swam as a dog back to the mainland. ... I/njourneyed north and slipped into the Hogwarts/ngrounds as a dog. I've been living in the forest ever/nsince, except when I came to watch the Quidditch, of/ncourse. You fly as well as your father did, Harry. ..."/n/nHe looked at Harry, who did not look away./n/n"Believe me," croaked Black. "Believe me, Harry. I/nnever betrayed James and Lily. I would have died/nbefore I betrayed them."/n/nAnd at long last, Harry believed him. Throat too tight/nto speak, he nodded./n/n"No!"/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nPettigrew had fallen to his knees as though Harry's/nnod had been his own death sentence. He shuffled/nforward on his knees, groveling, his hands clasped in/nfront of him as though praying./n/n"Sirius — it's me ... it's Peter ... your friend ... you/nwouldn't ..."/n/nBlack kicked out and Pettigrew recoiled./n/n"There's enough filth on my robes without you/ntouching them," said Black./n/n"Remus!" Pettigrew squeaked, turning to Lupin/ninstead, writhing imploringly in front of him. "You/ndon't believe this ... wouldn't Sirius have told you/nthey'd changed the plan?"/n/n"Not if he thought I was the spy, Peter," said Lupin. "I/nassume that's why you didn't tell me, Sirius?" he said/ncasually over Pettigrew's head./n/n"Forgive me, Remus," said Black./n/n"Not at all, Padfoot, old friend," said Lupin, who was/nnow rolling up his sleeves. "And will you, in turn,/nforgive me for believing you were the spy?"/n/n"Of course," said Black, and the ghost of a grin flitted/nacross his gaunt face. He, too, began rolling up his/nsleeves. "Shall we kill him together?"/n/n"Yes, I think so," said Lupin grimly./n/n"You wouldn't ... you won't... ," gasped Pettigrew. And/nhe scrambled around to Ron./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"Ron ... haven't I been a good friend ... a good pet?/n/nYou won't let them kill me, Ron, will you ... you're on/nmy side, aren't you?"/n/nBut Ron was staring at Pettigrew with the utmost/nrevulsion./n/n"I let you sleep in my bed\" he said./n/n"Kind boy ... kind master ..." Pettigrew crawled toward/nRon, "you won't let them do it. ... I was your rat. ... I/nwas a good pet. ..."/n/n"If you made a better rat than a human, it's not much/nto boast about, Peter," said Black harshly. Ron, going/nstill paler with pain, wrenched his broken leg out of/nPettigrew's reach. Pettigrew turned on his knees,/nstaggered forward, and seized the hem of Hermione's/nrobes./n/n"Sweet girl ... clever girl ... you — you won't let them./n... Help me. ..."/n/nHermione pulled her robes out of Pettigrew's/nclutching hands and backed away against the wall,/nlooking horrified./n/nPettigrew knelt, trembling uncontrollably, and turned/nhis head slowly toward Harry./n/n"Harry ... Harry ... you look just like your father .../njust like him. ..."/n/n"HOW DARE YOU SPEAK TO HARRY?" roared Black./n"HOW DARE YOU FACE HIM? HOW DARE YOU TALK/nABOUT JAMES IN FRONT OF HIM?"/n/n"Harry," whispered Pettigrew, shuffling toward him,/nhands outstretched. "Harry, James wouldn't have/n/n/n/n/n/nwanted me killed. ... James would have understood,/nHarry ... he would have shown me mercy. ..."/n/n/n/nBoth Black and Lupin strode forward, seized/nPettigrew's shoulders, and threw him backward onto/nthe floor. He sat there, twitching with terror, staring/nup at them./n/n"You sold Lily and James to Voldemort," said Black,/nwho was shaking too. "Do you deny it?"/n/nPettigrew burst into tears. It was horrible to watch,/nlike an oversized, balding baby, cowering on the floor./n/n"Sirius, Sirius, what could I have done? The Dark/nLord . . . you have no idea ... he has weapons you can't/nimagine. ... I was scared, Sirius, I was never brave/nlike you and Remus and James. I never meant it to/nhappen. ... He-Who-Must-Not-Be-Named forced me —/n/n/n/n"DONT LIE!" bellowed Black. "YOU'D BEEN PASSING/nINFORMATION TO HIM FOR A YEAR BEFORE LILY/nAND JAMES DIED! YOU WERE HIS SPY!"/n/n"He — he was taking over everywhere!" gasped/nPettigrew. "Wh — what was there to be gained by/nrefusing him?"/n/n"What was there to be gained by fighting the most evil/nwizard who has ever existed?" said Black, with a/nterribly fury in his face. "Only innocent lives, Peter!"/n/n"You don't understand!" whined Pettigrew. "He would/nhave killed me, Sirius!"/n/n"THEN YOU SHOULD HAVE DIED!" roared Black./n"DIED RATHER THAN BETRAY YOUR FRIENDS, AS/nWE WOULD HAVE DONE FOR YOU!"/n/n/n/n/n/nBlack and Lupin stood shoulder to shoulder, wands/nraised./n/n"You should have realized," said Lupin quietly, "if/nVoldemort didn't kill you, we would. Good-bye, Peter."/n/nHermione covered her face with her hands and turned/nto the wall./n/n"NO!" Harry yelled. He ran forward, placing himself in/nfront of Pettigrew, facing the wands. "You can't kill/nhim," he said breathlessly. "You can't."/n/nBlack and Lupin both looked staggered./n/n"Harry, this piece of vermin is the reason you have no/nparents," Black snarled. "This cringing bit of filth/nwould have seen you die too, without turning a hair./nYou heard him. His own stinking skin meant more to/nhim than your whole family."/n/n"I know," Harry panted. "We'll take him up to the/ncastle. We'll hand him over to the dementors. ... He/ncan go to Azkaban ... but don't kill him."/n/n"Harry!" gasped Pettigrew, and he flung his arms/naround Harry's knees. "You — thank you — it's more/nthan I deserve — thank you — "/n/n"Get off me," Harry spat, throwing Pettigrew's hands/noff him in disgust. "I'm not doing this for you. I'm/ndoing it because — I don't reckon my dad would've/nwanted them to become killers — just for you."/n/nNo one moved or made a sound except Pettigrew,/nwhose breath was coming in wheezes as he clutched/nhis chest. Black and Lupin were looking at each/nother. Then, with one movement, they lowered their/nwands./n/n/n/n/n/n"You're the only person who has the right to decide,/nHarry," said Black. "But think ... think what he did./n/n/n/n"He can go to Azkaban," Harry repeated. "If anyone/ndeserves that place, he does. ..."/n/nPettigrew was still wheezing behind him./n/n"Very well," said Lupin. "Stand aside, Harry."/n/nHarry hesitated./n/n"I'm going to tie him up," said Lupin. "That's all, I/nswear."/n/nHarry stepped out of the way. Thin cords shot from/nLupin's wand this time, and next moment, Pettigrew/nwas wriggling on the floor, bound and gagged./n/n"But if you transform, Peter," growled Black, his own/nwand pointing at Pettigrew too, "we will kill you. You/nagree, Harry?"/n/nHarry looked down at the pitiful figure on the floor/nand nodded so that Pettigrew could see him./n/n"Right," said Lupin, suddenly businesslike. "Ron, I/ncan't mend bones nearly as well as Madam Pomfrey,/nso I think it's best if we just strap your leg up until we/ncan get you to the hospital wing."/n/nHe hurried over to Ron, bent down, tapped Ron's leg/nwith his wand, and muttered, "Ferula." Bandages/nspun up Ron's leg, strapping it tightly to a splint./nLupin helped him to his feet; Ron put his weight/ngingerly on the leg and didn't wince./n/n"That's better," he said. "Thanks."/n/n/n/n/n/n"What about Professor Snape?" said Hermione in a/nsmall voice, looking down at Snape's prone figure./n/n/n/n"There's nothing seriously wrong with him," said/nLupin, bending over Snape and checking his pulse./n"You were just a little — overenthusiastic. Still out/ncold. Er — perhaps it will be best if we don't revive/nhim until we're safely back in the castle. We can take/nhim like this. ..."/n/nHe muttered, "Mobilicorpus." As though invisible/nstrings were tied to Snape's wrists, neck, and knees,/nhe was pulled into a standing position, head still/nlolling unpleasantly, like a grotesque puppet. He hung/na few inches above the ground, his limp feet dangling./nLupin picked up the Invisibility Cloak and tucked it/nsafely into his pocket./n/n"And two of us should be chained to this," said Black,/nnudging Pettigrew with his toe. "Just to make sure."/n/n"I'll do it," said Lupin./n/n"And me," said Ron savagely, limping forward./n/nBlack conjured heavy manacles from thin air; soon/nPettigrew was upright again, left arm chained to/nLupin's right, right arm to Ron's left. Ron's face was/nset. He seemed to have taken Scabbers's true identity/nas a personal insult. Crookshanks leapt lightly off the/nbed and led the way out of the room, his bottlebrush/ntail held jauntily high./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n

title: The Dementor's Kiss
text: /nHarry had never been part of a stranger group./nCrookshanks led the way down the stairs; Lupin,/nPettigrew, and Ron went next, looking like entrants in/na six-legged race. Next came Professor Snape, drifting/ncreepily along, his toes hitting each stair as they/ndescended, held up by his own wand, which was/nbeing pointed at him by Sirius. Harry and Hermione/nbrought up the rear./n/nGetting back into the tunnel was difficult. Lupin,/nPettigrew, and Ron had to turn sideways to manage/nit; Lupin still had Pettigrew covered with his wand./nHarry could see them edging awkwardly along the/ntunnel in single file. Crookshanks was still in the/nlead. Harry went right after Black, who was still/nmaking Snape drift along ahead of them; he kept/nbumping his lolling head on the low ceiling. Harry/nhad the impression Black was making no effort to/nprevent this./n/n/n/n/n/n/n"You know what this means?" Black said abruptly to/nHarry as they made their slow progress along the/ntunnel. "Turning Pettigrew in?"/n/n"You're free," said Harry./n/n"Yes ... ," said Black. "But I'm also — I don't know if/nanyone ever told you — I'm your godfather."/n/n"Yeah, I knew that," said Harry./n/n"Well ... your parents appointed me your guardian,"/nsaid Black stiffly. "If anything happened to them ..."/n/nHarry waited. Did Black mean what he thought he/nmeant?/n/n"I'll understand, of course, if you want to stay with/nyour aunt and uncle," said Black. "But ... well .../nthink about it. Once my name's cleared ... if you/nwanted a ... a different home ..."/n/nSome sort of explosion took place in the pit of Harry's/nstomach./n/n"What — live with you?" he said, accidentally cracking/nhis head on a bit of rock protruding from the ceiling./n"Leave the Dursleys?"/n/n"Of course, I thought you wouldn't want to," said/nBlack quickly. "I understand, I just thought I'd — "/n/n"Are you insane?" said Harry, his voice easily as/ncroaky as Black's. "Of course I want to leave the/nDursleys! Have you got a house? When can I move/nin?"/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nBlack turned right around to look at him; Snape's/nhead was scraping the ceiling but Black didn't seem/nto care./n/n"You want to?" he said. "You mean it?"/n/n"Yeah, I mean it!" said Harry./n/nBlack's gaunt face broke into the first true smile/nHarry had seen upon it. The difference it made was/nstartling, as though a person ten years younger were/nshining through the starved mask; for a moment, he/nwas recognizable as the man who had laughed at/nHarry's parents' wedding./n/nThey did not speak again until they had reached the/nend of the tunnel. Crookshanks darted up first; he/nhad evidently pressed his paw to the knot on the/ntrunk, because Lupin, Pettigrew, and Ron clambered/nupward without any sound of savaging branches./n/nBlack saw Snape up through the hole, then stood/nback for Harry and Hermione to pass. At last, all of/nthem were out./n/nThe grounds were very dark now; the only light came/nfrom the distant windows of the castle. Without a/nword, they set off. Pettigrew was still wheezing and/noccasionally whimpering. Harry's mind was buzzing./nHe was going to leave the Dursleys. He was going to/nlive with Sirius Black, his parents' best friend. ... He/nfelt dazed. ... What would happen when he told the/nDursleys he was going to live with the convict they'd/nseen on television... !/n/n"One wrong move, Peter," said Lupin threateningly/nahead. His wand was still pointed sideways at/nPettigrew's chest./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nSilently they tramped through the grounds, the castle/nlights growing slowly larger. Snape was still drifting/nweirdly ahead of Black, his chin bumping on his/nchest. And then —/n/nA cloud shifted. There were suddenly dim shadows on/nthe ground. Their party was bathed in moonlight./n/nSnape collided with Lupin, Pettigrew, and Ron, who/nhad stopped abruptly. Black froze. He flung out one/narm to make Harry and Hermione stop./n/nHarry could see Lupin's silhouette. He had gone rigid./nThen his limbs began to shake./n/n"Oh, my — " Hermione gasped. "He didn't take his/npotion tonight! He's not safe!"/n/n"Run," Black whispered. "Run. Now."/n/nBut Harry couldn't run. Ron was chained to Pettigrew/nand Lupin. He leapt forward but Black caught him/naround the chest and threw him back./n/n"Leave it to me — RUN!"/n/nThere was a terrible snarling noise. Lupin's head was/nlengthening. So was his body. His shoulders were/nhunching. Hair was sprouting visibly on his face and/nhands, which were curling into clawed paws./nCrookshanks's hair was on end again; he was backing/naway —/n/nAs the werewolf reared, snapping its long jaws, Sirius/ndisappeared from Harry's side. He had transformed./nThe enormous, bearlike dog bounded forward. As the/nwerewolf wrenched itself free of the manacle binding/nit, the dog seized it about the neck and pulled it/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nbackward, away from Ron and Pettigrew. They were/nlocked, jaw to jaw, claws ripping at each other —/n/nHarry stood, transfixed by the sight, too intent upon/nthe battle to notice anything else. It was Hermione's/nscream that alerted him —/n/nPettigrew had dived for Lupin's dropped wand. Ron,/nunsteady on his bandaged leg, fell. There was a bang,/na burst of light — and Ron lay motionless on the/nground. Another bang — Crookshanks flew into the/nair and back to the earth in a heap./n/n" ExpelliarmusV' Harry yelled, pointing his own wand/nat Pettigrew; Lupin's wand flew high into the air and/nout of sight. "Stay where you are!" Harry shouted,/nrunning forward./n/nToo late. Pettigrew had transformed. Harry saw his/nbald tail whip through the manacle on Ron's/noutstretched arm and heard a scurrying through the/ngrass./n/nThere was a howl and a rumbling growl; Harry turned/nto see the werewolf taking flight; it was galloping into/nthe forest —/n/n"Sirius, he's gone, Pettigrew transformed!" Harry/nyelled./n/nBlack was bleeding; there were gashes across his/nmuzzle and back, but at Harry's words he scrambled/nup again, and in an instant, the sound of his paws/nfaded to silence as he pounded away across the/ngrounds./n/nHarry and Hermione dashed over to Ron./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"What did he do to him?" Hermione whispered. Ron's/neyes were only half-closed, his mouth hung open; he/nwas definitely alive, they could hear him breathing,/nbut he didn't seem to recognize them./n/n"I don't know. ..."/n/nHarry looked desperately around. Black and Lupin/nboth gone . . . they had no one but Snape for company,/nstill hanging, unconscious, in midair./n/n"We'd better get them up to the castle and tell/nsomeone," said Harry, pushing his hair out of his/neyes, trying to think straight. Come — "/n/nBut then, from beyond the range of their vision, they/nheard a yelping, a whining: a dog in pain. .../n/n"Sirius," Harry muttered, staring into the darkness./n/nHe had a moment's indecision, but there was nothing/nthey could do for Ron at the moment, and by the/nsound of it, Black was in trouble —/n/nHarry set off at a run, Hermione right behind him./n/nThe yelping seemed to be coming from the ground/nnear the edge of the lake. They pelted toward it, and/nHarry, running flat out, felt the cold without realizing/nwhat it must mean —/n/nThe yelping stopped abruptly. As they reached the/nlakeshore, they saw why — Sirius had turned back/ninto a man. He was crouched on all fours, his hands/nover his head./n/n"iVooo," he moaned. "Noooo ... please. ..."/n/nAnd then Harry saw them. Dementors, at least a/nhundred of them, gliding in a black mass around the/n/n/n/n/n/nlake toward them. He spun around, the familiar, icy/ncold penetrating his insides, fog starting to obscure/nhis vision; more were appearing out of the darkness/non every side; they were encircling them. .../n/n"Hermione, think of something happy!" Harry yelled,/nraising his wand, blinking furiously to try and clear/nhis vision, shaking his head to rid it of the faint/nscreaming that had started inside it —/n/nI'm going to live with my godfather. I'm leaving the/nDursleys./n/nHe forced himself to think of Black, and only Black,/nand began to chant: "Expecto patronum). Expecto/npatronum)."/n/nBlack gave a shudder, rolled over, and lay motionless/non the ground, pale as death./n/nHell be all right. I'm going to go and live with him./n/n"Expecto patronum). Hermione, help me! Expecto/npatronum)."/n/n"Expecto — " Hermione whispered, "expecto — expecto/n/n/n/nBut she couldn't do it. The dementors were closing in,/nbarely ten feet from them. They formed a solid wall/naround Harry and Hermione, and were getting closer./n/n/n/n"EXPECTO PATRONUM" Harry yelled, trying to blot/nthe screaming from his ears. "EXPECTO PATRONUM."/n/nA thin wisp of silver escaped his wand and hovered/nlike mist before him. At the same moment, Harry felt/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nHermione collapse next to him. He was alone .../ncompletely alone. .../n/n"Expecto — expecto patronum — "/n/nHarry felt his knees hit the cold grass. Fog was/nclouding his eyes. With a huge effort, he fought to/nremember — Sirius was innocent — innocent — We'll/nbe okay — I'm going to live with him —/n/n" Expecto patronum J" he gasped./n/nBy the feeble light of his formless Patronus, he saw a/ndementor halt, very close to him. It couldn't walk/nthrough the cloud of silver mist Harry had conjured./n/nA dead, slimy hand slid out from under the cloak. It/nmade a gesture as though to sweep the Patronus/naside./n/n"No — no — " Harry gasped. "He's innocent ... expecto/n— expecto patronum — "/n/nHe could feel them watching him, hear their rattling/nbreath like an evil wind around him. The nearest/ndementor seemed to be considering him. Then it/nraised both its rotting hands — and lowered its hood./n/nWhere there should have been eyes, there was only/nthin, gray scabbed skin, stretched blankly over empty/nsockets. But there was a mouth ... a gaping,/nshapeless hole, sucking the air with the sound of a/ndeath rattle./n/nA paralyzing terror filled Harry so that he couldn't/nmove or speak. His Patronus flickered and died./n/nWhite fog was blinding him. He had to fight ... expecto/npatronum ... he couldn't see ... and in the distance, he/nheard the familiar screaming . . . expecto patronum . . ./n/n/n/n/n/nhe groped in the mist for Sirius, and found his arm .../nthey weren't going to take him. .../n/nBut a pair of strong, clammy hands suddenly/nattached themselves around Harry's neck. They were/nforcing his face upward. ... He could feel its breath. .../nIt was going to get rid of him first. ... He could feel its/nputrid breath. . . . His mother was screaming in his/nears. ... She was going to be the last thing he ever/nheard —/n/nAnd then, through the fog that was drowning him, he/nthought he saw a silvery light growing brighter and/nbrighter. ... He felt himself fall forward onto the grass./n... Facedown, too weak to move, sick and shaking,/nHarry opened his eyes. The dementor must have/nreleased him. The blinding light was illuminating the/ngrass around him. ... The screaming had stopped, the/ncold was ebbing away. . . ./n/nSomething was driving the dementors back. ... It was/ncircling around him and Black and Hermione. ... They/nwere leaving. ... The air was warm again. .../n/nWith every ounce of strength he could muster, Harry/nraised his head a few inches and saw an animal amid/nthe light, galloping away across the lake. ... Eyes/nblurred with sweat, Harry tried to make out what it/nwas. ... It was as bright as a unicorn. ... Fighting to/nstay conscious, Harry watched it canter to a halt as it/nreached the opposite shore. For a moment, Harry/nsaw, by its brightness, somebody welcoming it back/n. . . raising his hand to pat it . . . someone who looked/nstrangely familiar ... but it couldn't be .../n/nHarry didn't understand. He couldn't think anymore./nHe felt the last of his strength leave him, and his head/nhit the ground as he fainted./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n
