And then there's his/nUmgubular Slashkilter — "/n/n"Don't ask," Harry muttered to Cho as she opened her/nmouth, looking puzzled. She giggled./n/n"Hey, Harry," Hermione called from the other end of/nthe room, "have you checked the time?"/n/nHe looked down at his watch and received a shock —/nit was already ten past nine, which meant they/nneeded to get back to their common rooms/nimmediately or risk being caught and punished by/nFilch for being out-of-bounds. He blew his whistle;/n/n/n/n/neverybody stopped shouting, " Expelliarmusl" and the/nlast couple of wands clattered to the floor./n/n"Well, that was pretty good," said Harry, "but we've/noverrun, we'd better leave it here. Same time, same/nplace next week?"/n/n"Sooner!" said Dean Thomas eagerly and many people/nnodded in agreement./n/nAngelina, however, said quickly, "The Quidditch/nseason's about to start, we need team practices too!"/n/n"Let's say next Wednesday night, then," said Harry,/n"and we can decide on additional meetings then.../nCome on, we'd better get going..."/n/nHe pulled out the Marauder's Map again and checked/nit carefully for signs of teachers on the seventh floor./nHe let them all leave in threes and fours, watching/ntheir tiny dots anxiously to see that they returned/nsafely to their dormitories: the Hufflepuffs to the/nbasement corridor that also led to the kitchens, the/nRavenclaws to a tower on the west side of the castle,/nand the Gryffindors along the corridor to the seventh/nfloor and the Fat Lady's portrait./n/n"That was really, really good, Harry," said Hermione,/nwhen finally it was just her, Harry, and Ron left./n/n"Yeah, it was!" said Ron enthusiastically, as they/nslipped out of the door and watched it melt back into/nstone behind them. "Did you see me disarm/nHermione, Harry?"/n/n"Only once," said Hermione, stung. "I got you loads/nmore than you got me — "/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"I did not only get you once, I got you at least three/ntimes — "/n/n"Well, if you're counting the one where you tripped/nover your own feet and knocked the wand out of my/nhand — "/n/nThey argued all the way back to the common room,/nbut Harry was not listening to them. He had one eye/non the Marauder's Map, but he was also thinking of/nhow Cho had said he made her nervous.../n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n

title: The Lion And The Serpent
text: /nHarry felt as though he were carrying some kind of/ntalisman inside his chest over the following two/nweeks, a glowing secret that supported him through/nUmbridge's classes and even made it possible for him/nto smile blandly as he looked into her horrible bulging/neyes. He and the D.A. were resisting her under her/nvery nose, doing the very thing that she and the/nMinistry most feared, and whenever he was supposed/nto be reading Wilbert Slinkhard's book during her/nlessons he dwelled instead on satisfying memories of/ntheir most recent meetings, remembering how Neville/nhad successfully disarmed Hermione, how Colin/nCreevey had mastered the Impediment Jinx after/nthree meetings' hard effort, how Parvati Patil had/nproduced such a good Reductor Curse that she had/nreduced the table carrying all the Sneakoscopes to/ndust./n/nHe was finding it almost impossible to fix a regular/nnight of the week for D.A. meetings, as they had to/naccommodate three separate Quidditch teams'/npractices, which were often rearranged depending on/n/n/n/n/nthe weather conditions; but Harry was not sorry/nabout this, he had a feeling that it was probably/nbetter to keep the timing of their meetings/nunpredictable. If anyone was watching them, it would/nbe hard to make out a pattern./n/nHermione soon devised a very clever method of/ncommunicating the time and date of the next meeting/nto all the members in case they needed to change it at/nshort notice, because it would look so suspicious if/npeople from different Houses were seen crossing the/nGreat Hall to talk to each other too often. She gave/neach of the members of the D.A. a fake Galleon (Ron/nbecame very excited when he saw the basket at first,/nconvinced that she was actually giving out gold)./n/n"You see the numerals around the edge of the coins?"/nHermione said, holding one up for examination at the/nend of their fourth meeting. The coin gleamed fat and/nyellow in the light from the torches. "On real Galleons/nthat's just a serial number referring to the goblin who/ncast the coin. On these fake coins, though, the/nnumbers will change to reflect the time and date of/nthe next meeting. The coins will grow hot when the/ndate changes, so if you're carrying them in a pocket/nyou'll be able to feel them. We take one each, and/nwhen Harry sets the date of the next meeting he'll/nchange the numbers on his coin, and because I've put/na Protean Charm on them, they'll all change to mimic/nhis."/n/nA blank silence greeted Hermione 's words. She looked/naround at all the faces upturned to her, rather/ndisconcerted./n/n"Well — I thought it was a good idea," she said/nuncertainly, "I mean, even if Umbridge asked us to/nturn out our pockets, there's nothing fishy about/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/ncarrying a Galleon, is there? But ... well, if you don't/nwant to use them ..."/n/n"You can do a Protean Charm?" said Terry Boot./n/n"Yes," said Hermione./n/n"But that's ... that's N.E.W.T. standard, that is," he/nsaid weakly./n/n"Oh," said Hermione, trying to look modest. "Oh .../nwell ... yes, I suppose it is..."/n/n"How come you're not in Ravenclaw?" he demanded,/nstaring at Hermione with something close to wonder./n"With brains like yours?"/n/n"Well, the Sorting Hat did seriously consider putting/nme in Ravenclaw during my Sorting," said Hermione/nbrightly, "but it decided on Gryffindor in the end. So/ndoes that mean we're using the Galleons?"/n/nThere was a murmur of assent and everybody moved/nforward to collect one from the basket. Harry looked/nsideways at Hermione./n/n"You know what these remind me of?"/n/n"No, what's that?"/n/n"The Death Eaters' scars. Voldemort touches one of/nthem, and all their scars burn, and they know they've/ngot to join him."/n/n"Well ... yes," said Hermione quietly. "That is where I/ngot the idea ... but you'll notice I decided to engrave/nthe date on bits of metal rather than on our members'/nskin..."/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"Yeah ... I prefer your way," said Harry, grinning, as/nhe slipped his Galleon into his pocket. "I suppose the/nonly danger with these is that we might accidentally/nspend them."/n/n"Fat chance," said Ron, who was examining his own/nfake Galleon with a slightly mournful air. "I haven't/ngot any real Galleons to confuse it with."/n/nAs the first Quidditch match of the season, Gryffindor/nversus Slytherin, drew nearer, their D.A. meetings/nwere put on hold because Angelina insisted on almost/ndaily practices. The fact that the Quidditch Cup had/nnot been held for so long added considerably to the/ninterest and excitement surrounding the forthcoming/ngame. The Ravenclaws and Hufflepuffs were taking a/nlively interest in the outcome, for they, of course,/nwould be playing both teams over the coming year;/nand the Heads of House of the competing teams,/nthough they attempted to disguise it under a decent/npretense of sportsmanship, were determined to see/ntheir side's victory. Harry realized how much/nProfessor McGonagall cared about beating Slytherin/nwhen she abstained from giving them homework in/nthe week leading up to the match./n/n"I think you've got enough to be getting on with at the/nmoment," she said loftily. Nobody could quite believe/ntheir ears until she looked directly at Harry and Ron/nand said grimly, "I've become accustomed to seeing/nthe Quidditch Cup in my study, boys, and I really/ndon't want to have to hand it over to Professor Snape,/nso use the extra time to practice, won't you?"/n/nSnape was no less obviously partisan: He had booked/nthe Quidditch pitch for Slytherin practice so often/nthat the Gryffindors had difficulty getting on it to/nplay. He was also turning a deaf ear to the many/nreports of Slytherin attempts to hex Gryffindor/n/n/n/n/nplayers in the corridors. When Alicia Spinnet turned/nup in the hospital wing with her eyebrows growing so/nthick and fast that they obscured her vision and/nobstructed her mouth, Snape insisted that she must/nhave attempted a Hair-Thickening Charm on herself/nand refused to listen to the fourteen eyewitnesses who/ninsisted that they had seen the Slytherin Keeper,/n/nMiles Bletchley, hit her from behind with a jinx while/nshe worked in the library./n/nHarry felt optimistic about Gryffindor's chances; they/nhad, after all, never lost to Malfoy's team. Admittedly/nRon was still not performing to Wood's standard, but/nhe was working extremely hard to improve. His/ngreatest weakness was a tendency to lose confidence/nwhen he made a blunder; if he let in one goal he/nbecame flustered and was therefore likely to miss/nmore. On the other hand, Harry had seen Ron make/nsome truly spectacular saves when he was on form:/nDuring one memorable practice, he had hung one-/nhanded from his broom and kicked the Quaffle so/nhard away from the goal hoop that it soared the/nlength of the pitch and through the center hoop at the/nother end. The rest of the team felt this save/ncompared favorably with one made recently by Barry/nRyan, the Irish International Keeper, against Poland's/ntop Chaser, Ladislaw Zamojski. Even Fred had said/nthat Ron might yet make him and George proud, and/nthat they were seriously considering admitting that he/nwas related to them, something he assured Ron they/nhad been trying to deny for four years./n/nThe only thing really worrying Harry was how much/nRon was allowing the tactics of the Slytherin team to/nupset him before they even got onto the pitch. Harry,/nof course, had endured their snide comments for/nmore than four years, so whispers of, "Hey, Potty, I/nheard Warrington's sworn to knock you off your/nbroom on Saturday," far from chilling his blood, made/n/n/n/n/nhim laugh. "Warrington's aim's so pathetic I'd be/nmore worried if he was aiming for the person next to/nme," he retorted, which made Ron and Hermione/nlaugh and wiped the smirk off Pansy Parkinson's face./n/nBut Ron had never endured a relentless campaign of/ninsults, jeers, and intimidation. When Slytherins,/nsome of them seventh years and considerably larger/nthan he was, muttered as they passed in the/ncorridors, "Got your bed booked in the hospital wing,/nWeasley?" he did not laugh, but turned a delicate/nshade of green. When Draco Malfoy imitated Ron/ndropping the Quaffle (which he did whenever they/nwere within sight of each other), Ron's ears glowed/nred and his hands shook so badly that he was likely/nto drop whatever he was holding at the time too./n/nOctober extinguished itself in a rush of howling winds/nand driving rain and November arrived, cold as frozen/niron, with hard frosts every morning and icy drafts/nthat bit at exposed hands and faces. The skies and/nthe ceiling of the Great Hall turned a pale, pearly/ngray, the mountains around Hogwarts became/nsnowcapped, and the temperature in the castle/ndropped so far that many students wore their thick/nprotective dragon skin gloves in the corridors between/nlessons./n/nThe morning of the match dawned bright and cold./nWhen Harry awoke he looked around at Ron's bed/nand saw him sitting bolt upright, his arms around his/nknees, staring fixedly into space./n/n"You all right?" said Harry./n/nRon nodded but did not speak. Harry was reminded/nforcibly of the time that Ron had accidentally put a/nslug- vomiting charm on himself. He looked just as/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/npale and sweaty as he had done then, not to mention/nas reluctant to open his mouth./n/n/n/n"You just need some breakfast," Harry said bracingly./n"C'mon."/n/nThe Great Hall was filling up fast when they arrived,/nthe talk louder and the mood more exuberant than/nusual. As they passed the Slytherin table there was/nan upsurge of noise; Harry looked around and saw/nthat nearly everyone there was wearing, in addition to/nthe usual green-and-silver scarves and hats, silver/nbadges in the shape of what seemed to be crowns. For/nsome reason many of them waved at Ron, laughing/nuproariously. Harry tried to see what was written on/nthe badges as he walked by, but he was too/nconcerned to get Ron past their table quickly to linger/nlong enough to read them./n/nThey received a rousing welcome at the Gryffindor/ntable, where everyone was wearing red and gold, but/nfar from raising Ron's spirits the cheers seemed to/nsap the last of his morale; he collapsed onto the/nnearest bench looking as though he were facing his/nfinal meal./n/n"I must've been mental to do this," he said in a croaky/nwhisper. "Mental."/n/n"Don't be thick," said Harry firmly, passing him a/nchoice of cereals. "You're going to be fine. It's normal/nto be nervous."/n/n"I'm rubbish," croaked Ron. "I'm lousy. I can't play to/nsave my life. What was I thinking?"/n/n"Get a grip," said Harry sternly. "Look at that save/nyou made with your foot the other day, even Fred and/nGeorge said it was brilliant — "/n/n/n/n/n/nRon turned a tortured face to Harry./n/n/n/n"That was an accident," he whispered miserably. "I/ndidn't mean to do it — I slipped off my broom when/nnone of you were looking and I was trying to get back/non and I kicked the Quaffle by accident."/n/n"Well," said Harry, recovering quickly from this/nunpleasant surprise, "a few more accidents like that/nand the game's in the bag, isn't it?"/n/nHermione and Ginny sat down opposite them wearing/nred-and-gold scarves, gloves, and rosettes./n/n"How're you feeling?" Ginny asked Ron, who was now/nstaring into the dregs of milk at the bottom of his/nempty cereal bowl as though seriously considering/nattempting to drown himself in them./n/n"He's just nervous," said Harry./n/n"Well, that's a good sign, I never feel you perform as/nwell in exams if you're not a bit nervous," said/nHermione heartily./n/n"Hello," said a vague and dreamy voice from behind/nthem. Harry looked up: Luna Lovegood had drifted/nover from the Ravenclaw table. Many people were/nstaring at her and a few openly laughing and/npointing; she had managed to procure a hat shaped/nlike a life-size lion's head, which was perched/nprecariously on her head./n/n"I'm supporting Gryffindor," said Luna, pointing/nunnecessarily at her hat. "Look what it does..."/n/nShe reached up and tapped the hat with her wand. It/nopened its mouth wide and gave an extremely realistic/nroar that made everyone in the vicinity jump./n/n/n/n/n/n"It's good, isn't it?" said Luna happily. "I wanted to/nhave it chewing up a serpent to represent Slytherin,/nyou know, but there wasn't time. Anyway ... good/nluck, Ronald!"/n/nShe drifted away. They had not quite recovered from/nthe shock of Luna's hat before Angelina came/nhurrying toward them, accompanied by Katie and/nAlicia, whose eyebrows had mercifully been returned/nto normal by Madam Pomfrey./n/n"When you're ready," she said, "we're going to go/nstraight down to the pitch, check out conditions and/nchange."/n/n"We'll be there in a bit," Harry assured her. "Ron's/njust got to have some breakfast."/n/nIt became clear after ten minutes, however, that Ron/nwas not capable of eating anything more and Harry/nthought it best to get him down to the changing/nrooms. As they rose from the table, Hermione got up/ntoo, and taking Harry's arm, she drew him to one/nside./n/n"Don't let Ron see what's on those Slytherins'/nbadges," she whispered urgently./n/nHarry looked questioningly at her, but she shook her/nhead warningly; Ron had just ambled over to them,/nlooking lost and desperate./n/n"Good luck, Ron," said Hermione, standing on tiptoe/nand kissing him on the cheek. "And you, Harry — "/n/nRon seemed to come to himself slightly as they/nwalked back across the Great Hall. He touched the/nspot on his face where Hermione had kissed him,/nlooking puzzled, as though he was not quite sure/n/n/n/n/n/nwhat had just happened. He seemed too distracted to/nnotice much around him, but Harry cast a curious/nglance at the crown-shaped badges as they passed/nthe Slytherin table, and this time he made out the/nwords etched onto them:/n/nWEASLEY/n/nIS OUR KING/n/nWith an unpleasant feeling that this could mean/nnothing good, he hurried Ron across the entrance/nhall, down the stone steps, and out into the icy air./n/nThe frosty grass crunched under their feet as they/nhurried down the sloping lawns toward the stadium./nThere was no wind at all and the sky was a uniform/npearly white, which meant that visibility would be/ngood without the drawback of direct sunlight in the/neyes. Harry pointed out these encouraging factors to/nRon as they walked, but he was not sure that Ron/nwas listening./n/nAngelina had changed already and was talking to the/nrest of the team when they entered. Harry and Ron/npulled on their robes (Ron attempted to do his up/nback-to-front for several minutes before Alicia took/npity on him and went to help) and then sat down to/nlisten to the pre-match talk while the babble of voices/noutside grew steadily louder as the crowd came/npouring out of the castle toward the pitch./n/n"Okay, Eve only just found out the final lineup for/nSlytherin," said Angelina, consulting a piece of/nparchment. "Last year's Beaters, Derrick and Bole,/nhave left now, but it looks as though Montague's/nreplaced them with the usual gorillas, rather than/nanyone who can fly particularly well. They're two/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nblokes called Crabbe and Goyle, I don't know much/nabout them — "/n/n"We do," said Harry and Ron together./n/n"Well, they don't look bright enough to tell one end of/na broom from another," said Angelina, pocketing her/nparchment, "but then I was always surprised Derrick/nand Bole managed to find their way onto the pitch/nwithout signposts."/n/n"Crabbe and Goyle are in the same mold," Harry/nassured her./n/nThey could hear hundreds of footsteps mounting the/nbanked benches of the spectators' stands now. Some/npeople were singing, though Harry could not make/nout the words. He was starting to feel nervous, but he/nknew his butterflies were as nothing to Ron's, who/nwas clutching his stomach and staring straight ahead/nagain, his jaw set and his complexion pale gray./n/n"It's time," said Angelina in a hushed voice, looking at/nher watch. "C'mon everyone ... good luck."/n/nThe team rose, shouldered their brooms, and/nmarched in single file out of the changing room and/ninto the dazzling sunlight. A roar of sound greeted/nthem in which Harry could still hear singing, though/nit was muffled by the cheers and whistles./n/nThe Slytherin team were standing waiting for them./nThey too were wearing those silver crown-shaped/nbadges. The new captain, Montague, was built along/nthe same lines as Dudley, with massive forearms like/nhairy hams. Behind him lurked Crabbe and Goyle,/nalmost as large, blinking stupidly in the sunlight,/nswinging their new Beaters' bats. Malfoy stood to one/nside, the sunlight gleaming on his white-blond head./n/n/n/n/nHe caught Harry's eye and smirked, tapping the/ncrown-shaped badge on his chest./n/n"Captains shake hands," ordered the umpire, Madam/nHooch, as Angelina and Montague reached each/nother. Harry could tell that Montague was trying to/ncrush Angelina's fingers, though she did not wince./n"Mount your brooms..."/n/nMadam Hooch placed her whistle in her mouth and/nblew./n/nThe balls were released and the fourteen players shot/nupward; out of the corner of his eye Harry saw Ron/nstreak off toward the goal hoops. He zoomed higher,/ndodging a Bludger, and set off on a wide lap of the/npitch, gazing around for a glint of gold; on the other/nside of the stadium, Draco Malfoy was doing exactly/nthe same./n/n"And it's Johnson, Johnson with the Quaffle, what a/nplayer that girl is, I've been saying it for years but she/nstill won't go out with me — "/n/n"JORDAN!" yelled Professor McGonagall./n/n"Just a fun fact, Professor, adds a bit of interest —/nand she's ducked Warrington, she's passed/nMontague, she's — ouch — been hit from behind by a/nBludger from Crabbe... Montague catches the Quaffle,/nMontague heading back up the pitch and — nice/nBludger there from George Weasley, that's a Bludger/nto the head for Montague, he drops the Quaffle,/ncaught by Katie Bell, Katie Bell of Gryffindor reverse/npasses to Alicia Spinnet and Spinnet's away — "/n/nLee Jordan's commentary rang through the stadium/nand Harry listened as hard as he could through the/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nwind whistling in his ears and the din of the crowd,/nall yelling and booing and singing —/n/n" — dodges Warrington, avoids a Bludger — close call,/nAlicia — and the crowd are loving this, just listen to/nthem, what's that they're singing?"/n/nAnd as Lee paused to listen the song rose loud and/nclear from the sea of green and silver in the Slytherin/nsection of the stands:/n/nWeasley cannot save a thing,/n/nHe cannot block a single ring,/n/nThat's why Slytherins all sing:/n/nWeasley is our King./n/nWeasley was born in a bin,/n/nHe always lets the Quaffle in,/n/nWeasley will make sure we win,/n/nWeasley is our King./n/n" — and Alicia passes back to Angelina!" Lee shouted,/nand as Harry swerved, his insides boiling at what he/nhad just heard, he knew Lee was trying to drown out/nthe sound of the singing. "Come on now, Angelina —/nlooks like she's got just the Keeper to beat! — SHE/nSHOOTS — SHE — aaaah ..."/n/nBletchley, the Slytherin Keeper, had saved the goal;/nhe threw the Quaffle to Warrington who sped off with/nit, zigzagging in between Alicia and Katie; the singing/nfrom below grew louder and louder as he drew nearer/nand nearer Ron —/n/nWeasley is our King,/n/nWeasley is our King,/n/nHe always lets the Quaffle in,/n/nWeasley is our King./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nHarry could not help himself: Abandoning his search/nfor the Snitch, he turned his Firebolt toward Ron, a/nlone figure at the far end of the pitch, hovering before/nthe three goal hoops while the massive Warrington/npelted toward him .../n/n" — and it's Warrington with the Quaffle, Warrington/nheading for goal, he's out of Bludger range with just/nthe Keeper ahead — "/n/nA great swell of song rose from the Slytherin stands/nbelow:/n/nWeasley cannot save a thing,/n/nHe cannot block a single ring . . ./n/n" — so it's the first test for new Gryffindor Keeper,/nWeasley, brother of Beaters, Fred and George, and a/npromising new talent on the team — come on, Ron!"/n/nBut the scream of delight came from the Slytherin/nend: Ron had dived wildly, his arms wide, and the/nQuaffle had soared between them, straight through/nRon's central hoop./n/n"Slytherin score!" came Lee's voice amid the cheering/nand booing from the crowds below. "So that's ten-nil/nto Slytherin — bad luck, Ron ..."/n/nThe Slytherins sang even louder:/n/nWEASLEY WAS BORN IN A BIN,/n/nHE ALWAYS LETS THE QUAFFLE IN .../n/n" — and Gryffindor back in possession and it's Katie/nBell tanking up the pitch — " cried Lee valiantly,/nthough the singing was now so deafening that he/ncould hardly make himself heard above it./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nWEASLEY WILL MAKE SURE WE WIN,/n/nWEASLEY IS OUR KING . . ./n/n"Harry, WHAT ARE YOU DOING?" screamed Angelina,/nsoaring past him to keep up with Katie. "GET/nGOING!"/n/nHarry realized that he had been stationary in midair/nfor more than a minute, watching the progress of the/nmatch without sparing a thought for the whereabouts/nof the Snitch; horrified, he went into a dive and/nstarted circling the pitch again, staring around, trying/nto ignore the chorus now thundering through the/nstadium:/n/nWEASLEY IS OUR KING,/n/nWEASLEY IS OUR KING . . ./n/nThere was no sign of the Snitch anywhere he looked;/nMalfoy was still circling the stadium just like Harry./nThey passed midway around the pitch going in/nopposite directions and Harry heard Malfoy singing/nloudly,/n/nWEASLEY WAS BORN IN A BIN . . ./n/n" — and it's Warrington again," bellowed Lee, "who/npasses to Pucey, Pucey's off past Spinnet, come on/nnow Angelina, you can take him — turns out you/ncan't — but nice Bludger from Fred Weasley, I mean,/nGeorge Weasley, oh who cares, one of them anyway,/nand Warrington drops the Quaffle and Katie Bell — er/n— drops it too — so that's Montague with the Quaffle,/nSlytherin Captain Montague takes the Quaffle, and/nhe's off up the pitch, come on now Gryffindor, block/nhim!"/n/nHarry zoomed around the end of the stadium behind/nthe Slytherin goal hoops, willing himself not to look at/n/n/n/n/n/nwhat was going on at Ron's end; as he sped past the/nSlytherin Keeper, he heard Bletchley singing along/nwith the crowd below,/n/nWEASLEY CANNOT SAVE A THING . . ./n/n" — and Pucey's dodged Alicia again, and he's heading/nstraight for goal, stop it, Ron!"/n/nHarry did not have to look to see what had happened:/nThere was a terrible groan from the Gryffindor end,/ncoupled with fresh screams and applause from the/nSlytherins. Looking down, Harry saw the pug-faced/nPansy Parkinson right at the front of the stands, her/nback to the pitch as she conducted the Slytherin/nsupporters who were roaring:/n/nTHAT'S WHY SLYTHERINS ALL SING:/n/nWEASLEY IS OUR KING./n/nBut twenty-nil was nothing, there was still time for/nGryffindor to catch up or catch the Snitch, a few goals/nand they would be in the lead as usual, Harry/nassured himself, bobbing and weaving through the/nother players in pursuit of something shiny that/nturned out to be Montague's watch strap.../n/nBut Ron let in two more goals. There was an edge of/npanic in Harry's desire to find the Snitch now. If he/ncould just get it soon and finish the game quickly .../n/n" — and Katie Bell of Gryffindor dodges Pucey, ducks/nMontague, nice swerve, Katie, and she throws to/nJohnson, Angelina Johnson takes the Quaffle, she's/npast Warrington, she's heading for goal, come on now/nAngelina — GRYFFINDOR SCORE! It's forty-ten, forty-/nten to Slytherin and Pucey has the Quaffle..."/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nHarry could hear Luna's ludicrous lion hat roaring/namidst the Gryffindor cheers and felt heartened; only/nthirty points in it, that was nothing, they could pull/nback easily. Harry ducked a Bludger that Crabbe had/nsent rocketing in his direction and resumed his/nfrantic scouring of the pitch for the Snitch, keeping/none eye on Malfoy in case he showed signs of having/nspotted it, but Malfoy, like him, was continuing to/nsoar around the stadium, searching fruitlessly . . ./n/n" — Pucey throws to Warrington, Warrington to/nMontague, Montague back to Pucey — Johnson/nintervenes, Johnson takes the Quaffle, Johnson to/nBell, this looks good — I mean bad — Bell's hit by a/nBludger from Goyle of Slytherin and it's Pucey in/npossession again ..."/n/nWEASLEY WAS BORN IN A BIN,/n/nHE ALWAYS LETS THE QUAFFLE IN,/n/nWEASLEY WILL MAKE SURE WE WIN —/n/nBut Harry had seen it at last: The tiny fluttering/nGolden Snitch was hovering feet from the ground at/nthe Slytherin end of the pitch./n/nHe dived.../n/nIn a matter of seconds, Malfoy was streaking out of/nthe sky on Harry's left, a green-and-silver blur lying/nflat on his broom.../n/nThe Snitch skirted the foot of one of the goal hoops/nand scooted off toward the other side of the stands;/nits change of direction suited Malfoy, who was nearer./nHarry pulled his Firebolt around, he and Malfoy were/nnow neck and neck . . ./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nFeet from the ground, Harry lifted his right hand from/nhis broom, stretching toward the Snitch ... to his/nright, Malfoy's arm extended too, reaching, groping .../n/nIt was over in two breathless, desperate, windswept/nseconds — Harry's fingers closed around the tiny,/nstruggling ball — Malfoy's fingernails scrabbled the/nback of Harry's hand hopelessly — Harry pulled his/nbroom upward, holding the struggling ball in his/nhand and the Gryffindor spectators screamed their/napproval.../n/nThey were saved, it did not matter that Ron had let in/nthose goals, nobody would remember as long as/nGryffindor had won —/n/nWHAM/n/nA Bludger hit Harry squarely in the small of the back/nand he flew forward off his broom; luckily he was only/nfive or six feet above the ground, having dived so low/nto catch the Snitch, but he was winded all the same/nas he landed flat on his back on the frozen pitch. He/nheard Madam Hooch's shrill whistle, an uproar in the/nstands compounded of catcalls, angry yells and/njeering, a thud, then Angelina's frantic voice./n/n"Are you all right?"/n/n" 'Course I am," said Harry grimly, taking her hand/nand allowing her to pull him to his feet. Madam/nHooch was zooming toward one of the Slytherin/nplayers above him, though he could not see who it/nwas at this angle./n/n"It was that thug, Crabbe," said Angelina angrily. "He/nwhacked the Bludger at you the moment he saw you'd/ngot the Snitch — but we won, Harry, we won!"/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nHarry heard a snort from behind him and turned/naround, still holding the Snitch tightly in his hand:/nDraco Malfoy had landed close by; white-faced with/nfury, he was still managing to sneer./n/n"Saved Weasley's neck, haven't you?" he said to/nHarry. "I've never seen a worse Keeper ... but then he/nwas born in a bin... Did you like my lyrics, Potter?"/n/nHarry did not answer; he turned away to meet the/nrest of the team who were now landing one by one,/nyelling and punching the air in triumph, all except/nRon, who had dismounted from his broom over by the/ngoalposts and was making his way slowly back to the/nchanging rooms alone./n/n"We wanted to write another couple of verses!" Malfoy/ncalled, as Katie and Alicia hugged Harry. "But we/ncouldn't find rhymes for fat and ugly — we wanted to/nsing about his mother, see — "/n/n"Talk about sour grapes," said Angelina, casting/nMalfoy a disgusted look./n/n" — we couldn't fit in useless loser either — for his/nfather, you know — "/n/nFred and George had realized what Malfoy was talking/nabout. Halfway through shaking Harry's hand they/nstiffened, looking around at Malfoy./n/n"Leave it," said Angelina at once, taking Fred by the/narm. "Leave it, Fred, let him yell, he's just sore he/nlost, the jumped-up little — "/n/n" — but you like the Weasleys, don't you, Potter?" said/nMalfoy, sneering. "Spend holidays there and/neverything, don't you? Can't see how you stand the/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nstink, but I suppose when you've been dragged up by/nMuggles even the Weasleys' hovel smells okay — "/n/nHarry grabbed hold of George; meanwhile it was/ntaking the combined efforts of Angelina, Alicia, and/nKatie to stop Fred leaping on Malfoy, who was/nlaughing openly. Harry looked around for Madam/nHooch, but she was still berating Crabbe for his illegal/nBludger attack./n/n"Or perhaps," said Malfoy, leering as he backed away,/n"you can remember what your mother's house stank/nlike, Potter, and Weasley's pigsty reminds you of it — "/n/nHarry was not aware of releasing George, all he knew/nwas that a second later both of them were sprinting at/nMalfoy. He had completely forgotten the fact that all/nthe teachers were watching: All he wanted to do was/ncause Malfoy as much pain as possible. With no time/nto draw out his wand, he merely drew back the fist/nclutching the Snitch and sank it as hard as he could/ninto Malfoy's stomach —/n/n"Harry! HARRY! GEORGE! 1VO!"/n/nHe could hear girls' voices screaming, Malfoy yelling,/nGeorge swearing, a whistle blowing, and the bellowing/nof the crowd around him, but he did not care, not/nuntil somebody in the vicinity yelled " IMPEDIMENTA !"/nand only when he was knocked over backward by the/nforce of the spell did he abandon the attempt to/npunch every inch of Malfoy he could reach.../n/n"What do you think you're doing?" screamed Madam/nHooch, as Harry leapt to his feet again; it was she/nwho had hit him with the Impediment Jinx. She was/nholding her whistle in one hand and a wand in the/nother, her broom lay abandoned several feet away./nMalfoy was curled up on the ground, whimpering and/n/n/n/n/nmoaning, his nose bloody; George was sporting a/nswollen lip; Fred was still being forcibly restrained by/nthe three Chasers, and Crabbe was cackling in the/nbackground. "I've never seen behavior like it — back/nup to the castle, both of you, and straight to your/nHead of House's office! Go! Now\"/n/nHarry and George marched off the pitch, both/npanting, neither saying a word to each other. The/nhowling and jeering of the crowd grew fainter and/nfainter until they reached the entrance hall, where/nthey could hear nothing except the sound of their own/nfootsteps. Harry became aware that something was/nstill struggling in his right hand, the knuckles of/nwhich he had bruised against Malfoy's jaw; looking/ndown he saw the Snitch's silver wings protruding/nfrom between his fingers, struggling for release./n/nThey had barely reached the door of Professor/nMcGonagall's office when she came marching along/nthe corridor behind them. She was wearing a/nGryffindor scarf, but tore it from her throat with/nshaking hands as she strode toward them, looking/nlivid./n/n"In!" she said furiously, pointing to the door. Harry/nand George entered. She strode around behind her/ndesk and faced them, quivering with rage as she/nthrew the Gryffindor scarf aside onto the floor./n/n"Well?" she said. "I have never seen such a disgraceful/nexhibition. Two onto one! Explain yourselves!"/n/n"Malfoy provoked us," said Harry stiffly./n/n"Provoked you?" shouted Professor McGonagall,/nslamming a fist onto her desk so that her tartan/nbiscuit tin slid sideways off it and burst open, littering/nthe floor with Ginger Newts. "He'd just lost, hadn't he,/n/n/n/n/n/nof course he wanted to provoke you! But what on/nearth he can have said that justified what you two — "/n/n"He insulted my parents," snarled George. "And/nHarry's mother."/n/n"But instead of leaving it to Madam Hooch to sort out,/nyou two decided to give an exhibition of Muggle/ndueling, did you?" bellowed Professor McGonagall./n"Have you any idea what you've — ?"/n/n"Hem, hem."/n/nGeorge and Harry both spun around. Dolores/nUmbridge was standing in the doorway wrapped in a/ngreen tweed cloak that greatly enhanced her/nresemblance to a giant toad, and smiling in the/nhorribly sickly, ominous way that Harry had come to/nassociate with imminent misery./n/n"May I help, Professor McGonagall?" asked Professor/nUmbridge in her most poisonously sweet voice./n/nBlood rushed into Professor McGonagall's face./n/n"Help?" she repeated in a constricted voice. "What do/nyou mean, 'help'?"/n/nProfessor Umbridge moved forward into the office, still/nsmiling her sickly smile./n/n"Why, I thought you might be grateful for a little extra/nauthority."/n/nHarry would not have been surprised to see sparks fly/nfrom Professor McGonagall's nostrils./n/n"You thought wrong," she said, turning her back on/nUmbridge. "Now, you two had better listen closely. I/n/n/n/n/n/ndo not care what provocation Malfoy offered you, I do/nnot care if he insulted every family member you/npossess, your behavior was disgusting and I am/ngiving each of you a week's worth of detention! Do not/nlook at me like that, Potter, you deserve it! And if/neither of you ever — "/n/n"Hem, hem."/n/nProfessor McGonagall closed her eyes as though/npraying for patience as she turned her face toward/nProfessor Umbridge again./n/n" Yes?"/n/n"I think they deserve rather more than detentions,"/nsaid Umbridge, smiling still more broadly./n/nProfessor McGonagall's eyes flew open. "But/nunfortunately," she said, with an attempt at a/nreciprocal smile that made her look as though she/nhad lockjaw, "it is what I think that counts, as they/nare in my House, Dolores."/n/n"Well, actually, Minerva," simpered Umbridge, "I think/nyou'll find that what I think does count. Now, where/nis it? Cornelius just sent it... I mean," she gave a little/nfalse laugh as she rummaged in her handbag, "the/nMinister just sent it... Ah yes ..."/n/nShe had pulled out a piece of parchment that she now/nunfurled, clearing her throat fussily before starting to/nread what it said./n/n"Hem, hem ... 'Educational Decree Number Twenty-/nfive ...'"/n/n"Not another one!" exclaimed Professor McGonagall/nviolently./n/n/n/n/n/n"Well, yes," said Umbridge, still smiling. "As a matter/nof fact, Minerva, it was you who made me see that we/nneeded a further amendment... You remember how/nyou overrode me, when I was unwilling to allow the/nGryffindor Quidditch team to re-form? How you took/nthe case to Dumbledore, who insisted that the team/nbe allowed to play? Well, now, I couldn't have that. I/ncontacted the Minister at once, and he quite agreed/nwith me that the High Inquisitor has to have the/npower to strip pupils of privileges, or she — that is to/nsay, I — would have less authority than common/nteachers! And you see now, don't you, Minerva, how/nright I was in attempting to stop the Gryffindor team/nre-forming? Dreadful tempers . . . Anyway, I was/nreading out our amendment ... hem, hem ... The High/nInquisitor will henceforth have supreme authority/nover all punishments, sanctions, and removal of/nprivileges pertaining to the students of Hogwarts, and/nthe power to alter such punishments, sanctions, and/nremovals of privileges as may have been ordered by/nother staff members. Signed, Cornelius Fudge,/nMinister of Magic, Order of Merlin First Class, etc.,/netc...'"/n/nShe rolled up the parchment and put it back into her/nhandbag, still smiling./n/n"So ... I really think I will have to ban these two from/nplaying Quidditch ever again," she said, looking from/nHarry to George and back again./n/nHarry felt the Snitch fluttering madly in his hand./n/n"Ban us?" he said, and his voice sounded strangely/ndistant. "From playing ... ever again?"/n/n"Yes, Mr. Potter, I think a lifelong ban ought to do the/ntrick," said Umbridge, her smile widening still further/nas she watched him struggle to comprehend what she/n/n/n/n/n/nhad said. "You and Mr. Weasley here. And I think, to/nbe safe, this young man's twin ought to be stopped/ntoo — if his teammates had not restrained him, I feel/nsure he would have attacked young Mr. Malfoy as/nwell. I will want their broomsticks confiscated, of/ncourse; I shall keep them safely in my office, to make/nsure there is no infringement of my ban. But I am not/nunreasonable, Professor McGonagall," she continued,/nturning back to Professor McGonagall who was now/nstanding as still as though carved from ice, staring at/nher. "The rest of the team can continue playing, I saw/nno signs of violence from any of them. Well ... good/nafternoon to you." And with a look of the utmost/nsatisfaction Umbridge left the room, leaving a/nhorrified silence in her wake./n/n"Banned," said Angelina in a hollow voice, late that/nevening in the common room. " Banned . No Seeker/nand no Beaters . . . What on earth are we going to do?"/n/nIt did not feel as though they had won the match at/nall. Everywhere Harry looked there were disconsolate/nand angry faces; the team themselves were slumped/naround the fire, all apart from Ron, who had not been/nseen since the end of the match./n/n"It's just so unfair," said Alicia numbly. "I mean, what/nabout Crabbe and that Bludger he hit after the/nwhistle had been blown? Has she banned him?"/n/n"No," said Ginny miserably; she and Hermione were/nsitting on either side of Harry. "He just got lines, I/nheard Montague laughing about it at dinner."/n/n"And banning Fred when he didn't even do anything!"/nsaid Alicia furiously, pummeling her knee with her/nfist./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"It's not my fault I didn't," said Fred, with a very ugly/nlook on his face. "I would've pounded the little/nscumbag to a pulp if you three hadn't been holding/nme back."/n/nHarry stared miserably at the dark window. Snow was/nfalling. The Snitch he had caught earlier was now/nzooming around and around the common room;/npeople were watching its progress as though/nhypnotized and Crookshanks was leaping from chair/nto chair, trying to catch it./n/n"I'm going to bed," said Angelina, getting slowly to her/nfeet./n/n"Maybe this will all turn out to have been a bad/ndream... Maybe I'll wake up tomorrow and find we/nhaven't played yet..."/n/nShe was soon followed by Alicia and Katie. Fred and/nGeorge sloped off to bed some time later, glowering at/neveryone they passed, and Ginny went not long after/nthat. Only Harry and Hermione were left beside the/nfire./n/n"Have you seen Ron?" Hermione asked in a low voice./nHarry shook his head./n/n"I think he's avoiding us," said Hermione. "Where do/nyou think he — ?"/n/nBut at that precise moment, there was a creaking/nsound behind them as the Fat Lady swung forward/nand Ron came clambering through the portrait hole./nHe was very pale indeed and there was snow in his/nhair. When he saw Harry and Hermione he stopped/ndead in his tracks./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"Where have you been?" said Hermione anxiously,/nspringing up./n/n/n/n"Walking," Ron mumbled. He was still wearing his/nQuidditch things./n/n"You look frozen," said Hermione. "Come and sit/ndown!"/n/nRon walked to the fireside and sank into the chair/nfarthest from Harry's, not looking at him. The stolen/nSnitch zoomed over their heads./n/n"I'm sorry," Ron mumbled, looking at his feet./n/n"What for?" said Harry./n/n"For thinking I can play Quidditch," said Ron. "I'm/ngoing to resign first thing tomorrow."/n/n"If you resign," said Harry testily, "there'll only be/nthree players left on the team." And when Ron looked/npuzzled, he said, "I've been given a lifetime ban. So've/nFred and George."/n/n"What?" Ron yelped./n/nHermione told him the full story; Harry could not bear/nto tell it again. When she had finished, Ron looked/nmore anguished than ever./n/n"This is all my fault — "/n/n"You didn't make me punch Malfoy," said Harry/nangrily./n/n" — if I wasn't so lousy at Quidditch — "/n/n" — it's got nothing to do with that — "/n/n/n/n/n/n" — it was that song that wound me up — "/n/n" — it would've wound anyone up — "/n/nHermione got up and walked to the window, away/nfrom the argument, watching the snow swirling down/nagainst the pane./n/n"Look, drop it, will you!" Harry burst out. "It's bad/nenough without you blaming yourself for everything!"/n/nRon said nothing but sat gazing miserably at the/ndamp hem of his robes. After a while he said in a dull/nvoice, "This is the worst I've ever felt in my life."/n/n"Join the club," said Harry bitterly./n/n"Well," said Hermione, her voice trembling slightly. "I/ncan think of one thing that might cheer you both up."/n/n"Oh yeah?" said Harry skeptically./n/n"Yeah," said Hermione, turning away from the pitch-/nblack, snow-flecked window, a broad smile spreading/nacross her face. "Hagrid's back."/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n

title: Hagrid's Tale
text: /nHarry sprinted up to the boys' dormitory to fetch the/nInvisibility Cloak and the Marauder's Map from his/ntrunk; he was so quick that he and Ron were ready to/nleave at least five minutes before Hermione hurried/nback down from the girls' dormitories, wearing scarf,/ngloves, and one of her own knobbly elf hats./n/n"Well, it's cold out there!" she said defensively, as Ron/nclicked his tongue impatiently./n/nThey crept through the portrait hole and covered/nthemselves hastily in the cloak — Ron had grown so/nmuch he now needed to crouch to prevent his feet/nshowing — then, moving slowly and cautiously, they/nproceeded down the many staircases, pausing at/nintervals to check the map for signs of Filch or Mrs./nNorris. They were lucky; they saw nobody but Nearly/nHeadless Nick, who was gliding along absentmindedly/nhumming something that sounded horribly like/n"Weasley Is Our King." They crept across the entrance/nhall and then out into the silent, snowy grounds./n/nWith a great leap of his heart, Harry saw little golden/nsquares of light ahead and smoke coiling up from/n/n/n/n/nHagrid's chimney. He set off at a quick march, the/nother two jostling and bumping along behind him,/nand they crunched excitedly through the thickening/nsnow until at last they reached the wooden front door;/nwhen Harry raised his fist and knocked three times, a/ndog started barking frantically inside./n/n"Hagrid, it's us!" Harry called through the keyhole./n/n"Shoulda known!" said a gruff voice./n/nThey beamed at one another under the cloak; they/ncould tell that Hagrid's voice was pleased. "Bin home/nthree seconds ... Out the way, Fang ... Out the way,/nyeh dozy dog ..."/n/nThe bolt was drawn back, the door creaked open, and/nHagrid's head appeared in the gap./n/nHermione screamed./n/n"Merlin's beard, keep it down!" said Hagrid hastily,/nstaring wildly over their heads. "Under that cloak, are/nyeh? Well, get in, get in!"/n/n"I'm sorry!" Hermione gasped, as the three of them/nsqueezed past Hagrid into the house and pulled the/ncloak off themselves so he could see them. "I just —/noh, Hagrid)."/n/n"It's nuthin', it's nuthin'!" said Hagrid hastily,/nshutting the door behind them and hurrying to close/nall the curtains, but Hermione continued to gaze up/nat him in horror./n/nHagrid's hair was matted with congealed blood, and/nhis left eye had been reduced to a puffy slit amid a/nmass of purple-and-black bruises. There were many/ncuts on his face and hands, some of them still/n/n/n/n/n/nbleeding, and he was moving gingerly, which made/nHarry suspect broken ribs. It was obvious that he had/nonly just got home; a thick black traveling cloak lay/nover the back of a chair and a haversack large enough/nto carry several small children leaned against the wall/ninside the door. Hagrid himself, twice the size of a/nnormal man and three times as broad, was now/nlimping over to the fire and placing a copper kettle/nover it./n/n"What happened to you?" Harry demanded, while/nFang danced around them all, trying to lick their/nfaces./n/n"Told yeh, nuthin said Hagrid firmly. "Want a/ncuppa?"/n/n"Come off it," said Ron, "you're in a right state!"/n/n"I'm tellin'yeh, I'm fine," said Hagrid, straightening/nup and turning to beam at them all, but wincing./n"Blimey, it's good ter see you three again — had good/nsummers, did yeh?"/n/n"Hagrid, you've been attacked!" said Ron./n/n"Fer the las' time, it's nuthin'!" said Hagrid firmly./n/n"Would you say it was nothing if one of us turned up/nwith a pound of mince instead of a face?" Ron/ndemanded./n/n"You ought to go and see Madam Pomfrey, Hagrid,"/nsaid Hermione anxiously. "Some of those cuts look/nnasty."/n/n"I'm dealin' with it, all righ'?" said Hagrid repressively./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nHe walked across to the enormous wooden table that/nstood in the middle of his cabin and twitched aside a/ntea towel that had been lying on it. Underneath was a/nraw, bloody, green-tinged steak slightly larger than/nthe average car tire./n/n"You're not going to eat that, are you, Hagrid?" said/nRon, leaning in for a closer look. "It looks poisonous."/n/n"It's s 'posed ter look like that, it's dragon meat,"/nHagrid said. "An' I didn' get it ter eat."/n/nHe picked up the steak and slapped it over the left/nside of his face. Greenish blood trickled down into his/nbeard as he gave a soft moan of satisfaction./n/n"Tha's better. It helps with the stingin', yeh know."/n/n"So are you going to tell us what's happened to you?"/nHarry asked./n/n"Can', Harry. Top secret. More'n me job's worth ter/ntell yeh that."/n/n"Did the giants beat you up, Hagrid?" asked Hermione/nquietly./n/nHagrid's fingers slipped on the dragon steak, and it/nslid squelchily onto his chest./n/n"Giants?" said Hagrid, catching the steak before it/nreached his belt and slapping it back over his face./n"Who said anythin' abou' giants? Who yeh bin talkin'/nto? Who's told yeh what I've — who's said I've bin —/neh?"/n/n"We guessed," said Hermione apologetically./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"Oh, yeh did, did yeh?" said Hagrid, fixing her sternly/nwith the eye that was not hidden by the steak./n/n"It was kind of ... obvious," said Ron. Harry nodded./n/nHagrid glared at them, then snorted, threw the steak/nonto the table again and strode back to the kettle,/nwhich was now whistling./n/n"Never known kids like you three fer knowin' more'n/nyeh oughta," he muttered, splashing boiling water/ninto three of his bucket-shaped mugs. "An' I'm not/ncomplimentin' yeh, neither. Nosy, some'd call it./nInterferin'."/n/nBut his beard twitched./n/n"So you have been to look for giants?" said Harry,/ngrinning as he sat down at the table./n/nHagrid set tea in front of each of them, sat down,/npicked up his steak again, and slapped it back over/nhis face./n/n"Yeah, all righ'," he grunted, "I have."/n/n"And you found them?" said Hermione in a hushed/nvoice./n/n"Well, they're not that difficult ter find, ter be honest,"/nsaid Hagrid. "Pretty big, see."/n/n"Where are they?" said Ron./n/n"Mountains," said Hagrid unhelpfully./n/n"So why don't Muggles — ?"/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"They do," said Hagrid darkly. "O'ny their deaths are/nalways put down ter mountaineerin' accidents, aren'/nthey?"/n/nHe adjusted the steak a little so that it covered the/nworst of the bruising./n/n"Come on, Hagrid, tell us what you've been up to!"/nsaid Ron. "Tell us about being attacked by the giants/nand Harry can tell you about being attacked by the/ndementors — "/n/nHagrid choked in his mug and dropped his steak at/nthe same time; a large quantity of spit, tea, and/ndragon blood was sprayed over the table as Hagrid/ncoughed and spluttered and the steak slid, with a soft/nsplat, onto the floor./n/n"Whadda yeh mean, attacked by dementors?" growled/nHagrid./n/n"Didn't you know?" Hermione asked him, wide-eyed./n/n"I don' know anything that's been happenin' since I/nleft. I was on a secret mission, wasn' I, didn' wan'/nowls followin' me all over the place — ruddy/ndementors! Yeh're not serious?"/n/n"Yeah, I am, they turned up in Little Whinging and/nattacked my cousin and me, and then the Ministry of/nMagic expelled me — "/n/n"WHAT?"/n/n" — and I had to go to a hearing and everything, but/ntell us about the giants first."/n/n"You were expelled?"/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"Tell us about your summer and I'll tell you about/nmine."/n/nHagrid glared at him through his one open eye. Harry/nlooked right back, an expression of innocent/ndetermination on his face./n/n"Oh, all righ'," Hagrid said in a resigned voice./n/nHe bent down and tugged the dragon steak out of/nFang's mouth./n/n"Oh, Hagrid, don't, it's not hygien — " Hermione/nbegan, but Hagrid had already slapped the meat back/nover his swollen eye. He took another fortifying gulp of/ntea and then said, "Well, we set off righ' after term/nended — "/n/n"Madame Maxime went with you, then?" Hermione/ninterjected./n/n"Yeah, tha's right," said Hagrid, and a softened/nexpression appeared on the few inches of face that/nwere not obscured by beard or green steak. "Yeah, it/nwas jus' the pair of us. An' I'll tell yeh this, she's not/nafraid of roughin' it, Olympe. Yeh know, she's a fine,/nwell-dressed woman, an' knowin' where we was goin' I/nwondered 'ow she'd feel abou' clamberin' over/nboulders an' sleepin' in caves an' tha', bu' she never/ncomplained once."/n/n"You knew where you were going?" Harry asked. "You/nknew where the giants were?"/n/n"Well, Dumbledore knew, an' he told us," said Hagrid./n/n"Are they hidden?" asked Ron.
