"We've tried the Leaky/nCauldron in Diagon Alley and the Three Broomsticks/nand even the Hog's Head — "/n/n"Idiot girl, Dumbledore won't be sitting in a pub when/nthe whole Ministry's looking for him!" shouted/nUmbridge, disappointment etched in every sagging/nline of her face./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"But — but we needed to tell him something/nimportant!" wailed Hermione, holding her hands more/ntightly over her face, not, Harry knew, out of anguish,/nbut to disguise the continued absence of tears./n/n"Yes?" said Umbridge with a sudden resurgence of/nexcitement. "What was it you wanted to tell him?"/n/n"We ... we wanted to tell him it's r-ready!" choked/nHermione./n/n"What's ready?" demanded Umbridge, and now she/ngrabbed Hermione 's shoulders again and shook her/nslightly. "What's ready, girl?"/n/n"The ... the weapon," said Hermione./n/n"Weapon? Weapon?" said Umbridge, and her eyes/nseemed to pop with excitement. "You have been/ndeveloping some method of resistance? A weapon you/ncould use against the Ministry? On Professor/nDumbledore's orders, of course?"/n/n"Y-y-yes," gasped Hermione. "But he had to leave/nbefore it was finished and n-n-now we've finished it/nfor him, and we c-c-can't find him t-t-to tell him!"/n/n"What kind of weapon is it?" said Umbridge harshly,/nher stubby hands still tight on Hermione 's shoulders./n/n"We don't r-r-really understand it," said Hermione,/nsniffing loudly. "We j-j-just did what P-P-Professor/nDumbledore told us t-t-to do ..."/n/nUmbridge straightened up, looking exultant./n/n"Lead me to the weapon," she said./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n'Tm not showing ... them," said Hermione shrilly,/nlooking around at the Slytherins through her fingers./n/n"It is not for you to set conditions," said Professor/nUmbridge harshly./n/n"Fine," said Hermione, now sobbing into her hands/nagain, "fine ... let them see it, I hope they use it on/nyou! In fact, I wish you'd invite loads and loads of/npeople to come and see! Th-that would serve you right/n— oh, I'd love it if the wh-whole school knew where it/nwas, and how to u-use it, and then if you annoy any/nof them they'll be able to s-sort you out!"/n/nThese words had a powerful impact on Umbridge. She/nglanced swiftly and suspiciously around at her/nInquisitorial Squad, her bulging eyes resting for a/nmoment on Malfoy, who was too slow to disguise the/nlook of eagerness and greed that had appeared on his/nface./n/nUmbridge contemplated Hermione for another long/nmoment and then spoke in what she clearly thought/nwas a motherly voice. "All right, dear, let's make it/njust you and me ... and we'll take Potter too, shall we?/nGet up, now — "/n/n"Professor," said Malfoy eagerly, "Professor Umbridge,/n/nI think some of the squad should come with you to/nlook after — "/n/n"I am a fully qualified Ministry official, Malfoy, do you/nreally think I cannot manage two wandless teenagers/nalone?" asked Umbridge sharply. "In any case, it does/nnot sound as though this weapon is something that/nschoolchildren should see. You will remain here until/nI return and make sure none of these" — she gestured/naround at Ron, Ginny, Neville, and Luna — "escape."/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"All right," said Malfoy, looking sulky and/ndisappointed./n/n"And you two can go ahead of me and show me the/nway," said Umbridge, pointing at Harry and Hermione/nwith her wand. "Lead on..."/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n

title: Fight And Flight
text: /nHarry had no idea what Hermione was planning, or/neven whether she had a plan. He walked half a pace/nbehind her as they headed down the corridor outside/nUmb ridge's office, knowing it would look very/nsuspicious if he appeared not to know where they/nwere going. He did not dare attempt to talk to her;/nUmbridge was walking so closely behind them that he/ncould hear her ragged breathing./n/nHermione led the way down the stairs into the/nentrance hall. The din of loud voices and the clatter of/ncutlery on plates echoed from out of the double doors/nto the Great Hall. It seemed incredible to Harry that/ntwenty feet away were people who were enjoying/ndinner, celebrating the end of exams, not a care in the/nworld.../n/nHermione walked straight out of the oak front doors/nand down the stone steps into the balmy evening air./nThe sun was falling toward the tops of the trees in the/nForbidden Forest now as Hermione marched/npurposefully across the grass, Umbridge jogging to/n/n/n/nkeep up. Their long dark shadows rippled over the/ngrass behind them like cloaks./n/n/n/n"It's hidden in Hagrid's hut, is it?" said Umbridge/neagerly in Harry's ear./n/n"Of course not," said Hermione scathingly. "Hagrid/nmight have set it off accidentally."/n/n"Yes," said Umbridge, whose excitement seemed to be/nmounting. "Yes, he would have done, of course, the/ngreat half-breed oaf..."/n/nShe laughed. Harry felt a strong urge to swing around/nand seize her by the throat, but resisted. His scar was/nthrobbing in the soft evening air but it had not yet/nburned white-hot, as he knew it would if Voldemort/nhad moved in for the kill.../n/n"Then ... where is it?" asked Umbridge, with a hint of/nuncertainty in her voice as Hermione continued to/nstride toward the forest./n/n"In there, of course," said Hermione, pointing into the/ndark trees. "It had to be somewhere that students/nweren't going to find it accidentally, didn't it?"/n/n"Of course," said Umbridge, though she sounded a/nlittle apprehensive now. "Of course ... very well, then/n... you two stay ahead of me."/n/n"Can we have your wand, then, if we're going first?"/nHarry asked her./n/n"No, I don't think so, Mr. Potter," said Umbridge/nsweetly, poking him in the back with it. "The Ministry/nplaces a rather higher value on my life than yours, I'm/nafraid."/n/n/n/n/n/nAs they reached the cool shade of the first trees,/n/nHarry tried to catch Hermione 's eye; walking into the/nforest without wands seemed to him to be more/nfoolhardy than anything they had done so far this/nevening. She, however, merely gave Umbridge a/ncontemptuous glance and plunged straight into the/ntrees, moving at such a pace that Umbridge, with her/nshorter legs, had difficulty in keeping up./n/n"Is it very far in?" Umbridge asked, as her robe ripped/non a bramble./n/n"Oh yes," said Hermione. "Yes, it's well hidden."/n/nHarry's misgivings increased. Hermione was not/ntaking the path they had followed to visit Grawp, but/nthe one he had followed three years ago to the lair of/nthe monster Aragog. Hermione had not been with him/non that occasion; he doubted she had any idea what/ndanger lay at the end of it./n/n"Er — are you sure this is the right way?" he asked/nher pointedly./n/n"Oh yes," she said in a steely voice, crashing through/nthe undergrowth with what he thought was a wholly/nunnecessary amount of noise. Behind them,/n/nUmbridge tripped over a fallen sapling. Neither of/nthem paused to help her up again; Hermione merely/nstrode on, calling loudly over her shoulder, "It's a bit/nfurther in!"/n/n"Hermione, keep your voice down," Harry muttered,/nhurrying to catch up with her. "Anything could be/nlistening in here — "/n/n"I want us heard," she answered quietly, as Umbridge/njogged noisily after them. "You'll see..."/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nThey walked on for what seemed a long time, until/nthey were once again so deep into the forest that the/ndense tree canopy blocked out all light. Harry had the/nfeeling he had had before in the forest, one of being/nwatched by unseen eyes.../n/n"How much further?" demanded Umbridge angrily/nfrom behind him./n/n"Not far now!" shouted Hermione, as they emerged/ninto a dim, dank clearing. "Just a little bit — "/n/nAn arrow flew through the air and landed with a/nmenacing thud in the tree just over her head. The air/nwas suddenly full of the sound of hooves. Harry could/nfeel the forest floor trembling; Umbridge gave a little/nscream and pushed him in front of her like a shield —/n/nHe wrenched himself free of her and turned. Around/nfifty centaurs were emerging on every side, their bows/nraised and loaded, pointing at Harry, Hermione, and/nUmbridge, who backed slowly into the center of the/nclearing, Umbridge uttering odd little whimpers of/nterror. Harry looked sideways at Hermione. She was/nwearing a triumphant smile./n/n"Who are you?" said a voice./n/nHarry looked left. The chestnut-bodied centaur called/nMagorian was walking toward them out of the circle;/nhis bow, like the others', was raised. On Harry's right,/nUmbridge was still whimpering, her wand trembling/nviolently as she pointed it at the advancing centaur./n/n"I asked you who are you, human," said Magorian/nroughly./n/n"I am Dolores Umbridge!" said Umbridge in a high-/npitched, terrified voice. "Senior Undersecretary to the/n/n/n/n/n/nMinister of Magic and Headmistress and High/nInquisitor of Hogwarts!"/n/n/n/n"You are from the Ministry of Magic?" said Magorian,/nas many of the centaurs in the surrounding circle/nshifted restlessly./n/n"That's right!" said Umbridge in an even higher voice./n"So be very careful! By the laws laid down by the/nDepartment for the Regulation and Control of Magical/nCreatures, any attack by half-breeds such as/nyourselves on a human — "/n/n" What did you call us?" shouted a wild-looking black/ncentaur, whom Harry recognized as Bane. There was/na great deal of angry muttering and tightening of/nbowstrings around them./n/n"Don't call them that!" Hermione said furiously, but/nUmbridge did not appear to have heard her. Still/npointing her shaking wand at Magorian, she/ncontinued, "Law Fifteen B states clearly that 'Any/nattack by a magical creature who is deemed to have/nnear-human intelligence, and therefore considered/nresponsible for its actions — ' "/n/n" 'Near-human intelligence'?" repeated Magorian, as/nBane and several others roared with rage and pawed/nthe ground. "We consider that a great insult, human!/nOur intelligence, thankfully, far outstrips your own —/n/n/n/n"What are you doing in our forest?" bellowed the/nhard-faced gray centaur whom Harry and Hermione/nhad seen on their last trip into the forest. "Why are/nyou here?"/n/n"Your forest?" said Umbridge, shaking now not only/nwith fright but also, it seemed, with indignation. "I/n/n/n/n/n/nwould remind you that you live here only because the/nMinistry of Magic permits you certain areas of land —/n/n/n/nAn arrow flew so close to her head that it caught at/nher mousy hair in passing. She let out an earsplitting/nscream and threw her hands over her head while/nsome of the centaurs bellowed their approval and/nothers laughed raucously. The sound of their wild,/nneighing laughter echoing around the dimly lit/nclearing and the sight of their pawing hooves was/nextremely unnerving./n/n"Whose forest is it now, human?" bellowed Bane./n/n"Filthy half-breeds!" she screamed, her hands still/ntight over her head. "Beasts! Uncontrolled animals!"/n/n"Be quiet!" shouted Hermione, but it was too late —/nUmbridge pointed her wand at Magorian and/nscreamed, " Incarcerousl"/n/nRopes flew out of midair like thick snakes, wrapping/nthemselves tightly around the centaur's torso and/ntrapping his arms. He gave a cry of rage and reared/nonto his hind legs, attempting to free himself, while/nthe other centaurs charged./n/nHarry grabbed Hermione and pulled her to the/nground. Facedown on the forest floor he knew a/nmoment of terror as hooves thundered around him,/nbut the centaurs leapt over and around them,/nbellowing and screaming with rage./n/n"Nooooo!" he heard Umbridge shriek. "Noooooo ... I/nam Senior Undersecretary ... you cannot ... unhand/nme, you animals ... nooooo!"/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nHe saw a flash of red light and knew that she had/nattempted to Stun one of them — then she screamed/nvery loudly. Lifting his head a few inches, Harry saw/nthat Umbridge had been seized from behind by Bane/nand lifted high into the air, wriggling and yelling with/nfright. Her wand fell from her hand to the ground and/nHarry's heart leapt, if he could just reach it —/n/nBut as he stretched out a hand toward it, a centaur's/nhoof descended upon the wand and it broke cleanly in/nhalf./n/n"Now!" roared a voice in Harry's ear and a thick hairy/narm descended from thin air and dragged him/nupright; Hermione too had been pulled to her feet./nOver the plunging, many-colored backs and heads of/nthe centaurs Harry saw Umbridge being borne away/nthrough the trees by Bane, still screaming nonstop;/nher voice grew fainter and fainter until they could no/nlonger hear it over the trampling of hooves/nsurrounding them./n/n"And these?" said the hard-faced, gray centaur/nholding Hermione./n/n"They are young," said a slow, doleful voice from/nbehind Harry. "We do not attack foals."/n/n"They brought her here, Ronan," replied the centaur/nwho had such a firm grip on Harry. "And they are not/nso young... He is nearing manhood, this one..."/n/nHe shook Harry by the neck of his robes./n/n"Please," said Hermione breathlessly, "please, don't/nattack us, we don't think like her, we aren't Ministry/nof Magic employees! We only came in here because we/nhoped you'd drive her off for us — "/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nHarry knew at once from the look on the face of the/ngray centaur holding Hermione that she had made a/nterrible mistake in saying this. The gray centaur/nthrew back his head, his back legs stamping/nfuriously, and bellowed, "You see, Ronan? They/nalready have the arrogance of their kind! So we were/nto do your dirty work, were we, human girl? We were/nto act as your servants, drive away your enemies like/nobedient hounds?"/n/n"No!" said Hermione in a horrorstruck squeak. "Please/n— I didn't mean that! I just hoped you'd be able to —/nto help us — "/n/nBut she seemed to be going from bad to worse./n/n"We do not help humans!" snarled the centaur/nholding Harry, tightening his grip and rearing a little/nat the same time, so that Harry's feet left the ground/nmomentarily. "We are a race apart and proud to be/nso... We will not permit you to walk from here,/nboasting that we did your bidding!"/n/n"We're not going to say anything like that!" Harry/nshouted. "We know you didn't do anything because/nwe wanted you to — "/n/nBut nobody seemed to be listening to him. A bearded/ncentaur toward the back of the crowd shouted, "They/ncame here unasked, they must pay the/nconsequences!"/n/nA roar of approval met these words and a dun-colored/ncentaur shouted, "They can join the woman!"/n/n"You said you didn't hurt the innocent!" shouted/nHermione, real tears sliding down her face now. "We/nhaven't done anything to hurt you, we haven't used/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nwands or threats, we just want to go back to school,/nplease let us go back — "/n/n"We are not all like the traitor Firenze, human girl!"/nshouted the gray centaur, to more neighing roars of/napproval from his fellows. "Perhaps you thought us/npretty talking horses? We are an ancient people who/nwill not stand wizard invasions and insults! We do not/nrecognize your laws, we do not acknowledge your/nsuperiority, we are — "/n/nBut they did not hear what else centaurs were, for at/nthat moment there came a crashing noise on the edge/nof the clearing so loud that all of them — Harry,/nHermione, and the fifty or so centaurs filling the/nclearing — looked around. Harry's centaur let him fall/nto the ground again as his hands flew to his bow and/nquiver of arrows; Hermione had been dropped too,/nand Harry hurried toward her as two thick tree/ntrunks parted ominously and the monstrous form of/nGrawp the giant appeared in the gap./n/nThe centaurs nearest him backed into those behind./nThe clearing was now a forest of bows and arrows/nwaiting to be fired, all pointing upward at the/nenormous grayish face now looming over them from/njust beneath the thick canopy of branches. Grawp 's/nlopsided mouth was gaping stupidly. They could see/nhis bricklike yellow teeth glimmering in the half-light,/nhis dull sludge-colored eyes narrowed as he squinted/ndown at the creatures at his feet. Broken ropes trailed/nfrom both ankles./n/nHe opened his mouth even wider./n/n"Hagger."/n/nHarry did not know what "hagger" meant, or what/nlanguage it was from, nor did he much care — he was/n/n/n/n/n/nwatching Grawp 's feet, which were almost as long as/nHarry's whole body. Hermione gripped his arm tightly;/nthe centaurs were quite silent, staring up at the giant,/nwhose huge, round head moved from side to side as/nhe continued to peer amongst them as though looking/nfor something he had dropped./n/n"Haggeii" he said again, more insistently./n/n"Get away from here, giant!" called Magorian. "You/nare not welcome among us!"/n/nThese words seemed to make no impression/nwhatsoever on Grawp. He stooped a little (the/ncentaurs' arms tensed on their bows) and then/nbellowed, "HAGGER!"/n/nA few of the centaurs looked worried now. Hermione,/nhowever, gave a gasp./n/n"Harry!" she whispered. "I think he's trying to say/n'Hagrid'!"/n/n/n/nAt this precise moment Grawp caught sight of them,/nthe only two humans in a sea of centaurs. He lowered/nhis head another foot or so, staring intently at them./nHarry could feel Hermione shaking as Grawp opened/nhis mouth wide again and said, in a deep, rumbling/nvoice, "Hermy."/n/n"Goodness," said Hermione, gripping Harry's arm so/ntightly it was growing numb and looking as though/nshe was about to faint, "he — he remembered!"/n/n"HERMY!" roared Grawp. "WHERE HAGGER?"/n/n"I don't know!" squealed Hermione, terrified. "I'm/nsorry, Grawp, I don't know!"/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"GRAWP WANT HAGGER!"/n/n/n/nOne of the giant's massive hands swooped down upon/nthem — Hermione let out a real scream, ran a few/nsteps backward and fell over. Wandless, Harry braced/nhimself to punch, kick, bite, or whatever else it took/nas the hand flew toward him and knocked a snow-/nwhite centaur off his legs./n/nIt was what the centaurs had been waiting for —/nGrawp's outstretched fingers were a foot from Harry/nwhen fifty arrows went soaring through the air at the/ngiant, peppering his enormous face, causing him to/nhowl with pain and rage and straighten up again,/nrubbing his face with his enormous hands, breaking/noff the arrow shafts but forcing the heads in still/ndeeper./n/nHe yelled and stamped his enormous feet and the/ncentaurs scattered out of the way. Pebble-sized/ndroplets of Grawp's blood showered Harry as he/npulled Hermione to her feet and the pair of them ran/nas fast as they could for the shelter of the trees. Once/nthere they looked back — Grawp was snatching/nblindly at the centaurs as blood ran all down his face;/nthey were retreating in disorder, galloping away/nthrough the trees on the other side of the clearing. As/nHarry and Hermione watched, Grawp gave another/nroar of fury and plunged after them, smashing more/ntrees aside as he went./n/n"Oh no," said Hermione, quaking so badly that her/nknees gave way. "Oh, that was horrible. And he might/nkill them all..."/n/n"I'm not that fussed, to be honest," said Harry/nbitterly./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nThe sounds of the galloping centaurs and the/nblundering giant were growing fainter and fainter. As/nHarry listened to them his scar gave another great/nthrob and a wave of terror swept over him./n/nThey had wasted so much time — they were even/nfurther from rescuing Sirius than they had been when/nhe had had the vision. Not only had Harry managed/nto lose his wand but they were stuck in the middle of/nthe Forbidden Forest with no means of transport/nwhatsoever./n/n"Smart plan," he spat at Hermione, keen to release/nsome of his fury. "Really smart plan. Where do we go/nfrom here?"/n/n"We need to get back up to the castle," said Hermione/nfaintly./n/n"By the time we've done that, Sirius 11 probably be/ndead!" said Harry, kicking a nearby tree in temper;/nthere was a high-pitched chattering overhead and he/nlooked up to see an angry bowtruckle flexing its long/ntwiglike fingers at him./n/n"Well, we can't do anything without wands," said/nHermione hopelessly, dragging herself up again./n"Anyway, Harry, how exactly were you planning to get/nall the way to London?"/n/n"Yeah, we were just wondering that," said a familiar/nvoice from behind her./n/nHarry and Hermione moved instinctively together,/npeering through the trees, as Ron came into sight,/nwith Ginny, Neville, and Luna hurrying along behind/nhim. All of them looked a little the worse for wear —/nthere were several long scratches running the length/nof Ginny's cheek, a large purple lump was swelling/n/n/n/n/nabove Neville's right eye, Ron's lip was bleeding worse/nthan ever — but all were looking rather pleased with/nthemselves./n/n"So," said Ron, pushing aside a low-hanging branch/nand holding out Harry's wand, "had any ideas?"/n/n"How did you get away?" asked Harry in amazement,/ntaking his wand from Ron./n/n"Couple of Stunners, a Disarming Charm, Neville/nbrought off a really nice little Impediment Jinx," said/nRon airily, now handing back Hermione's wand too./n"But Ginny was best, she got Malfoy — Bat-Bogey Hex/n— it was superb, his whole face was covered in the/ngreat flapping things. Anyway, we saw you heading/ninto the forest out of the window and followed./n/nWhat've you done with Umbridge?"/n/n"She got carried away," said Harry. "By a herd of/ncentaurs."/n/n"And they left you behind?" asked Ginny, looking/nastonished./n/n"No, they got chased off by Grawp," said Harry./n/n"Who's Grawp?" Luna asked interestedly./n/n"Hagrid's little brother," said Ron promptly. "Anyway,/nnever mind that now. Harry, what did you find out in/nthe fire? Has You-Know-Who got Sirius or — ?"/n/n"Yes," said Harry, as his scar gave another painful/nprickle, "and I'm sure Sirius is still alive, but I can't/nsee how we're going to get there to help him."/n/nThey all fell silent, looking rather scared. The problem/nfacing them seemed insurmountable./n/n/n/n/n/n"Well, we'll have to fly, won't we?" said Luna in the/nclosest thing to a matter-of-fact voice Harry had ever/nheard her use./n/n/n/n"Okay," said Harry irritably, rounding on her, "first of/nall, "we' aren't doing anything if you're including/nyourself in that, and second of all, Ron's the only one/nwith a broomstick that isn't being guarded by a/nsecurity troll, so — "/n/n"I've got a broom!" said Ginny./n/n"Yeah, but you're not coming," said Ron angrily./n/n"Excuse me, but I care what happens to Sirius as/nmuch as you do!" said Ginny, her jaw set so that her/nresemblance to Fred and George was suddenly/nstriking./n/n"You're too — " Harry began./n/n"I'm three years older than you were when you fought/nYou-Know-Who over the Sorcerer's Stone," she said/nfiercely, "and it's because of me Malfoy's stuck back/nin Umbridge's office with giant flying bogeys attacking/nhim — "/n/n/n/n"Yeah, but — "/n/n"We were all in the D.A. together," said Neville quietly./n"It was all supposed to be about fighting You-Know-/nWho, wasn't it? And this is the first chance we've had/nto do something real — or was that all just a game or/nsomething?"/n/n"No — of course it wasn't — " said Harry impatiently./n/n"Then we should come too," said Neville simply. "We/nwant to help."/n/n/n/n/n/n"That's right," said Luna, smiling happily./n/n/n/nHarry's eyes met Ron's. He knew that Ron was/nthinking exactly what he was: If he could have chosen/nany members of the D.A. in addition to himself, Ron,/nand Hermione to join him in the attempt to rescue/nSirius, he would not have picked Ginny, Neville, or/nLuna./n/n"Well, it doesn't matter anyway," said Harry/nfrustratedly, "because we still don't know how to get/nthere — "/n/n"I thought we'd settled that?" said Luna maddeningly./n"We're flying!"/n/n"Look," said Ron, barely containing his anger, "you/nmight be able to fly without a broomstick but the rest/nof us can't sprout wings whenever we — "/n/n"There are other ways of flying than with/nbroomsticks," said Luna serenely./n/n"I s'pose we're going to ride on the back of the Kacky/nSnorgle or whatever it is?" Ron demanded./n/n"The Crumple-Horned Snorkack can't fly," said Luna/nin a dignified voice, "but they can, and Hagrid says/nthey're very good at finding places their riders are/nlooking for."/n/nHarry whirled around. Standing between two trees,/ntheir white eyes gleaming eerily, were two thestrals,/nwatching the whispered conversation as though they/nunderstood every word./n/n"Yes!" he whispered, moving toward them. They/ntossed their reptilian heads, throwing back long black/nmanes, and Harry stretched out his hand eagerly and/n/n/n/n/n/npatted the nearest one's shining neck. How could he/never have thought them ugly?/n/n"Is it those mad horse things?" said Ron uncertainly,/nstaring at a point slightly to the left of the thestral/nHarry was patting. "Those ones you can't see unless/nyou've watched someone snuff it?"/n/n"Yeah," said Harry./n/n"How many?"/n/n"Just two."/n/n"Well, we need three," said Hermione, who was still/nlooking a little shaken, but determined just the same./n/n"Four, Hermione," said Ginny, scowling./n/n"I think there are six of us, actually," said Luna/ncalmly, counting./n/n"Don't be stupid, we can't all go!" said Harry angrily./n"Look, you three" — he pointed at Neville, Ginny, and/nLuna — "you're not involved in this, you're not — "/n/nThey burst into more protests. His scar gave another,/nmore painful, twinge. Every moment they delayed was/nprecious; he did not have time to argue./n/n"Okay, fine, it's your choice," he said curtly. "But/nunless we can find more thestrals you're not going to/nbe able — "/n/n"Oh, more of them will come," said Ginny confidently,/nwho like Ron was squinting in quite the wrong/ndirection, apparently under the impression that she/nwas looking at the horses./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"What makes you think that?"/n/n"Because in case you hadn't noticed, you and/nHermione are both covered in blood," she said coolly,/n"and we know Hagrid lures thestrals with raw meat,/nso that's probably why these two turned up in the/nfirst place..."/n/nHarry felt a soft tug on his robes at that moment and/nlooked down to see the closest thestral licking his/nsleeve, which was damp with Grawp's blood./n/n"Okay, then," he said, a bright idea occurring. "Ron/nand I will take these two and go ahead, and Hermione/ncan stay here with you three and she'll attract more/nthestrals — "/n/n"I'm not staying behind!" said Hermione furiously./n/n"There's no need," said Luna, smiling. "Look, here/ncome more now... You two must really smell..."/n/nHarry turned. No fewer than six or seven thestrals/nwere picking their way through the trees now, their/ngreat leathery wings folded tight to their bodies, their/neyes gleaming through the darkness. He had no/nexcuse now.../n/n"All right," he said angrily, "pick one and get on,/nthen."/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n

title: The Department Of Mysteries
text: /nHarry wound his hand tightly into the mane of the/nnearest thestral, placed a foot on a stump nearby,/nand scrambled clumsily onto the horse's silken back./nIt did not object, but twisted its head around, fangs/nbared, and attempted to continue its eager licking of/nhis robes./n/nHe found there was a way of lodging his knees behind/nthe wing joints that made him feel more secure and/nlooked around at the others. Neville had heaved/nhimself over the back of the next thestral and was/nnow attempting to swing one short leg over the/ncreature's back. Luna was already in place, sitting/nsidesaddle and adjusting her robes as though she did/nthis every day. Ron, Hermione, and Ginny, however,/nwere still standing motionless on the spot,/nopenmouthed and staring./n/n"What?" he said./n/n"How're we supposed to get on?" said Ron faintly./n"When we can't see the things?"/n/n/n/n/n"Oh it's easy," said Luna, sliding obligingly from her/nthestral and marching over to him, Hermione, and/nGinny. "Come here..."/n/nShe pulled them over to the other thestrals standing/naround and one by one managed to help them onto/nthe backs of their mounts. All three looked extremely/nnervous as she wound their hands into the horses'/nmanes and told them to grip tightly before getting/nback onto her own steed./n/n"This is mad," Ron said faintly, moving his free hand/ngingerly up and down his horse's neck. "Mad ... if I/ncould just see it — "/n/n"You'd better hope it stays invisible," said Harry/ndarkly. "We all ready, then?"/n/nThey all nodded and he saw five pairs of knees tighten/nbeneath their robes./n/n"Okay ..."/n/nHe looked down at the back of his thestral's glossy/nblack head and swallowed. "Ministry of Magic,/nvisitors' entrance, London, then," he said uncertainly./n"Er ... if you know ... where to go ..."/n/nFor a moment his thestral did nothing at all. Then,/nwith a sweeping movement that nearly unseated him,/nthe wings on either side extended, the horse crouched/nslowly and then rocketed upward so fast and so/nsteeply that Harry had to clench his arms and legs/ntightly around the horse to avoid sliding backward/nover its bony rump. He closed his eyes and put his/nface down into the horse's silky mane as they burst/nthrough the topmost branches of the trees and soared/nout into a bloodred sunset./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nHarry did not think he had ever moved so fast: The/nthestral streaked over the castle, its wide wings/nhardly beating. The cooling air was slapping Harry's/nface; eyes screwed up against the rushing wind, he/nlooked around and saw his five fellows soaring along/nbehind him, each of them bent as low as possible into/nthe neck of their thestral to protect themselves from/nits slipstream./n/nThey were over the Hogwarts grounds, they had/npassed Hogsmeade. Harry could see mountains and/ngullies below them. In the falling darkness Harry saw/nsmall collections of lights as they passed over more/nvillages, then a winding road on which a single car/nwas beetling its way home through the hills.../n/n"This is bizarre!" Harry heard Ron yell from/nsomewhere behind him, and he imagined how it must/nfeel to be speeding along at this height with no visible/nmeans of support.../n/nTwilight fell: The sky turned to a light, dusky purple/nlittered with tiny silver stars, and soon it was only the/nlights of Muggle towns that gave them any clue of how/nfar from the ground they were or how very fast they/nwere traveling. Harry's arms were wrapped tightly/naround his horse's neck as he willed it to go even/nfaster. How much time had elapsed since he had seen/nSirius lying on the Department of Mysteries floor?/n/nHow much longer would he be able to resist/nVoldemort? All Harry knew for sure was that Sirius/nhad neither done as Voldemort wanted, nor died, for/nhe was convinced that either outcome would cause/nhim to feel Voldemort's jubilation or fury course/nthrough his own body, making his scar sear as/npainfully as it had on the night Mr. Weasley was/nattacked.../n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nOn they flew through the gathering darkness; Harry's/nface felt stiff and cold, his legs numb from gripping/nthe thestral's sides so tightly, but he did not dare/nshift positions lest he slip... He was deaf from the/nthundering in his ears and his mouth was dry and/nfrozen from the rush of cold night air. He had lost all/nsense of how far they had come; all his faith was in/nthe beast below him, still streaking purposefully/nthrough the night, barely flapping its wings as it sped/never onward.../n/nIf they were too late . . ./n/nHe's still alive, he's still fighting, I can feel it.../n/nIf Voldemort decided Sirius was not going to crack .../nI'd know.../n/nHarry's stomach gave a jolt. The thestral's head was/nsuddenly pointing toward the ground and he had/nactually slid forward a few inches along its neck. They/nwere descending at last... He heard one of the girls/nshriek behind him and twisted around dangerously/nbut could see no sign of a falling body. . . Presumably/nthey had received a shock from the change of/nposition, just as he had.../n/nAnd now bright orange lights were growing larger and/nrounder on all sides. They could see the tops of/nbuildings, streams of headlights like luminous insect/neyes, squares of pale yellow that were windows. Quite/nsuddenly, it seemed, they were hurtling toward the/npavement. Harry gripped the thestral with every last/nounce of his strength, braced for a sudden impact,/nbut the horse touched the dark ground as lightly as a/nshadow and Harry slid from his back, looking around/nat the street where the overflowing dumpster still/nstood a short way from the vandalized telephone box,/n/n/n/n/nboth drained of color in the flat orange glare of the/nstreetlights./n/nRon landed a short way away and toppled/nimmediately off his thestral onto the pavement./n/n"Never again," he said, struggling to his feet. He made/nas though to stride away from his thestral, but,/nunable to see it, collided with its hindquarters and/nalmost fell over again. "Never, ever again ... that was/nthe worst — "/n/nHermione and Ginny touched down on either side of/nhim. Both slid off their mounts a little more gracefully/nthan Ron, though with similar expressions of relief at/nbeing back on firm ground. Neville jumped down,/nshaking, but Luna dismounted smoothly./n/n"Where do we go from here, then?" she asked Harry in/na politely interested voice, as though this was all a/nrather interesting day- trip./n/n"Over here," he said. He gave his thestral a quick,/ngrateful pat, then led the way quickly to the battered/ntelephone box and opened the door. "Come on\" he/nurged the others as they hesitated./n/nRon and Ginny marched in obediently; Hermione,/nNeville, and Luna squashed themselves in after them;/nHarry took one glance back at the thestrals, now/nforaging for scraps of rotten food inside the dumpster,/nthen forced himself into the box after Luna./n/n"Whoever's nearest the receiver, dial six two four four/ntwo!" he said./n/nRon did it, his arm bent bizarrely to reach the dial. As/nit whirred back into place the cool female voice/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nsounded inside the box, "Welcome to the Ministry of/nMagic. Please state your name and business."/n/n"Harry Potter, Ron Weasley, Hermione Granger,"/n/nHarry said very quickly, "Ginny Weasley, Neville/nLongbottom, Luna Lovegood ... We're here to save/nsomeone, unless your Ministry can do it first!"/n/n"Thank you," said the cool female voice. "Visitors,/nplease take the badges and attach them to the front of/nyour robes."/n/nHalf a dozen badges slid out of the metal chute where/nreturned coins usually appeared. Hermione scooped/nthem up and handed them mutely to Harry over/nGinny 's head; he glanced at the topmost one./n/nHARRY POTTER/nRESCUE MISSION/n/n"Visitor to the Ministry, you are required to submit to/na search and present your wand for registration at the/nsecurity desk, which is located at the far end of the/nAtrium."/n/n"Fine!" Harry said loudly, as his scar gave another/nthrob. "Now can we move?"/n/nThe floor of the telephone box shuddered and the/npavement rose up past the glass windows of the/ntelephone box. The scavenging thestrals were sliding/nout of sight, blackness closed over their heads, and/nwith a dull grinding noise they sank down into the/ndepths of the Ministry of Magic./n/nA chink of soft golden light hit their feet and,/nwidening, rose up their bodies. Harry bent his knees/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nand held his wand as ready as he could in such/ncramped conditions, peering through the glass to see/nwhether anybody was waiting for them in the Atrium,/nbut it seemed to be completely empty. The light was/ndimmer than it had been by day. There were no fires/nburning under the mantelpieces set into the walls,/nbut he saw as the lift slid smoothly to a halt that/ngolden symbols continued to twist sinuously in the/ndark blue ceiling./n/n"The Ministry of Magic wishes you a pleasant/nevening," said the woman's voice./n/nThe door of the telephone box burst open; Harry/ntoppled out of it, followed by Neville and Luna. The/nonly sound in the Atrium was the steady rush of/nwater from the golden fountain, where jets from the/nwands of the witch and wizard, the point of the/ncentaur's arrow, the tip of the goblin's hat, and the/nhouse-elf's ears continued to gush into the/nsurrounding pool./n/n"Come on," said Harry quietly and the six of them/nsprinted off down the hall, Harry in the lead, past the/nfountain, toward the desk where the security man/nwho had weighed Harry's wand had sat and which/nwas now deserted./n/nHarry felt sure that there ought to be a security/nperson there, sure that their absence was an ominous/nsign, and his feeling of foreboding increased as they/npassed through the golden gates to the lifts. He/npressed the nearest down button and a lift clattered/ninto sight almost immediately, the golden grilles slid/napart with a great, echoing clanking, and they dashed/ninside. Harry stabbed the number nine button, the/ngrilles closed with a bang, and the lift began to/ndescend, jangling and rattling. Harry had not realized/nhow noisy the lifts were on the day that he had come/n/n/n/n/nwith Mr. Weasley — he was sure that the din would/nraise every security person within the building, yet/nwhen the lift halted, the cool female voice said,/n"Department of Mysteries," and the grilles slid open/nagain, they stepped out into the corridor where/nnothing was moving but the nearest torches,/nflickering in the rush of air from the lift./n/nHarry turned toward the plain black door. After/nmonths and months of dreaming about it, he was/nhere at last.../n/n"Let's go," he whispered, and he led the way down the/ncorridor, Luna right behind him, gazing around with/nher mouth slightly open./n/n"Okay, listen," said Harry, stopping again within six/nfeet of the door. "Maybe . . . maybe a couple of people/nshould stay here as a — as a lookout, and — "/n/n"And how're we going to let you know something's/ncoming?" asked Ginny, her eyebrows raised. "You/ncould be miles away."/n/n"We're coming with you, Harry," said Neville./n/n"Let's get on with it," said Ron firmly./n/nHarry still did not want to take them all with him, but/nit seemed he had no choice. He turned to face the/ndoor and walked forward. Just as it had in his dream,/nit swung open and he marched forward, leading the/nothers over the threshold./n/nThey were standing in a large, circular room./nEverything in here was black including the floor and/nceiling — identical, unmarked, handle-less black/ndoors were set at intervals all around the black walls,/ninterspersed with branches of candles whose flames/n/n/n/n/nburned blue, their cool, shimmering light reflected in/nthe shining marble floor so that it looked as though/nthere was dark water underfoot./n/n"Someone shut the door," Harry muttered./n/nHe regretted giving this order the moment Neville had/nobeyed it. Without the long chink of light from the/ntorch-lit corridor behind them, the place became so/ndark that for a moment the only things they could see/nwere the bunches of shivering blue flames on the/nwalls and their ghostly reflections in the floor below./n/nIn his dream, Harry had always walked purposefully/nacross this room to the door immediately opposite the/nentrance and walked on. But there were around a/ndozen doors here. Just as he was gazing ahead at the/ndoors opposite him, trying to decide which was the/nright one, there was a great rumbling noise and the/ncandles began to move sideways. The circular wall/nwas rotating./n/nHermione grabbed Harry's arm as though frightened/nthe floor might move too, but it did not. For a few/nseconds the blue flames around them were blurred to/nresemble neon lines as the wall sped around and/nthen, quite as suddenly as it had started, the/nrumbling stopped and everything became stationary/nonce again./n/nHarry's eyes had blue streaks burned into them; it/nwas all he could see./n/n"What was that about?" whispered Ron fearfully./n/n"I think it was to stop us knowing which door we/ncame in from," said Ginny in a hushed voice./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nHarry realized at once that she was right: He could no/nsooner have picked the exit from the other doors than/nlocated an ant upon the jet-black floor. Meanwhile,/nthe door through which they needed to proceed could/nbe any of the dozen surrounding them./n/n"How're we going to get back out?" said Neville/nuncomfortably./n/n"Well, that doesn't matter now," said Harry forcefully,/nblinking to try and erase the blue lines from his/nvision, and clutching his wand tighter than ever. "We/nwon't need to get out till we've found Sirius — "/n/n"Don't go calling for him, though!" Hermione said/nurgently, but Harry had never needed her advice less;/nhis instinct was to keep as quiet as possible for the/ntime being./n/n"Where do we go, then, Harry?" Ron asked./n/n"I don't — " Harry began. He swallowed. "In the/ndreams I went through the door at the end of the/ncorridor from the lifts into a dark room — that's this/none — and then I went through another door into a/nroom that kind of ... glitters. We should try a few/ndoors," he said hastily. "I'll know the right way when I/nsee it. C'mon."/n/nHe marched straight at the door now facing him, the/nothers following close behind him, set his left hand/nagainst its cool, shining surface, raised his wand,/nready to strike the moment it opened, and pushed. It/nswung open easily./n/nAfter the darkness of the first room, the lamps/nhanging low on golden chains from this ceiling gave/nthe impression that this long rectangular room was/nmuch brighter, though there were no glittering,/n/n/n/n/n/nshimmering lights such as Harry had seen in his/ndreams. The place was quite empty except for a few/ndesks and, in the very middle of the room, an/nenormous glass tank of deep-green water, big enough/nfor all of them to swim in, which contained a number/nof pearly white objects that were drifting around lazily/nin the liquid./n/n"What're those things?" whispered Ron./n/n"Dunno," said Harry./n/n"Are they fish?" breathed Ginny./n/n"Aquavirius maggots!" said Luna excitedly. "Dad said/nthe Ministry were breeding — "/n/n"No," said Hermione. She sounded odd. She moved/nforward to look through the side of the tank. "They're/nbrains."/n/n"Brains?"/n/n"Yes ... I wonder what they're doing with them?"/n/nHarry joined her at the tank. Sure enough, there/ncould be no mistake now that he saw them at close/nquarters. Glimmering eerily they drifted in and out of/nsight in the depths of the green water, looking/nsomething like slimy cauliflowers./n/n"Let's get out of here," said Harry. "This isn't right, we/nneed to try another door — "/n/n"There are doors here too," said Ron, pointing around/nthe walls. Harry's heart sank; how big was this place?/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"In my dream I went through that dark room into the/nsecond one," he said. "I think we should go back and/ntry from there."/n/nSo they hurried back into the dark, circular room; the/nghostly shapes of the brains were now swimming/nbefore Harry's eyes instead of the blue candle flames./n/n"Wait!" said Hermione sharply, as Luna made to close/nthe door of the brain room behind them. " FlagrateV'/n/nShe drew with her wand in midair and a fiery X/nappeared on the door. No sooner had the door clicked/nshut behind them than there was a great rumbling,/nand once again the wall began to revolve very fast, but/nnow there was a great red-gold blur in amongst the/nfaint blue, and when all became still again, the fiery/ncross still burned, showing the door they had already/ntried./n/n"Good thinking," said Harry. "Okay, let's try this one/n/n/n/nAgain he strode directly at the door facing him and/npushed it open, his wand still raised, the others at his/nheels./n/nThis room was larger than the last, dimly lit and/nrectangular, and the center of it was sunken, forming/na great stone pit some twenty feet below them. They/nwere standing on the topmost tier of what seemed to/nbe stone benches running all around the room and/ndescending in steep steps like an amphitheater, or the/ncourtroom in which Harry had been tried by the/nWizengamot. Instead of a chained chair, however,/nthere was a raised stone dais in the center of the/nlowered floor, and upon this dais stood a stone/narchway that looked so ancient, cracked, and/ncrumbling that Harry was amazed the thing was still/n/n/n/n/nstanding. Unsupported by any surrounding wall, the/narchway was hung with a tattered black curtain or/nveil which, despite the complete stillness of the cold/nsurrounding air, was fluttering very slightly as though/nit had just been touched./n/n"Who's there?" said Harry, jumping down onto the/nbench below. There was no answering voice, but the/nveil continued to flutter and sway./n/n"Careful!" whispered Hermione./n/nHarry scrambled down the benches one by one until/nhe reached the stone bottom of the sunken pit. His/nfootsteps echoed loudly as he walked slowly toward/nthe dais. The pointed archway looked much taller/nfrom where he stood now than when he had been/nlooking down on it from above. Still the veil swayed/ngently, as though somebody had just passed through/nit./n/n"Sirius?" Harry spoke again, but much more quietly/nnow that he was nearer./n/nHe had the strangest feeling that there was someone/nstanding right behind the veil on the other side of the/narchway. Gripping his wand very tightly, he edged/naround the dais, but there was nobody there. All that/ncould be seen was the other side of the tattered black/nveil./n/n"Let's go," called Hermione from halfway up the stone/nsteps. "This isn't right, Harry, come on, let's go..."/n/nShe sounded scared, much more scared than she had/nin the room where the brains swam, yet Harry/nthought the archway had a kind of beauty about it,/nold though it was. The gently rippling veil intrigued/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nhim; he felt a very strong inclination to climb up on/nthe dais and walk through it./n/n"Harry, let's go, okay?" said Hermione more forcefully./n/n"Okay," he said, but he did not move. He had just/nheard something. There were faint whispering,/nmurmuring noises coming from the other side of the/nveil./n/n"What are you saying?" he said very loudly, so that/nthe words echoed all around the surrounding stone/nbenches./n/n"Nobody's talking, Harry!" said Hermione, now moving/nover to him./n/n"Someone's whispering behind there," he said, moving/nout of her reach and continuing to frown at the veil./n/n"Is that you, Ron?"/n/n"I'm here, mate," said Ron, appearing around the side/nof the archway./n/n"Can't anyone else hear it?" Harry demanded, for the/nwhispering and murmuring was becoming louder;/nwithout really meaning to put it there, he found his/nfoot was on the dais./n/n"I can hear them too," breathed Luna, joining them/naround the side of the archway and gazing at the/nswaying veil. "There are people in there\"/n/n"What do you mean, 'in there'?" demanded Hermione,/njumping down from the bottom step and sounding/nmuch angrier than the occasion warranted. "There/nisn't any 'in there,' it's just an archway, there's no/nroom for anybody to be there — Harry, stop it, come/naway — "/n/n/n/n/n/nShe grabbed his arm and pulled, but he resisted./n/n"Harry, we are supposed to be here for Sirius!" she/nsaid in a high-pitched, strained voice./n/n"Sirius," Harry repeated, still gazing, mesmerized, at/nthe continuously swaying veil. "Yeah ..."/n/nAnd then something slid back into place in his brain:/nSirius, captured, bound, and tortured, and he was/nstaring at this archway. . ./n/nHe took several paces back from the dais and/nwrenched his eyes from the veil./n/n"Let's go," he said./n/n"That's what I've been trying to — well, come on,/nthen!" said Hermione, and she led the way back/naround the dais. On the other side, Ginny and Neville/nwere staring, apparently entranced, at the veil too./nWithout speaking, Hermione took hold of Ginny's/narm, Ron Neville's, and they marched them firmly/nback to the lowest stone bench and clambered all the/nway back up to the door./n/n"What d'you reckon that arch was?" Harry asked/nHermione as they regained the dark circular room./n/n"I don't know, but whatever it was, it was dangerous,"/nshe said firmly, again inscribing a fiery cross upon/nthe door./n/nOnce more the wall spun and became still again./nHarry approached a door at random and pushed. It/ndid not move./n/n"What's wrong?" said Hermione./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"It's ... locked ..." said Harry, throwing his weight at/nthe door, but it did not budge./n/n/n/n"This is it, then, isn't it?" said Ron excitedly, joining/nHarry in the attempt to force the door open. "Bound/nto be!"/n/n"Get out of the way!" said Hermione sharply. She/npointed her wand at the place where a lock would/nhave been on an ordinary door and said, "Alohomora\"/n/nNothing happened./n/n"Sirius's knife!" said Harry, and he pulled it out from/ninside his robes and slid it into the crack between the/ndoor and the wall. The others all watched eagerly as/nhe ran it from top to bottom, withdrew it, and then/nflung his shoulder again at the door. It remained as/nfirmly shut as ever. What was more, when Harry/nlooked down at the knife, he saw that the blade had/nmelted./n/n"Right, we're leaving that room," said Hermione/ndecisively./n/n"But what if that's the one?" said Ron, staring at it/nwith a mixture of apprehension and longing./n/n"It can't be, Harry could get through all the doors in/nhis dream," said Hermione, marking the door with/nanother fiery cross as Harry replaced the now-useless/nhandle of Sirius's knife in his pocket./n/n"You know what could be in there?" said Luna/neagerly, as the wall started to spin yet again./n/n"Something blibbering, no doubt," said Hermione/nunder her breath, and Neville gave a nervous little/nlaugh./n/n/n/n/n/nThe wall slid back to a halt and Harry, with a feeling/nof increasing desperation, pushed the next door open./n/n"This is it!"/n/nHe knew it at once by the beautiful, dancing,/ndiamond-sparkling light. As Harry's eyes became/nmore accustomed to the brilliant glare he saw clocks/ngleaming from every surface, large and small,/ngrandfather and carriage, hanging in spaces between/nthe bookcases or standing on desks ranging the/nlength of the room, so that a busy, relentless ticking/nfilled the place like thousands of minuscule,/nmarching footsteps. The source of the dancing,/ndiamond-bright light was a towering crystal bell jar/nthat stood at the far end of the room./n/n"This way!"/n/nHarry's heart was pumping frantically now that he/nknew they were on the right track. He led the way/nforward down the narrow space between the lines of/nthe desks, heading, as he had done in his dream, for/nthe source of the light, the crystal bell jar quite as tall/nas he was that stood on a desk and appeared to be/nfull of a billowing, glittering wind./n/n"Oh look)." said Ginny, as they drew nearer, pointing/nat the very heart of the bell jar./n/nDrifting along in the sparkling current inside was a/ntiny, jewel-bright egg. As it rose in the jar it cracked/nopen and a hummingbird emerged, which was carried/nto the very top of the jar, but as it fell on the draft, its/nfeathers became bedraggled and damp again, and by/nthe time it had been borne back to the bottom of the/njar it had been enclosed once more in its egg./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"Keep going!" said Harry sharply, because Ginny/nshowed signs of wanting to stop and watch the egg's/nprogress back into a bird./n/n"You dawdled enough by that old arch!" she said/ncrossly, but followed him past the bell jar to the only/ndoor behind it./n/n"This is it," Harry said again, and his heart was now/npumping so hard and fast he felt it must interfere/nwith his speech. "It's through here — "/n/nHe glanced around at them all. They had their wands/nout and looked suddenly serious and anxious. He/nlooked back at the door and pushed. It swung open./n/nThey were there, they had found the place: high as a/nchurch and full of nothing but towering shelves/ncovered in small, dusty, glass orbs. They glimmered/ndully in the light issuing from more candle brackets/nset at intervals along the shelves. Like those in the/ncircular room behind them, their flames were burning/nblue. The room was very cold./n/nHarry edged forward and peered down one of the/nshadowy aisles between two rows of shelves. He could/nnot hear anything nor see the slightest sign of/nmovement./n/n"You said it was row ninety-seven," whispered/nHermione./n/n"Yeah," breathed Harry, looking up at the end of the/nclosest row. Beneath the branch of blue-glowing/ncandles protruding from it glimmered the silver figure/n53 ./n/n"We need to go right, I think," whispered Hermione,/nsquinting to the next row. "Yes ... that's fifty-four..."/n/n/n/n/n/n"Keep your wands out," Harry said softly./n/nThey crept forward, staring behind them as they went/non down the long alleys of shelves, the farther ends of/nwhich were in near total darkness. Tiny, yellowing/nlabels had been stuck beneath each glass orb on the/nshelf. Some of them had a weird, liquid glow; others/nwere as dull and dark within as blown lightbulbs./n/nThey passed row eighty-four ... eighty-five ... Harry/nwas listening hard for the slightest sound of/nmovement, but Sirius might be gagged now, or else/nunconscious ... or, said an unbidden voice inside his/nhead, he might already be dead.../n/nI'd have felt it, he told himself, his heart now/nhammering against his Adam's apple. I'd already/nknow.../n/n"Ninety-seven!" whispered Hermione./n/nThey stood grouped around the end of the row, gazing/ndown the alley beside it. There was nobody there./n/n"He's right down at the end," said Harry, whose/nmouth had become slightly dry. "You can't see/nproperly from here..."/n/nAnd he led them forward, between the towering rows/nof glass balls, some of which glowed softly as they/npassed.../n/n"He should be near here," whispered Harry, convinced/nthat every step was going to bring the ragged form of/nSirius into view upon the darkened floor. "Anywhere/nhere ... really close ..."/n/n"Harry?" said Hermione tentatively, but he did not/nwant to respond. His mouth was very dry now./n/n/n/n/n/n"Somewhere about ... here ..." he said./n/n/n/nThey had reached the end of the row and emerged/ninto more dim candlelight. There was nobody there at/nall. All was echoing, dusty silence./n/n"He might be ..." Harry whispered hoarsely, peering/ndown the alley next door. "Or maybe ..." He hurried to/nlook down the one beyond that./n/n"Harry?" said Hermione again./n/n"What?" he snarled./n/n"I ... I don't think Sirius is here."/n/nNobody spoke. Harry did not want to look at any of/nthem. He felt sick. He did not understand why Sirius/nwas not here. He had to be here. This was where he,/nHarry, had seen him.../n/nHe ran up the space at the end of the rows, staring/ndown them. Empty aisle after empty aisle flickered/npast. He ran the other way, back past his staring/ncompanions. There was no sign of Sirius anywhere,/nnor any hint of a struggle./n/n"Harry?" Ron called./n/n"What?"/n/nHe did not want to hear what Ron had to say, did not/nwant to hear Ron tell him he had been stupid, or/nsuggest that they ought to go back to Hogwarts. But/nthe heat was rising in his face and he felt as though/nhe would like to skulk down here in the darkness for/na long while before facing the brightness of the Atrium/nabove and the others' accusing stares.../n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"Have you seen this?" said Ron./n/n/n/n"What?" said Harry, but eagerly this time — it had to/nbe a sign that Sirius had been there, a clue — he/nstrode back to where they were all standing, a little/nway down row ninety-seven, but found nothing except/nRon staring at one of the dusty glass spheres on the/nshelves./n/n"What?" Harry repeated glumly./n/n"It's — it's got your name on," said Ron./n/nHarry moved a little closer. Ron was pointing at one of/nthe small glass spheres that glowed with a dull inner/nlight, though it was very dusty and appeared not to/nhave been touched for many years./n/n"My name?" said Harry blankly./n/nHe stepped forward. Not as tall as Ron, he had to/ncrane his neck to read the yellowish label affixed to/nthe shelf right beneath the dusty glass ball. In spidery/nwriting was written a date of some sixteen years/npreviously, and below that:/n/nS.P.T. to A.P.W.B.D./n/nDark Lord/n/nand (?) Harry Potter/n/nHarry stared at it./n/n"What is it?" Ron asked, sounding unnerved. "What's/nyour name doing down here?"/n/nHe glanced along at the other labels on that stretch of/nshelf./n/n/n/n/n/n'Tm not here," he said, sounding perplexed. "None of/nthe rest of us are here..."/n/n"Harry, I don't think you should touch it," said/nHermione sharply, as he stretched out his hand./n/n"Why not?" he said. "It's something to do with me,/nisn't it?"/n/n"Don't, Harry," said Neville suddenly. Harry looked/naround at him. Neville's round face was shining/nslightly with sweat. He looked as though he could not/ntake much more suspense./n/n"It's got my name on," said Harry./n/nAnd feeling slightly reckless, he closed his fingers/naround the dusty ball's surface. He had expected it to/nfeel cold, but it did not. On the contrary, it felt as/nthough it had been lying in the sun for hours, as/nthough the glow of light within was warming it./nExpecting, even hoping, that something dramatic was/ngoing to happen, something exciting that might make/ntheir long and dangerous journey worthwhile after all,/nhe lifted the glass ball down from its shelf and stared/nat it./n/nNothing whatsoever happened. The others moved in/ncloser around Harry, gazing at the orb as he brushed/nit free of the clogging dust./n/nAnd then, from right behind them, a drawling voice/nsaid, "Very good, Potter. Now turn around, nice and/nslowly, and give that to me."/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n35/n/n/n/n

title: Beyond The Veil
text: /nBlack shapes were emerging out of thin air all around/nthem, blocking their way left and right; eyes glinted/nthrough slits in hoods, a dozen lit wand tips were/npointing directly at their hearts. Ginny gave a gasp of/nhorror./n/n"To me, Potter," repeated the drawling voice of Lucius/nMalfoy as he held out his hand, palm up./n/nHarry's insides plummeted sickeningly. They were/ntrapped and outnumbered two to one./n/n"To me," said Malfoy yet again./n/n"Where's Sirius?" Harry said./n/nSeveral of the Death Eaters laughed. A harsh female/nvoice from the midst of the shadowy figures to Harry's/nleft said triumphantly, "The Dark Lord always/nknows!"/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"Always," echoed Malfoy softly. "Now, give me the/nprophecy, Potter."/n/n/n/n"I want to know where Sirius is!"/n/n"I want to know where Sirius is!" mimicked the woman/nto his left./n/nShe and her fellow Death Eaters had closed in so that/nthey were mere feet away from Harry and the others,/nthe light from their wands dazzling Harry's eyes./n/n"You've got him," said Harry, ignoring the rising panic/nin his chest, the dread he had been fighting since/nthey had first entered the ninety-seventh row. "He's/nhere. I know he is."/n/n"The little baby woke up fwightened and fort what it/ndweamed was twoo," said the woman in a horrible,/nmock-baby voice. Harry felt Ron stir beside him./n/n"Don't do anything," he muttered. "Not yet — "/n/nThe woman who had mimicked him let out a raucous/nscream of laughter./n/n"You hear him? You hear him? Giving instructions to/nthe other children as though he thinks of fighting us!"/n/n"Oh, you don't know Potter as I do, Bellatrix," said/nMalfoy softly. "He has a great weakness for heroics;/nthe Dark Lord understands this about him. Now give/nme the prophecy, Potter."/n/n"I know Sirius is here," said Harry, though panic was/ncausing his chest to constrict and he felt as though/nhe could not breathe properly. "I know you've got/nhim!"/n/n/n/n/n/nMore of the Death Eaters laughed, though the woman/nstill laughed loudest of all./n/n"It's time you learned the difference between life and/ndreams, Potter," said Malfoy. "Now give me the/nprophecy, or we start using wands."/n/n"Go on, then," said Harry, raising his own wand to/nchest height. As he did so, the five wands of Ron,/nHermione, Neville, Ginny, and Luna rose on either/nside of him. The knot in Harry's stomach tightened. If/nSirius really was not here, he had led his friends to/ntheir deaths for no reason at all.../n/nBut the Death Eaters did not strike./n/n"Hand over the prophecy and no one need get hurt,"/nsaid Malfoy coolly./n/nIt was Harry's turn to laugh./n/n"Yeah, right!" he said. "I give you this — prophecy, is/nit? And you'll just let us skip off home, will you?"/n/nThe words were hardly out of his mouth when the/nfemale Death Eater shrieked, "Accio Proph — "/n/nHarry was just ready for her. He shouted "Protego\"/nbefore she had finished her spell, and though the/nglass sphere slipped to the tips of his fingers he/nmanaged to cling on to it./n/n"Oh, he knows how to play, little bitty baby Potter,"/nshe said, her mad eyes staring through the slits in/nher hood. "Very well, then — "/n/n"I TOLD YOU, NO!" Lucius Malfoy roared at the/nwoman. "If you smash it — !"/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nHarry's mind was racing. The Death Eaters wanted/nthis dusty spun-glass sphere. He had no interest in it./nHe just wanted to get them all out of this alive, make/nsure that none of his friends paid a terrible price for/nhis stupidity .../n/nThe woman stepped forward, away from her fellows,/nand pulled off her hood. Azkaban had hollowed/nBellatrix Lestrange's face, making it gaunt and skull-/nlike, but it was alive with a feverish, fanatical glow./n/n"You need more persuasion?" she said, her chest/nrising and falling rapidly. "Very well — take the/nsmallest one," she ordered the Death Eaters beside/nher. "Let him watch while we torture the little girl. I'll/ndo it."/n/nHarry felt the others close in around Ginny. He/nstepped sideways so that he was right in front of her,/nthe prophecy held up to his chest./n/n"You'll have to smash this if you want to attack any of/nus," he told Bellatrix. "I don't think your boss will be/ntoo pleased if you come back without it, will he?"/n/nShe did not move; she merely stared at him, the tip of/nher tongue moistening her thin mouth./n/n"So," said Harry, "what kind of prophecy are we/ntalking about anyway?"/n/nHe could not think what to do but to keep talking./nNeville's arm was pressed against his, and he could/nfeel him shaking. He could feel one of the other's/nquickened breath on the back of his head. He was/nhoping they were all thinking hard about ways to get/nout of this, because his mind was blank./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"What kind of prophecy?" repeated Bellatrix, the grin/nfading from her face. "You jest, Harry Potter."/n/n/n/n"Nope, not jesting," said Harry, his eyes flicking from/nDeath Eater to Death Eater, looking for a weak link, a/nspace through which they could escape. "How come/nVoldemort wants it?"/n/nSeveral of the Death Eaters let out low hisses./n/n"You dare speak his name?" whispered Bellatrix./n/n"Yeah," said Harry, maintaining his tight grip on the/nglass ball, expecting another attempt to bewitch it/nfrom him. "Yeah, IVe got no problem saying Vol — "/n/n"Shut your mouth!" Bellatrix shrieked. "You dare/nspeak his name with your unworthy lips, you dare/nbesmirch it with your half-blood's tongue, you dare —/n/n/n/n"Did you know he's a half-blood too?" said Harry/nrecklessly. Hermione gave a little moan in his ear./n"Voldemort? Yeah, his mother was a witch but his/ndad was a Muggle — or has he been telling you lot/nhe's pureblood?"/n/n"STUPEF — "/n/n"iVO!"/n/nA jet of red light had shot from the end of Bellatrix/nLestrange's wand, but Malfoy had deflected it. His/nspell caused hers to hit the shelf a foot to the left of/nHarry and several of the glass orbs there shattered./n/nTwo figures, pearly white as ghosts, fluid as smoke,/nunfurled themselves from the fragments of broken/nglass upon the floor and each began to speak. Their/n/n/n/n/n/nvoices vied with each other, so that only fragments of/nwhat they were saying could be heard over Malfoy and/nBellatrix's shouts./n/n/n/n"... at the Solstice will come a new ..." said the figure/nof an old, bearded man./n/n"DO NOT ATTACK! WE NEED THE PROPHECY!"/n/n"He dared — he dares — " shrieked Bellatrix/nincoherently. " — He stands there — filthy half-blood/n/n/n/n"WAIT UNTIL WEVE GOT THE PROPHECY!" bawled/nMalfoy./n/n"... and none will come after ..." said the figure of a/nyoung woman./n/nThe two figures that had burst from the shattered/nspheres had melted into thin air. Nothing remained of/nthem or their erstwhile homes but fragments of glass/nupon the floor. They had, however, given Harry an/nidea. The problem was going to be conveying it to the/nothers./n/n"You haven't told me what's so special about this/nprophecy I'm supposed to be handing over," he said,/nplaying for time. He moved his foot slowly sideways,/nfeeling around for someone else's./n/n"Do not play games with us, Potter," said Malfoy./n/n"I'm not playing games," said Harry, half his mind on/nthe conversation, half on his wandering foot. And/nthen he found someone's toes and pressed down upon/nthem. A sharp intake of breath behind him told him/nthey were Hermione's./n/n/n/n/n/n"What?" she whispered./n/n"Dumbledore never told you that the reason you bear/nthat scar was hidden in the bowels of the Department/nof Mysteries?" said Malfoy sneeringly./n/n"I — what?" said Harry, and for a moment he quite/nforgot his plan. "What about my scar?"/n/n" What?" whispered Hermione more urgently behind/nhim./n/n"Can this be?" said Malfoy, sounding maliciously/ndelighted; some of the Death Eaters were laughing/nagain, and under cover of their laughter, Harry hissed/nto Hermione, moving his lips as little as possible,/n"Smash shelves — "/n/n"Dumbledore never told you?" Malfoy repeated. "Well,/nthis explains why you didn't come earlier, Potter, the/nDark Lord wondered why — "/n/n" — when I say go — "/n/n" — you didn't come running when he showed you the/nplace where it was hidden in your dreams. He/nthought natural curiosity would make you want to/nhear the exact wording..."/n/n"Did he?" said Harry. Behind him he felt rather than/nheard Hermione passing his message to the others/nand he sought to keep talking, to distract the Death/nEaters. "So he wanted me to come and get it, did he?/nWhy?"/n/n"Why?" Malfoy sounded incredulously delighted./n"Because the only people who are permitted to/nretrieve a prophecy from the Department of Mysteries,/nPotter, are those about whom it was made, as the/n/n/n/n/n/nDark Lord discovered when he attempted to use/nothers to steal it for him."/n/n"And why did he want to steal a prophecy about me?"/n/n"About both of you, Potter, about both of you .../nHaven't you ever wondered why the Dark Lord tried to/nkill you as a baby?"/n/nHarry stared into the slitted eyeholes through which/nMalfoy's gray eyes were gleaming. Was this prophecy/nthe reason Harry's parents had died, the reason he/ncarried his lightning-bolt scar? Was the answer to all/nof this clutched in his hand?/n/n"Someone made a prophecy about Voldemort and/nme?" he said quietly, gazing at Lucius Malfoy, his/nfingers tightening over the warm glass sphere in his/nhand. It was hardly larger than a Snitch and still/ngritty with dust. "And he's made me come and get it/nfor him? Why couldn't he come and get it himself?"/n/n"Get it himself?" shrieked Bellatrix on a cackle of mad/nlaughter. "The Dark Lord, walk into the Ministry of/nMagic, when they are so sweetly ignoring his return?/nThe Dark Lord, reveal himself to the Aurors, when at/nthe moment they are wasting their time on my dear/ncousin?"/n/n"So he's got you doing his dirty work for him, has/nhe?" said Harry. "Like he tried to get Sturgis to steal it/n— and Bode?"/n/n"Very good, Potter, very good ..." said Malfoy slowly./n"But the Dark Lord knows you are not unintell — "/n/n"NOW!" yelled Harry./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nFive different voices behind him bellowed "REDUCTOl"/nFive curses flew in five different directions and the/nshelves opposite them exploded as they hit. The/ntowering structure swayed as a hundred glass/nspheres burst apart, pearly-white figures unfurled/ninto the air and floated there, their voices echoing/nfrom who knew what long-dead past amid the torrent/nof crashing glass and splintered wood now raining/ndown upon the floor —/n/n"RUN!" Harry yelled, and as the shelves swayed/nprecariously and more glass spheres began to pour/nfrom above, he seized a handful of Hermione's robes/nand dragged her forward, one arm over his head as/nchunks of shelf and shards of glass thundered down/nupon them. A Death Eater lunged forward through/nthe cloud of dust and Harry elbowed him hard in the/nmasked face. They were all yelling, there were cries of/npain, thunderous crashes as the shelves collapsed/nupon themselves, weirdly echoing fragments of the/nSeers unleashed from their spheres —/n/nHarry found the way ahead clear and saw Ron,/n/nGinny, and Luna sprint past him, their arms over/ntheir heads. Something heavy struck him on the side/nof the face but he merely ducked his head and/nsprinted onward; a hand caught him by the shoulder;/nhe heard Hermione shout "Stupefy\" and the hand/nreleased him at once./n/nThey were at the end of row ninety-seven; Harry/nturned right and began to sprint in earnest. He could/nhear footsteps right behind him and Hermione's voice/nurging Neville on. The door through which they had/ncome was ajar straight ahead, Harry could see the/nglittering light of the bell jar, he pelted through it, the/nprophecy still clutched tight and safe in his hand,/nwaited for the others to hurtle over the threshold/nbefore slamming the door behind them —/n/n/n/n/n/n" Colloportus\" gasped Hermione and the door sealed/nitself with an odd squelching noise./n/n"Where — where are the others?" gasped Harry./n/nHe had thought that Ron, Luna, and Ginny had been/nahead of them, that they would be waiting in this/nroom, but there was nobody there./n/n"They must have gone the wrong way!" whispered/nHermione, terror in her face./n/n"Listen!" whispered Neville./n/nFootsteps and shouts echoed from behind the door/nthey had just sealed. Harry put his ear close to the/ndoor to listen and heard Lucius Malfoy roar: "Leave/nNott, leave him, I say, the Dark Lord will not care for/nNott's injuries as much as losing that prophecy —/nJugson, come back here, we need to organize! Well/nsplit into pairs and search, and don't forget, be gentle/nwith Potter until we've got the prophecy, you can kill/nthe others if necessary — Bellatrix, Rodolphus, you/ntake the left, Crabbe, Rabastan, go right — Jugson,/nDolohov, the door straight ahead — Macnair and/nAvery, through here — Rookwood, over there —/nMulciber, come with me!"/n/n"What do we do?" Hermione asked Harry, trembling/nfrom head to foot./n/n"Well, we don't stand here waiting for them to find us,/nfor a start," said Harry. "Let's get away from this/ndoor..."/n/nThey ran, quietly as they could, past the shimmering/nbell jar where the tiny egg was hatching and/nunhatching, toward the exit into the circular hallway/nat the far end of the room. They were almost there/n/n/n/n/n/nwhen Harry heard something large and heavy collide/nwith the door Hermione had charmed shut./n/n"Stand aside!" said a rough voice. "Alohomora\"/n/nAs the door flew open, Harry, Hermione, and Neville/ndived under desks. They could see the bottom of the/ntwo Death Eaters' robes drawing nearer, their feet/nmoving rapidly./n/n"They might've run straight through to the hall," said/nthe rough voice./n/n"Check under the desks," said another./n/nHarry saw the knees of the Death Eaters bend. Poking/nhis wand out from under the desk he shouted,/n"STUPEFY]"/n/nA jet of red light hit the nearest Death Eater; he fell/nbackward into a grandfather clock and knocked it/nover. The second Death Eater, however, had leapt/naside to avoid Harry's spell and now pointed his own/nwand at Hermione, who had crawled out from under/nthe desk to get a better aim./n/n"Avada — "/n/nHarry launched himself across the floor and grabbed/nthe Death Eater around the knees, causing him to/ntopple and his aim to go awry. Neville overturned his/ndesk in his anxiety to help; pointing his wand wildly/nat the struggling pair he cried, "EXPELLIARMUS\"/n/nBoth Harry's and the Death Eater's wands flew out of/ntheir hands and soared back toward the entrance to/nthe Hall of Prophecy; both scrambled to their feet and/ncharged after them, the Death Eater in front and/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nHarry hot on his heels, Neville bringing up the rear,/nplainly horrors truck at what he had done./n/n/n/n"Get out of the way, Harry!" yelled Neville, clearly/ndetermined to repair the damage./n/nHarry flung himself sideways as Neville took aim/nagain and shouted, " STUPEFY !"/n/nThe jet of red light flew right over the Death Eater's/nshoulder and hit a glass-fronted cabinet on the wall/nfull of variously shaped hourglasses. The cabinet fell/nto the floor and burst apart, glass flying everywhere,/nthen sprang back up onto the wall, fully mended,/nthen fell down again, and shattered —/n/nThe Death Eater had snatched up his wand, which/nlay on the floor beside the glittering bell jar. Harry/nducked down behind another desk as the man turned/n— his mask had slipped so that he could not see, he/nripped it off with his free hand and shouted, "STUP —/n/n/n/n"STUPEFY]" screamed Hermione, who had just caught/nup with them. The jet of red light hit the Death Eater/nin the middle of his chest; he froze, his arm still/nraised, his wand fell to the floor with a clatter and he/ncollapsed backward toward the bell jar. Harry/nexpected to hear a clunk, for the man to hit solid glass/nand slide off the jar onto the floor, but instead, his/nhead sank through the surface of the bell jar as/nthough it was nothing but a soap bubble and he came/nto rest, sprawled on his back on the table, with his/nhead lying inside the jar full of glittering wind./n/n"Accio Wand\" cried Hermione. Harry's wand flew from/na dark corner into her hand and she threw it to him./n/n"Thanks," he said, "right, let's get out of — "/n/n/n/n/n/n"Look out!" said Neville, horrified, staring at the Death/nEater's head in the bell jar./n/nAll three of them raised their wands again, but none/nof them struck. They were all gazing, openmouthed,/nappalled, at what was happening to the man's head./n/nIt was shrinking very fast, growing balder and balder,/nthe black hair and stubble retracting into his skull,/nhis cheeks smooth, his skull round and covered with/na peachlike fuzz.../n/nA baby's head now sat grotesquely on top of the thick,/nmuscled neck of the Death Eater as he struggled to/nget up again. But even as they watched, their mouths/nopen, the head began to swell to its previous/nproportions again, thick black hair was sprouting/nfrom the pate and chin.../n/n"It's time," said Hermione in an awestruck voice./n/n" Time ..."/n/nThe Death Eater shook his ugly head again, trying to/nclear it, but before he could pull himself together/nagain, it began to shrink back to babyhood once/nmore.../n/nThere was a shout from a room nearby, then a crash/nand a scream./n/n"RON?" Harry yelled, turning quickly from the/nmonstrous transformation taking place before them./n"GINNY? LUNA?"/n/n"Harry!" Hermione screamed./n/nThe Death Eater had pulled his head out of the bell/njar. His appearance was utterly bizarre, his tiny/nbaby's head bawling loudly while his thick arms/n/n/n/n/n/nflailed dangerously in all directions, narrowly missing/nHarry, who ducked. Harry raised his wand but to his/namazement Hermione seized his arm./n/n"You can't hurt a baby!"/n/nThere was no time to argue the point. Harry could/nhear more footsteps growing louder from the Hall of/nProphecy they had just left and knew, too late, that/nhe ought not to have shouted and given away their/nposition./n/n"Come on!" he said again, and leaving the ugly baby-/nheaded Death Eater staggering behind them, they/ntook off for the door that stood ajar at the other end of/nthe room, leading back into the black hallway./n/nThey had run halfway toward it when Harry saw/nthrough the open door two more Death Eaters/nrunning across the black room toward them. Veering/nleft he burst instead into a small, dark, cluttered/noffice and slammed the door behind them./n/n"Collo — " began Hermione, but before she could/ncomplete the spell the door had burst open again and/nthe two Death Eaters had come hurtling inside. With/na cry of triumph, both yelled, " IMPEDIMENT A\"/n/nHarry, Hermione, and Neville were all knocked/nbackward off their feet. Neville was thrown over the/ndesk and disappeared from view, Hermione smashed/ninto a bookcase and was promptly deluged in a/ncascade of heavy books; the back of Harry's head/nslammed into the stone wall behind him, tiny lights/nburst in front of his eyes, and for a moment he was/ntoo dizzy and bewildered to react./n/n"WEVE GOT HIM!" yelled the Death Eater nearest/nHarry, "IN AN OFFICE OFF — "/n/n/n/n/n/n" Silenciol " cried Hermione, and the man's voice was/nextinguished. He continued to mouth through the/nhole in his mask, but no sound came out; he was/nthrust aside by his fellow./n/n"Petrificus Totalusl" shouted Harry, as the second/nDeath Eater raised his wand. His arms and legs/nsnapped together and he fell forward, facedown onto/nthe rug at Harry's feet, stiff as a board and unable to/nmove at all./n/n"Well done, Ha — "/n/nBut the Death Eater Hermione had just struck dumb/nmade a sudden slashing movement with his wand/nfrom which flew a streak of what looked like purple/nflame. It passed right across Hermione's chest; she/ngave a tiny "oh!" as though of surprise and then/ncrumpled onto the floor where she lay motionless./n/n"HERMIONE!"/n/nHarry fell to his knees beside her as Neville crawled/nrapidly toward her from under the desk, his wand/nheld up in front of him. The Death Eater kicked out/nhard at Neville's head as he emerged — his foot broke/nNeville's wand in two and connected with his face —/nNeville gave a howl of pain and recoiled, clutching his/nmouth and nose. Harry twisted around, his own wand/nheld high, and saw that the Death Eater had ripped/noff his mask and was pointing his wand directly at/nHarry, who recognized the long, pale, twisted face/nfrom the Daily Prophet: Antonin Dolohov, the wizard/nwho had murdered the Prewetts./n/nDolohov grinned. With his free hand, he pointed from/nthe prophecy still clutched in Harry's hand, to/nhimself, then at Hermione. Though he could no longer/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nspeak his meaning could not have been clearer: Give/nme the prophecy, or you get the same as her.../n/n/n/n"Like you won't kill us all the moment I hand it over/nanyway!" said Harry./n/nA whine of panic inside his head was preventing him/nthinking properly. He had one hand on Hermione's/nshoulder, which was still warm, yet did not dare look/nat her properly. Don't let her be dead, don't let her be/ndead, it's my fault if she's dead.../n/n"Whaddever you do, Harry," said Neville fiercely from/nunder the desk, lowering his hands to show a clearly/nbroken nose and blood pouring down his mouth and/nchin, "don'd gib it to him!"/n/nThen there was a crash outside the door, and Dolohov/nlooked over his shoulder — the baby-headed Death/nEater had appeared in the doorway, his head bawling,/nhis great fists still flailing uncontrollably at everything/naround him./n/nHarry seized his chance: "PETRIFICUS TOT ALU S\"/n/nThe spell hit Dolohov before he could block it, and he/ntoppled forward across his comrade, both of them/nrigid as boards and unable to move an inch./n/n"Hermione," Harry said at once, shaking her as the/nbaby-headed Death Eater blundered out of sight/nagain. "Hermione, wake up..."/n/n"Whaddid he do to her?" said Neville, crawling out/nfrom under the desk again to kneel at her other side,/nblood streaming from his rapidly swelling nose.
