"I/ndunno..."/n/nNeville groped for Hermione's wrist./n/n/n/n/n/n"Dat's a pulse, Harry, I'b sure id is..."/n/n/n/nSuch a powerful wave of relief swept through Harry/nthat for a moment he felt light-headed./n/n"She's alive?"/n/n"Yeah, I dink so..."/n/nThere was a pause in which Harry listened hard for/nthe sounds of more footsteps, but all he could hear/nwere the whimpers and blunderings of the baby/nDeath Eater in the next room./n/n"Neville, we're not far from the exit," Harry whispered./n"We're right next to that circular room... If we can just/nget you across it and find the right door before any/nmore Death Eaters come, I'll bet you can get/nHermione up the corridor and into the lift... Then you/ncould find someone... Raise the alarm ..."/n/n"And whad are you going do do?" said Neville,/nmopping his bleeding nose with his sleeve and/nfrowning at Harry./n/n"I've got to find the others," said Harry./n/n"Well, I'b going do find dem wid you," said Neville/nfirmly./n/n"But Hermione — "/n/n"We'll dake her wid us," said Neville firmly. "I'll carry/nher — you're bedder at fighding dem dan I ab — "/n/nHe stood up and seized one of Hermione's arms,/nglared at Harry, who hesitated, then grabbed the/nother and helped hoist Hermione's limp form over/nNeville's shoulders./n/n/n/n/n/n"Wait," said Harry, snatching up Hermione's wand/nfrom the floor and shoving it into Nevilles hand,/n/n"you'd better take this..."/n/nNeville kicked aside the broken fragments of his own/nwand as they walked slowly toward the door./n/n"My gran's going do kill be," said Neville thickly, blood/nspattering from his nose as he spoke, "dat was by/ndad's old wand..."/n/nHarry stuck his head out of the door and looked/naround cautiously. The baby-headed Death Eater was/nscreaming and banging into things, toppling/ngrandfather clocks and overturning desks, bawling/nand confused, while the glass cabinet that Harry now/nsuspected had contained Time-Turners continued to/nfall, shatter, and repair itself on the wall behind them./n/n"He's never going to notice us," he whispered. "C'mon/n... keep close behind me..."/n/nThey crept out of the office and back toward the door/ninto the black hallway, which now seemed completely/ndeserted. They walked a few steps forward, Neville/ntottering slightly due to Hermione's weight. The door/nof the Time Room swung shut behind them, and the/nwalls began to rotate once more. The recent blow on/nthe back of Harry's head seemed to have unsteadied/nhim; he narrowed his eyes, swaying slightly, until the/nwalls stopped moving again. With a sinking heart/nHarry saw that Hermione's fiery crosses had faded/nfrom the doors./n/n"So which way d'you reck — ?"/n/nBut before they could make a decision as to which/nway to try, a door to their right sprang open and three/npeople fell out of it./n/n/n/n/n/n"Ron!" croaked Harry, dashing toward them. "Ginny/n— are you all — ?"/n/n"Harry," said Ron, giggling weakly, lurching forward,/nseizing the front of Harry's robes and gazing at him/nwith unfocused eyes. "There you are... Ha ha ha .../nYou look funny, Harry... You're all messed up.../n/nRon's face was very white and something dark was/ntrickling from the corner of his mouth. Next moment/nhis knees had given way, but he still clutched the/nfront of Harry's robes, so that Harry was pulled into a/nkind of bow./n/n"Ginny?" Harry said fearfully. "What happened?"/n/nBut Ginny shook her head and slid down the wall into/na sitting position, panting and holding her ankle./n/n"I think her ankle's broken, I heard something crack,"/nwhispered Luna, who was bending over her and who/nalone seemed to be unhurt. "Four of them chased us/ninto a dark room full of planets, it was a very odd/nplace, some of the time we were just floating in the/ndark — "/n/n"Harry, we saw Uranus up close!" said Ron, still/ngiggling feebly. "Get it, Harry? We saw Uranus — ha/nha ha — "/n/nA bubble of blood grew at the corner of Ron's mouth/nand burst./n/n"Anyway, one of them grabbed Ginny's foot, I used the/nReductor Curse and blew up Pluto in his face, but ..."/n/nLuna gestured hopelessly at Ginny, who was/nbreathing in a very shallow way, her eyes still closed./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"And what about Ron?" said Harry fearfully, as Ron/ncontinued to giggle, still hanging off the front of/nHarry's robes./n/n"I don't know what they hit him with," said Luna/nsadly, "but he's gone a bit funny, I could hardly get/nhim along at all..."/n/n"Harry," said Ron, pulling Harry's ear down to his/nmouth and still giggling weakly, "you know who this/ngirl is, Harry? She's Loony ... Loony Lovegood ... ha/nha ha..."/n/n"We've got to get out of here," said Harry firmly./n/n"Luna, can you help Ginny?"/n/n"Yes," said Luna, sticking her wand behind her ear for/nsafekeeping, putting an arm around Ginny's waist/nand pulling her up./n/n"It's only my ankle, I can do it myself!" said Ginny/nimpatiently, but next moment she had collapsed/nsideways and grabbed Luna for support. Harry pulled/nRon's arm over his shoulder just as, so many months/nago, he had pulled Dudley's. He looked around: They/nhad a one-in-twelve chance of getting the exit right/nthe first time —/n/nHe heaved Ron toward a door; they were within a few/nfeet of it when another door across the hall burst/nopen and three Death Eaters sped into the hall, led by/nBellatrix Lestrange./n/n" There they are!" she shrieked./n/nStunning Spells shot across the room: Harry smashed/nhis way through the door ahead, flung Ron/nunceremoniously from him, and ducked back to help/nNeville in with Hermione. They were all over the/n/n/n/n/n/nthreshold just in time to slam the door against/nBellatrix./n/n/n/n" Colloportus\" shouted Harry, and he heard three/nbodies slam into the door on the other side./n/n"It doesn't matter!" said a man's voice. "There are/nother ways in — WEVE GOT THEM, THEY'RE HERE!"/n/nHarry spun around. They were back in the Brain/nRoom and, sure enough, there were doors all around/nthe walls. He could hear footsteps in the hall behind/nthem as more Death Eaters came running to join the/nfirst./n/n"Luna — Neville — help me!"/n/nThe three of them tore around the room, sealing the/ndoors as they went: Harry crashed into a table and/nrolled over the top of it in his haste to reach the next/ndoor./n/n" Colloportusl"/n/nThere were footsteps running along behind the doors;/n/nevery now and then another heavy body would launch/n/nitself against one, so it creaked and shuddered. Luna/n/nand Neville were bewitching the doors along the/n/nopposite wall — then, as Harry reached the very top of/n/nthe room, he heard Luna cry, "Collo — aaaaaaaaargh/n??/n/n/n/nHe turned in time to see her flying through the air./n/nFive Death Eaters were surging into the room through/nthe door she had not reached in time; Luna hit a/ndesk, slid over its surface and onto the floor on the/nother side where she lay sprawled, as still as/nHermione./n/n/n/n/n/n"Get Potter!" shrieked Bellatrix, and she ran at him./nHe dodged her and sprinted back up the room; he/nwas safe as long as they thought they might hit the/nprophecy —/n/n"Hey!" said Ron, who had staggered to his feet and/nwas now tottering drunkenly toward Harry, giggling./n"Hey, Harry, there are brains in here, ha ha ha, isn't/nthat weird, Harry?"/n/n"Ron, get out of the way, get down — "/n/nBut Ron had already pointed his wand at the tank./n/n"Honest, Harry, they're brains — look — Accio Brain\"/n/nThe scene seemed momentarily frozen. Harry, Ginny,/nand Neville and each of the Death Eaters turned in/nspite of themselves to watch the top of the tank as a/nbrain burst from the green liquid like a leaping fish./nFor a moment it seemed suspended in midair, then it/nsoared toward Ron, spinning as it came, and what/nlooked like ribbons of moving images flew from it,/nunraveling like rolls of film —/n/n"Ha ha ha, Harry, look at it — " said Ron, watching it/ndisgorge its gaudy innards. "Harry, come and touch/nit, bet it's weird — "/n/n"RON, NO!"/n/nHarry did not know what would happen if Ron/ntouched the tentacles of thought now flying behind/nthe brain, but he was sure it would not be anything/ngood. He darted forward but Ron had already caught/nthe brain in his outstretched hands./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nThe moment they made contact with his skin, the/ntentacles began wrapping themselves around Ron's/narms like ropes./n/n"Harry, look what's happen — no — no, I don't like it/n— no, stop — stop — "/n/nBut the thin ribbons were spinning around Ron's/nchest now. He tugged and tore at them as the brain/nwas pulled tight against him like an octopus's body./n/n"Diffindol" yelled Harry, trying to sever the feelers/nwrapping themselves tightly around Ron before his/neyes, but they would not break. Ron fell over, still/nthrashing against his bonds./n/n"Harry, it'll suffocate him!" screamed Ginny,/nimmobilized by her broken ankle on the floor — then/na jet of red light flew from one of the Death Eater's/nwands and hit her squarely in the face. She keeled/nover sideways and lay there unconscious./n/n" STUBEFYl" shouted Neville, wheeling around and/nwaving Hermione's wand at the oncoming Death/nEaters. "STUBEFY, STUBEFYl"/n/nBut nothing happened — one of the Death Eaters/nshot their own Stunning Spell at Neville; it missed/nhim by inches. Harry and Neville were now the only/ntwo left fighting the five Death Eaters, two of whom/nsent streams of silver light like arrows past them that/nleft craters in the wall behind them. Harry ran for it/nas Bellatrix Lestrange sprinted right at him. Holding/nthe prophecy high above his head he sprinted back/nup the room; all he could think of doing was to draw/nthe Death Eaters away from the others./n/nIt seemed to have worked. They streaked after him,/nknocking chairs and tables flying but not daring to/n/n/n/n/n/nbewitch him in case they hurt the prophecy, and he/ndashed through the only door still open, the one/nthrough which the Death Eaters themselves had/ncome. Inwardly praying that Neville would stay with/nRon — find some way of releasing him — he ran a few/nfeet into the new room and felt the floor vanish —/n/nHe was falling down steep stone step after steep stone/nstep, bouncing on every tier until at last, with a crash/nthat knocked all the breath out of his body, he landed/nflat on his back in the sunken pit where the stone/narchway stood on its dais. The whole room was/nringing with the Death Eaters' laughter. He looked up/nand saw the five who had been in the Brain Room/ndescending toward him, while as many more emerged/nthrough other doorways and began leaping from/nbench to bench toward him. Harry got to his feet/nthough his legs were trembling so badly they barely/nsupported him. The prophecy was still miraculously/nunbroken in his left hand, his wand clutched tightly/nin his right. He backed away, looking around, trying/nto keep all the Death Eaters within his sights. The/nback of his legs hit something solid; he had reached/nthe dais where the archway stood. He climbed/nbackward onto it./n/nThe Death Eaters all halted, gazing at him. Some were/npanting as hard as he was. One was bleeding badly;/nDolohov, freed of the full Body-Bind, was leering, his/nwand pointing straight at Harry's face./n/n"Potter, your race is run," drawled Lucius Malfoy,/npulling off his mask. "Now hand me the prophecy like/na good boy..."/n/n"Let — let the others go, and I'll give it to you!" said/nHarry desperately./n/nA few of the Death Eaters laughed./n/n/n/n/n/n"You are not in a position to bargain, Potter," said/nLucius Malfoy, his pale face flushed with pleasure./n/n"You see, there are ten of us and only one of you ... or/nhasn't Dumbledore ever taught you how to count?"/n/n"He's dot alone!" shouted a voice from above them./n/n"He's still god be!"/n/nHarry's heart sank. Neville was scrambling down the/nstone benches toward them, Hermione's wand held/nfast in his trembling hand./n/n"Neville — no — go back to Ron — "/n/n"STUBEFYl" Neville shouted again, pointing his wand/nat each Death Eater in turn, "STUBEFYl. STUBE — "/n/nOne of the largest Death Eaters seized Neville from/nbehind, pinioning his arms to his sides. He struggled/nand kicked; several of the Death Eaters laughed./n/n"It's Longbottom, isn't it?" sneered Lucius Malfoy./n/n"Well, your grandmother is used to losing family/nmembers to our cause... Your death will not come as/na great shock..."/n/n"Longbottom?" repeated Bellatrix, and a truly evil/nsmile lit her gaunt face. "Why, I have had the/npleasure of meeting your parents, boy..."/n/n"I DOE YOU HAB!" roared Neville, and he fought so/nhard against his captor's encircling grip that the/nDeath Eater shouted, "Someone Stun him!"/n/n"No, no, no," said Bellatrix. She looked transported,/nalive with excitement as she glanced at Harry, then/nback at Neville. "No, let's see how long Longbottom/nlasts before he cracks like his parents... Unless Potter/nwants to give us the prophecy — "/n/n/n/n/n/n"DON'D GIB ID DO DEM!" roared Neville, who seemed/nbeside himself, kicking and writhing as Bellatrix drew/nnearer to him and his captor, her wand raised./n/n"DON'D GIB ID DO DEM, HARRY!"/n/nBellatrix raised her wand. "Cruciol"/n/nNeville screamed, his legs drawn up to his chest so/nthat the Death Eater holding him was momentarily/nholding him off the ground. The Death Eater dropped/nhim and he fell to the floor, twitching and screaming/nin agony./n/n"That was just a taster!" said Bellatrix, raising her/nwand so that Neville's screams stopped and he lay/nsobbing at her feet. She turned and gazed up at/nHarry. "Now, Potter, either give us the prophecy, or/nwatch your little friend die the hard way!"/n/nHarry did not have to think; there was no choice. The/nprophecy was hot with the heat from his clutching/nhand as he held it out. Malfoy jumped forward to take/nit./n/nThen, high above them, two more doors burst open/nand five more people sprinted into the room: Sirius,/nLupin, Moody, Tonks, and Kingsley./n/nMalfoy turned and raised his wand, but Tonks had/nalready sent a Stunning Spell right at him. Harry did/nnot wait to see whether it had made contact, but/ndived off the dais out of the way. The Death Eaters/nwere completely distracted by the appearance of the/nmembers of the Order, who were now raining spells/ndown upon them as they jumped from step to step/ntoward the sunken floor: Through the darting bodies,/nthe flashes of light, Harry could see Neville crawling/nalong. He dodged another jet of red light and flung/nhimself flat on the ground to reach Neville./n/n/n/n/n/n"Are you okay?" he yelled, as another spell soared/ninches over their heads./n/n/n/n"Yes," said Neville, trying to pull himself up./n/n"And Ron?"/n/n"I dink he's all right — he was still fighding the brain/nwhen I left — "/n/nThe stone floor between them exploded as a spell hit/nit, leaving a crater right where Neville's hand had/nbeen seconds before. Both scrambled away from the/nspot, then a thick arm came out of nowhere, seized/nHarry around the neck and pulled him upright, so/nthat his toes were barely touching the floor./n/n"Give it to me," growled a voice in his ear, "give me the/nprophecy — "/n/nThe man was pressing so tightly on Harry's windpipe/nthat he could not breathe — through watering eyes he/nsaw Sirius dueling with a Death Eater some ten feet/naway. Kingsley was fighting two at once; Tonks, still/nhalfway up the tiered seats, was firing spells down at/nBellatrix — nobody seemed to realize that Harry was/ndying... He turned his wand backward toward the/nman's side, but had no breath to utter an incantation,/nand the man's free hand was groping toward the hand/nin which Harry was grasping the prophecy —/n/n"AARGH!"/n/nNeville had come lunging out of nowhere: Unable to/narticulate a spell, he had jabbed Hermione's wand/nhard into the eyehole of the Death Eater's mask. The/nman relinquished Harry at once with a howl of pain/nand Harry whirled around to face him and gasped,/n"STUPEFY]"/n/n/n/n/n/nThe Death Eater keeled over backward and his mask/nslipped off. It was Macnair, Buckbeak's would-be/nkiller, one of his eyes now swollen and bloodshot./n/n"Thanks!" Harry said to Neville, pulling him aside as/nSirius and his Death Eater lurched past, dueling so/nfiercely that their wands were blurs. Then Harry's foot/nmade contact with something round and hard and he/nslipped — for a moment he thought he had dropped/nthe prophecy, then saw Moody's magic eye spinning/naway across the floor./n/nIts owner was lying on his side, bleeding from the/nhead, and his attacker was now bearing down upon/nHarry and Neville: Dolohov, his long pale face twisted/nwith glee./n/n"Tarantallegrcd" he shouted, his wand pointing at/nNeville, whose legs went immediately into a kind of/nfrenzied tap dance, unbalancing him and causing him/nto fall to the floor again. "Now, Potter — "/n/nHe made the same slashing movement with his wand/nthat he had used on Hermione just as Harry yelled,/n"Protego\"/n/nHarry felt something streak across his face like a/nblunt knife but the force of it knocked him sideways,/nand he fell over Neville's jerking legs, but the Shield/nCharm had stopped the worst of the spell./n/nDolohov raised his wand again. "Accio Proph — "/n/nSirius hurtled out of nowhere, rammed Dolohov with/nhis shoulder, and sent him flying out of the way. The/nprophecy had again flown to the tips of Harry's fingers/nbut he had managed to cling to it. Now Sirius and/nDolohov were dueling, their wands flashing like/nswords, sparks flying from their wand tips —/n/n/n/n/n/nDolohov drew back his wand to make the same/nslashing movement he had used on Harry and/nHermione. Springing up, Harry yelled, "Petrificus/nTotalusl" Once again, Dolohov's arms and legs/nsnapped together and he keeled over backward,/nlanding with a crash on his back./n/n"Nice one!" shouted Sirius, forcing Harry's head down/nas a pair of Stunning Spells flew toward them. "Now I/nwant you to get out of — "/n/nThey both ducked again. A jet of green light had/nnarrowly missed Sirius; across the room Harry saw/nTonks fall from halfway up the stone steps, her limp/nform toppling from stone seat to stone seat, and/nBellatrix, triumphant, running back toward the fray./n/n"Harry, take the prophecy, grab Neville, and run!"/nSirius yelled, dashing to meet Bellatrix. Harry did not/nsee what happened next: Kingsley swayed across his/nfield of vision, battling with the pockmarked/nRookwood, now mask-less; another jet of green light/nflew over Harry's head as he launched himself toward/nNeville —/n/n"Can you stand?" he bellowed in Neville's ear, as/nNeville's legs jerked and twitched uncontrollably. "Put/nyour arm round my neck — "/n/nNeville did so — Harry heaved — Neville's legs were/nstill flying in every direction, they would not support/nhim and then, out of nowhere, a man lunged at them./nBoth fell backward, Neville's legs waving wildly like an/noverturned beetle's, Harry with his left arm held up in/nthe air to try and save the small glass ball from being/nsmashed./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"The prophecy, give me the prophecy, Potter!" snarled/nLucius Malfoy's voice in his ear, and Harry felt the tip/nof Malfoy's wand pressing hard between his ribs./n/n"No — get — off — me ... Neville — catch it!"/n/nHarry flung the prophecy across the floor, Neville/nspun himself around on his back and scooped the/nball to his chest. Malfoy pointed the wand instead at/nNeville, but Harry jabbed his own wand back over his/nshoulder and yelled, "Impedimental"/n/nMalfoy was blasted off his back. As Harry scrambled/nup again he looked around and saw Malfoy smash/ninto the dais on which Sirius and Bellatrix were now/ndueling. Malfoy aimed his wand at Harry and Neville/nagain, but before he could draw breath to strike,/nLupin had jumped between them./n/n"Harry, round up the others and GO!"/n/nHarry seized Neville by the shoulder of his robes and/nlifted him bodily onto the first tier of stone steps./nNeville's legs twitched and jerked and would not/nsupport his weight. Harry heaved again with all the/nstrength he possessed and they climbed another step/n/n/n/nA spell hit the stone bench at Harry's heel. It/ncrumbled away and he fell back to the step below:/nNeville sank to the ground, his legs still jerking and/nthrashing, and thrust the prophecy into his pocket./n/n"Come on!" said Harry desperately, hauling at/nNeville's robes. "Just try and push with your legs — "/n/nHe gave another stupendous heave and Neville's robes/ntore all along the left seam — the small spun-glass/nball dropped from his pocket and before either of/n/n/n/n/n/nthem could catch it, one of Neville's floundering feet/nkicked it. It flew some ten feet to their right and/nsmashed on the step beneath them. As both of them/nstared at the place where it had broken, appalled at/nwhat had happened, a pearly-white figure with hugely/nmagnified eyes rose into the air, unnoticed by any but/nthem. Harry could see its mouth moving, but in all/nthe crashes and screams and yells surrounding them,/nnot one word of the prophecy could he hear. The/nfigure stopped speaking and dissolved into/nnothingness./n/n"Harry, I'b sorry!" cried Neville, his face anguished as/nhis legs continued to flounder, "I'b so sorry, Harry, I/ndidn'd bean do — ■"/n/n"It doesn't matter!" Harry shouted. "Just try and/nstand, let's get out of — "/n/n" Dubbledorel" said Neville, his sweaty face suddenly/ntransported, staring over Harry's shoulder./n/n"What?"/n/n"DUBBLEDORE!"/n/nHarry turned to look where Neville was staring./n/nDirectly above them, framed in the doorway from the/nBrain Room, stood Albus Dumbledore, his wand aloft,/nhis face white and furious. Harry felt a kind of electric/ncharge surge through every particle of his body —/nthey were saved./n/nDumbledore sped down the steps past Neville and/nHarry, who had no more thought of leaving./nDumbledore was already at the foot of the steps when/nthe Death Eaters nearest realized he was there. There/nwere yells; one of the Death Eaters ran for it,/nscrabbling like a monkey up the stone steps opposite./n/n/n/n/nDumbledore's spell pulled him back as easily and/neffortlessly as though he had hooked him with an/ninvisible line —/n/n/n/nOnly one couple were still battling, apparently/nunaware of the new arrival. Harry saw Sirius duck/nBellatrix's jet of red light: He was laughing at her./n"Come on, you can do better than that!" he yelled, his/nvoice echoing around the cavernous room./n/nThe second jet of light hit him squarely on the chest./n/nThe laughter had not quite died from his face, but his/neyes widened in shock./n/nHarry released Neville, though he was unaware of/ndoing so. He was jumping down the steps again,/npulling out his wand, as Dumbledore turned to the/ndais too./n/nIt seemed to take Sirius an age to fall. His body/ncurved in a graceful arc as he sank backward through/nthe ragged veil hanging from the arch.../n/nAnd Harry saw the look of mingled fear and surprise/non his godfather's wasted, once-handsome face as he/nfell through the ancient doorway and disappeared/nbehind the veil, which fluttered for a moment as/nthough in a high wind and then fell back into place./n/nHarry heard Bellatrix Lestrange's triumphant scream,/nbut knew it meant nothing — Sirius had only just/nfallen through the archway, he would reappear from/nthe other side any second.../n/nBut Sirius did not reappear./n/n"SIRIUS!" Harry yelled, "SIRIUS!"/n/n/n/n/n/nHe had reached the floor, his breath coming in/nsearing gasps. Sirius must be just behind the curtain,/nhe, Harry, would pull him back out again.../n/nBut as he reached the ground and sprinted toward/nthe dais, Lupin grabbed Harry around the chest,/nholding him back./n/n"There's nothing you can do, Harry — "/n/n"Get him, save him, he's only just gone through!"/n/n"It's too late, Harry — "/n/n"We can still reach him — "/n/nHarry struggled hard and viciously, but Lupin would/nnot let go.../n/n"There's nothing you can do, Harry ... nothing... He's/ngone."/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n

title: The Only One He Ever Feared
text: /n"He hasn't gone!" Harry yelled./n/nHe did not believe it, he would not believe it; still he/nfought Lupin with every bit of strength he had: Lupin/ndid not understand, people hid behind that curtain,/nhe had heard them whispering the first time he had/nentered the room — Sirius was hiding, simply lurking/nout of sight —/n/n"SIRIUS!" he bellowed, "SIRIUS!"/n/n"He can't come back, Harry," said Lupin, his voice/nbreaking as he struggled to contain Harry. "He can't/ncome back, because he's d — "/n/n"HE — IS — NOT — DEAD!" roared Harry. "SIRIUS!"/n/nThere was movement going on around them, pointless/nbustling, the flashes of more spells. To Harry it was/nmeaningless noise, the deflected curses flying past/nthem did not matter, nothing mattered except that/nLupin stop pretending that Sirius, who was standing/n/n/n/nfeet from them behind that old curtain, was not going/nto emerge at any moment, shaking back his dark hair/nand eager to reenter the battle —/n/nLupin dragged Harry away from the dais, Harry still/nstaring at the archway, angry at Sirius now for/nkeeping him waiting —/n/nBut some part of him realized, even as he fought to/nbreak free from Lupin, that Sirius had never kept him/nwaiting before... Sirius had risked everything, always,/nto see Harry, to help him... If Sirius was not/nreappearing out of that archway when Harry was/nyelling for him as though his life depended on it, the/nonly possible explanation was that he could not come/nback. . . That he really was . . ./n/nDumbledore had most of the remaining Death Eaters/ngrouped in the middle of the room, seemingly/nimmobilized by invisible ropes. Mad-Eye Moody had/ncrawled across the room to where Tonks lay and was/nattempting to revive her. Behind the dais there were/nstill flashes of light, grunts, and cries — Kingsley had/nrun forward to continue Sirius's duel with Bellatrix./n/n"Harry?"/n/nNeville had slid down the stone benches one by one to/nthe place where Harry stood. Harry was no longer/nstruggling against Lupin, who maintained a/nprecautionary grip on his arm nevertheless./n/n"Harry ... I'b really sorry..." said Neville. His legs were/nstill dancing uncontrollably. "Was dat man — was/nSirius Black a — a friend of yours?"/n/nHarry nodded./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"Here," said Lupin quietly, and pointing his wand at/nNeville's legs he said, "Finite." The spell was lifted./nNeville's legs fell back onto the floor and remained/nstill. Lupin's face was pale. "Let's — let's find the/nothers. Where are they all, Neville?"/n/nLupin turned away from the archway as he spoke. It/nsounded as though every word was causing him pain./n/n"Dey're all back dere," said Neville. "A brain addacked/nRon bud I dink he's all righd — and Herbione's/nunconscious, bud we could feel a bulse — "/n/nThere was a loud bang and a yell from behind the/ndais. Harry saw Kingsley, yelling in pain, hit the/nground. Bellatrix Lestrange turned tail and ran as/nDumbledore whipped around. He aimed a spell at her/nbut she deflected it. She was halfway up the steps/nnow —/n/n"Harry — no!" cried Lupin, but Harry had already/nripped his arm from Lupin's slackened grip./n/n"SHE KILLED SIRIUS!" bellowed Harry. "SHE KILLED/nHIM — I'LL KILL HER!"/n/nAnd he was off, scrambling up the stone benches./nPeople were shouting behind him but he did not care./nThe hem of Bellatrix's robes whipped out of sight/nahead and they were back in the room where the/nbrains were swimming. . ./n/nShe aimed a curse over her shoulder. The tank rose/ninto the air and tipped. Harry was deluged in the foul-/nsmelling potion within. The brains slipped and slid/nover him and began spinning their long, colored/ntentacles, but he shouted, "Wingardium Levioscd" and/nthey flew into the air away from him. Slipping and/nsliding he ran on toward the door. He leapt over Luna,/n/n/n/n/nwho was groaning on the floor, past Ginny, who said,/n"Harry — what — ?" past Ron, who giggled feebly, and/nHermione, who was still unconscious. He wrenched/nopen the door into the circular black hall and saw/nBellatrix disappearing through a door on the other/nside of the room — beyond her was the corridor/nleading back to the lifts./n/nHe ran, but she had slammed the door behind her/nand the walls had begun to rotate again. Once more/nhe was surrounded by streaks of blue light from the/nwhirling candelabra./n/n"Where's the exit?" he shouted desperately, as the/nwall rumbled to a halt again. "Where's the way out?"/n/nThe room seemed to have been waiting for him to ask./nThe door right behind him flew open, and the corridor/ntoward the lifts stretched ahead of him, torch- lit and/nempty. He ran.../n/nHe could hear a lift clattering ahead of him. He/nsprinted up the passageway, swung around the/ncorner, and slammed his fist onto the button to call a/nsecond lift. It jangled and banged lower and lower; the/ngrilles slid open and Harry dashed inside, now/nhammering the button marked Atrium. The doors slid/nshut and he was rising. . ./n/nHe forced his way out of the lift before the grilles were/nfully open and looked around. Bellatrix was almost at/nthe telephone lift at the other end of the hall, but she/nlooked back as he sprinted toward her, and aimed/nanother spell at him. He dodged behind the Fountain/nof Magical Brethren; the spell zoomed past him and/nhit the wrought gold gates at the other end of the/nAtrium so that they rang like bells. There were no/nmore footsteps. She had stopped running. He/ncrouched behind the statues, listening./n/n/n/n/n/n" Come out, come out, little HarryV' she called in her/nmock-baby voice, which echoed off the polished/nwooden floors. "What did you come after me for, then?/n/nI thought you were here to avenge my dear cousin!"/n/n"I am!" shouted Harry, and a score of ghostly Harry's/nseemed to chorus I am\ I am\ I am\ all around the/nroom./n/n"Aaaaaah . . . did you love him, little baby Potter?"/n/nHatred rose in Harry such as he had never known/nbefore. He flung himself out from behind the fountain/nand bellowed "CrucioV'/n/nBellatrix screamed. The spell had knocked her off her/nfeet, but she did not writhe and shriek with pain as/nNeville had — she was already on her feet again,/nbreathless, no longer laughing. Harry dodged behind/nthe golden fountain again — her counterspell hit the/nhead of the handsome wizard, which was blown off/nand landed twenty feet away, gouging long scratches/ninto the wooden floor./n/n"Never used an Unforgivable Curse before, have you,/nboy?" she yelled. She had abandoned her baby voice/nnow. "You need to mean them, Potter! You need to/nreally want to cause pain — to enjoy it — righteous/nanger won't hurt me for long — I'll show you how it is/ndone, shall I? I'll give you a lesson — "/n/nHarry had been edging around the fountain on the/nother side. She screamed, "Cruciol" and he was forced/nto duck down again as the centaur's arm, holding its/nbow, spun off and landed with a crash on the floor a/nshort distance from the golden wizard's head./n/n"Potter, you cannot win against me!" she cried. He/ncould hear her moving to the right, trying to get a/n/n/n/n/n/nclear shot of him. He backed around the statue away/nfrom her, crouching behind the centaur's legs, his/nhead level with the house-elf's. "I was and am the/nDark Lord's most loyal servant, I learned the Dark/nArts from him, and I know spells of such power that/nyou, pathetic little boy, can never hope to compete — "/n/n"Stupefy\" yelled Harry. He had edged right around to/nwhere the goblin stood beaming up at the now/nheadless wizard and taken aim at her back as she/npeered around the fountain for him. She reacted so/nfast he barely had time to duck./n/n"Protegol"/n/nThe jet of red light, his own Stunning Spell, bounced/nback at him. Harry scrambled back behind the/nfountain, and one of the goblin's ears went flying/nacross the room./n/n"Potter, I am going to give you one chance!" shouted/nBellatrix. "Give me the prophecy — roll it out toward/nme now — and I may spare your life!"/n/n"Well, you're going to have to kill me, because it's/ngone!" Harry roared — and as he shouted it, pain/nseared across his forehead. His scar was on fire/nagain, and he felt a surge of fury that was quite/nunconnected with his own rage. "And he knows!" said/nHarry with a mad laugh to match Bellatrix 's own./n/n"Your dear old mate Voldemort knows it's gone! He's/nnot going to be happy with you, is he?"/n/n"What? What do you mean?" she cried, and for the/nfirst time there was fear in her voice./n/n"The prophecy smashed when I was trying to get/nNeville up the steps! What do you think Voldemort'll/nsay about that, then?"/n/n/n/n/n/nHis scar seared and burned... The pain of it was/nmaking his eyes stream.../n/n/n/n"LIAR!" she shrieked, but he could hear the terror/nbehind the anger now. "YOU'VE GOT IT, POTTER,/nAND YOU WILL GIVE IT TO ME — Accio Prophecy !/nACCIO PROPHECY !"/n/nHarry laughed again because he knew it would/nincense her, the pain building in his head so badly he/nthought his skull might burst. He waved his empty/nhand from behind the one-eared goblin and withdrew/nit quickly as she sent another jet of green light flying/nat him./n/n"Nothing there!" he shouted. "Nothing to summon! It/nsmashed and nobody heard what it said, tell your/nboss that — "/n/n"No!" she screamed. "It isn't true, you're lying —/nMASTER, I TRIED, I TRIED — DO NOT PUNISH ME/n/n/n/n"Don't waste your breath!" yelled Harry, his eyes/nscrewed up against the pain in his scar, now more/nterrible than ever. "He can't hear you from here!"/n/n"Can't I, Potter?" said a high, cold voice./n/nHarry opened his eyes./n/nTall, thin, and black-hooded, his terrible snakelike/nface white and gaunt, his scarlet, slit-pupiled eyes/nstaring ... Lord Voldemort had appeared in the middle/nof the hall, his wand pointing at Harry who stood/nfrozen, quite unable to move./n/n"So you smashed my prophecy?" said Voldemort/nsoftly, staring at Harry with those pitiless red eyes./n/n/n/n/n/n"No, Bella, he is not lying... I see the truth looking at/nme from within his worthless mind... Months of/npreparation, months of effort . . . and my Death Eaters/nhave let Harry Potter thwart me again..."/n/n"Master, I am sorry, I knew not, I was fighting the/nAnimagus Black!" sobbed Bellatrix, flinging herself/ndown at Voldemort's feet as he paced slowly nearer./n"Master, you should know — "/n/n"Be quiet, Bella," said Voldemort dangerously. "I shall/ndeal with you in a moment. Do you think I have/nentered the Ministry of Magic to hear your sniveling/napologies?"/n/n"But Master — he is here — he is below — "/n/nVoldemort paid no attention./n/n"I have nothing more to say to you, Potter," he said/nquietly. "You have irked me too often, for too long./nAVADA KEDAVRAl"/n/nHarry had not even opened his mouth to resist. His/nmind was blank, his wand pointing uselessly at the/nfloor./n/nBut the headless golden statue of the wizard in the/nfountain had sprung alive, leaping from its plinth,/nand landed on the floor with a crash between Harry/nand Voldemort. The spell merely glanced off its chest/nas the statue flung out its arms, protecting Harry./n/n"What — ?" said Voldemort, staring around. And then/nhe breathed, "Dumbledore!"/n/nHarry looked behind him, his heart pounding./nDumbledore was standing in front of the golden gates./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nVoldemort raised his wand and sent another jet of/ngreen light at Dumbledore, who turned and was gone/nin a whirling of his cloak; next second he had/nreappeared behind Voldemort and waved his wand/ntoward the remnants of the fountain; the other/nstatues sprang to life too. The statue of the witch ran/nat Bellatrix, who screamed and sent spells streaming/nuselessly off its chest, before it dived at her, pinning/nher to the floor. Meanwhile, the goblin and the house-/nelf scuttled toward the fireplaces set along the wall,/nand the one-armed centaur galloped at Voldemort,/nwho vanished and reappeared beside the pool. The/nheadless statue thrust Harry backward, away from/nthe fight, as Dumbledore advanced on Voldemort and/nthe golden centaur cantered around them both./n/n"It was foolish to come here tonight, Tom," said/nDumbledore calmly. "The Aurors are on their way — "/n/n"By which time I shall be gone, and you dead!" spat/nVoldemort. He sent another Killing Curse at/nDumbledore but missed, instead hitting the security/nguards desk, which burst into flame./n/nDumbledore flicked his own wand. The force of the/nspell that emanated from it was such that Harry,/nthough shielded by his stone guard, felt his hair/nstand on end as it passed, and this time Voldemort/nwas forced to conjure a shining silver shield out of/nthin air to deflect it. The spell, whatever it was,/ncaused no visible damage to the shield, though a/ndeep, gonglike note reverberated from it, an oddly/nchilling sound.../n/n"You do not seek to kill me, Dumbledore?" called/nVoldemort, his scarlet eyes narrowed over the top of/nthe shield. "Above such brutality, are you?"/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"We both know that there are other ways of/ndestroying a man, Tom," Dumbledore said calmly,/ncontinuing to walk toward Voldemort as though he/nhad not a fear in the world, as though nothing had/nhappened to interrupt his stroll up the hall. "Merely/ntaking your life would not satisfy me, I admit — "/n/n"There is nothing worse than death, Dumbledore!"/nsnarled Voldemort./n/n"You are quite wrong," said Dumbledore, still closing/nin upon Voldemort and speaking as lightly as though/nthey were discussing the matter over drinks. Harry/nfelt scared to see him walking along, undefended,/nshieldless. He wanted to cry out a warning, but his/nheadless guard kept shunting him backward toward/nthe wall, blocking his every attempt to get out from/nbehind it. "Indeed, your failure to understand that/nthere are things much worse than death has always/nbeen your greatest weakness — "/n/nAnother jet of green light flew from behind the silver/nshield. This time it was the one-armed centaur,/ngalloping in front of Dumbledore, that took the blast/nand shattered into a hundred pieces, but before the/nfragments had even hit the floor, Dumbledore had/ndrawn back his wand and waved it as though/nbrandishing a whip. A long thin flame flew from the/ntip; it wrapped itself around Voldemort, shield and all./nFor a moment, it seemed Dumbledore had won, but/nthen the fiery rope became a serpent, which/nrelinquished its hold upon Voldemort at once and/nturned, hissing furiously, to face Dumbledore./n/nVoldemort vanished. The snake reared from the floor,/nready to strike —/n/n/n/nThere was a burst of flame in midair above/nDumbledore just as Voldemort reappeared, standing/n/n/n/n/n/non the plinth in the middle of the pool where so/nrecently the five statues had stood./n/n/n/n"Look outi" Harry yelled./n/nBut even as he shouted, one more jet of green light/nhad flown at Dumbledore from Voldemort's wand and/nthe snake had struck —/n/nFawkes swooped down in front of Dumbledore,/nopened his beak wide, and swallowed the jet of green/nlight whole. He burst into flame and fell to the floor,/nsmall, wrinkled, and flightless. At the same moment,/nDumbledore brandished his wand in one, long, fluid/nmovement — the snake, which had been an instant/nfrom sinking its fangs into him, flew high into the air/nand vanished in a wisp of dark smoke; the water in/nthe pool rose up and covered Voldemort like a cocoon/nof molten glass —/n/nFor a few seconds Voldemort was visible only as a/ndark, rippling, faceless figure, shimmering and/nindistinct upon the plinth, clearly struggling to throw/noff the suffocating mass —/n/nThen he was gone, and the water fell with a crash/nback into its pool, slopping wildly over the sides,/ndrenching the polished floor./n/n"MASTER!" screamed Bellatrix./n/nSure it was over, sure Voldemort had decided to flee,/nHarry made to run out from behind his statue guard,/nbut Dumbledore bellowed, "Stay where you are,/n/nHarry!"/n/nFor the first time, Dumbledore sounded frightened./nHarry could not see why. The hall was quite empty/nbut for themselves, the sobbing Bellatrix still trapped/n/n/n/n/n/nunder her statue, and the tiny baby Fawkes croaking/nfeebly on the floor —/n/nAnd then Harry's scar burst open. He knew he was/ndead: it was pain beyond imagining, pain past/nendurance —/n/nHe was gone from the hall, he was locked in the coils/nof a creature with red eyes, so tightly bound that/nHarry did not know where his body ended and the/ncreature's began. They were fused together, bound by/npain, and there was no escape —/n/nAnd when the creature spoke, it used Harry's mouth,/nso that in his agony he felt his jaw move.../n/n" Kill me now, Dumbledore..."/n/nBlinded and dying, every part of him screaming for/nrelease, Harry felt the creature use him again.../n/n"If death is nothing, Dumbledore, kill the boy..."/n/nLet the pain stop, thought Harry. Let him kill us... End/nit, Dumbledore... Death is nothing compared to this.../n/nAnd I'll see Sirius again.../n/nAnd as Harry's heart filled with emotion, the/ncreature's coils loosened, the pain was gone, Harry/nwas lying facedown on the floor, his glasses gone,/nshivering as though he lay upon ice, not wood.../n/nAnd there were voices echoing through the hall, more/nvoices than there should have been: Harry opened his/neyes, saw his glasses lying at the heel of the headless/nstatue that had been guarding him, but which now/nlay flat on its back, cracked and immobile. He put/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nthem on and raised his head an inch to find/nDumbledore's crooked nose inches from his own./n/n/n/n"Are you all right, Harry?"/n/n"Yes," said Harry, shaking so violently he could not/nhold his head up properly. "Yeah, I'm — where's/nVoldemort, where — who are all these — what's — "/n/nThe Atrium was full of people. The floor was reflecting/nemerald-green flames that had burst into life in all/nthe fireplaces along one wall, and a stream of witches/nand wizards was emerging from them. As Dumbledore/npulled him back to his feet, Harry saw the tiny gold/nstatues of the house-elf and the goblin leading a/nstunned-looking Cornelius Fudge forward./n/n"He was there!" shouted a scarlet-robed man with a/nponytail, who was pointing at a pile of golden rubble/non the other side of the hall, where Bellatrix had lain/ntrapped moments before. "I saw him, Mr. Fudge, I/nswear, it was You-Know-Who, he grabbed a woman/nand Disapparated!"/n/n"I know, Williamson, I know, I saw him too!" gibbered/nFudge, who was wearing pajamas under his/npinstriped cloak and was gasping as though he had/njust run miles. "Merlin's beard — here — here! — in/nthe Ministry of Magic! — great heavens above — it/ndoesn't seem possible — my word — how can this/nbe?"/n/n"If you proceed downstairs into the Department of/nMysteries, Cornelius," said Dumbledore, apparently/nsatisfied that Harry was all right, and walking forward/nso that the newcomers realized he was there for the/nfirst time (a few of them raised their wands, others/nsimply looked amazed; the statues of the elf and/ngoblin applauded and Fudge jumped so much that/n/n/n/n/nhis slipper-clad feet left the floor), "you will find/nseveral escaped Death Eaters contained in the Death/nChamber, bound by an Anti-Disapparation Jinx and/nawaiting your decision as to what to do with them."/n/n"Dumbledore!" gasped Fudge, apparently beside/nhimself with amazement. "You — here — I — I — "/n/nHe looked wildly around at the Aurors he had brought/nwith him, and it could not have been clearer that he/nwas in half a mind to cry, "Seize him!"/n/n"Cornelius, I am ready to fight your men — and win/nagain!" said Dumbledore in a thunderous voice. "But/na few minutes ago you saw proof, with your own eyes,/nthat I have been telling you the truth for a year. Lord/nVoldemort has returned, you have been chasing the/nwrong men for twelve months, and it is time you/nlistened to sense!"/n/n"I — don't — well — " blustered Fudge, looking around/nas though hoping somebody was going to tell him/nwhat to do. When nobody did, he said, "Very well —/nDawlish! Williamson! Go down to the Department of/nMysteries and see ... Dumbledore, you — you will/nneed to tell me exactly — the Fountain of Magical/nBrethren — what happened?" he added in a kind of/nwhimper, staring around at the floor, where the/nremains of the statues of the witch, wizard, and/ncentaur now lay scattered./n/n"We can discuss that after I have sent Harry back to/nHogwarts," said Dumbledore./n/n"Harry — Harry Potter?"/n/nFudge spun around and stared at Harry, who was/nstill standing against the wall beside the fallen statue/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nthat had been guarding him during Dumbledore and/nVoldemort's duel./n/n"He-here?" said Fudge. "Why — what's all this/nabout?"/n/n"I shall explain everything," repeated Dumbledore,/n"when Harry is back at school."/n/nHe walked away from the pool to the place where the/ngolden wizard's head lay on the floor. He pointed his/nwand at it and muttered, "Portus." The head glowed/nblue and trembled noisily against the wooden floor for/na few seconds, then became still once more./n/n"Now see here, Dumbledore!" said Fudge, as/nDumbledore picked up the head and walked back to/nHarry carrying it. "You haven't got authorization for/nthat Portkey! You can't do things like that right in/nfront of the Minister of Magic, you — you — "/n/nHis voice faltered as Dumbledore surveyed him/nmagisterially over his half-moon spectacles./n/n"You will give the order to remove Dolores Umbridge/nfrom Hogwarts," said Dumbledore. "You will tell your/nAurors to stop searching for my Care of Magical/nCreatures teacher so that he can return to work. I will/ngive you ..." Dumbledore pulled a watch with twelve/nhands from his pocket and glanced at it, "half an/nhour of my time tonight, in which I think we shall be/nmore than able to cover the important points of what/nhas happened here. After that, I shall need to return/nto my school. If you need more help from me you are,/nof course, more than welcome to contact me at/nHogwarts. Letters addressed to the headmaster will/nfind me."/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nFudge goggled worse than ever. His mouth was open/nand his round face grew pinker under his rumpled/ngray hair./n/n"I — you — "/n/nDumbledore turned his back on him./n/n"Take this Portkey, Harry."/n/nHe held out the golden head of the statue, and Harry/nplaced his hand upon it, past caring what he did next/nor where he went./n/n"I shall see you in half an hour," said Dumbledore/nquietly. "One ... two ... three ..."/n/nHarry felt the familiar sensation of a hook being/njerked behind his navel. The polished wooden floor/nwas gone from beneath his feet; the Atrium, Fudge,/nand Dumbledore had all disappeared, and he was/nflying forward in a whirlwind of color and sound. . ./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n

title: The Lost Prophecy
text: /nHarry's feet hit solid ground again; his knees buckled/na little and the golden wizard's head fell with a/nresounding clunk to the floor. He looked around and/nsaw that he had arrived in Dumbledore's office./n/nEverything seemed to have repaired itself during the/nheadmaster's absence. The delicate silver instruments/nstood again upon the spindle-legged tables, puffing/nand whirring serenely. The portraits of the/nheadmasters and headmistresses were snoozing in/ntheir frames, heads lolling back in armchairs or/nagainst the edge of their pictures. Harry looked/nthrough the window. There was a cool line of pale/ngreen along the horizon: Dawn was approaching./n/nThe silence and the stillness, broken only by the/noccasional grunt or snuffle of a sleeping portrait, was/nunbearable to him. If his surroundings could have/nreflected the feelings inside him, the pictures would/nhave been screaming in pain. He walked around the/nquiet, beautiful office, breathing quickly, trying not to/nthink. But he had to think... There was no escape.../n/n/n/nIt was his fault Sirius had died; it was all his fault. If/nhe, Harry, had not been stupid enough to fall for/nVoldemort's trick, if he had not been so convinced/nthat what he had seen in his dream was real, if he/nhad only opened his mind to the possibility that/nVoldemort was, as Hermione had said, banking on/nHarry's love of playing the hero . . ./n/nIt was unbearable, he would not think about it, he/ncould not stand it... There was a terrible hollow inside/nhim he did not want to feel or examine, a dark hole/nwhere Sirius had been, where Sirius had vanished./n/nHe did not want to have to be alone with that great,/nsilent space, he could not stand it —/n/nA picture behind him gave a particularly loud/ngrunting snore, and a cool voice said, "Ah ... Harry/nPotter ..."/n/nPhineas Nigellus gave a long yawn, stretching his/narms as he watched Harry with shrewd, narrow eyes./n/n"And what brings you here in the early hours of the/nmorning?" said Phineas. "This office is supposed to be/nbarred to all but the rightful headmaster. Or has/nDumbledore sent you here? Oh, don't tell me ..." He/ngave another shuddering yawn. "Another message for/nmy worthless great-great-grandson?"/n/nHarry could not speak. Phineas Nigellus did not know/nthat Sirius was dead, but Harry could not tell him. To/nsay it aloud would be to make it final, absolute,/nirretrievable./n/nA few more of the portraits had stirred now. Terror of/nbeing interrogated made Harry stride across the room/nand seize the doorknob./n/n/n/nIt would not turn. He was shut in./n/n/n/n/n/n"I hope this means," said the corpulent, red-nosed/nwizard who hung on the wall behind Dumbledore's/ndesk, "that Dumbledore will soon be back with us?"/n/nHarry turned. The wizard was eyeing him with great/ninterest. Harry nodded. He tugged again on the/ndoorknob behind his back, but it remained/nimmovable./n/n"Oh good," said the wizard. "It has been very dull/nwithout him, very dull indeed."/n/nHe settled himself on the thronelike chair on which he/nhad been painted and smiled benignly upon Harry./n/n"Dumbledore thinks very highly of you, as I am sure/nyou know," he said comfortably. "Oh yes. Holds you/nin great esteem."/n/nThe guilt filling the whole of Harry's chest like some/nmonstrous, weighty parasite now writhed and/nsquirmed. Harry could not stand this, he could not/nstand being Harry anymore... He had never felt more/ntrapped inside his own head and body, never wished/nso intensely that he could be somebody — anybody —/nelse.../n/nThe empty fireplace burst into emerald-green flame,/nmaking Harry leap away from the door, staring at the/nman spinning inside the grate. As Dumbledore's tall/nform unfolded itself from the fire, the wizards and/nwitches on the surrounding walls jerked awake. Many/nof them gave cries of welcome./n/n"Thank you," said Dumbledore softly./n/nHe did not look at Harry at first, but walked over to/nthe perch beside the door and withdrew, from an/ninside pocket of his robes, the tiny, ugly, featherless/n/n/n/n/n/nFawkes, whom he placed gently on the tray of soft/nashes beneath the golden post where the full-grown/nFawkes usually stood./n/n"Well, Harry," said Dumbledore, finally turning away/nfrom the baby bird, "you will be pleased to hear that/nnone of your fellow students are going to suffer/nlasting damage from the night's events."/n/nHarry tried to say "Good," but no sound came out. It/nseemed to him that Dumbledore was reminding him/nof the amount of damage he had caused by his/nactions tonight, and although Dumbledore was for/nonce looking at him directly, and though his/nexpression was kindly rather than accusatory, Harry/ncould not bear to meet his eyes./n/n"Madam Pomfrey is patching everybody up now," said/nDumbledore. "Nymphadora Tonks may need to spend/na little time in St. Mungo's, but it seems that she will/nmake a full recovery."/n/nHarry contented himself with nodding at the carpet,/nwhich was growing lighter as the sky outside grew/npaler. He was sure that all the portraits around the/nroom were listening eagerly to every word Dumbledore/nspoke, wondering where Dumbledore and Harry had/nbeen and why there had been injuries./n/n"I know how you are feeling, Harry," said Dumbledore/nvery quietly./n/n"No, you don't," said Harry, and his voice was/nsuddenly loud and strong. And yet, knowing/nhow important it was that my plan should succeed, I/n/n/n/n/n/ntold myself that I would not permit this flaw to min it./n/nI alone could prevent this, so I alone must be strong./nAnd here was my first test, as you lay in the hospital/nwing, weak from your struggle with Voldemort."/n/n"I don't understand what you're saying," said Harry./n/n"Don't you remember asking me, as you lay in the/nhospital wing, why Voldemort had tried to kill you/nwhen you were a baby?"/n/nHarry nodded./n/n"Ought I to have told you then?"/n/nHarry stared into the blue eyes and said nothing, but/nhis heart was racing again./n/n"You do not see the flaw in the plan yet? No .../nperhaps not. Well, as you know, I decided not to/nanswer you. Eleven, I told myself, was much too/nyoung to know. I had never intended to tell you when/nyou were eleven. The knowledge would be too much at/nsuch a young age./n/n"I should have recognized the danger signs then. I/nshould have asked myself why I did not feel more/ndisturbed that you had already asked me the question/nto which I knew, one day, I must give a terrible/nanswer. I should have recognized that I was too happy/nto think that I did not have to do it on that particular/nday. . . You were too young, much too young./n/n"And so we entered your second year at Hogwarts./n/nAnd once again you met challenges even grown/nwizards have never faced. Once again you acquitted/nyourself beyond my wildest dreams. You did not ask/nme again, however, why Voldemort had left that mark/nupon you. We discussed your scar, oh yes... We came/n/n/n/n/nvery, very close to the subject. Why did I not tell you/neverything?/n/n"Well, it seemed to me that twelve was, after all,/nhardly better than eleven to receive such information./n/nI allowed you to leave my presence, bloodstained,/nexhausted but exhilarated, and if I felt a twinge of/nunease that I ought, perhaps, have told you then, it/nwas swiftly silenced. You were still so young, you see,/nand I could not find it in me to spoil that night of/ntriumph.../n/n"Do you see, Harry? Do you see the flaw in my/nbrilliant plan now? I had fallen into the trap I had/nforeseen, that I had told myself I could avoid, that I/nmust avoid."/n/n"I don't — "/n/n"I cared about you too much," said Dumbledore/nsimply. "I cared more for your happiness than your/nknowing the truth, more for your peace of mind than/nmy plan, more for your life than the lives that might/nbe lost if the plan failed. In other words, I acted/nexactly as Voldemort expects we fools who love to act./n/n"Is there a defense? I defy anyone who has watched/nyou as I have — and I have watched you more closely/nthan you can have imagined — not to want to save/nyou more pain than you had already suffered. What/ndid I care if numbers of nameless and faceless people/nand creatures were slaughtered in the vague future, if/nin the here and now you were alive, and well, and/nhappy? I never dreamed that I would have such a/nperson on my hands./n/n"We entered your third year. I watched from afar as/nyou struggled to repel dementors, as you found/nSirius, learned what he was and rescued him. Was I/n/n/n/n/n/nto tell you then, at the moment when you had/ntriumphantly snatched your godfather from the jaws/nof the Ministry? But now, at the age of thirteen, my/nexcuses were running out. Young you might be, but/nyou had proved you were exceptional. My conscience/nwas uneasy, Harry. I knew the time must come/nsoon.../n/n"But you came out of the maze last year, having/nwatched Cedric Diggory die, having escaped death so/nnarrowly yourself . . . and I did not tell you, though I/nknew, now Voldemort had returned, I must do it/nsoon. And now, tonight, I know you have long been/nready for the knowledge I have kept from you for so/nlong, because you have proved that I should have/nplaced the burden upon you before this. My only/ndefense is this: I have watched you struggling under/nmore burdens than any student who has ever passed/nthrough this school, and I could not bring myself to/nadd another — the greatest one of all."/n/nHarry waited, but Dumbledore did not speak./n/n"I still don't understand."/n/n"Voldemort tried to kill you when you were a child/nbecause of a prophecy made shortly before your birth./nHe knew the prophecy had been made, though he did/nnot know its full contents. He set out to kill you when/nyou were still a baby, believing he was fulfilling the/nterms of the prophecy. He discovered, to his cost, that/nhe was mistaken, when the curse intended to kill you/nbackfired. And so, since his return to his body, and/nparticularly since your extraordinary escape from him/nlast year, he has been determined to hear that/nprophecy in its entirety. This is the weapon he has/nbeen seeking so assiduously since his return: the/nknowledge of how to destroy you."/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nThe sun had risen fully now. Dumbledore's office was/nbathed in it. The glass case in which the sword of/nGodric Gryffindor resided gleamed white and opaque,/nthe fragments of the instruments Harry had thrown to/nthe floor glistened like raindrops, and behind him, the/nbaby Fawkes made soft chirruping noises in his nest/nof ashes./n/n"The prophecy's smashed," Harry said blankly. "I was/npulling Neville up those benches in the — the room/nwhere the archway was, and I ripped his robes and it/nfell..."/n/n"The thing that smashed was merely the record of the/nprophecy kept by the Department of Mysteries. But/nthe prophecy was made to somebody, and that person/nhas the means of recalling it perfectly."/n/n"Who heard it?" asked Harry, though he thought he/nknew the answer already./n/n"I did," said Dumbledore. "On a cold, wet night/nsixteen years ago, in a room above the bar at the/nHog's Head Inn. I had gone there to see an applicant/nfor the post of Divination teacher, though it was/nagainst my inclination to allow the subject of/nDivination to continue at all. The applicant, however,/nwas the great-great-granddaughter of a very famous,/nvery gifted Seer, and I thought it common politeness/nto meet her. I was disappointed. It seemed to me that/nshe had not a trace of the gift herself. I told her,/ncourteously I hope, that I did not think she would be/nsuitable for the post. I turned to leave."/n/nDumbledore got to his feet and walked past Harry to/nthe black cabinet that stood beside Fawkes's perch./n/nHe bent down, slid back a catch, and took from inside/nit the shallow stone basin, carved with runes around/nthe edges, in which Harry had seen his father/n/n/n/n/ntormenting Snape. Dumbledore walked back to the/ndesk, placed the Pensieve upon it, and raised his/nwand to his own temple. From it, he withdrew silvery,/ngossamer-fine strands of thought clinging to the/nwand, and deposited them in the basin. He sat back/ndown behind his desk and watched his thoughts swirl/nand drift inside the Pensieve for a moment. Then,/nwith a sigh, he raised his wand and prodded the/nsilvery substance with its tip./n/nA figure rose out of it, draped in shawls, her eyes/nmagnified to enormous size behind her glasses, and/nshe revolved slowly, her feet in the basin. But when/nSibyll Trelawney spoke, it was not in her usual/nethereal, mystic voice, but in the harsh, hoarse tones/nHarry had heard her use once before./n/n"The one with the power to vanquish the Dark Lord/napproaches... Born to those who have thrice defied/nhim, born as the seventh month dies . . . and the Dark/nLord will mark him as his equal, but he will have/npower the Dark Lord knows not ... and either must die/nat the hand of the other for neither can live while the/nother survives... The one with the power to vanquish/nthe Dark Lord will be born as the seventh month/ndies..."/n/nThe slowly revolving Professor Trelawney sank back/ninto the silver mass below and vanished./n/nThe silence within the office was absolute. Neither/nDumbledore nor Harry nor any of the portraits made/na sound. Even Fawkes had fallen silent./n/n"Professor Dumbledore?" Harry said very quietly, for/nDumbledore, still staring at the Pensieve, seemed/ncompletely lost in thought. "It ... did that mean .../nWhat did that mean?"/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"It meant," said Dumbledore, "that the person who/nhas the only chance of conquering Lord Voldemort for/ngood was born at the end of July, nearly sixteen years/nago. This boy would be born to parents who had/nalready defied Voldemort three times."/n/nHarry felt as though something was closing in upon/nhim. His breathing seemed difficult again./n/n"It means — me?"/n/nDumbledore surveyed him for a moment through his/nglasses./n/n"The odd thing is, Harry," he said softly, "that it may/nnot have meant you at all. Sibyll's prophecy could/nhave applied to two wizard boys, both born at the end/nof July that year, both of whom had parents in the/nOrder of the Phoenix, both sets of parents having/nnarrowly escaped Voldemort three times. One, of/ncourse, was you. The other was Neville Longbottom."/n/n"But then . . . but then, why was it my name on the/nprophecy and not Neville's?"/n/n"The official record was relabeled after Voldemort 's/nattack on you as a child," said Dumbledore. "It/nseemed plain to the keeper of the Hall of Prophecy/nthat Voldemort could only have tried to kill you/nbecause he knew you to be the one to whom Sibyll/nwas referring."/n/n"Then — it might not be me?" said Harry./n/n"I am afraid," said Dumbledore slowly, looking as/nthough every word cost him a great effort, "that there/nis no doubt that it is you."/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"But you said — Neville was born at the end of July/ntoo — and his mum and dad — "/n/n"You are forgetting the next part of the prophecy, the/nfinal identifying feature of the boy who could/nvanquish Voldemort... Voldemort himself would 'mark/nhim as his equal.' And so he did, Harry. He chose/nyou, not Neville. He gave you the scar that has proved/nboth blessing and curse."/n/n"But he might have chosen wrong!" said Harry. "He/nmight have marked the wrong person!"/n/n"He chose the boy he thought most likely to be a/ndanger to him," said Dumbledore. "And notice this,/nHarry. He chose, not the pureblood (which, according/nto his creed, is the only kind of wizard worth being or/nknowing), but the half-blood, like himself. He saw/nhimself in you before he had ever seen you, and in/nmarking you with that scar, he did not kill you, as he/nintended, but gave you powers, and a future, which/nhave fitted you to escape him not once, but four times/nso far — something that neither your parents, nor/nNeville's parents, ever achieved."/n/n"Why did he do it, then?" said Harry, who felt numb/nand cold. "Why did he try and kill me as a baby? He/nshould have waited to see whether Neville or I looked/nmore dangerous when we were older and tried to kill/nwhoever it was then — "/n/n"That might, indeed, have been the more practical/ncourse," said Dumbledore, "except that Voldemort's/ninformation about the prophecy was incomplete. The/nHog's Head Inn, which Sibyll chose for its cheapness,/nhas long attracted, shall we say, a more interesting/nclientele than the Three Broomsticks. As you and/nyour friends found out to your cost, and I to mine/nthat night, it is a place where it is never safe to/n/n/n/n/nassume you are not being overheard. Of course, I had/nnot dreamed, when I set out to meet Sibyll Trelawney,/nthat I would hear anything worth overhearing. My —/nour — one stroke of good fortune was that the/neavesdropper was detected only a short way into the/nprophecy and thrown from the building."/n/n"So he only heard ... ?"/n/n"He heard only the first part, the part foretelling the/nbirth of a boy in July to parents who had thrice defied/nVoldemort. Consequently, he could not warn his/nmaster that to attack you would be to risk/ntransferring power to you — again marking you as his/nequal. So Voldemort never knew that there might be/ndanger in attacking you, that it might be wise to wait/nor to learn more. He did not know that you would/nhave 'power the Dark Lord knows not' — "/n/n"But I don't!" said Harry in a strangled voice. "I/nhaven't any powers he hasn't got, I couldn't fight the/nway he did tonight, I can't possess people or — or kill/nthem — "/n/n"There is a room in the Department of Mysteries,"/ninterrupted Dumbledore, "that is kept locked at all/ntimes. It contains a force that is at once more/nwonderful and more terrible than death, than human/nintelligence, than forces of nature. It is also, perhaps,/nthe most mysterious of the many subjects for study/nthat reside there. It is the power held within that/nroom that you possess in such quantities and which/nVoldemort has not at all. That power took you to save/nSirius tonight. That power also saved you from/npossession by Voldemort, because he could not bear/nto reside in a body so full of the force he detests. In/nthe end, it mattered not that you could not close your/nmind. It was your heart that saved you."/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nHarry closed his eyes. If he had not gone to save/nSirius, Sirius would not have died... More to stave off/nthe moment when he would have to think of Sirius/nagain, Harry asked, without caring much about the/nanswer, "The end of the prophecy ... it was something/nabout ... 'neither can live...' "/n/n" '... while the other survives,' " said Dumbledore./n/n"So," said Harry, dredging up the words from what felt/nlike a deep well of despair inside him, "so does that/nmean that . . . that one of us has got to kill the other/none ... in the end?"/n/n"Yes," said Dumbledore./n/nFor a long time, neither of them spoke. Somewhere/nfar beyond the office walls, Harry could hear the/nsound of voices, students heading down to the Great/nHall for an early breakfast, perhaps. It seemed/nimpossible that there could be people in the world/nwho still desired food, who laughed, who neither knew/nnor cared that Sirius Black was gone forever. Sirius/nseemed a million miles away already, even if a part of/nHarry still believed that if he had only pulled back/nthat veil, he would have found Sirius looking back at/nhim, greeting him, perhaps, with his laugh like a/nbark. . ./n/n"I feel I owe you another explanation, Harry," said/nDumbledore hesitantly. "You may, perhaps, have/nwondered why I never chose you as a prefect? I must/nconfess ... that I rather thought ... you had enough/nresponsibility to be going on with."/n/nHarry looked up at him and saw a tear trickling down/nDumbledore 's face into his long silver beard./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n

title: The Second War Begins
text: /nHE-WHO-MUST-NOT-BE-NAMED RETURNS/n/nIn a brief statement Friday night, Minister of Magic/nCornelius Fudge confirmed that He-Who-Must-Not-Be/nNamed has returned to this country and is active/nonce more./n/n"It is with great regret that I must confirm that the/nwizard styling himself Lord — well, you know who I/nmean — is alive and among us again," said Fudge,/nlooking tired and flustered as he addressed reporters./n"It is with almost equal regret that we report the mass/nrevolt of the dementors of Azkaban, who have shown/nthemselves averse to continuing in the Ministry's/nemploy. We believe that the dementors are currently/ntaking direction from Lord — Thingy./n/n"We urge the magical population to remain vigilant The/nMinistry is currently publishing guides to elementary/nhome and personal defense that will be delivered free/nto all Wizarding homes within the coming month. "/n/n/n/n/n/n/nThe Minister's statement was met with dismay and/nalarm from the Wizarding community, which as/nrecently as last Wednesday was receiving Ministry/nassurances that there was "no truth whatsoever in/nthese persistent rumors that You-Know-Who is/noperating amongst us once more."/n/nDetails of the events that led to the Ministry/nturnaround are still hazy, though it is believed that/nHe-Who-Must-Not-Be-Named and a select band of/nfollowers (known as Death Eaters) gained entry to the/nMinistry of Magic itself on Thursday evening./n/nAlbus Dumbledore, newly reinstated headmaster of/nHogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry,/nreinstated member of the International Confederation/nof Wizards, and reinstated Chief Warlock of the/nWizengamot, was unavailable for comment last night./nHe has insisted for a year that You-Know-Who was/nnot dead, as was widely hoped and believed, but/nrecruiting followers once more for a fresh attempt to/nseize power. Meanwhile the Boy Who Lived —/n/n"There you are, Harry, I knew they'd drag you into it/nsomehow," said Hermione, looking over the top of the/npaper at him./n/nThey were in the hospital wing. Harry was sitting on/nthe end of Ron's bed and they were both listening to/nHermione read the front page of the Sunday Prophet./nGinny, whose ankle had been mended in a trice by/nMadam Pomfrey, was curled up at the foot of/nHermione's bed; Neville, whose nose had likewise/nbeen returned to its normal size and shape, was in a/nchair between the two beds; and Luna, who had/ndropped in to visit clutching the latest edition of The/nQuibbler, was reading the magazine upside down and/napparently not taking in a word Hermione was saying./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"He's 'the Boy Who Lived' again now, though, isn't/nhe?" said Ron darkly. "Not such a show-off maniac/nanymore, eh?"/n/nHe helped himself to a handful of Chocolate Frogs/nfrom the immense pile on his bedside cabinet, threw a/nfew to Harry, Ginny, and Neville, and ripped off the/nwrapper of his own with his teeth. There were still/ndeep welts on his forearms where the brain's tentacles/nhad wrapped around him. According to Madam/nPomfrey, thoughts could leave deeper scarring than/nalmost anything else, though since she had started/napplying copious amounts of Dr. Ubbly's Oblivious/nUnction, there seemed to be some improvement./n/n"Yes, they're very complimentary about you now,/nHarry," said Hermione, now scanning down the/narticle. " 'A lone voice of truth ... perceived as/nunbalanced, yet never wavered in his story . . . forced to/nbear ridicule and slander ...' Hmmm," said Hermione,/nfrowning, "I notice they don't mention the fact that it/nwas them doing all the ridiculing and slandering,/nthough..."/n/nShe winced slightly and put a hand to her ribs. The/ncurse Dolohov had used on her, though less effective/nthan it would have been had he been able to say the/nincantation aloud, had nevertheless caused, in/nMadam Pomfrey's words, "quite enough damage to be/ngoing on with." Hermione was having to take ten/ndifferent types of potion every day and although she/nwas improving greatly, was already bored with the/nhospital wing./n/n" 'You-Know- Who's Last Attempt to Take Over, pages/ntwo to four, What the Ministry Should Have Told Us,/npage five, Why Nobody Listened to Albus Dumbledore,/npages six to eight, Exclusive Interview with Harry/nPotter, page nine ...' Well," said Hermione, folding up/n/n/n/n/nthe newspaper and throwing it aside, "it's certainly/ngiven them lots to write about. And that interview/nwith Harry isn't exclusive, it's the one that was in The/nQuibbler months ago..."/n/n"Daddy sold it to them," said Luna vaguely, turning a/npage of The Quibbler. "He got a very good price for it/ntoo, so we're going to go on an expedition to Sweden/nthis summer and see if we can catch a Crumple-/nHorned Snorkack."/n/nHermione seemed to struggle with herself for a/nmoment, then said, "That sounds lovely."/n/nGinny caught Harry's eye and looked away quickly,/ngrinning./n/n"So anyway," said Hermione, sitting up a little/nstraighter and wincing again, "what's going on in/nschool?"/n/n"Well, Flitwick's got rid of Fred and George's swamp,"/nsaid Ginny. "He did it in about three seconds. But he/nleft a tiny patch under the window and he's roped it/noff—"/n/n"Why?" said Hermione, looking startled./n/n"Oh, he just says it was a really good bit of magic,"/nsaid Ginny, shrugging./n/n"I think he left it as a monument to Fred and George,"/nsaid Ron through a mouthful of chocolate. "They sent/nme all these, you know," he told Harry, pointing at/nthe small mountain of Frogs beside him. "Must be/ndoing all right out of that joke shop, eh?"/n/nHermione looked rather disapproving and asked, "So/nhas all the trouble stopped now Dumbledore's back?"/n/n/n/n/n/n"Yes," said Neville, "everything's settled right back/ndown again."/n/n"I s'pose Filch is happy, is he?" asked Ron, propping a/nChocolate Frog card featuring Dumbledore against his/nwater jug./n/n"Not at all," said Ginny. "He's really, really miserable,/nactually..." She lowered her voice to a whisper. "He/nkeeps saying Umbridge was the best thing that ever/nhappened to Hogwarts..."/n/nAll six of them looked around. Professor Umbridge/nwas lying in a bed opposite them, gazing up at the/nceiling. Dumbledore had strode alone into the forest/nto rescue her from the centaurs. How he had done it/n— how he had emerged from the trees supporting/nProfessor Umbridge without so much as a scratch on/nhim — nobody knew, and Umbridge was certainly not/ntelling. Since she had returned to the castle she had/nnot, as far as any of them knew, uttered a single/nword. Nobody really knew what was wrong with her/neither. Her usually neat mousy hair was very untidy/nand there were bits of twig and leaf in it, but/notherwise she seemed to be quite unscathed./n/n"Madam Pomfrey says she's just in shock," whispered/nHermione./n/n"Sulking, more like," said Ginny/n/n"Yeah, she shows signs of life if you do this," said/nRon, and with his tongue he made soft clip-clopping/nnoises. Umbridge sat bolt upright, looking wildly/naround./n/n"Anything wrong, Professor?" called Madam Pomfrey,/npoking her head around her office door./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"No ... no ..." said Umbridge, sinking back into her/npillows, "no, I must have been dreaming..."/n/nHermione and Ginny muffled their laughter in the/nbedclothes./n/n"Speaking of centaurs," said Hermione, when she had/nrecovered a little, "who's Divination teacher now? Is/nFirenze staying?"/n/n"He's got to," said Harry, "the other centaurs won't/ntake him back, will they?"/n/n"It looks like he and Trelawney are both going to/nteach," said Ginny./n/n"Bet Dumbledore wishes he could've got rid of/nTrelawney for good," said Ron, now munching on his/nfourteenth Frog. "Mind you, the whole subjects/nuseless if you ask me, Firenze isn't a lot better..."/n/n"How can you say that?" Hermione demanded. "After/nwe've just found out that there are real prophecies?"/n/nHarry's heart began to race. He had not told Ron,/nHermione, or anyone else what the prophecy had/ncontained. Neville had told them it had smashed while/nHarry was pulling him up the steps in the Death/nRoom, and Harry had not yet corrected this/nimpression. He was not ready to see their expressions/nwhen he told them that he must be either murderer/nor victim, there was no other way.../n/n"It is a pity it broke," said Hermione quietly, shaking/nher head./n/n"Yeah, it is," said Ron. "Still, at least You-Know-Who/nnever found out what was in it either — where are/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nyou going?" he added, looking both surprised and/ndisappointed as Harry stood up./n/n"Er — Hagrid's," said Harry. "You know, he just got/nback and I promised I'd go down and see him and tell/nhim how you two are..."/n/n"Oh all right then," said Ron grumpily, looking out of/nthe dormitory window at the patch of bright blue sky/nbeyond. "Wish we could come ..."/n/n"Say hello to him for us!" called Hermione, as Harry/nproceeded down the ward. "And ask him what's/nhappening about ... about his little friend!"/n/nHarry gave a wave of his hand to show he had heard/nand understood as he left the dormitory./n/nThe castle seemed very quiet even for a Sunday./nEverybody was clearly out in the sunny grounds,/nenjoying the end of their exams and the prospect of a/nlast few days of term unhampered by studying or/nhomework. Harry walked slowly along the deserted/ncorridor, peering out of windows as he went. He could/nsee people messing around in the air over the/nQuidditch pitch and a couple of students swimming/nin the lake, accompanied by the giant squid./n/nHe was finding it hard at the moment to decide/nwhether he wanted to be with people or not./n/nWhenever he was in company he wanted to get away,/nand whenever he was alone he wanted company. He/nthought he might really go and visit Hagrid, though;/nhe had not talked to him properly since he had/nreturned.../n/nHarry had just descended the last marble step into/nthe entrance hall when Malfoy, Crabbe, and Goyle/nemerged from a door on the right that Harry knew led/n/n/n/n/n/ndown to the Slytherin common room. Harry stopped/ndead; so did Malfoy and the others. For a few/nmoments, the only sounds were the shouts, laughter,/nand splashes drifting into the hall from the grounds/nthrough the open front doors./n/nMalfoy glanced around. Harry knew he was checking/nfor signs of teachers. Then he looked back at Harry/nand said in a low voice, "You're dead, Potter."/n/nHarry raised his eyebrows. "Funny," he said, "you'd/nthink I'd have stopped walking around..."/n/nMalfoy looked angrier than Harry had ever seen him./nHe felt a kind of detached satisfaction at the sight of/nhis pale, pointed face contorted with rage./n/n"You're going to pay," said Malfoy in a voice barely/nlouder than a whisper. "I'm going to make you pay for/nwhat you've done to my father..."/n/n"Well, I'm terrified now," said Harry sarcastically. "I/ns'pose Lord Voldemort's just a warm-up act compared/nto you three — what's the matter?" he said, for/nMalfoy, Crabbe, and Goyle had all looked stricken at/nthe sound of the name. "He's your dad's mate, isn't/nhe? Not scared of him, are you?"/n/n"You think you're such a big man, Potter," said/nMalfoy, advancing now, Crabbe and Goyle flanking/nhim. "You wait. I'll have you. You can't land my father/nin prison — "/n/n"I thought I just had," said Harry./n/n"The dementors have left Azkaban," said Malfoy/nquietly. "Dad and the others'll be out in no time..."/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"Yeah, I expect they will," said Harry. "Still, at least/neveryone knows what scumbags they are now — "/n/nMalfoy's hand flew toward his wand, but Harry was/ntoo quick for him. He had drawn his own wand before/nMalfoy's fingers had even entered the pocket of his/nrobes./n/n"Potter!"/n/nThe voice rang across the entrance hall; Snape had/nemerged from the staircase leading down to his office,/nand at the sight of him Harry felt a great rush of/nhatred beyond anything he felt toward Malfoy . . ./nWhatever Dumbledore said, he would never forgive/nSnape ... never .../n/n"What are you doing, Potter?" said Snape coldly as/never, as he strode over to the four of them./n/n"I'm trying to decide what curse to use on Malfoy, sir,"/nsaid Harry fiercely./n/nSnape stared at him./n/n"Put that wand away at once," he said curtly. "Ten/npoints from Gryff — "/n/nSnape looked toward the giant hourglasses on the/nwalls and gave a sneering smile./n/n"Ah. At the front of the/ngroup stood Mr. and Mrs. Weasley, dressed in their/nMuggle best, and Fred and George, who were both/nwearing brand-new jackets in some lurid green, scaly/nmaterial./n/n"Ron, Ginny!" called Mrs. Weasley, hurrying forward/nand hugging her children tightly. "Oh, and Harry dear/n— how are you?"/n/n"Fine," lied Harry, as she pulled him into a tight/nembrace. Over her shoulder he saw Ron goggling at/nthe twins' new clothes./n/n"What are they supposed to be?" he asked, pointing at/nthe jackets./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"Finest dragon skin, little bro," said Fred, giving his/nzip a little tweak. "Business is booming and we/nthought we'd treat ourselves."/n/n"Hello, Harry," said Lupin, as Mrs. Weasley let go of/nHarry and turned to greet Hermione./n/n"Hi," said Harry.
