Occasionally one of them started/nforward excitedly, as if they had seen something/ninteresting at last, only to fall back looking/ndisappointed./n/nOn the first day of September there were more people/nlurking in the square than ever before. Half a dozen/nmen in long cloaks stood silent and watchful, gazing/nas ever at houses eleven and thirteen, but the thing/nfor which they were waiting still appeared elusive. As/nevening drew in, bringing with it an unexpected gust/nof chilly rain for the first time in weeks, there/noccurred one of those inexplicable moments when/nthey appeared to have seen something interesting./n/nThe man with the twisted face pointed and his closest/ncompanion, a podgy, pallid man, started forward, but/na moment later they had relaxed into their previous/nstate of inactivity, looking frustrated and/ndisappointed./n/nMeanwhile, inside number twelve, Harry had just/nentered the hall. He had nearly lost his balance as he/nApparated onto the top step just outside the front/ndoor, and thought that the Death Eaters might have/ncaught a glimpse of his momentarily exposed elbow./nShutting the front door carefully behind him, he/npulled off the Invisibility Cloak, draped it over his/narm, and hurried along the gloomy hallway toward/nthe door that led to the basement, a stolen copy of the/nDaily Prophet clutched in his hand./n/nThe usual low whisper of "Severus Snape?" greeted/nhim, the chill wind swept him, and his tongue rolled/nup for a moment./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"I didn't kill you," he said, once it had unrolled, then/nheld his breath as the dusty jinx-figure exploded. He/nwaited until he was halfway down the stairs to the/nkitchen, out of earshot of Mrs. Black and clear of the/ndust cloud, before calling, "I've got news, and you/nwon't like it."/n/nThe kitchen was almost unrecognizable. Every surface/nnow shone: Copper pots and pans had been/nburnished to a rosy glow; the wooden tabletop/ngleamed; the goblets and plates already laid for/ndinner glinted in the light from a merrily blazing fire,/non which a cauldron was simmering. Nothing in the/nroom, however, was more dramatically different than/nthe house-elf who now came hurrying toward Harry,/ndressed in a snowy-white towel, his ear hair as clean/nand fluffy as cotton wool, Regulus's locket bouncing/non his thin chest./n/n"Shoes off, if you please, Master Harry, and hands/nwashed before dinner," croaked Kreacher, seizing the/nInvisibility Cloak and slouching off to hang it on a/nhook on the wall, beside a number of old-fashioned/nrobes that had been freshly laundered./n/n"What's happened?" Ron asked apprehensively. He/nand Hermione had been poring over a sheaf of/nscribbled notes and hand-drawn maps that littered/nthe end of the long kitchen table, but now they/nwatched Harry as he strode toward them and threw/ndown the newspaper on top of their scattered/nparchment./n/nA large picture of a familiar, hook-nosed, black-haired/nman stared up at them all, beneath a headline that/nread:/n/nSEVERUS SNAPE CONFIRMED AS HOGWARTS/nHEADMASTER/n/n/n/n/n/n"No!" said Ron and Hermione loudly./n/nHermione was quickest; she snatched up the/nnewspaper and began to read the accompanying story/nout loud./n/n" 'Severus Snape, long-standing Potions master at/nHogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry, was/ntoday appointed headmaster in the most important of/nseveral staffing changes at the ancient school./nFollowing the resignation of the previous Muggle/nStudies teacher, Alecto Carrow will take over the post/nwhile her brother, Amycus, fills the position of Defense/nAgainst the Dark Arts professor./n/n" 7 welcome the opportunity to uphold our finest/nWizarding traditions and values — ' Like committing/nmurder and cutting off people's ears, I suppose!/n/nSnape, headmaster! Snape in Dumbledore's study —/nMerlin's pants!" she shrieked, making both Harry and/nRon jump. She leapt up from the table and hurtled/nfrom the room, shouting as she went, "I'll be back in a/nminute!"/n/n" 'Merlin's pants?" repeated Ron, looking amused./n"She must be upset." He pulled the newspaper toward/nhim and perused the article about Snape./n/n"The other teachers won't stand for this. McGonagall/nand Flitwick and Sprout all know the truth, they/nknow how Dumbledore died. They won't accept Snape/nas headmaster. And who are these Carrows?"/n/n"Death Eaters," said Harry. "There are pictures of/nthem inside. They were at the top of the tower when/nSnape killed Dumbledore, so it's all friends together./nAnd," Harry went on bitterly, drawing up a chair, "I/ncan't see that the other teachers have got any choice/nbut to stay. If the Ministry and Voldemort are behind/n/n/n/n/nSnape it'll be a choice between staying and teaching,/nor a nice few years in Azkaban — and that's if they're/nlucky. I reckon they'll stay to try and protect the/nstudents."/n/nKreacher came bustling to the table with a large/ntureen in his hands, and ladled out soup into pristine/nbowls, whistling between his teeth as he did so./n/n"Thanks, Kreacher," said Harry, flipping over the/nProphet so as not to have to look at Snape 's face./n/n"Well, at least we know exactly where Snape is now."/n/nHe began to spoon soup into his mouth. The quality/nof Kreacher's cooking had improved dramatically ever/nsince he had been given Regulus's locket: Today's/nFrench onion was as good as Harry had ever tasted./n/n"There are still a load of Death Eaters watching the/nhouse," he told Ron as he ate, "more than usual. It's/nlike they're hoping we'll march out carrying our/nschool trunks and head off for the Hogwarts Express."/n/nRon glanced at his watch./n/n"I've been thinking about that all day. It left nearly six/nhours ago. Weird, not being on it, isn't it?"/n/nIn his mind's eye Harry seemed to see the scarlet/nsteam engine as he and Ron had once followed it by/nair, shimmering between fields and hills, a rippling/nscarlet caterpillar. He was sure Ginny, Neville, and/nLuna were sitting together at this moment, perhaps/nwondering where he, Ron, and Hermione were, or/ndebating how best to undermine Snape 's new regime./n/n"They nearly saw me coming back in just now," Harry/nsaid. "I landed badly on the top step, and the Cloak/nslipped."/n/n/n/n/n/n"I do that every time. Oh, here she is," Ron added,/ncraning around in his seat to watch Hermione/nreentering the kitchen. "And what in the name of/nMerlin's most baggy Y Fronts was that about?"/n/n"I remembered this," Hermione panted./n/nShe was carrying a large, framed picture, which she/nnow lowered to the floor before seizing her small,/nbeaded bag from the kitchen sideboard. Opening it,/nshe proceeded to force the painting inside, and/ndespite the fact that it was patently too large to fit/ninside the tiny bag, within a few seconds it had/nvanished, like so much else, into the bag's capacious/ndepths./n/n"Phineas Nigellus," Hermione explained as she threw/nthe bag onto the kitchen table with the usual/nsonorous, clanking crash./n/n"Sorry?" said Ron, but Harry understood. The painted/nimage of Phineas Nigellus Black was able to flit/nbetween his portrait in Grimmauld Place and the one/nthat hung in the headmaster's office at Hogwarts: the/ncircular tower-top room where Snape was no doubt/nsitting right now, in triumphant possession of/nDumbledore's collection of delicate, silver magical/ninstruments, the stone Pensieve, the Sorting Hat and,/nunless it had been moved elsewhere, the sword of/nGryffindor./n/n"Snape could send Phineas Nigellus to look inside this/nhouse for him," Hermione explained to Ron as she/nresumed her seat. "But let him try it now, all Phineas/nNigellus will be able to see is the inside of my/nhandbag."/n/n"Good thinking!" said Ron, looking impressed./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"Thank you," smiled Hermione, pulling her soup/ntoward her. "So, Harry, what else happened today?"/n/n"Nothing," said Harry. "Watched the Ministry entrance/nfor seven hours. No sign of her. Saw your dad,/nthough, Ron. He looks fine."/n/nRon nodded his appreciation of this news. They had/nagreed that it was far too dangerous to try and/ncommunicate with Mr. Weasley while he walked in/nand out of the Ministry, because he was always/nsurrounded by other Ministry workers. It was,/nhowever, reassuring to catch these glimpses of him,/neven if he did look very strained and anxious./n/n"Dad always told us most Ministry people use the/nFloo Network to get to work," Ron said. "That's why/nwe haven't seen Umbridge, she'd never walk, she'd/nthink she's too important."/n/n"And what about that funny old witch and that little/nwizard in the navy robes?" Hermione asked./n/n"Oh yeah, the bloke from Magical Maintenance," said/nRon./n/n"How do you know he works for Magical/nMaintenance?" Hermione asked, her soupspoon/nsuspended in midair./n/n"Dad said everyone from Magical Maintenance wears/nnavy blue robes."/n/n"But you never told us that!"/n/nHermione dropped her spoon and pulled toward her/nthe sheaf of notes and maps that she and Ron had/nbeen examining when Harry had entered the kitchen./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"There's nothing in here about navy blue robes,/nnothing!" she said, flipping feverishly through the/npages./n/n"Well, does it really matter?"/n/n"Ron, it all matters! If we're going to get into the/nMinistry and not give ourselves away when they're/nbound to be on the lookout for intruders, every little/ndetail matters! We've been over and over this, I mean,/nwhat's the point of all these reconnaissance trips if/nyou aren't even bothering to tell us — "/n/n"Blimey, Hermione, I forget one little thing — "/n/n"You do realize, don't you, that there's probably no/nmore dangerous place in the whole world for us to be/nright now than the Ministry of — "/n/n"I think we should do it tomorrow," said Harry./n/nHermione stopped dead, her jaw hanging; Ron choked/na little over his soup./n/n"Tomorrow?" repeated Hermione. "You aren't serious,/nHarry?"/n/n"I am," said Harry. "I don't think we're going to be/nmuch better prepared than we are now even if we/nskulk around the Ministry entrance for another/nmonth. The longer we put it off, the farther away that/nlocket could be. There's already a good chance/nUmbridge has chucked it away; the thing doesn't/nopen."/n/n"Unless," said Ron, "she's found a way of opening it/nand she's now possessed."/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"Wouldn't make any difference to her, she was so evil/nin the first place," Harry shrugged./n/nHermione was biting her lip, deep in thought./n/n"We know everything important," Harry went on,/naddressing Hermione. "We know they've stopped/nApparition in and out of the Ministry. We know only/nthe most senior Ministry members are allowed to/nconnect their homes to the Floo Network now,/nbecause Ron heard those two Unspeakables/ncomplaining about it. And we know roughly where/nUmbridge's office is, because of what you heard that/nbearded bloke saying to his mate — "/n/n" 'I'll be up on level one, Dolores wants to see me,' "/nHermione recited immediately./n/n"Exactly," said Harry. "And we know you get in using/nthose funny coins, or tokens, or whatever they are,/nbecause I saw that witch borrowing one from her/nfriend — "/n/n"But we haven't got any!"/n/n"If the plan works, we will have," Harry continued/ncalmly./n/n"I don't know, Harry, I don't know. ... There are an/nawful lot of things that could go wrong, so much/nrelies on chance. ..."/n/n"That'll be true even if we spend another three/nmonths preparing," said Harry. "It's time to act."/n/nHe could tell from Ron's and Hermione's faces that/nthey were scared; he was not particularly confident/nhimself, and yet he was sure the time had come to/nput their plan into operation./n/n/n/n/n/nThey had spent the previous four weeks taking it in/nturns to don the Invisibility Cloak and spy on the/nofficial entrance to the Ministry, which Ron, thanks to/nMr. Weasley, had known since childhood. They had/ntailed Ministry workers on their way in, eavesdropped/non their conversations, and learned by careful/nobservation which of them could be relied upon to/nappear, alone, at the same time every day./nOccasionally there had been a chance to sneak a/nDaily Prophet out of somebody's briefcase. Slowly they/nhad built up the sketchy maps and notes now stacked/nin front of Hermione./n/n"All right," said Ron slowly, "let's say we go for it/ntomorrow. ... I think it should just be me and Harry."/n/n"Oh, don't start that again!" sighed Hermione. "I/nthought we'd settled this."/n/n"It's one thing hanging around the entrances under/nthe Cloak, but this is different, Hermione." Ron/njabbed a finger at a copy of the Daily Prophet dated/nten days previously. "You're on the list of Muggle-/nborns who didn't present themselves for/ninterrogation!"/n/n"And you're supposed to be dying of spattergroit at/nthe Burrow! If anyone shouldn't go, it's Harry, he's got/na ten-thousand-Galleon price on his head — "/n/n"Fine, I'll stay here," said Harry. "Let me know if you/never defeat Voldemort, won't you?"/n/nAs Ron and Hermione laughed, pain shot through the/nscar on Harry's forehead. His hand jumped to it: He/nsaw Hermione's eyes narrow, and he tried to pass off/nthe movement by brushing his hair out of his eyes./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"Well, if all three of us go well have to Disapparate/nseparately," Ron was saying. "We can't all fit under/nthe Cloak anymore."/n/nHarry's scar was becoming more and more painful./n/nHe stood up. At once, Kreacher hurried forward./n/n"Master has not finished his soup, would Master/nprefer the savory stew, or else the treacle tart to/nwhich Master is so partial?"/n/n"Thanks, Kreacher, but I'll be back in a minute — er/n— bathroom."/n/nAware that Hermione was watching him suspiciously,/nHarry hurried up the stairs to the hall and then to the/nfirst landing, where he dashed into the bathroom and/nbolted the door again. Grunting with pain, he/nslumped over the black basin with its taps in the form/nof open-mouthed serpents and closed his eyes. .../n/nHe was gliding along a twilit street. The buildings on/neither side of him had high, timbered gables; they/nlooked like gingerbread houses./n/nHe approached one of them, then saw the whiteness/nof his own long-fingered hand against the door. He/nknocked. He felt a mounting excitement. .../n/nThe door opened: A laughing woman stood there. Her/nface fell as she looked into Harry's face: humor gone,/nterror replacing it. .../n/n"Gregorovitch?" said a high, cold voice./n/nShe shook her head: She was trying to close the door./nA white hand held it steady, prevented her shutting/nhim out. .../n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"I want Gregorovitch."/n/n"Er wohnt hier nicht mehr\" she cried, shaking her/nhead. "He no live here! He no live here! I know him/nnot!"/n/nAbandoning the attempt to close the door, she began/nto back away down the dark hall, and Harry followed,/ngliding toward her, and his long-fingered hand had/ndrawn his wand./n/n"Where is he?"/n/n"Das weifi ich nichti He move! I know not, I know not!"/n/nHe raised the wand. She screamed. Two young/nchildren came running into the hall. She tried to/nshield them with her arms. There was a flash of green/nlight —/n/n"Harry! HARRY!"/n/nHe opened his eyes; he had sunk to the floor./nHermione was pounding on the door again./n/n"Harry, open up!"/n/nHe had shouted out, he knew it. He got up and/nunbolted the door; Hermione toppled inside at once,/nregained her balance, and looked around/nsuspiciously. Ron was right behind her, looking/nunnerved as he pointed his wand into the corners of/nthe chilly bathroom./n/n"What were you doing?" asked Hermione sternly./n/n"What d'you think I was doing?" asked Harry with/nfeeble bravado./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"You were yelling your head off!" said Ron./n/n"Oh yeah ... I must've dozed off or — "/n/n"Harry, please don't insult our intelligence," said/nHermione, taking deep breaths. "We know your scar/nhurt downstairs, and you're white as a sheet."/n/nHarry sat down on the edge of the bath./n/n"Fine. I've just seen Voldemort murdering a woman./nBy now he's probably killed her whole family. And he/ndidn't need to. It was Cedric all over again, they were/njust there. ..."/n/n"Harry, you aren't supposed to let this happen/nanymore!" Hermione cried, her voice echoing through/nthe bathroom. "Dumbledore wanted you to use/nOcclumency! He thought the connection was/ndangerous — Voldemort can use it, Harry! What good/nis it to watch him kill and torture, how can it help?"/n/n"Because it means I know what he's doing," said/nHarry./n/n"So you're not even going to try to shut him out?"/n/n"Hermione, I can't. You know I'm lousy at/nOcclumency, I never got the hang of it."/n/n"You never really tried!" she said hotly. "I don't get it,/nHarry — do you like having this special connection or/nrelationship or what — whatever — "/n/nShe faltered under the look he gave her as he stood/n/nup./n/n/n/n"Like it?" he said quietly. "Would you like it?"/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"I — no — I'm sorry, Harry, I didn't mean — "/n/n"I hate it, I hate the fact that he can get inside me,/nthat I have to watch him when he's most dangerous./nBut I'm going to use it."/n/n"Dumbledore — "/n/n"Forget Dumbledore. This is my choice, nobody else's./nI want to know why he's after Gregorovitch."/n/n"Who?"/n/n"He's a foreign wandmaker," said Harry. "He made/nKrum's wand and Krum reckons he's brilliant."/n/n"But according to you," said Ron, "Voldemort's got/nOllivander locked up somewhere. If he's already got a/nwandmaker, what does he need another one for?"/n/n"Maybe he agrees with Krum, maybe he thinks/nGregorovitch is better ... or else he thinks/nGregorovitch will be able to explain what my wand did/nwhen he was chasing me, because Ollivander didn't/nknow."/n/nHarry glanced into the cracked, dusty mirror and saw/nRon and Hermione exchanging skeptical looks behind/nhis back./n/n"Harry, you keep talking about what your wand did,"/nsaid Hermione, "but you made it happen! Why are/nyou so determined not to take responsibility for your/nown power?"/n/n"Because I know it wasn't me! And so does Voldemort,/nHermione! We both know what really happened!"/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nThey glared at each other: Harry knew that he had/nnot convinced Hermione and that she was marshaling/ncounterarguments, against both his theory on his/nwand and the fact that he was permitting himself to/nsee into Voldemort's mind. To his relief, Ron/nintervened./n/n"Drop it," he advised her. "It's up to him. And if we're/ngoing to the Ministry tomorrow, don't you reckon we/nshould go over the plan?"/n/nReluctantly, as the other two could tell, Hermione let/nthe matter rest, though Harry was quite sure she/nwould attack again at the first opportunity. In the/nmeantime, they returned to the basement kitchen,/nwhere Kreacher served them all stew and treacle tart./n/nThey did not get to bed until late that night, after/nspending hours going over and over their plan until/nthey could recite it, word perfect, to each other./n/nHarry, who was now sleeping in Sirius's room, lay in/nbed with his wandlight trained on the old photograph/nof his father, Sirius, Lupin, and Pettigrew, and/nmuttered the plan to himself for another ten minutes./nAs he extinguished his wand, however, he was/nthinking not of Polyjuice Potion, Puking Pastilles, or/nthe navy blue robes of Magical Maintenance; he/nthought of Gregorovitch the wandmaker, and how/nlong he could hope to remain hidden while Voldemort/nsought him so determinedly./n/nDawn seemed to follow midnight with indecent haste./n/n"You look terrible," was Ron's greeting as he entered/nthe room to wake Harry./n/n"Not for long," said Harry, yawning./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nThey found Hermione downstairs in the kitchen. She/nwas being served coffee and hot rolls by Kreacher and/nwearing the slightly manic expression that Harry/nassociated with exam review./n/n"Robes," she said under her breath, acknowledging/ntheir presence with a nervous nod and continuing to/npoke around in her beaded bag, "Polyjuice Potion .../nInvisibility Cloak ... Decoy Detonators ... You should/neach take a couple just in case. ... Puking Pastilles,/nNosebleed Nougat, Extendable Ears ..."/n/nThey gulped down their breakfast, then set off/nupstairs, Kreacher bowing them out and promising to/nhave a steak-and-kidney pie ready for them when/nthey returned./n/n"Bless him," said Ron fondly, "and when you think I/nused to fantasize about cutting off his head and/nsticking it on the wall."/n/nThey made their way onto the front step with/nimmense caution: They could see a couple of puffy-/neyed Death Eaters watching the house from across/nthe misty square./n/nHermione Disapparated with Ron first, then came/nback for Harry./n/nAfter the usual brief spell of darkness and near/nsuffocation, Harry found himself in the tiny alleyway/nwhere the first phase of their plan was scheduled to/ntake place. It was as yet deserted, except for a couple/nof large bins; the first Ministry workers did not/nusually appear here until at least eight o'clock./n/n"Right then," said Hermione, checking her watch./n/n"She ought to be here in about five minutes. When/nI've Stunned her — "/n/n/n/n/n/n"Hermione, we know," said Ron sternly. "And I/nthought we were supposed to open the door before/nshe got here?"/n/nHermione squealed./n/n"I nearly forgot! Stand back — "/n/nShe pointed her wand at the padlocked and heavily/ngraffitied fire door beside them, which burst open/nwith a crash. The dark corridor behind it led, as they/nknew from their careful scouting trips, into an empty/ntheater. Hermione pulled the door back toward her, to/nmake it look as though it was still closed./n/n"And now," she said, turning back to face the other/ntwo in the alleyway, "we put on the Cloak again — "/n/n" — and we wait," Ron finished, throwing it over/nHermione 's head like a blanket over a birdcage and/nrolling his eyes at Harry./n/nLittle more than a minute later, there was a tiny pop/nand a little Ministry witch with flyaway gray hair/nApparated feet from them, blinking a little in the/nsudden brightness; the sun had just come out from/nbehind a cloud. She barely had time to enjoy the/nunexpected warmth, however, before Hermione 's/nsilent Stunning Spell hit her in the chest and she/ntoppled over./n/n"Nicely done, Hermione," said Ron, emerging from/nbehind a bin beside the theater door as Harry took off/nthe Invisibility Cloak. Together they carried the little/nwitch into the dark passageway that led backstage./nHermione plucked a few hairs from the witch's head/nand added them to a flask of muddy Polyjuice Potion/nshe had taken from the beaded bag. Ron was/nrummaging through the little witch's handbag./n/n/n/n/n/n"She's Mafalda Hopkirk," he said, reading a small/ncard that identified their victim as an assistant in the/nImproper Use of Magic Office. "You'd better take this,/nHermione, and here are the tokens."/n/nHe passed her several small golden coins, all/nembossed with the letters M.O.M., which he had/ntaken from the witch's purse./n/nHermione drank the Polyjuice Potion, which was now/na pleasant heliotrope color, and within seconds stood/nbefore them, the double of Mafalda Hopkirk. As she/nremoved Mafalda's spectacles and put them on, Harry/nchecked his watch./n/n"We're running late, Mr. Magical Maintenance will be/nhere any second."/n/nThey hurried to close the door on the real Mafalda;/nHarry and Ron threw the Invisibility Cloak over/nthemselves but Hermione remained in view, waiting./nSeconds later there was another pop, and a small,/nferrety-looking wizard appeared before them./n/n"Oh, hello, Mafalda."/n/n"Hello!" said Hermione in a quavery voice. "How are/nyou today?"/n/n"Not so good, actually," replied the little wizard, who/nlooked thoroughly downcast./n/nAs Hermione and the wizard headed for the main/nroad, Harry and Ron crept along behind them./n/n"I'm sorry to hear you're under the weather," said/nHermione, talking firmly over the little wizard as he/ntried to expound upon his problems; it was essential/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nto stop him from reaching the street. "Here, have a/nsweet."/n/n"Eh? Oh, no thanks — "/n/n"I insist!" said Hermione aggressively, shaking the bag/nof pastilles in his face. Looking rather alarmed, the/nlittle wizard took one./n/nThe effect was instantaneous. The moment the/npastille touched his tongue, the little wizard started/nvomiting so hard that he did not even notice as/nHermione yanked a handful of hairs from the top of/nhis head./n/n"Oh dear!" she said, as he splattered the alley with/nsick. "Perhaps you'd better take the day off!"/n/n"No — no!" He choked and retched, trying to continue/non his way despite being unable to walk straight. "I/nmust — today — must go — "/n/n"But that's just silly!" said Hermione, alarmed. "You/ncan't go to work in this state — I think you ought to/ngo to St. Mungo's and get them to sort you out!"/n/nThe wizard had collapsed, heaving, onto all fours, still/ntrying to crawl toward the main street./n/n"You simply can't go to work like this!" cried/nHermione./n/nAt last he seemed to accept the truth of her words./nUsing a repulsed Hermione to claw his way back into/na standing position, he turned on the spot and/nvanished, leaving nothing behind but the bag Ron/nhad snatched from his hand as he went and some/nflying chunks of vomit./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"Urgh," said Hermione, holding up the skirts of her/nrobe to avoid the puddles of sick. "It would have made/nmuch less mess to Stun him too."/n/n"Yeah," said Ron, emerging from under the cloak/nholding the wizard's bag, "but I still think a whole pile/nof unconscious bodies would have drawn more/nattention. Keen on his job, though, isn't he? Chuck us/nthe hair and the potion, then."/n/nWithin two minutes, Ron stood before them, as small/nand ferrety as the sick wizard, and wearing the navy/nblue robes that had been folded in his bag./n/n"Weird he wasn't wearing them today, wasn't it,/nseeing how much he wanted to go? Anyway, I'm Reg/nCattermole, according to the label in the back."/n/n"Now wait here," Hermione told Harry, who was still/nunder the Invisibility Cloak, "and we'll be back with/nsome hairs for you."/n/nHe had to wait ten minutes, but it seemed much/nlonger to Harry, skulking alone in the sick-splattered/nalleyway beside the door concealing the Stunned/nMafalda. Finally Ron and Hermione reappeared./n/n"We don't know who he is," Hermione said, passing/nHarry several curly black hairs, "but he's gone home/nwith a dreadful nosebleed! Here, he's pretty tall, you'll/nneed bigger robes. ..."/n/nShe pulled out a set of the old robes Kreacher had/nlaundered for them, and Harry retired to take the/npotion and change./n/nOnce the painful transformation was complete he was/nmore than six feet tall and, from what he could tell/nfrom his well-muscled arms, powerfully built. He also/n/n/n/n/n/nhad a beard. Stowing the Invisibility Cloak and his/nglasses inside his new robes, he rejoined the other/ntwo./n/n"Blimey, that's scary," said Ron, looking up at Harry,/nwho now towered over him./n/n"Take one of Mafalda's tokens," Hermione told Harry,/n"and let's go, it's nearly nine."/n/nThey stepped out of the alleyway together. Fifty yards/nalong the crowded pavement there were spiked black/nrailings flanking two flights of steps, one labeled/nGENTLEMEN, the other LADIES./n/n"See you in a moment, then," said Hermione/nnervously, and she tottered off down the steps to/nLADIES. Harry and Ron joined a number of oddly/ndressed men descending into what appeared to be an/nordinary underground public toilet, tiled in grimy/nblack and white./n/n"Morning, Reg!" called another wizard in navy blue/nrobes as he let himself into a cubicle by inserting his/ngolden token into a slot in the door. "Blooming pain in/nthe bum, this, eh? Forcing us all to get to work this/nway! Who are they expecting to turn up, Harry/nPotter?"/n/nThe wizard roared with laughter at his own wit. Ron/ngave a forced chuckle./n/n"Yeah," he said, "stupid, isn't it?"/n/nAnd he and Harry let themselves into adjoining/ncubicles./n/nTo Harry's left and right came the sound of flushing./nHe crouched down and peered through the gap at the/n/n/n/n/n/nbottom of the cubicle, just in time to see a pair of/nbooted feet climbing into the toilet next door. He/nlooked left and saw Ron blinking at him./n/n"We have to flush ourselves in?" he whispered./n/n"Looks like it," Harry whispered back; his voice came/nout deep and gravelly./n/nThey both stood up. Feeling exceptionally foolish,/nHarry clambered into the toilet./n/nHe knew at once that he had done the right thing;/nthough he appeared to be standing in water, his/nshoes, feet, and robes remained quite dry. He reached/nup, pulled the chain, and next moment had zoomed/ndown a short chute, emerging out of a fireplace into/nthe Ministry of Magic./n/nHe got up clumsily; there was a lot more of his body/nthan he was accustomed to. The great Atrium seemed/ndarker than Harry remembered it. Previously a golden/nfountain had filled the center of the hall, casting/nshimmering spots of light over the polished wooden/nfloor and walls. Now a gigantic statue of black stone/ndominated the scene. It was rather frightening, this/nvast sculpture of a witch and a wizard sitting on/nornately carved thrones, looking down at the Ministry/nworkers toppling out of fireplaces below them./nEngraved in foot-high letters at the base of the statue/nwere the words MAGIC IS MIGHT./n/nHarry received a heavy blow on the back of the legs:/nAnother wizard had just flown out of the fireplace/nbehind him./n/n"Out of the way, can't y — oh, sorry, Runcorn!"/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nClearly frightened, the balding wizard hurried away./nApparently the man whom Harry was impersonating,/nRuncorn, was intimidating./n/n"Psst!" said a voice, and he looked around to see a/nwispy little witch and the ferrety wizard from Magical/nMaintenance gesturing to him from over beside the/nstatue. Harry hastened to join them./n/n"You got in all right, then?" Hermione whispered to/nHarry./n/n"No, he's still stuck in the bog," said Ron./n/n"Oh, very funny ... It's horrible, isn't it?" she said to/nHarry, who was staring up at the statue. "Have you/nseen what they're sitting on?/n/nHarry looked more closely and realized that what he/nhad thought were decoratively carved thrones were/nactually mounds of carved humans: hundreds and/nhundreds of naked bodies, men, women, and/nchildren, all with rather stupid, ugly faces, twisted/nand pressed together to support the weight of the/nhandsomely robed wizards./n/n"Muggles," whispered Hermione. "In their rightful/nplace. Come on, let's get going."/n/nThey joined the stream of witches and wizards moving/ntoward the golden gates at the end of the hall, looking/naround as surreptitiously as possible, but there was/nno sign of the distinctive figure of Dolores Umbridge./nThey passed through the gates and into a smaller/nhall, where queues were forming in front of twenty/ngolden grilles housing as many lifts. They had barely/njoined the nearest one when a voice said,/n/n"Cattermole!"/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nThey looked around: Harry's stomach turned over./nOne of the Death Eaters who had witnessed/nDumbledore's death was striding toward them. The/nMinistry workers beside them fell silent, their eyes/ndowncast; Harry could feel fear rippling through/nthem. The man's scowling, slightly brutish face was/nsomehow at odds with his magnificent, sweeping/nrobes, which were embroidered with much gold/nthread. Someone in the crowd around the lifts called/nsycophantically, "Morning, Yaxley!" Yaxley ignored/nthem./n/n"I requested somebody from Magical Maintenance to/nsort out my office, Cattermole. It's still raining in/nthere."/n/nRon looked around as though hoping somebody else/nwould intervene, but nobody spoke./n/n"Raining ... in your office? That's — that's not good, is/nit?"/n/n/n/nRon gave a nervous laugh. Yaxley's eyes widened./n/n"You think it's funny, Cattermole, do you?"/n/nA pair of witches broke away from the queue for the/nlift and bustled off./n/n"No," said Ron, "no, of course — "/n/n"You realize that I am on my way downstairs to/ninterrogate your wife, Cattermole? In fact, I'm quite/nsurprised you're not down there holding her hand/nwhile she waits. Already given her up as a bad job,/nhave you? Probably wise. Be sure and marry a/npureblood next time."/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nHermione had let out a little squeak of horror. Yaxley/nlooked at her. She coughed feebly and turned away./n/n"I — I — " stammered Ron./n/n"But if my wife were accused of being a Mudblood,"/nsaid Yaxley, " — not that any woman I married would/never be mistaken for such filth — and the Head of the/nDepartment of Magical Law Enforcement needed a job/ndoing, I would make it my priority to do that job,/nCattermole. Do you understand me?"/n/n"Yes," whispered Ron./n/n"Then attend to it, Cattermole, and if my office is not/ncompletely dry within an hour, your wife's Blood/nStatus will be in even graver doubt than it is now."/n/nThe golden grille before them clattered open. With a/nnod and unpleasant smile to Harry, who was/nevidently expected to appreciate this treatment of/nCattermole, Yaxley swept away toward another lift./nHarry, Ron, and Hermione entered theirs, but nobody/nfollowed them: It was as if they were infectious. The/ngrilles shut with a clang and the lift began to move/nupward./n/n"What am I going to do?" Ron asked the other two at/nonce; he looked stricken. "If I don't turn up, my wife/n— I mean, Cattermole 's wife — "/n/n"Well come with you, we should stick together — "/nbegan Harry, but Ron shook his head feverishly./n/n"That's mental, we haven't got much time. You two/nfind Umbridge, I'll go and sort out Yaxley's office —/nbut how do I stop it raining?"/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"Try Finite Incantatem," said Hermione at once, "that/nshould stop the rain if it's a hex or curse; if it doesn't,/nsomething's gone wrong with an Atmospheric Charm,/nwhich will be more difficult to fix, so as an interim/nmeasure try Impervius to protect his belongings — "/n/n"Say it again, slowly — " said Ron, searching his/npockets desperately for a quill, but at that moment/nthe lift juddered to a halt. A disembodied female voice/nsaid, "Level four, Department for the Regulation and/nControl of Magical Creatures, incorporating Beast,/nBeing, and Spirit Divisions, Goblin Liaison Office, and/nPest Advisory Bureau," and the grilles slid open again,/nadmitting a couple of wizards and several pale violet/npaper airplanes that fluttered around the lamp in the/nceiling of the lift./n/n"Morning, Albert," said a bushily whiskered man,/nsmiling at Harry. He glanced over at Ron and/nHermione as the lift creaked upward once more;/nHermione was now whispering frantic instructions to/nRon. The wizard leaned toward Harry, leering, and/nmuttered, "Dirk Cresswell, eh? From Goblin Liaison?/nNice one, Albert. I'm pretty confident I'll get his job/nnow!"/n/nHe winked. Harry smiled back, hoping that this would/nsuffice. The lift stopped; the grilles opened once more./n/n"Level two, Department of Magical Law Enforcement,/nincluding the Improper Use of Magic Office, Auror/nHeadquarters, and Wizengamot Administration/nServices," said the disembodied witch's voice./n/nHarry saw Hermione give Ron a little push and he/nhurried out of the lift, followed by the other wizards,/nleaving Harry and Hermione alone. The moment the/ngolden door had closed Hermione said, very fast,/n"Actually, Harry, I think I'd better go after him, I don't/n/n/n/n/nthink he knows what he's doing and if he gets caught/nthe whole thing — "/n/n/n/n"Level one, Minister of Magic and Support Staff."/n/nThe golden grilles slid apart again and Hermione/ngasped. Four people stood before them, two of them/ndeep in conversation: a longhaired wizard wearing/nmagnificent robes of black and gold, and a squat,/ntoadlike witch wearing a velvet bow in her short hair/nand clutching a clipboard to her chest./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n

title: The Muggle-Born Registration Commission
text: /n"Ah, Mafalda!" said Umbridge, looking at Hermione./n"Travers sent you, did he?"/n/n"Y-yes," squeaked Hermione./n/n"Good, youll do perfectly well." Umbridge spoke to the/nwizard in black and gold. "That's that problem solved,/nMinister, if Mafalda can be spared for record-keeping/nwe shall be able to start straightaway." She consulted/nher clipboard. "Ten people today and one of them the/nwife of a Ministry employee! Tut, tut ... even here, in/nthe heart of the Ministry!" She stepped into the lift/nbeside Hermione, as did the two wizards who had/nbeen listening to Umbridge's conversation with the/nMinister. "We'll go straight down, Mafalda, you'll find/neverything you need in the courtroom. Good morning,/nAlbert, aren't you getting out?"/n/n"Yes, of course," said Harry in Runcorn's deep voice./n/n/n/n/n/n/nHarry stepped out of the lift. The golden grilles/nclanged shut behind him. Glancing over his shoulder,/nHarry saw Hermione's anxious face sinking back out/nof sight, a tall wizard on either side of her, Umbridge's/nvelvet hair-bow level with her shoulder./n/n"What brings you up here, Runcorn?" asked the new/nMinister of Magic. His long black hair and beard were/nstreaked with silver, and a great overhanging/nforehead shadowed his glinting eyes, putting Harry in/nmind of a crab looking out from beneath a rock./n/n"Needed a quick word with," Harry hesitated for a/nfraction of a second, "Arthur Weasley. Someone said/nhe was up on level one."/n/n"Ah," said Pius Thicknesse. "Has he been caught/nhaving contact with an Undesirable?"/n/n"No," said Harry, his throat dry. "No, nothing like/nthat."/n/n"Ah, well. It's only a matter of time," said Thicknesse./n"If you ask me, the blood traitors are as bad as the/nMudbloods. Good day, Runcorn."/n/n"Good day, Minister."/n/nHarry watched Thicknesse march away along the/nthickly carpeted corridor. The moment the Minister/nhad passed out of sight, Harry tugged the Invisibility/nCloak out from under his heavy black cloak, threw it/nover himself, and set off along the corridor in the/nopposite direction. Runcorn was so tall that Harry/nwas forced to stoop to make sure his big feet were/nhidden./n/nPanic pulsed in the pit of his stomach. As he passed/ngleaming wooden door after gleaming wooden door,/n/n/n/n/n/neach bearing a small plaque with the owner's name/nand occupation upon it, the might of the Ministry, its/ncomplexity, its impenetrability, seemed to force itself/nupon him so that the plan he had been carefully/nconcocting with Ron and Hermione over the past four/nweeks seemed laughably childish. They had/nconcentrated all their efforts on getting inside without/nbeing detected: They had not given a moment's/nthought to what they would do if they were forced to/nseparate. Now Hermione was stuck in court/nproceedings, which would undoubtedly last hours;/n/nRon was struggling to do magic that Harry was sure/nwas beyond him, a woman's liberty possibly/ndepending on the outcome; and he, Harry, was/nwandering around on the top floor when he knew/nperfectly well that his quarry had just gone down in/nthe lift./n/nHe stopped walking, leaned against a wall, and tried/nto decide what to do. The silence pressed upon him:/nThere was no bustling or talk or swift footsteps here;/nthe purple-carpeted corridors were as hushed as/nthough the Muffliato charm had been cast over the/nplace./n/nHer office must be up here, Harry thought./n/nIt seemed most unlikely that Umbridge would keep/nher jewelry in her office, but on the other hand it/nseemed foolish not to search it to make sure. He/ntherefore set off along the corridor again, passing/nnobody but a frowning wizard who was murmuring/ninstructions to a quill that floated in front of him,/nscribbling on a trail of parchment./n/nNow paying attention to the names on the doors,/n/nHarry turned a corner. Halfway along the next/ncorridor he emerged into a wide, open space where a/ndozen witches and wizards sat in rows at small desks/n/n/n/n/n/nnot unlike school desks, though much more highly/npolished and free from graffiti. Harry paused to watch/nthem, for the effect was quite mesmerizing. They were/nall waving and twiddling their wands in unison, and/nsquares of colored paper were flying in every direction/nlike little pink kites. After a few seconds, Harry/nrealized that there was a rhythm to the proceedings,/nthat the papers all formed the same pattern; and after/na few more seconds he realized that what he was/nwatching was the creation of pamphlets — that the/npaper squares were pages, which, when assembled,/nfolded, and magicked into place, fell into neat stacks/nbeside each witch or wizard./n/nHarry crept closer, although the workers were so/nintent on what they were doing that he doubted they/nwould notice a carpet-muffled footstep, and he slid a/ncompleted pamphlet from the pile beside a young/nwitch. He examined it beneath the Invisibility Cloak./nIts pink cover was emblazoned with a golden title:/n/nMUDBLOODS/n/nand the Dangers They Pose to/na Peaceful Pure-Blood Society/n/nBeneath the title was a picture of a red rose with a/nsimpering face in the middle of its petals, being/nstrangled by a green weed with fangs and a scowl./nThere was no author's name upon the pamphlet, but/nagain, the scars on the back of his right hand seemed/nto tingle as he examined it. Then the young witch/nbeside him confirmed his suspicion as she said, still/nwaving and twirling her wand, "Will the old hag be/ninterrogating Mudbloods all day, does anyone know?"/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"Careful," said the wizard beside her, glancing around/nnervously; one of his pages slipped and fell to the/nfloor./n/n"What, has she got magic ears as well as an eye,/nnow?"/n/nThe witch glanced toward the shining mahogany door/nfacing the space full of pamphlet-makers; Harry/nlooked too, and rage reared in him like a snake./n/nWhere there might have been a peephole on a Muggle/nfront door, a large, round eye with a bright blue iris/nhad been set into the wood — an eye that was/nshockingly familiar to anybody who had known/nAlastor Moody./n/nFor a split second Harry forgot where he was and/nwhat he was doing there: He even forgot that he was/ninvisible. He strode straight over to the door to/nexamine the eye. It was not moving: It gazed blindly/nupward, frozen. The plaque beneath it read:/n/nDOLORES UMBRIDGE/n/nSENIOR UNDERSECRETARY TO THE MINISTER/n/nBelow that, a slightly shinier new plaque read:/n/nHEAD OF THE MUGGLE-BORN/n/nREGISTRATION COMMISSION/n/nHarry looked back at the dozen pamphlet-makers:/nThough they were intent upon their work, he could/nhardly suppose that they would not notice if the door/nof an empty office opened in front of them. He/ntherefore withdrew from an inner pocket an odd/nobject with little waving legs and a rubber-bulbed/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nhorn for a body. Crouching down beneath the Cloak,/nhe placed the Decoy Detonator on the ground./n/nIt scuttled away at once through the legs of the/nwitches and wizards in front of him. A few moments/nlater, during which Harry waited with his hand upon/nthe doorknob, there came a loud bang and a great/ndeal of acrid black smoke billowed from a corner. The/nyoung witch in the front row shrieked: Pink pages/nflew everywhere as she and her fellows jumped up,/nlooking around for the source of the commotion./n/nHarry turned the doorknob, stepped into Umbridge's/noffice, and closed the door behind him./n/nHe felt he had stepped back in time. The room was/nexactly like Umbridge's office at Hogwarts: Lace/ndraperies, doilies, and dried flowers covered every/navailable surface. The walls bore the same/nornamental plates, each featuring a highly colored,/nberibboned kitten, gamboling and frisking with/nsickening cuteness. The desk was covered with a/nflouncy, flowered cloth. Behind Mad-Eye's eye, a/ntelescopic attachment enabled Umbridge to spy on/nthe workers on the other side of the door. Harry took/na look through it and saw that they were all still/ngathered around the Decoy Detonator. He wrenched/nthe telescope out of the door, leaving a hole behind,/npulled the magical eyeball out of it, and placed it in/nhis pocket. Then he turned to face the room again,/nraised his wand, and murmured, "Accio Locket."/n/nNothing happened, but he had not expected it to; no/ndoubt Umbridge knew all about protective charms/nand spells. He therefore hurried behind her desk and/nbegan pulling open the drawers. He saw quills and/nnotebooks and Spellotape; enchanted paper clips that/ncoiled snakelike from their drawer and had to be/nbeaten back; a fussy little lace box full of spare hair/nbows and clips; but no sign of a locket./n/n/n/n/n/nThere was a filing cabinet behind the desk: Harry set/nto searching it. Like Filch 's filing cabinets at/nHogwarts, it was full of folders, each labeled with a/nname. It was not until Harry reached the bottommost/ndrawer that he saw something to distract him from/nhis search: Mr. Weasley's file./n/nHe pulled it out and opened it./n/nARTHUR WEASLEY/n/nBLOOD STATUS: Pureblood, but with unacceptable/npro-Muggle leanings. Known member of the Order of/nthe Phoenix./n/nFAMILY: Wife (pureblood), seven children, two/nyoungest at Hogwarts. NB: Youngest son currently at/nhome, seriously ill, Ministry inspectors have/nconfirmed./n/nSECURITY STATUS: TRACKED. All movements are/nbeing monitored. Strong likelihood Undesirable No. 1/nwill contact (has stayed with Weasley family/npreviously)/n/n/n/n"Undesirable Number One," Harry muttered under his/nbreath as he replaced Mr. Weasley's folder and shut/nthe drawer. He had an idea he knew who that was,/nand sure enough, as he straightened up and glanced/naround the office for fresh hiding places, he saw a/nposter of himself on the wall, with the words/nundesirable no. 1 emblazoned across his chest. A/nlittle pink note was stuck to it with a picture of a/nkitten in the corner. Harry moved across to read it/nand saw that Umbridge had written, "To be punished."/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nAngrier than ever, he proceeded to grope in the/nbottoms of the vases and baskets of dried flowers, but/nwas not at all surprised that the locket was not there./nHe gave the office one last sweeping look, and his/nheart skipped a beat. Dumbledore was staring at him/nfrom a small rectangular mirror, propped up on a/nbookcase beside the desk./n/nHarry crossed the room at a run and snatched it up,/nbut realized the moment he touched it that it was not/na mirror at all. Dumbledore was smiling wistfully out/nof the front cover of a glossy book. Harry had not/nimmediately noticed the curly green writing across his/nhat — The Life and Lies ofAlbus Dumbledore — nor/nthe slightly smaller writing across his chest: "by Rita/nSkeeter, bestselling author of Armando Dippet: Master/nor Moron?"/n/nHarry opened the book at random and saw a full-page/nphotograph of two teenage boys, both laughing/nimmoderately with their arms around each other's/nshoulders. Dumbledore, now with elbow-length hair,/nhad grown a tiny wispy beard that recalled the one on/nKrum's chin that had so annoyed Ron. The boy who/nroared in silent amusement beside Dumbledore had a/ngleeful, wild look about him. His golden hair fell in/ncurls to his shoulders. Harry wondered whether it/nwas a young Doge, but before he could check the/ncaption, the door of the office opened./n/nIf Thicknesse had not been looking over his shoulder/nas he entered, Harry would not have had time to pull/nthe Invisibility Cloak over himself. As it was, he/nthought Thicknesse might have caught a glimpse of/nmovement, because for a moment or two he remained/nquite still, staring curiously at the place where Harry/nhad just vanished. Perhaps deciding that all he had/nseen was Dumbledore scratching his nose on the/nfront of the book, for Harry had hastily replaced it/n/n/n/n/nupon the shelf, Thicknesse finally walked to the desk/nand pointed his wand at the quill standing ready in/nthe ink pot. It sprang out and began scribbling a note/nto Umbridge. Very slowly, hardly daring to breathe,/nHarry backed out of the office into the open area/nbeyond./n/nThe pamphlet-makers were still clustered around the/nremains of the Decoy Detonator, which continued to/nhoot feebly as it smoked. Harry hurried off up the/ncorridor as the young witch said, "I bet it sneaked up/nhere from Experimental Charms, they're so careless,/nremember that poisonous duck?"/n/nSpeeding back toward the lifts, Harry reviewed his/noptions. It had never been likely that the locket was/nhere at the Ministry, and there was no hope of/nbewitching its whereabouts out of Umbridge while she/nwas sitting in a crowded court. Their priority now had/nto be to leave the Ministry before they were exposed,/nand try again another day. The first thing to do was to/nfind Ron, and then they could work out a way of/nextracting Hermione from the courtroom./n/nThe lift was empty when it arrived. Harry jumped in/nand pulled off the Invisibility Cloak as it started its/ndescent. To his enormous relief, when it rattled to a/nhalt at level two, a soaking-wet and wild-eyed Ron got/nin./n/n/n/n"M-morning," he stammered to Harry as the lift set off/nagain./n/n"Ron, it's me, Harry!"/n/n"Harry! Blimey, I forgot what you looked like — why/nisn't Hermione with you?"/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"She had to go down to the courtrooms with/nUmbridge, she couldn't refuse, and — "/n/nBut before Harry could finish the lift had stopped/nagain: The doors opened and Mr. Weasley walked/ninside, talking to an elderly witch whose blonde hair/nwas teased so high it resembled an anthill./n/n"... I quite understand what you're saying, Wakanda,/nbut I'm afraid I cannot be party to — "/n/nMr. Weasley broke off; he had noticed Harry. It was/nvery strange to have Mr. Weasley glare at him with/nthat much dislike. The lift doors closed and the four/nof them trundled downward once more./n/n"Oh, hello, Reg," said Mr. Weasley, looking around at/nthe sound of steady dripping from Ron's robes. "Isn't/nyour wife in for questioning today? Er — what's/nhappened to you? Why are you so wet?"/n/n"Yaxley's office is raining," said Ron. He addressed/nMr. Weasley's shoulder, and Harry felt sure he was/nscared that his father might recognize him if they/nlooked directly into each other's eyes. "I couldn't stop/nit, so they've sent me to get Bernie — Pillsworth, I/nthink they said — "/n/n"Yes, a lot of offices have been raining lately," said Mr./nWeasley. "Did you try Meteolojinx Recanto? It worked/nfor Bletchley."/n/n"Meteolojinx Recanto?" whispered Ron. "No, I didn't./nThanks, D — I mean, thanks, Arthur."/n/nThe lift doors opened; the old witch with the anthill/nhair left, and Ron darted past her out of sight. Harry/nmade to follow him, but found his path blocked as/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nPercy Weasley strode into the lift, his nose buried in/nsome papers he was reading./n/n/n/nNot until the doors had clanged shut again did Percy/nrealize he was in a lift with his father. He glanced up,/nsaw Mr. Weasley, turned radish red, and left the lift/nthe moment the doors opened again. For the second/ntime, Harry tried to get out, but this time found his/nway blocked by Mr. Weasley's arm./n/n"One moment, Runcorn."/n/nThe lift doors closed and as they clanked down/nanother floor, Mr. Weasley said, "I hear you laid/ninformation about Dirk Cresswell."/n/nHarry had the impression that Mr. Weasley's anger/nwas no less because of the brush with Percy. He/ndecided his best chance was to act stupid./n/n"Sorry?" he said./n/n"Don't pretend, Runcorn," said Mr. Weasley fiercely./n"You tracked down the wizard who faked his family/ntree, didn't you?"/n/n"I — so what if I did?" said Harry./n/n"So Dirk Cresswell is ten times the wizard you are,"/nsaid Mr. Weasley quietly, as the lift sank ever lower./n"And if he survives Azkaban, you 11 have to answer to/nhim, not to mention his wife, his sons, and his friends/n/n/n/n"Arthur," Harry interrupted, "you know you're being/ntracked, don't you?"/n/n"Is that a threat, Runcorn?" said Mr. Weasley loudly./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"No," said Harry, "it's a fact! They're watching your/nevery move — "/n/nThe lift doors opened. They had reached the Atrium./nMr. Weasley gave Harry a scathing look and swept/nfrom the lift. Harry stood there, shaken. He wished he/nwas impersonating somebody other than Runcorn. .../nThe lift doors clanged shut./n/nHarry pulled out the Invisibility Cloak and put it back/non. He would try to extricate Hermione on his own/nwhile Ron was dealing with the raining office. When/nthe doors opened, he stepped out into a torch-lit/nstone passageway quite different from the wood-/npaneled and carpeted corridors above. As the lift/nrattled away again, Harry shivered slightly, looking/ntoward the distant black door that marked the/nentrance to the Department of Mysteries./n/nHe set off, his destination not the black door, but the/ndoorway he remembered on the left-hand side, which/nopened onto the flight of stairs down to the court/nchambers. His mind grappled with possibilities as he/ncrept down them: He still had a couple of Decoy/nDetonators, but perhaps it would be better to simply/nknock on the courtroom door, enter as Runcorn, and/nask for a quick word with Mafalda? Of course, he did/nnot know whether Runcorn was sufficiently important/nto get away with this, and even if he managed it,/nHermione 's non-reappearance might trigger a search/nbefore they were clear of the Ministry. . . ./n/nLost in thought, he did not immediately register the/nunnatural chill that was creeping over him, as if he/nwere descending into fog. It was becoming colder and/ncolder with every step he took: a cold that reached/nright down into his throat and tore at his lungs. And/nthen he felt that stealing sense of despair, of/nhopelessness, filling him, expanding inside him. .../n/n/n/n/nDementors, he thought./n/n/n/nAnd as he reached the foot of the stairs and turned to/nhis right he saw a dreadful scene. The dark passage/noutside the courtrooms was packed with tall, black-/nhooded figures, their faces completely hidden, their/nragged breathing the only sound in the place. The/npetrified Muggle-borns brought in for questioning sat/nhuddled and shivering on hard wooden benches. Most/nof them were hiding their faces in their hands,/nperhaps in an instinctive attempt to shield themselves/nfrom the dementors' greedy mouths. Some were/naccompanied by families, others sat alone. The/ndementors were gliding up and down in front of them,/nand the cold, and the hopelessness, and the despair/nof the place laid themselves upon Harry like a curse./n/n/n/nFight it, he told himself, but he knew that he could/nnot conjure a Patronus here without revealing himself/ninstantly. So he moved forward as silently as he/ncould, and with every step he took numbness seemed/nto steal over his brain, but he forced himself to think/nof Hermione and of Ron, who needed him./n/nMoving through the towering black figures was/nterrifying: The eyeless faces hidden beneath their/nhoods turned as he passed, and he felt sure that they/nsensed him, sensed, perhaps, a human presence that/nstill had some hope, some resilience. .../n/nAnd then, abruptly and shockingly amid the frozen/nsilence, one of the dungeon doors on the left of the/ncorridor was flung open and screams echoed out of it./n/n"No, no, I'm half-blood, I'm half-blood, I tell you! My/nfather was a wizard, he was, look him up, Arkie/nAlderton, he's a well-known broomstick designer, look/n/n/n/n/n/nhim up, I tell you — get your hands off me, get your/nhands off—"/n/n/n/n"This is your final warning," said Umbridge's soft/nvoice, magically magnified so that it sounded clearly/nover the man's desperate screams. "If you struggle,/nyou will be subjected to the Dementor's Kiss."/n/nThe man's screams subsided, but dry sobs echoed/nthrough the corridor./n/n"Take him away," said Umbridge./n/nTwo dementors appeared in the doorway of the/ncourtroom, their rotting, scabbed hands clutching the/nupper arms of a wizard who appeared to be fainting./nThey glided away down the corridor with him, and the/ndarkness they trailed behind them swallowed him/nfrom sight./n/n"Next — Mary Cattermole," called Umbridge./n/nA small woman stood up; she was trembling from/nhead to foot. Her dark hair was smoothed back into a/nbun and she wore long, plain robes. Her face was/ncompletely bloodless. As she passed the dementors,/nHarry saw her shudder./n/nHe did it instinctively, without any sort of plan,/nbecause he hated the sight of her walking alone into/nthe dungeon: As the door began to swing closed, he/nslipped into the courtroom behind her./n/nIt was not the same room in which he had once been/ninterrogated for improper use of magic. This one was/nmuch smaller, though the ceiling was quite as high; it/ngave the claustrophobic sense of being stuck at the/nbottom of a deep well./n/n/n/n/n/nThere were more dementors in here, casting their/nfreezing aura over the place; they stood like faceless/nsentinels in the corners farthest from the high, raised/nplatform. Here, behind a balustrade, sat Umbridge,/nwith Yaxley on one side of her, and Hermione, quite/nas white-faced as Mrs. Cattermole, on the other. At/nthe foot of the platform, a bright-silver, long-haired/ncat prowled up and down, up and down, and Harry/nrealized that it was there to protect the prosecutors/nfrom the despair that emanated from the dementors:/nThat was for the accused to feel, not the accusers./n/n"Sit down," said Umbridge in her soft, silky voice./n/nMrs. Cattermole stumbled to the single seat in the/nmiddle of the floor beneath the raised platform. The/nmoment she had sat down, chains clinked out of the/narms of the chair and bound her there./n/n"You are Mary Elizabeth Cattermole?" asked/nUmbridge./n/nMrs. Cattermole gave a single, shaky nod./n/n"Married to Reginald Cattermole of the Magical/nMaintenance Department?"/n/nMrs. Cattermole burst into tears./n/n"I don't know where he is, he was supposed to meet/nme here!"/n/nUmbridge ignored her./n/n"Mother to Maisie, Ellie, and Alfred Cattermole?"/n/nMrs. Cattermole sobbed harder than ever./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"They're frightened, they think I might not come home/n/n/n/n"Spare us," spat Yaxley. "The brats of Mudbloods do/nnot stir our sympathies."/n/nMrs. Cattermole's sobs masked Harry's footsteps as/nhe made his way carefully toward the steps that led/nup to the raised platform. The moment he had passed/nthe place where the Patronus cat patrolled, he felt the/nchange in temperature: It was warm and comfortable/nhere. The Patronus, he was sure, was Umbridge's,/nand it glowed brightly because she was so happy/nhere, in her element, upholding the twisted laws she/nhad helped to write. Slowly and very carefully he/nedged his way along the platform behind Umbridge,/nYaxley, and Hermione, taking a seat behind the latter./nHe was worried about making Hermione jump. He/nthought of casting the Muffliato charm upon/nUmbridge and Yaxley, but even murmuring the word/nmight cause Hermione alarm. Then Umbridge raised/nher voice to address Mrs. Cattermole, and Harry/nseized his chance./n/n"I'm behind you," he whispered into Hermione's ear./n/nAs he had expected, she jumped so violently she/nnearly overturned the bottle of ink with which she/nwas supposed to be recording the interview, but both/nUmbridge and Yaxley were concentrating upon Mrs./nCattermole, and this went unnoticed./n/n"A wand was taken from you upon your arrival at the/nMinistry today, Mrs. Cattermole," Umbridge was/nsaying. "Eight-and-three-quarter inches, cherry,/nunicorn-hair core. Do you recognize that description?"/n/nMrs. Cattermole nodded, mopping her eyes on her/nsleeve./n/n/n/n/n/n"Could you please tell us from which witch or wizard/nyou took that wand?"/n/n/n/n"T-took?" sobbed Mrs. Cattermole. "I didn't t-take it/nfrom anybody. I b-bought it when I was eleven years/nold. It — it — it — chose me."/n/nShe cried harder than ever./n/nUmbridge laughed a soft girlish laugh that made/nHarry want to attack her. She leaned forward over the/nbarrier, the better to observe her victim, and/nsomething gold swung forward too, and dangled over/nthe void: the locket./n/nHermione had seen it; she let out a little squeak, but/nUmbridge and Yaxley, still intent upon their prey,/nwere deaf to everything else./n/n"No," said Umbridge, "no, I don't think so, Mrs./nCattermole. Wands only choose witches or wizards./nYou are not a witch. I have your responses to the/nquestionnaire that was sent to you here — Mafalda,/npass them to me."/n/nUmbridge held out a small hand: She looked so/ntoadlike at that moment that Harry was quite/nsurprised not to see webs between the stubby fingers./nHermione 's hands were shaking with shock. She/nfumbled in a pile of documents balanced on the chair/nbeside her, finally withdrawing a sheaf of parchment/nwith Mrs. Cattermole's name on it./n/n"That's — that's pretty, Dolores," she said, pointing at/nthe pendant gleaming in the ruffled folds of/nUmbridge's blouse./n/n"What?" snapped Umbridge, glancing down. "Oh yes/n— an old family heirloom," she said, patting the locket/n/n/n/n/n/nlying on her large bosom. "The S stands for Selwyn. .../nI am related to the Selwyns. ... Indeed, there are few/npure-blood families to whom I am not related. ... A/npity," she continued in a louder voice, flicking/nthrough Mrs. Cattermole's questionnaire, "that the/nsame cannot be said for you. 'Parents' professions:/ngreengrocers.' "/n/nYaxley laughed jeeringly. Below, the fluffy silver cat/npatrolled up and down, and the dementors stood/nwaiting in the corners./n/nIt was Umbridge's lie that brought the blood surging/ninto Harry's brain and obliterated his sense of caution/n— that the locket she had taken as a bribe from a/npetty criminal was being used to bolster her own/npure-blood credentials. He raised his wand, not even/ntroubling to keep it concealed beneath the Invisibility/nCloak, and said, "Stupefyl"/n/nThere was a flash of red light; Umbridge crumpled/nand her forehead hit the edge of the balustrade: Mrs./nCattermole's papers slid off her lap onto the floor and,/ndown below, the prowling silver cat vanished. Ice-cold/nair hit them like an oncoming wind: Yaxley, confused,/nlooked around for the source of the trouble and saw/nHarry's disembodied hand and wand pointing at him./nHe tried to draw his own wand, but too late:/n/n"Stupefyl"/n/nYaxley slid to the ground to lie curled on the floor./n"Harry!"/n/n"Hermione, if you think I was going to sit here and let/nher pretend — "/n/n"Harry, Mrs. Cattermole!"/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nHarry whirled around, throwing off the Invisibility/nCloak; down below, the dementors had moved out of/ntheir corners; they were gliding toward the woman/nchained to the chair: Whether because the Patronus/nhad vanished or because they sensed that their/nmasters were no longer in control, they seemed to/nhave abandoned restraint. Mrs. Cattermole let out a/nterrible scream of fear as a slimy, scabbed hand/ngrasped her chin and forced her face back./n/n"EXPECTO PATRONUM"/n/nThe silver stag soared from the tip of Harry's wand/nand leaped toward the dementors, which fell back and/nmelted into the dark shadows again. The stag's light,/nmore powerful and more warming than the cat's/nprotection, filled the whole dungeon as it cantered/naround and around the room./n/n"Get the Horcrux," Harry told Hermione./n/nHe ran back down the steps, stuffing the Invisibility/nCloak back into his bag, and approached Mrs./nCattermole./n/n"You?" she whispered, gazing into his face. "But —/nbut Reg said you were the one who submitted my/nname for questioning!"/n/n"Did I?" muttered Harry, tugging at the chains/nbinding her arms. "Well, I've had a change of heart./nDiffindol" Nothing happened. "Hermione, how do I get/nrid of these chains?"/n/n"Wait, I'm trying something up here — "/n/n"Hermione, we're surrounded by dementors!"/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"I know that, Harry, but if she wakes up and the/nlocket's gone — I need to duplicate it — Geminio\/nThere ... That should fool her. ..."/n/n/n/nHermione came running downstairs./n/n"Let's see. ... Relashiol"/n/nThe chains clinked and withdrew into the arms of the/nchair. Mrs. Cattermole looked just as frightened as/never before./n/n"I don't understand," she whispered./n/n"You're going to leave here with us," said Harry,/npulling her to her feet. "Go home, grab your children,/nand get out, get out of the country if you've got to./nDisguise yourselves and run. You've seen how it is,/nyou won't get anything like a fair hearing here."/n/n"Harry," said Hermione, "how are we going to get out/nof here with all those dementors outside the door?"/n/n"Patronuses," said Harry, pointing his wand at his/nown: The stag slowed and walked, still gleaming/nbrightly, toward the door. "As many as we can/nmuster; do yours, Hermione."/n/n"Expec — Expecto patronum," said Hermione. Nothing/nhappened./n/n"It's the only spell she ever has trouble with," Harry/ntold a completely bemused Mrs. Cattermole. "Bit/nunfortunate, really ... Come on, Hermione. ..."/n/n"Expecto patronum)."/n/nA silver otter burst from the end of Hermione 's wand/nand swam gracefully through the air to join the stag./n/n/n/n/n/n"C'mon," said Harry, and he led Hermione and Mrs./nCattermole to the door./n/nWhen the Patronuses glided out of the dungeon there/nwere cries of shock from the people waiting outside./nHarry looked around; the dementors were falling back/non both sides of them, melding into the darkness,/nscattering before the silver creatures./n/n"It's been decided that you should all go home and go/ninto hiding with your families," Harry told the waiting/nMuggle-borns, who were dazzled by the light of the/nPatronuses and still cowering slightly. "Go abroad if/nyou can. Just get well away from the Ministry. That's/nthe — er — new official position. Now, if you'll just/nfollow the Patronuses, you'll be able to leave from the/nAtrium."/n/nThey managed to get up the stone steps without being/nintercepted, but as they approached the lifts Harry/nstarted to have misgivings. If they emerged into the/nAtrium with a silver stag, an otter soaring alongside/nit, and twenty or so people, half of them accused/nMuggle-borns, he could not help feeling that they/nwould attract unwanted attention. He had just/nreached this unwelcome conclusion when the lift/nclanged to a halt in front of them./n/n"Reg!" screamed Mrs. Cattermole, and she threw/nherself into Ron's arms. "Runcorn let me out, he/nattacked Umbridge and Yaxley, and he's told all of us/nto leave the country, I think we'd better do it, Reg, I/nreally do, let's hurry home and fetch the children and/n— why are you so wet?"/n/n"Water," muttered Ron, disengaging himself. "Harry,/nthey know there are intruders inside the Ministry,/nsomething about a hole in Umbridge's office door, I/nreckon we've got five minutes if that — "/n/n/n/n/n/nHermione 's Patronus vanished with a pop as she/nturned a horror-struck face to Harry./n/n"Harry, if we're trapped here — !"/n/n"We won't be if we move fast," said Harry. He/naddressed the silent group behind them, who were all/ngawping at him./n/n"Who's got wands?"/n/nAbout half of them raised their hands./n/n"Okay, all of you who haven't got wands need to/nattach yourself to somebody who has. We'll need to be/nfast before they stop us. Come on."/n/nThey managed to cram themselves into two lifts./nHarry's Patronus stood sentinel before the golden/ngrilles as they shut and the lifts began to rise./n/n"Level eight," said the witch's cool voice, "Atrium."/n/nHarry knew at once that they were in trouble. The/nAtrium was full of people moving from fireplace to/nfireplace, sealing them off./n/n"Harry!" squeaked Hermione. "What are we going to —/n?"/n/n"STOP!" Harry thundered, and the powerful voice of/nRuncorn echoed through the Atrium: The wizards/nsealing the fireplaces froze. "Follow me," he whispered/nto the group of terrified Muggle-borns, who moved/nforward in a huddle, shepherded by Ron and/nHermione./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"What's up, Albert?" said the same balding wizard/nwho had followed Harry out of the fireplace earlier. He/nlooked nervous./n/n/n/n"This lot need to leave before you seal the exits," said/nHarry with all the authority he could muster./n/nThe group of wizards in front of him looked at one/nanother./n/n"We've been told to seal all exits and not let anyone —/n/n/n/n" Are you contradicting me?" Harry blustered. "Would/nyou like me to have your family tree examined, like I/nhad Dirk Cresswell's?"/n/n"Sorry!" gasped the balding wizard, backing away. "I/ndidn't mean nothing, Albert, but I thought ... I/nthought they were in for questioning and ..."/n/n"Their blood is pure," said Harry, and his deep voice/nechoed impressively through the hall. "Purer than/nmany of yours, I daresay. Off you go," he boomed to/nthe Muggle-borns, who scurried forward into the/nfireplaces and began to vanish in pairs. The Ministry/nwizards hung back, some looking confused, others/nscared and resentful. Then:/n/n"Mary!"/n/nMrs. Cattermole looked over her shoulder. The real/nReg Cattermole, no longer vomiting but pale and wan,/nhad just come running out of a lift./n/n"R-Reg?"/n/nShe looked from her husband to Ron, who swore/nloudly./n/n/n/n/n/nThe balding wizard gaped, his head turning/nludicrously from one Reg Cattermole to the other./n/n/n/n"Hey — what's going on? What is this?"/n/n"Seal the exit! SEAL IT!"/n/nYaxley had burst out of another lift and was running/ntoward the group beside the fireplaces, into which all/nof the Muggle-borns but Mrs. Cattermole had now/nvanished. As the balding wizard lifted his wand, Harry/nraised an enormous fist and punched him, sending/nhim flying through the air./n/n"He's been helping Muggle-borns escape, Yaxley!"/nHarry shouted./n/nThe balding wizard's colleagues set up an uproar,/nunder cover of which Ron grabbed Mrs. Cattermole,/npulled her into the still-open fireplace, and/ndisappeared. Confused, Yaxley looked from Harry to/nthe punched wizard, while the real Reg Cattermole/nscreamed, "My wife! Who was that with my wife?/nWhat's going on?"/n/nHarry saw Yaxley's head turn, saw an inkling of the/ntruth dawn in that brutish face./n/n"Come on!" Harry shouted at Hermione; he seized her/nhand and they jumped into the fireplace together as/nYaxley's curse sailed over Harry's head. They spun for/na few seconds before shooting up out of a toilet into a/ncubicle. Harry flung open the door; Ron was standing/nthere beside the sinks, still wrestling with Mrs./nCattermole./n/n"Reg, I don't understand — "/n/n"Let go, I'm not your husband, you've got to go home!"/n/n/n/n/n/nThere was a noise in the cubicle behind them; Harry/nlooked around; Yaxley had just appeared./n/n"LET'S GO!" Harry yelled. He seized Hermione by the/nhand and Ron by the arm and turned on the spot./n/nDarkness engulfed them, along with the sensation of/ncompressing bands, but something was wrong. .../nHermione 's hand seemed to be sliding out of his grip./n/n/n/nHe wondered whether he was going to suffocate; he/ncould not breathe or see and the only solid things in/nthe world were Ron's arm and Hermione 's fingers,/nwhich were slowly slipping away. . . ./n/nAnd then he saw the door of number twelve,/nGrimmauld Place, with its serpent door knocker, but/nbefore he could draw breath, there was a scream and/na flash of purple light; Hermione 's hand was suddenly/nvicelike upon his and everything went dark again./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n

title: The Thief
text: /nHarry opened his eyes and was dazzled by gold and/ngreen; he had no idea what had happened, he only/nknew that he was lying on what seemed to be leaves/nand twigs. Struggling to draw breath into lungs that/nfelt flattened, he blinked and realized that the gaudy/nglare was sunlight streaming through a canopy of/nleaves far above him. Then an object twitched close to/nhis face. He pushed himself onto his hands and/nknees, ready to face some small, fierce creature, but/nsaw that the object was Ron's foot. Looking around,/nHarry saw that they and Hermione were lying on a/nforest floor, apparently alone./n/nHarry's first thought was of the Forbidden Forest, and/nfor a moment, even though he knew how foolish and/ndangerous it would be for them to appear in the/ngrounds of Hogwarts, his heart leapt at the thought of/nsneaking through the trees to Hagrid's hut. However,/nin the few moments it took for Ron to give a low groan/nand Harry to start crawling toward him, he realized/nthat this was not the Forbidden Forest: The trees/n/n/n/n/n/n/nlooked younger, they were more widely spaced, the/nground clearer./n/n/n/nHe met Hermione, also on her hands and knees, at/nRon's head. The moment his eyes fell upon Ron, all/nother concerns fled Harry's mind, for blood drenched/nthe whole of Ron's left side and his face stood out,/ngrayish- white, against the leaf-strewn earth. The/nPolyjuice Potion was wearing off now: Ron was/nhalfway between Cattermole and himself in/nappearance, his hair turning redder and redder as his/nface drained of the little color it had left./n/n"What's happened to him?"/n/n"Splinched," said Hermione, her fingers already busy/nat Ron's sleeve, where the blood was wettest and/ndarkest./n/nHarry watched, horrified, as she tore open Ron's/nshirt. He had always thought of Splinching as/nsomething comical, but this . . . His insides crawled/nunpleasantly as Hermione laid bare Ron's upper arm,/nwhere a great chunk of flesh was missing, scooped/ncleanly away as though by a knife./n/n"Harry, quickly, in my bag, there's a small bottle/nlabeled 'Essence of Dittany' — "/n/n"Bag — right — "/n/nHarry sped to the place where Hermione had landed,/nseized the tiny beaded bag, and thrust his hand/ninside it. At once, object after object began presenting/nitself to his touch: He felt the leather spines of books,/nwoolly sleeves of jumpers, heels of shoes —/n/n"Quickly\"/n/n/n/n/n/nHe grabbed his wand from the ground and pointed it/ninto the depths of the magical bag./n/n"Accio Dittany\"/n/nA small brown bottle zoomed out of the bag; he/ncaught it and hastened back to Hermione and Ron,/nwhose eyes were now half-closed, strips of white/neyeball all that were visible between his lids./n/n"He's fainted," said Hermione, who was also rather/npale; she no longer looked like Mafalda, though her/nhair was still gray in places. "Unstopper it for me,/nHarry, my hands are shaking."/n/nHarry wrenched the stopper off the little bottle,/nHermione took it and poured three drops of the potion/nonto the bleeding wound. Greenish smoke billowed/nupward and when it had cleared, Harry saw that the/nbleeding had stopped. The wound now looked several/ndays old; new skin stretched over what had just been/nopen flesh./n/n"Wow," said Harry./n/n"It's all I feel safe doing," said Hermione shakily./n"There are spells that would put him completely right,/nbut I daren't try in case I do them wrong and cause/nmore damage. ... He's lost so much blood already. ..."/n/n"How did he get hurt? I mean" — Harry shook his/nhead, trying to clear it, to make sense of whatever had/njust taken place — "why are we here? I thought we/nwere going back to Grimmauld Place?"/n/nHermione took a deep breath. She looked close to/ntears./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"Harry, I don't think we're going to be able to go back/nthere."/n/n"What d'you — ?"/n/n"As we Disapparated, Yaxley caught hold of me and I/ncouldn't get rid of him, he was too strong, and he was/nstill holding on when we arrived at Grimmauld Place,/nand then — well, I think he must have seen the door,/nand thought we were stopping there, so he slackened/nhis grip and I managed to shake him off and I brought/nus here instead!"/n/n"But then, where's he? Hang on. ... You don't mean/nhe's at Grimmauld Place? He can't get in there?"/n/nHer eyes sparkled with unshed tears as she nodded./n/n"Harry, I think he can. I — I forced him to let go with/na Revulsion Jinx, but I'd already taken him inside the/nFidelius Charm's protection. Since Dumbledore died,/nwe're Secret-Keepers, so I've given him the secret,/nhaven't I?"/n/nThere was no pretending; Harry was sure she was/nright. It was a serious blow. If Yaxley could now get/ninside the house, there was no way that they could/nreturn. Even now, he could be bringing other Death/nEaters in there by Apparition. Gloomy and oppressive/nthough the house was, it had been their one safe/nrefuge: even, now that Kreacher was so much happier/nand friendlier, a kind of home. With a twinge of regret/nthat had nothing to do with food, Harry imagined the/nhouse-elf busying himself over the steak-and-kidney/npie that Harry, Ron, and Hermione would never eat./n/n"Harry, I'm sorry, I'm so sorry!"/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"Don't be stupid, it wasn't your fault! If anything, it/nwas mine. ..."/n/nHarry put his hand in his pocket and drew out Mad-/nEye's eye. Hermione recoiled, looking horrified./n/n"Umbridge had stuck it to her office door, to spy on/npeople. I couldn't leave it there ... but that's how they/nknew there were intruders."/n/nBefore Hermione could answer, Ron groaned and/nopened his eyes. He was still gray and his face/nglistened with sweat./n/n"How d'you feel?" Hermione whispered./n/n"Lousy," croaked Ron, wincing as he felt his injured/narm. "Where are we?"/n/n"In the woods where they held the Quidditch World/nCup," said Hermione. "I wanted somewhere enclosed,/nundercover, and this was — "/n/n" — the first place you thought of," Harry finished for/nher, glancing around at the apparently deserted/nglade. He could not help remembering what had/nhappened the last time they had Apparated to the/nfirst place Hermione had thought of — how Death/nEaters had found them within minutes. Had it been/nLegilimency? Did Voldemort or his henchmen know,/neven now, where Hermione had taken them?/n/n"D'you reckon we should move on?" Ron asked Harry,/nand Harry could tell by the look on Ron's face that he/nwas thinking the same./n/n"I dunno."/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nRon still looked pale and clammy. He had made no/nattempt to sit up and it looked as though he was too/nweak to do so. The prospect of moving him was/ndaunting./n/n"Let's stay here for now," Harry said./n/nLooking relieved, Hermione sprang to her feet./n/n"Where are you going?" asked Ron./n/n"If we're staying, we should put some protective/nenchantments around the place," she replied, and/nraising her wand, she began to walk in a wide circle/naround Harry and Ron, murmuring incantations as/nshe went. Harry saw little disturbances in the/nsurrounding air: It was as if Hermione had cast a/nheat haze upon their clearing./n/n"Salvio Hexia ... Protego Totalum ... Repello Muggletum/n... Muffliato ... You could get out the tent, Harry. ..."/n/n"Tent?"/n/n"In the bag!"/n/n"In the ... of course," said Harry./n/nHe did not bother to grope inside it this time, but/nused another Summoning Charm. The tent emerged/nin a lumpy mass of canvas, rope, and poles. Harry/nrecognized it, partly because of the smell of cats, as/nthe same tent in which they had slept on the night of/nthe Quidditch World Cup./n/n"I thought this belonged to that bloke Perkins at the/nMinistry?" he asked, starting to disentangle the tent/npegs./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"Apparently he didn't want it back, his lumbago's so/nbad," said Hermione, now performing complicated/nfigure-of-eight movements with her wand, "so Ron's/ndad said I could borrow it. ErectoV' she added,/npointing her wand at the misshapen canvas, which in/none fluid motion rose into the air and settled, fully/nconstructed, onto the ground before Harry, out of/nwhose startled hands a tent peg soared, to land with/na final thud at the end of a guy rope./n/n" Cave Inimicum," Hermione finished with a skyward/nflourish. "That's as much as I can do. At the very/nleast, we should know they're coming, I can't/nguarantee it will keep out Vol — "/n/n"Don't say the name!"
