The heat/nfrom the enchanted treasure rose in waves, and sweat/nran down Harry's face and back as he struggled to/n/n/n/n/n/nthink of a way up to the cup; and then he heard the/ndragon roar on the other side of the vault door, and/nthe sound of clanking growing louder and louder./n/nThey were truly trapped now: There was no way out/nexcept through the door, and a horde of goblins/nseemed to be approaching on the other side. Harry/nlooked at Ron and Hermione and saw terror in their/nfaces./n/n"Hermione," said Harry as the clanking grew louder,/n"I've got to get up there, we've got to get rid of it — "/n/nShe raised her wand, pointed it at Harry, and/nwhispered, "Levicorpus."/n/nHoisted into the air by his ankle, Harry hit a suit of/narmor and replicas burst out of it like white-hot/nbodies, filling the cramped space. With screams of/npain Ron, Hermione, and the two goblins were/nknocked aside into other objects, which also began to/nreplicate. Half buried in a rising tide of red-hot/ntreasure, they struggled and yelled as Harry thrust/nthe sword through the handle of Hufflepuff's cup,/nhooking it onto the blade./n/n"Impervius\" screeched Hermione in an attempt to/nprotect herself, Ron, and the goblins from the burning/nmetal./n/nThen the worst scream yet made Harry look down:/n/nRon and Hermione were waist-deep in treasure,/nstruggling to keep Bogrod from slipping beneath the/nrising tide, but Griphook had sunk out of sight and/nnothing but the tips of a few long fingers were left in/nview./n/nHarry seized Griphook's fingers and pulled. The/nblistered goblin emerged by degrees, howling./n/n/n/n/n/n"Liberacorpus\" yelled Harry, and with a crash he and/nGriphook landed on the surface of the swelling/ntreasure, and the sword flew out of Harry's hand./n/n"Get it!" Harry yelled, fighting the pain of the hot/nmetal on his skin, as Griphook clambered onto his/nshoulders again, determined to avoid the swelling/nmass of red-hot objects. "Where's the sword? It had/nthe cup on it!"/n/nThe clanking on the other side of the door was/ngrowing deafening — it was too late —/n/n"There!"/n/nIt was Griphook who had seen it and Griphook who/nlunged, and in that instant Harry knew that the/ngoblin had never expected them to keep their word./nOne hand holding tightly to a fistful of Harry's hair, to/nmake sure he did not fall into the heaving sea of/nburning gold, Griphook seized the hilt of the sword/nand swung it high out of Harry's reach./n/nThe tiny golden cup, skewered by the handle on the/nsword's blade, was flung into the air. The goblin still/nastride him, Harry dived and caught it, and although/nhe could feel it scalding his flesh he did not relinquish/nit, even while countless Hufflepuff cups burst from/nhis fist, raining down upon him as the entrance of the/nvault opened up again and he found himself sliding/nuncontrollably on an expanding avalanche of fiery/ngold and silver that bore him, Ron, and Hermione into/nthe outer chamber./n/nHardly aware of the pain from the burns covering his/nbody, and still borne along on the swell of replicating/ntreasure, Harry shoved the cup into his pocket and/nreached up to retrieve the sword, but Griphook was/ngone. Sliding from Harry's shoulders the moment he/n/n/n/n/ncould, he had sprinted for cover amongst the/nsurrounding goblins, brandishing the sword and/ncrying, "Thieves! Thieves! Help! Thieves!" He vanished/ninto the midst of the advancing crowd, all of whom/nwere holding daggers and who accepted him without/nquestion./n/nSlipping on the hot metal, Harry struggled to his feet/nand knew that the only way out was through./n/n"Stupefyl" he bellowed, and Ron and Hermione joined/nin: Jets of red light flew into the crowd of goblins, and/nsome toppled over, but others advanced, and Harry/nsaw several wizard guards running around the/ncorner./n/nThe tethered dragon let out a roar, and a gush of/nflame flew over the goblins: The wizards fled, doubled-/nup, back the way they had come, and inspiration, or/nmadness, came to Harry. Pointing his wand at the/nthick cuffs chaining the beast to the floor, he yelled,/n"Relashiol"/n/nThe cuffs broke open with loud bangs./n/n"This way!" Harry yelled, and still shooting Stunning/nSpells at the advancing goblins, he sprinted toward/nthe blind dragon./n/n"Harry — Harry — what are you doing?" cried/nHermione./n/n"Get up, climb up, come on — "/n/nThe dragon had not realized that it was free: Harry's/nfoot found the crook of its hind leg and he pulled/nhimself up onto its back. The scales were hard as/nsteel; it did not even seem to feel him. He stretched/nout an arm; Hermione hoisted herself up; Ron/n/n/n/n/nclimbed on behind them, and a second later the/ndragon became aware that it was untethered./n/nWith a roar it reared: Harry dug in his knees,/nclutching as tightly as he could to the jagged scales/nas the wings opened, knocking the shrieking goblins/naside like skittles, and it soared into the air. Harry,/nRon, and Hermione, flat on its back, scraped against/nthe ceiling as it dived toward the passage opening,/nwhile the pursuing goblins hurled daggers that/nglanced off its flanks./n/n"Well never get out, it's too big!" Hermione screamed,/nbut the dragon opened its mouth and belched flame/nagain, blasting the tunnel, whose floors and ceiling/ncracked and crumbled. By sheer force the dragon/nclawed and fought its way through. Harry's eyes were/nshut tight against the heat and dust: Deafened by the/ncrashing of rock and the dragon's roars, he could only/ncling to its back, expecting to be shaken off at any/nmoment; then he heard Hermione yelling, "Defodiol"/n/nShe was helping the dragon enlarge the passageway,/ncarving out the ceiling as it struggled upward toward/nthe fresher air, away from the shrieking and clanking/ngoblins: Harry and Ron copied her, blasting the/nceiling apart with more gouging spells. They passed/nthe underground lake, and the great crawling,/nsnarling beast seemed to sense freedom and space/nahead of it, and behind them the passage was full of/nthe dragon's thrashing, spiked tail, of great lumps of/nrock, gigantic fractured stalactites, and the clanking/nof the goblins seemed to be growing more muffled,/nwhile ahead, the dragon's fire kept their progress/nclear —/n/nAnd then at last, by the combined force of their spells/nand the dragon's brute strength, they had blasted/ntheir way out of the passage into the marble hallway./n/n/n/n/n/nGoblins and wizards shrieked and ran for cover, and/nfinally the dragon had room to stretch its wings:/nTurning its horned head toward the cool outside air it/ncould smell beyond the entrance, it took off, and with/nHarry, Ron, and Hermione still clinging to its back, it/nforced its way through the metal doors, leaving them/nbuckled and hanging from their hinges, as it/nstaggered into Diagon Alley and launched itself into/nthe sky./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n

title: The Final Hiding Place
text: /nThere was no means of steering; the dragon could not/nsee where it was going, and Harry knew that if it/nturned sharply or rolled in midair they would find it/nimpossible to cling onto its broad back. Nevertheless,/nas they climbed higher and higher, London unfurling/nbelow them like a gray-and-green map, Harry's/noverwhelming feeling was of gratitude for an escape/nthat had seemed impossible. Crouching low over the/nbeast's neck, he clung tight to the metallic scales, and/nthe cool breeze was soothing on his burned and/nblistered skin, the dragon's wings beating the air like/nthe sails of a windmill. Behind him, whether from/ndelight or fear he could not tell, Ron kept swearing at/nthe top of his voice, and Hermione seemed to be/nsobbing./n/nAfter five minutes or so, Harry lost some of his/nimmediate dread that the dragon was going to throw/nthem off, for it seemed intent on nothing but getting/nas far away from its underground prison as possible;/nbut the question of how and when they were to/ndismount remained rather frightening. He had no idea/n/n/n/n/nhow long dragons could fly without landing, nor how/nthis particular dragon, which could barely see, would/nlocate a good place to put down. He glanced around/nconstantly, imagining that he could feel his scar/nprickling. .../n/nHow long would it be before Voldemort knew that they/nhad broken into the Lestranges' vault? How soon/nwould the goblins of Gringotts notify Bellatrix? How/nquickly would they realize what had been taken? And/nthen, when they discovered that the golden cup was/nmissing? Voldemort would know, at last, that they/nwere hunting Horcruxes. .../n/nThe dragon seemed to crave cooler and fresher air: It/nclimbed steadily until they were flying through wisps/nof chilly cloud, and Harry could no longer make out/nthe little colored dots which were cars pouring in and/nout of the capital. On and on they flew, over/ncountryside parceled out in patches of green and/nbrown, over roads and rivers winding through the/nlandscape like strips of matte and glossy ribbon./n/n"What do you reckon it's looking for?" Ron yelled as/nthey flew farther and farther north./n/n"No idea," Harry bellowed back. His hands were numb/nwith cold but he did not dare attempt to shift his grip./nHe had been wondering for some time what they/nwould do if they saw the coast sail beneath them, if/nthe dragon headed for open sea; he was cold and/nnumb, not to mention desperately hungry and thirsty./nWhen, he wondered, had the beast itself last eaten?/nSurely it would need sustenance before long? And/nwhat if, at that point, it realized it had three highly/nedible humans sitting on its back?/n/nThe sun slipped lower in the sky, which was turning/nindigo; and still the dragon flew, cities and towns/n/n/n/n/n/ngliding out of sight beneath them, its enormous/nshadow sliding over the earth like a great dark cloud./nEvery part of Harry ached with the effort of holding on/nto the dragon's back./n/n"Is it my imagination," shouted Ron after a/nconsiderable stretch of silence, "or are we losing/nheight?"/n/nHarry looked down and saw deep green mountains/nand lakes, coppery in the sunset. The landscape/nseemed to grow larger and more detailed as he/nsquinted over the side of the dragon, and he/nwondered whether it had divined the presence of fresh/nwater by the flashes of reflected sunlight./n/nLower and lower the dragon flew, in great spiraling/ncircles, honing in, it seemed, upon one of the smaller/nlakes./n/n"I say we jump when it gets low enough!" Harry called/nback to the others. "Straight into the water before it/nrealizes we're here!"/n/nThey agreed, Hermione a little faintly, and now Harry/ncould see the dragon's wide yellow underbelly rippling/nin the surface of the water./n/n"NOW!"/n/nHe slithered over the side of the dragon and/nplummeted feetfirst toward the surface of the lake;/nthe drop was greater than he had estimated and he/nhit the water hard, plunging like a stone into a/nfreezing, green, reed-filled world. He kicked toward/nthe surface and emerged, panting, to see enormous/nripples emanating in circles from the places where/nRon and Hermione had fallen. The dragon did not/nseem to have noticed anything: It was already fifty/n/n/n/n/nfeet away, swooping low over the lake to scoop up/nwater in its scarred snout. As Ron and Hermione/nemerged, spluttering and gasping, from the depths of/nthe lake, the dragon flew on, its wings beating hard,/nand landed at last on a distant bank./n/nHarry, Ron, and Hermione struck out for the opposite/nshore. The lake did not seem to be deep: Soon it was/nmore a question of fighting their way through reeds/nand mud than swimming, and at last they flopped,/nsodden, panting, and exhausted, onto slippery grass./n/nHermione collapsed, coughing and shuddering./nThough Harry could have happily lain down and/nslept, he staggered to his feet, drew out his wand, and/nstarted casting the usual protective spells around/nthem./n/nWhen he had finished, he joined the others. It was the/nfirst time that he had seen them properly since/nescaping from the vault. Both had angry red burns all/nover their faces and arms, and their clothing was/nsinged away in places. They were wincing as they/ndabbed essence of dittany onto their many injuries./nHermione handed Harry the bottle, then pulled out/nthree bottles of pumpkin juice she had brought from/nShell Cottage and clean, dry robes for all of them./n/nThey changed and then gulped down the juice./n/n"Well, on the upside," said Ron finally, who was/nsitting watching the skin on his hands regrow, "we got/nthe Horcrux. On the downside — "/n/n" — no sword," said Harry through gritted teeth, as he/ndripped dittany through the singed hole in his jeans/nonto the angry burn beneath./n/n"No sword," repeated Ron. "That double-crossing little/nscab ..."/n/n/n/n/n/nHarry pulled the Horcrux from the pocket of the wet/njacket he had just taken off and set it down on the/ngrass in front of them. Glinting in the sun, it drew/ntheir eyes as they swigged their bottles of juice./n/n"At least we can't wear it this time, that'd look a bit/nweird hanging round our necks," said Ron, wiping his/nmouth on the back of his hand./n/nHermione looked across the lake to the far bank,/nwhere the dragon was still drinking./n/n"What'll happen to it, do you think?" she asked. "Will/nit be all right?"/n/n"You sound like Hagrid," said Ron. "It's a dragon,/nHermione, it can look after itself. It's us we need to/nworry about."/n/n"What do you mean?"/n/n"Well, I don't know how to break this to you," said/nRon, "but I think they might have noticed we broke/ninto Gringotts."/n/nAll three of them started to laugh, and once started, it/nwas difficult to stop. Harry's ribs ached, he felt/nlightheaded with hunger, but he lay back on the grass/nbeneath the reddening sky and laughed until his/nthroat was raw./n/n"What are we going to do, though?" said Hermione/nfinally, hiccuping herself back to seriousness. "He'll/nknow, won't he? You- Know- Who will know we know/nabout his Horcruxes!"/n/n"Maybe they'll be too scared to tell him?" said Ron/nhopefully. "Maybe they'll cover up — "/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nThe sky, the smell of lake water, the sound of Ron's/nvoice were extinguished: Pain cleaved Harry's head/nlike a sword stroke. He was standing in a dimly lit/nroom, and a semicircle of wizards faced him, and on/nthe floor at his feet knelt a small, quaking figure./n/n"What did you say to me?" His voice was high and/ncold, but fury and fear burned inside him. The one/nthing he had dreaded — but it could not be true, he/ncould not see how .../n/nThe goblin was trembling, unable to meet the red eyes/nhigh above his./n/n"Say it again!" murmured Voldemort. " Say it again)."/n/n"M-my Lord," stammered the goblin, its black eyes/nwide with terror, "m-my Lord ... we t-tried t-to st-stop/nthem. ... Im-impostors, my Lord ... broke — broke/ninto the — into the Lestranges' v-vault. ..."/n/n"Impostors? What impostors? I thought Gringotts had/nways of revealing impostors? Who were they?"/n/n"It was ... it was . . . the P-Potter b-boy and t-two/naccomplices. ..."/n/n"And they took?" he said, his voice rising, a terrible/nfear gripping him. "Tell me! What did they take?"/n/n"A ... a s-small golden c-cup, m-my Lord ..."/n/nThe scream of rage, of denial left him as if it were a/nstranger's: He was crazed, frenzied, it could not be/ntrue, it was impossible, nobody had ever known: How/nwas it possible that the boy could have discovered his/nsecret?/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nThe Elder Wand slashed through the air and green/nlight erupted through the room; the kneeling goblin/nrolled over, dead; the watching wizards scattered/nbefore him, terrified: Bellatrix and Lucius Malfoy/nthrew others behind them in their race for the door,/nand again and again his wand fell, and those who/nwere left were slain, all of them, for bringing him this/nnews, for hearing about the golden cup —/n/nAlone amongst the dead he stormed up and down,/nand they passed before him in vision: his treasures,/nhis safeguards, his anchors to immortality — the/ndiary was destroyed and the cup was stolen: What if,/nwhat if, the boy knew about the others? Could he/nknow, had he already acted, had he traced more of/nthem? Was Dumbledore at the root of this?/nDumbledore, who had always suspected him;/nDumbledore, dead on his orders; Dumbledore, whose/nwand was his now, yet who reached out from the/nignominy of death through the boy, the boy —/n/nBut surely if the boy had destroyed any of his/nHorcruxes, he, Lord Voldemort, would have known,/nwould have felt it? He, the greatest wizard of them all;/nhe, the most powerful; he, the killer of Dumbledore/nand of how many other worthless, nameless men:/nHow could Lord Voldemort not have known, if he,/nhimself, most important and precious, had been/nattacked, mutilated?/n/nTrue, he had not felt it when the diary had been/ndestroyed, but he had thought that was because he/nhad no body to feel, being less than ghost. ... No,/nsurely, the rest were safe. ... The other Horcruxes/nmust be intact. .../n/nBut he must know, he must be sure. ... He paced the/nroom, kicking aside the goblin's corpse as he passed,/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nand the pictures blurred and burned in his boiling/nbrain: the lake, the shack, and Hogwarts —/n/nA modicum of calm cooled his rage now: How could/nthe boy know that he had hidden the ring in the/nGaunt shack? No one had ever known him to be/nrelated to the Gaunts, he had hidden the connection,/nthe killings had never been traced to him: The ring,/nsurely, was safe./n/nAnd how could the boy, or anybody else, know about/nthe cave or penetrate its protection? The idea of the/nlocket being stolen was absurd. .../n/nAs for the school: He alone knew where in Hogwarts/nhe had stowed the Horcrux, because he alone had/nplumbed the deepest secrets of that place. .../n/nAnd there was still Nagini, who must remain close/nnow, no longer sent to do his bidding, under his/nprotection. .../n/nBut to be sure, to be utterly sure, he must return to/neach of his hiding places, he must redouble protection/naround each of his Horcruxes. ... A job, like the quest/nfor the Elder Wand, that he must undertake alone .../n/nWhich should he visit first, which was in most/ndanger? An old unease flickered inside him./nDumbledore had known his middle name. .../nDumbledore might have made the connection with/nthe Gaunts. ... Their abandoned home was, perhaps,/nthe least secure of his hiding places, it was there that/nhe would go first. .../n/nThe lake, surely impossible ... though was there a/nslight possibility that Dumbledore might have known/nsome of his past misdeeds, through the orphanage./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nAnd Hogwarts . . . but he knew that his Horcrux there/nwas safe; it would be impossible for Potter to enter/nHogsmeade without detection, let alone the school./nNevertheless, it would be prudent to alert Snape to/nthe fact that the boy might try to reenter the castle. .../nTo tell Snape why the boy might return would be/nfoolish, of course; it had been a grave mistake to trust/nBellatrix and Malfoy: Didn't their stupidity and/ncarelessness prove how unwise it was ever to trust?/n/nHe would visit the Gaunt shack first, then, and take/nNagini with him: He would not be parted from the/nsnake anymore . . . and he strode from the room,/nthrough the hall, and out into the dark garden where/nthe fountain played; he called the snake in/nParseltongue and it slithered out to join him like a/nlong shadow. .../n/nHarry's eyes flew open as he wrenched himself back/nto the present: He was lying on the bank of the lake in/nthe setting sun, and Ron and Hermione were looking/ndown at him. Judging by their worried looks, and by/nthe continued pounding of his scar, his sudden/nexcursion into Voldemort's mind had not passed/nunnoticed. He struggled up, shivering, vaguely/nsurprised that he was still wet to his skin, and saw/nthe cup lying innocently in the grass before him, and/nthe lake, deep blue shot with gold in the failing sun./n/n"He knows." His own voice sounded strange and low/nafter Voldemort's high screams. "He knows, and he's/ngoing to check where the others are, and the last/none," he was already on his feet, "is at Hogwarts. I/nknew it. I knew it."/n/n"What?"/n/nRon was gaping at him; Hermione sat up, looking/nworried./n/n/n/n/n/n"But what did you see? How do you know?"/n/n/n/n"I saw him find out about the cup, I — I was in his/nhead, he's" — Harry remembered the killings — "he's/nseriously angry, and scared too, he can't understand/nhow we knew, and now he's going to check the others/nare safe, the ring first. He thinks the Hogwarts one is/nsafest, because Snape's there, because it'll be so hard/nnot to be seen getting in, I think he'll check that one/nlast, but he could still be there within hours — "/n/n"Did you see where in Hogwarts it is?" asked Ron,/nnow scrambling to his feet too./n/n"No, he was concentrating on warning Snape, he/ndidn't think about exactly where it is — "/n/n"Wait, wait\" cried Hermione as Ron caught up the/nHorcrux and Harry pulled out the Invisibility Cloak/nagain. "We can't just go, we haven't got a plan, we/nneed to — "/n/n"We need to get going," said Harry firmly. He had/nbeen hoping to sleep, looking forward to getting into/nthe new tent, but that was impossible now. "Can you/nimagine what he's going to do once he realizes the/nring and the locket are gone? What if he moves the/nHogwarts Horcrux, decides it isn't safe enough?"/n/n"But how are we going to get in?"/n/n"Well go to Hogsmeade," said Harry, "and try to work/nsomething out once we see what the protection/naround the school's like. Get under the Cloak,/nHermione, I want to stick together this time."/n/n"But we don't really fit — "/n/n"It'll be dark, no one's going to notice our feet."/n/n/n/n/n/nThe flapping of enormous wings echoed across the/nblack water: The dragon had drunk its fill and risen/ninto the air. They paused in their preparations to/nwatch it climb higher and higher, now black against/nthe rapidly darkening sky, until it vanished over a/nnearby mountain. Then Hermione walked forward/nand took her place between the other two. Harry/npulled the Cloak down as far as it would go, and/ntogether they turned on the spot into the crushing/ndarkness./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n

title: The Missing Mirror
text: /nHarry's feet touched road. He saw the achingly/nfamiliar Hogsmeade High Street: dark shop fronts,/nand the outline of black mountains beyond the/nvillage, and the curve in the road ahead that led off/ntoward Hogwarts, and light spilling from the windows/nof the Three Broomsticks, and with a lurch of the/nheart he remembered, with piercing accuracy, how he/nhad landed here nearly a year before, supporting a/ndesperately weak Dumbledore; all this in a second,/nupon landing — and then, even as he relaxed his grip/nupon Ron's and Hermione's arms, it happened./n/nThe air was rent by a scream that sounded like/nVoldemort's when he had realized the cup had been/nstolen: It tore at every nerve in Harry's body, and he/nknew immediately that their appearance had caused/nit. Even as he looked at the other two beneath the/nCloak, the door of the Three Broomsticks burst open/nand a dozen cloaked and hooded Death Eaters/ndashed into the street, their wands aloft./n/n/n/n/n/n/nHarry seized Ron's wrist as he raised his wand; there/nwere too many of them to Stun: Even attempting it/nwould give away their position. One of the Death/nEaters waved his wand and the scream stopped, still/nechoing around the distant mountains./n/n"Accio Cloak)." roared one of the Death Eaters./n/nHarry seized its folds, but it made no attempt to/nescape: The Summoning Charm had not worked on it./n/n"Not under your wrapper, then, Potter?" yelled the/nDeath Eater who had tried the charm, and then to his/nfellows, "Spread out. He's here."/n/nSix of the Death Eaters ran toward them: Harry, Ron,/nand Hermione backed as quickly as possible down the/nnearest side street, and the Death Eaters missed/nthem by inches. They waited in the darkness,/nlistening to the footsteps running up and down,/nbeams of light flying along the street from the Death/nEaters' searching wands./n/n"Let's just leave!" Hermione whispered. "Disapparate/nnow!"/n/n"Great idea," said Ron, but before Harry could reply a/nDeath Eater shouted,/n/n"We know you're here, Potter, and there's no getting/naway! We'll find you!"/n/n"They were ready for us," whispered Harry. "They set/nup that spell to tell them we'd come. I reckon they've/ndone something to keep us here, trap us — "/n/n"What about dementors?" called another Death Eater./n"Let 'em have free rein, they'd find him quick enough!"/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"The Dark Lord wants Potter dead by no hand but his/n/n/n/n" — an' dementors won't kill him! The Dark Lord/nwants Potter's life, not his soul. He'll be easier to kill if/nhe's been Kissed first!"/n/nThere were noises of agreement. Dread filled Harry:/n/nTo repel dementors they would have to produce/nPatronuses, which would give them away/nimmediately./n/n"We're going to have to try to Disapparate, Harry!"/nHermione whispered./n/nEven as she said it, he felt the unnatural cold begin to/nsteal over the street. Light was sucked from the/nenvironment right up to the stars, which vanished. In/nthe pitch-blackness, he felt Hermione take hold of his/narm and together, they turned on the spot./n/nThe air through which they needed to move seemed to/nhave become solid: They could not Disapparate; the/nDeath Eaters had cast their charms well. The cold/nwas biting deeper and deeper into Harry's flesh. He,/nRon, and Hermione retreated down the side street,/ngroping their way along the wall, trying not to make a/nsound. Then, around the corner, gliding noiselessly,/ncame dementors, ten or more of them, visible because/nthey were of a denser darkness than their/nsurroundings, with their black cloaks and their/nscabbed and rotting hands. Could they sense fear in/nthe vicinity? Harry was sure of it: They seemed to be/ncoming more quickly now, taking those dragging,/nrattling breaths he detested, tasting despair on the/nair, closing in —/n/nHe raised his wand: He could not, would not, suffer/nthe Dementor's Kiss, whatever happened afterward. It/n/n/n/n/n/nwas of Ron and Hermione that he thought as he/nwhispered, "Expecto Patronum)."/n/nThe silver stag burst from his wand and charged: The/ndementors scattered and there was a triumphant yell/nfrom somewhere out of sight./n/n"It's him, down there, down there, I saw his Patronus,/nit was a stag!/n/nThe dementors had retreated, the stars were popping/nout again, and the footsteps of the Death Eaters were/nbecoming louder; but before Harry in his panic could/ndecide what to do, there was a grinding of bolts/nnearby, a door opened on the left-hand side of the/nnarrow street, and a rough voice said, "Potter, in here,/nquick!"/n/nHe obeyed without hesitation: The three of them/nhurtled through the open doorway./n/n"Upstairs, keep the Cloak on, keep quiet!" muttered a/ntall figure, passing them on his way into the street/nand slamming the door behind him./n/nHarry had had no idea where they were, but now he/nsaw, by the stuttering light of a single candle, the/ngrubby, sawdust- strewn bar of the Hog's Head Inn./nThey ran behind the counter and through a second/ndoorway, which led to a rickety wooden staircase that/nthey climbed as fast as they could. The stairs opened/nonto a sitting room with a threadbare carpet and a/nsmall fireplace, above which hung a single large oil/npainting of a blonde girl who gazed out at the room/nwith a kind of vacant sweetness./n/nShouts reached them from the street below. Still/nwearing the Invisibility Cloak, they crept toward the/ngrimy window and looked down. Their savior, whom/n/n/n/n/n/nHarry now recognized as the Hog's Head's barman,/nwas the only person not wearing a hood./n/n"So what?" he was bellowing into one of the hooded/nfaces. "So what? You send dementors down my street,/nI'll send a Patronus back at 'em! I'm not having 'em/nnear me, I've told you that, I'm not having it!"/n/n"That wasn't your Patronus!" said a Death Eater./n/n"That was a stag, it was Potter's!"/n/n"Stag!" roared the barman, and he pulled out a wand./n"Stag! You idiot — Expecto Patronum .!"/n/nSomething huge and horned erupted from the wand:/nHead down, it charged toward the High Street and out/nof sight./n/n"That's not what I saw — " said the Death Eater,/nthough with less certainty./n/n"Curfew's been broken, you heard the noise," one of/nhis companions told the barman. "Someone was out/nin the street against regulations — "/n/n"If I want to put my cat out, I will, and be damned to/nyour curfew!"/n/n" You set off the Caterwauling Charm?"/n/n"What if I did? Going to cart me off to Azkaban? Kill/nme for sticking my nose out my own front door? Do it,/nthen, if you want to! But I hope for your sakes you/nhaven't pressed your little Dark Marks and/nsummoned him. He's not going to like being called/nhere for me and my old cat, is he, now?"/n/n"Don't you worry about us," said one of the Death/nEaters, "worry about yourself, breaking curfew!"/n/n/n/n/n/n"And where will you lot traffick potions and poisons/nwhen my pub's closed down? What'll happen to your/nlittle sidelines then?"/n/n/n/n"Are you threatening — ?"/n/n/n/n"I keep my mouth shut, it's why you come here, isn't/nit?"/n/n/n/n"I still say I saw a stag Patronus!" shouted the first/nDeath Eater./n/n"Stag?" roared the barman. "It's a goat, idiot!"/n/n"All right, we made a mistake," said the second Death/nEater. "Break curfew again and we won't be so/nlenient!"/n/nThe Death Eaters strode back toward the High Street./nHermione moaned with relief, wove out from under/nthe Cloak, and sat down on a wobble-legged chair./nHarry drew the curtains tight shut, then pulled the/nCloak off himself and Ron. They could hear the/nbarman down below, rebolting the door of the bar,/nthen climbing the stairs./n/nHarry's attention was caught by something on the/nmantelpiece: a small, rectangular mirror propped on/ntop of it, right beneath the portrait of the girl./n/nThe barman entered the room./n/n"You bloody fools," he said gruffly, looking from one to/nthe other of them. "What were you thinking, coming/nhere?"/n/n"Thank you," said Harry. "We can't thank you/nenough. You saved our lives."/n/n/n/n/n/nThe barman grunted. Harry approached him, looking/nup into the face, trying to see past the long, stringy,/nwire-gray hair and beard. He wore spectacles. Behind/nthe dirty lenses, the eyes were a piercing, brilliant/nblue./n/n"It's your eye I've been seeing in the mirror."/n/nThere was silence in the room. Harry and the barman/nlooked at each other./n/n"You sent Dobby."/n/nThe barman nodded and looked around for the elf./n/n"Thought he'd be with you. Where Ve you left him?"/n/n"He's dead," said Harry. "Bellatrix Lestrange killed/nhim."/n/nThe barman's face was impassive. After a few/nmoments he said, "I'm sorry to hear it. I liked that/nelf."/n/nHe turned away, lighting lamps with prods of his/nwand, not looking at any of them./n/n"You're Aberforth," said Harry to the man's back./n/nHe neither confirmed nor denied it, but bent to light/nthe fire./n/n"How did you get this?" Harry asked, walking across/nto Sirius's mirror, the twin of the one he had broken/nnearly two years before. "Bought it from Dung 'bout a/nyear ago," said Aberforth. "Albus told me what it was./nBeen trying to keep an eye out for you."/n/nRon gasped./n/n/n/n/n/n"The silver doe!" he said excitedly. "Was that you too?"/n/n"What are you talking about?" said Aberforth./n/n"Someone sent a doe Patronus to us!"/n/n"Brains like that, you could be a Death Eater, son./nHaven't I just proved my Patronus is a goat?"/n/n"Oh," said Ron. "Yeah ... well, I'm hungry!" he added/ndefensively as his stomach gave an enormous rumble./n/n"I got food," said Aberforth, and he sloped out of the/nroom, reappearing moments later with a large loaf of/nbread, some cheese, and a pewter jug of mead, which/nhe set upon a small table in front of the fire./n/nRavenous, they ate and drank, and for a while there/nwas silence but for the crackle of the fire, the clink of/ngoblets, and the sound of chewing./n/n"Right then," said Aberforth when they had eaten/ntheir fill, and Harry and Ron sat slumped dozily in/ntheir chairs. "We need to think of the best way to get/nyou out of here. Can't be done by night, you heard/nwhat happens if anyone moves outdoors during/ndarkness: Caterwauling Charm's set off, they'll be/nonto you like bow-truckles on doxy eggs. I don't/nreckon I'll be able to pass off a stag as a goat a second/ntime. Wait for daybreak when curfew lifts, then you/ncan put your Cloak back on and set out on foot. Get/nright out of Hogsmeade, up into the mountains, and/nyou'll be able to Disapparate there. Might see Hagrid./nHe's been hiding in a cave up there with Grawp ever/nsince they tried to arrest him."/n/n"We're not leaving," said Harry. "We need to get into/nHogwarts."/n/n"Don't be stupid, boy," said Aberforth./n/n/n/n/n/n"We've got to," said Harry./n/n/n/n"What you've got to do," said Aberforth, leaning/nforward, "is to get as far from here as you can."/n/n"You don't understand. There isn't much time. We've/ngot to get into the castle. Dumbledore — I mean, your/nbrother — wanted us — "/n/nThe firelight made the grimy lenses of Aberforth 's/nglasses momentarily opaque, a bright flat white, and/nHarry remembered the blind eyes of the giant spider,/nAragog./n/n"My brother Albus wanted a lot of things," said/nAberforth, "and people had a habit of getting hurt/nwhile he was carrying out his grand plans. You get/naway from this school, Potter, and out of the country/nif you can. Forget my brother and his clever schemes./nHe's gone where none of this can hurt him, and you/ndon't owe him anything."/n/n"You don't understand," said Harry again./n/n"Oh, don't I?" said Aberforth quietly. "You don't think/nI understood my own brother? Think you knew Albus/nbetter than I did?"/n/n"I didn't mean that," said Harry, whose brain felt/nsluggish with exhaustion and from the surfeit of food/nand wine. "It's ... he left me a job."/n/n"Did he now?" said Aberforth. "Nice job, I hope?/nPleasant? Easy? Sort of thing you'd expect an/nunqualified wizard kid to be able to do without/noverstretching themselves?"/n/nRon gave a rather grim laugh. Hermione was looking/nstrained./n/n/n/n/n/n"I-it's not easy, no," said Harry. "But I've got to — "/n/n" 'Got to'? Why 'got to*? He's dead, isn't he?" said/nAberforth roughly. "Let it go, boy, before you follow/nhim! Save yourself!"/n/n"I can't."/n/n"Why not?"/n/n"I — " Harry felt overwhelmed; he could not explain, so/nhe took the offensive instead. "But you're fighting too,/nyou're in the Order of the Phoenix — "/n/n"I was," said Aberforth. "The Order of the Phoenix is/nfinished. You-Know-Who's won, it's over, and anyone/nwho's pretending different's kidding themselves. It'll/nnever be safe for you here, Potter, he wants you too/nbadly. So go abroad, go into hiding, save yourself./n/nBest take these two with you." He jerked a thumb at/nRon and Hermione. "They'll be in danger long as they/nlive now everyone knows they've been working with/nyou."/n/n"I can't leave," said Harry. "I've got a job — "/n/n"Give it to someone else!"/n/n"I can't. It's got to be me, Dumbledore explained it all/n/n/n/n"Oh, did he now? And did he tell you everything, was/nhe honest with you?"/n/nHarry wanted with all his heart to say "Yes," but/nsomehow the simple word would not rise to his lips./nAberforth seemed to know what he was thinking./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"I knew my brother, Potter. He learned secrecy at our/nmother's knee. Secrets and lies, that's how we grew/nup, and Albus ... he was a natural."/n/nThe old man's eyes traveled to the painting of the girl/nover the mantelpiece. It was, now Harry looked/naround properly, the only picture in the room. There/nwas no photograph of Albus Dumbledore, nor of/nanyone else./n/n"Mr. Dumbledore?" said Hermione rather timidly. "Is/nthat your sister? Ariana?"/n/n"Yes," said Aberforth tersely. "Been reading Rita/nSkeeter, have you, missy?"/n/nEven by the rosy light of the fire it was clear that/nHermione had turned red./n/n"Elphias Doge mentioned her to us," said Harry,/ntrying to spare Hermione./n/n"That old berk," muttered Aberforth, taking another/nswig of mead. "Thought the sun shone out of my/nbrother's every orifice, he did. Well, so did plenty of/npeople, you three included, by the looks of it."/n/nHarry kept quiet. He did not want to express the/ndoubts and uncertainties about Dumbledore that had/nriddled him for months now. He had made his choice/nwhile he dug Dobby's grave, he had decided to/ncontinue along the winding, dangerous path indicated/nfor him by Albus Dumbledore, to accept that he had/nnot been told everything that he wanted to know, but/nsimply to trust. He had no desire to doubt again; he/ndid not want to hear anything that would deflect him/nfrom his purpose. He met Aberforth 's gaze, which was/nso strikingly like his brother's: The bright blue eyes/ngave the same impression that they were X-raying the/n/n/n/n/nobject of their scrutiny, and Harry thought that/nAberforth knew what he was thinking and despised/nhim for it./n/n"Professor Dumbledore cared about Harry, very/nmuch," said Hermione in a low voice./n/n"Did he now?" said Aberforth. "Funny thing, how/nmany of the people my brother cared about very/nmuch ended up in a worse state than if he'd left 'em/nwell alone."/n/n"What do you mean?" asked Hermione breathlessly./n/n"Never you mind," said Aberforth./n/n"But that's a really serious thing to say!" said/nHermione. "Are you — are you talking about your/nsister?"/n/nAberforth glared at her: His lips moved as if he were/nchewing the words he was holding back. Then he/nburst into speech./n/n"When my sister was six years old, she was attacked,/nset upon, by three Muggle boys. They'd seen her/ndoing magic, spying through the back garden hedge:/nShe was a kid, she couldn't control it, no witch or/nwizard can at that age. What they saw scared them, I/nexpect. They forced their way through the hedge, and/nwhen she couldn't show them the trick, they got a bit/ncarried away trying to stop the little freak doing it."/n/nHermione 's eyes were huge in the firelight; Ron looked/nslightly sick. Aberforth stood up, tall as Albus, and/nsuddenly terrible in his anger and the intensity of his/npain./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"It destroyed her, what they did: She was never right/nagain. She wouldn't use magic, but she couldn't get/nrid of it; it turned inward and drove her mad, it/nexploded out of her when she couldn't control it, and/nat times she was strange and dangerous. But mostly/nshe was sweet and scared and harmless./n/n"And my father went after the bastards that did it,"/nsaid Aberforth, "and attacked them. And they locked/nhim up in Azkaban for it. He never said why he'd/ndone it, because if the Ministry had known what/nAriana had become, she'd have been locked up in St./nMungo's for good. They'd have seen her as a serious/nthreat to the International Statute of Secrecy,/nunbalanced like she was, with magic exploding out of/nher at moments when she couldn't keep it in any/nlonger./n/n"We had to keep her safe and quiet. We moved house,/nput it about she was ill, and my mother looked after/nher, and tried to keep her calm and happy./n/n"I was her favorite," he said, and as he said it, a/ngrubby schoolboy seemed to look out through/nAberforth's wrinkles and tangled beard. "Not Albus,/nhe was always up in his bedroom when he was home,/nreading his books and counting his prizes, keeping up/nwith his correspondence with 'the most notable/nmagical names of the day,' " Aberforth sneered. "He/ndidn't want to be bothered with her. She liked me/nbest. I could get her to eat when she wouldn't do it for/nmy mother, I could get her to calm down when she/nwas in one of her rages, and when she was quiet, she/nused to help me feed the goats./n/n"Then, when she was fourteen ... See, I wasn't there,"/nsaid Aberforth. "If I'd been there, I could have calmed/nher down. She had one of her rages, and my mother/nwasn't as young as she was, and ... it was an/n/n/n/n/n/naccident. Ariana couldn't control it. But my mother/nwas killed."/n/nHarry felt a horrible mixture of pity and repulsion; he/ndid not want to hear any more, but Aberforth kept/ntalking, and Harry wondered how long it had been/nsince he had spoken about this; whether, in fact, he/nhad ever spoken about it./n/n"So that put paid to Albus's trip round the world with/nlittle Doge. The pair of 'em came home for my/nmother's funeral and then Doge went off on his own,/nand Albus settled down as head of the family. Ha!"/n/nAberforth spat into the fire./n/n"I'd have looked after her, I told him so, I didn't care/nabout school, I'd have stayed home and done it. He/ntold me I had to finish my education and he'd take/nover from my mother. Bit of a comedown for Mr./nBrilliant, there's no prizes for looking after your half-/nmad sister, stopping her blowing up the house every/nother day. But he did all right for a few weeks . . . till/nhe came."/n/nAnd now a positively dangerous look crept over/nAberforth's face./n/n"Grindelwald. And at last, my brother had an equal to/ntalk to, someone just as bright and talented as he/nwas. And looking after Ariana took a backseat then,/nwhile they were hatching all their plans for a new/nWizarding order, and looking for Hallows, and/nwhatever else it was they were so interested in. Grand/nplans for the benefit of all Wizardkind, and if one/nyoung girl got neglected, what did that matter, when/nAlbus was working for the greater good?/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"But after a few weeks of it, I'd had enough, I had. It/nwas nearly time for me to go back to Hogwarts, so I/ntold 'em, both of 'em, face-to-face, like I am to you,/nnow," and Aberforth looked down at Harry, and it/ntook little imagination to see him as a teenager, wiry/nand angry, confronting his elder brother. "I told him,/nyou'd better give it up now. You can't move her, she's/nin no fit state, you can't take her with you, wherever it/nis you're planning to go, when you're making your/nclever speeches, trying to whip yourselves up a/nfollowing. He didn't like that," said Aberforth, and his/neyes were briefly occluded by the firelight on the/nlenses of his glasses: They shone white and blind/nagain. "Grindelwald didn't like that at all. He got/nangry. He told me what a stupid little boy I was,/ntrying to stand in the way of him and my brilliant/nbrother. ... Didn't I understand, my poor sister/nwouldn't have to be hidden once they'd changed the/nworld, and led the wizards out of hiding, and taught/nthe Muggles their place?/n/n"And there was an argument . . . and I pulled out my/nwand, and he pulled out his, and I had the Cruciatus/nCurse used on me by my brother's best friend — and/nAlbus was trying to stop him, and then all three of us/nwere dueling, and the flashing lights and the bangs/nset her off, she couldn't stand it — "/n/nThe color was draining from Aberforth 's face as/nthough he had suffered a mortal wound./n/n" — and I think she wanted to help, but she didn't/nreally know what she was doing, and I don't know/nwhich of us did it, it could have been any of us — and/nshe was dead."/n/nHis voice broke on the last word and he dropped/ndown into the nearest chair. Hermione's face was wet/nwith tears, and Ron was almost as pale as Aberforth./n/n/n/n/n/nHarry felt nothing but revulsion: He wished he had/nnot heard it, wished he could wash his mind clean of/nit./n/n"I'm so ... I'm so sorry," Hermione whispered./n/n"Gone," croaked Aberforth. "Gone forever."/n/nHe wiped his nose on his cuff and cleared his throat./n/n" 'Course, Grindelwald scarpered. He had a bit of a/ntrack record already, back in his own country, and he/ndidn't want Ariana set to his account too. And Albus/nwas free, wasn't he? Free of the burden of his sister,/nfree to become the greatest wizard of the — "/n/n"He was never free," said Harry./n/n"I beg your pardon?" said Aberforth./n/n"Never," said Harry. "The night that your brother died,/nhe drank a potion that drove him out of his mind. He/nstarted screaming, pleading with someone who wasn't/nthere. 'Don't hurt them, please ... hurt me instead.' "/n/nRon and Hermione were staring at Harry. He had/nnever gone into details about what had happened on/nthe island on the lake: The events that had taken/nplace after he and Dumbledore had returned to/nHogwarts had eclipsed it so thoroughly./n/n"He thought he was back there with you and/nGrindelwald, I know he did," said Harry, remembering/nDumbledore whimpering, pleading. "He thought he/nwas watching Grindelwald hurting you and Ariana. . . ./nIt was torture to him, if you'd seen him then, you/nwouldn't say he was free."/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nAberforth seemed lost in contemplation of his own/nknotted and veined hands. After a long pause he said,/n"How can you be sure, Potter, that my brother wasn't/nmore interested in the greater good than in you? How/ncan you be sure you aren't dispensable, just like my/nlittle sister?"/n/nA shard of ice seemed to pierce Harry's heart./n/n"I don't believe it. Dumbledore loved Harry," said/nHermione./n/n"Why didn't he tell him to hide, then?" shot back/nAberforth. "Why didn't he say to him, Take care of/nyourself, here's how to survive'?"/n/n"Because," said Harry before Hermione could answer,/n"sometimes you've got to think about more than your/nown safety! Sometimes you've got to think about the/ngreater good! This is war!"/n/n"You're seventeen, boy!"/n/n"I'm of age, and I'm going to keep fighting even if/nyou've given up!"/n/n"Who says I've given up?"/n/n" The Order of the Phoenix is finished,' " Harry/nrepeated. " Tou- Know- Who's won, it's over, and/nanyone who's pretending different's kidding/nthemselves.' "/n/n"I don't say I like it, but it's the truth!"/n/n"No, it isn't," said Harry. "Your brother knew how to/nfinish You-Know-Who and he passed the knowledge/non to me. I'm going to keep going until I succeed — or/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nI die. Don't think I don't know how this might end./nI've known it for years."/n/n/n/nHe waited for Aberforth to jeer or to argue, but he did/nnot. He merely scowled./n/n"We need to get into Hogwarts," said Harry again. "If/nyou can't help us, we'll wait till daybreak, leave you in/npeace, and try to find a way in ourselves. If you can/nhelp us — well, now would be a great time to mention/nit."/n/nAberforth remained fixed in his chair, gazing at Harry/nwith the eyes that were so extraordinarily like his/nbrother's. At last he cleared his throat, got to his feet,/nwalked around the little table, and approached the/nportrait of Ariana./n/n"You know what to do," he said./n/nShe smiled, turned, and walked away, not as people/nin portraits usually did, out of the sides of their/nframes, but along what seemed to be a long tunnel/npainted behind her. They watched her slight figure/nretreating until finally she was swallowed by the/ndarkness./n/n"Er — what — ?" began Ron./n/n"There's only one way in now," said Aberforth. "You/nmust know they've got all the old secret passageways/ncovered at both ends, dementors all around the/nboundary walls, regular patrols inside the school from/nwhat my sources tell me. The place has never been so/nheavily guarded. How you expect to do anything once/nyou get inside it, with Snape in charge and the/nCarrows as his deputies ... well, that's your lookout,/nisn't it? You say you're prepared to die."/n/n/n/n/n/n"But what ... ?" said Hermione, frowning at Ariana's/npicture./n/nA tiny white dot had reappeared at the end of the/npainted tunnel, and now Ariana was walking back/ntoward them, growing bigger and bigger as she came./nBut there was somebody else with her now, someone/ntaller than she was, who was limping along, looking/nexcited. His hair was longer than Harry had ever seen/nit: He appeared to have suffered several gashes to his/nface and his clothes were ripped and torn. Larger and/nlarger the two figures grew, until only their heads and/nshoulders filled the portrait. Then the whole thing/nswung forward on the wall like a little door, and the/nentrance to a real tunnel was revealed. And out of it,/nhis hair overgrown, his face cut, his robes ripped,/nclambered the real Neville Longbottom, who gave a/nroar of delight, leapt down from the mantelpiece, and/nyelled, "I knew you'd come! I knew it, HarryY'/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n

text: /n"Neville — what the — how — ?"/n/nBut Neville had spotted Ron and Hermione, and with/nyells of delight was hugging them too. The longer/nHarry looked at Neville, the worse he appeared: One/nof his eyes was swollen yellow and purple, there were/ngouge marks on his face, and his general air of/nunkemptness suggested that he had been living/nrough. Nevertheless, his battered visage shone with/nhappiness as he let go of Hermione and said again, "I/nknew you'd come! Kept telling Seamus it was a matter/nof time!"/n/n"Neville, what's happened to you?"/n/n"What? This?" Neville dismissed his injuries with a/nshake of the head. "This is nothing. Seamus is worse./nYou'll see. Shall we get going then? Oh," he turned to/nAberforth, "Ab, there might be a couple more people/non the way."/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"Couple more?" repeated Aberforth ominously. "What/nd'you mean, a couple more, Longbottom? There's a/ncurfew and a Caterwauling Charm on the whole/nvillage!"/n/n"I know, that's why they'll be Apparating directly into/nthe bar," said Neville. "Just send them down the/npassage when they get here, will you? Thanks a lot."/n/nNeville held out his hand to Hermione and helped her/nto climb up onto the mantelpiece and into the tunnel;/nRon followed, then Neville. Harry addressed/nAberforth./n/n"I don't know how to thank you. You've saved our/nlives twice."/n/n"Look after 'em, then," said Aberforth gruffly. "I might/nnot be able to save 'em a third time."/n/nHarry clambered up onto the mantelpiece and/nthrough the hole behind Ariana's portrait. There were/nsmooth stone steps on the other side: It looked as/nthough the passageway had been there for years./nBrass lamps hung from the walls and the earthy floor/nwas worn and smooth; as they walked, their shadows/nrippled, fanlike, across the wall./n/n"How long's this been here?" Ron asked as they set/noff. "It isn't on the Marauder's Map, is it, Harry? I/nthought there were only seven passages in and out of/nschool?"/n/n"They sealed off all of those before the start of the/nyear," said Neville. "There's no chance of getting/nthrough any of them now, not with curses over the/nentrances and Death Eaters and dementors waiting at/nthe exits." He started walking backward, beaming,/ndrinking them in. "Never mind that stuff. ... Is it true?/n/n/n/n/nDid you break into Gringotts? Did you escape on a/ndragon? It's everywhere, everyone's talking about it,/nTerry Boot got beaten up by Carrow for yelling about/nit in the Great Hall at dinner!"/n/n"Yeah, it's true," said Harry./n/nNeville laughed gleefully./n/n"What did you do with the dragon?"/n/n"Released it into the wild," said Ron. "Hermione was/nall for keeping it as a pet — "/n/n"Don't exaggerate, Ron — "/n/n"But what have you been doing? People have been/nsaying you've just been on the run, Harry, but I don't/nthink so. I think you've been up to something."/n/n"You're right," said Harry, "but tell us about/nHogwarts, Neville, we haven't heard anything."/n/n"It's been ... well, it's not really like Hogwarts/nanymore," said Neville, the smile fading from his face/nas he spoke. "Do you know about the Carrows?"/n/n"Those two Death Eaters who teach here?"/n/n"They do more than teach," said Neville. "They're in/ncharge of all discipline. They like punishment, the/nCarrows."/n/n"Like Umbridge?"/n/n"Nah, they make her look tame. The other teachers/nare all supposed to refer us to the Carrows if we do/nanything wrong. They don't, though, if they can avoid/nit. You can tell they all hate them as much as we do./n/n/n/n/n/n"Amycus, the bloke, he teaches what used to be/nDefense Against the Dark Arts, except now it's just/nthe Dark Arts. We're supposed to practice the/nCruciatus Curse on people who've earned detentions/n/n/n/n"What?"/n/nHarry, Ron, and Hermione's united voices echoed up/nand down the passage./n/n"Yeah," said Neville. "That's how I got this one," he/npointed at a particularly deep gash in his cheek, "I/nrefused to do it. Some people are into it, though;/nCrabbe and Goyle love it. First time they've ever been/ntop in anything, I expect./n/n"Alecto, Amycus's sister, teaches Muggle Studies,/nwhich is compulsory for everyone. We've all got to/nlisten to her explain how Muggles are like animals,/nstupid and dirty, and how they drove wizards into/nhiding by being vicious toward them, and how the/nnatural order is being reestablished. I got this one,"/nhe indicated another slash to his face, "for asking her/nhow much Muggle blood she and her brother have/ngot."/n/n"Blimey, Neville," said Ron, "there's a time and a place/nfor getting a smart mouth."/n/n"You didn't hear her," said Neville. "You wouldn't have/nstood it either. The thing is, it helps when people/nstand up to them, it gives everyone hope. I used to/nnotice that when you did it, Harry."/n/n"But they've used you as a knife sharpener," said/nRon, wincing slightly as they passed a lamp and/nNeville's injuries were thrown into even greater relief./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nNeville shrugged./n/n/n/n"Doesn't matter. They don't want to spill too much/npure blood, so they'll torture us a bit if we're mouthy/nbut they won't actually kill us."/n/nHarry did not know what was worse, the things that/nNeville was saying or the matter-of-fact tone in which/nhe said them./n/n"The only people in real danger are the ones whose/nfriends and relatives on the outside are giving trouble./nThey get taken hostage. Old Xeno Lovegood was/ngetting a bit too outspoken in The Quihhler, so they/ndragged Luna off the train on the way back for/nChristmas."/n/n"Neville, she's all right, we've seen her — "/n/n"Yeah, I know, she managed to get a message to me."/n/nFrom his pocket he pulled a golden coin, and Harry/nrecognized it as one of the fake Galleons that/nDumbledore's Army had used to send one another/nmessages./n/n"These have been great," said Neville, beaming at/nHermione. "The Carrows never rumbled how we were/ncommunicating, it drove them mad. We used to sneak/nout at night and put graffiti on the walls:/n/nDumbledore's Army, Still Recruiting, stuff like that./nSnape hated it."/n/n"You used to?" said Harry, who had noticed the past/ntense./n/n"Well, it got more difficult as time went on," said/nNeville. "We lost Luna at Christmas, and Ginny never/ncame back after Easter, and the three of us were sort/n/n/n/n/n/nof the leaders. The Carrows seemed to know I was/nbehind a lot of it, so they started coming down on me/nhard, and then Michael Corner went and got caught/nreleasing a first-year they'd chained up, and they/ntortured him pretty badly. That scared people off."/n/n"No kidding," muttered Ron, as the passage began to/nslope upward./n/n"Yeah, well, I couldn't ask people to go through what/nMichael did, so we dropped those kinds of stunts. But/nwe were still fighting, doing underground stuff, right/nup until a couple of weeks ago. That's when they/ndecided there was only one way to stop me, I suppose,/nand they went for Gran."/n/n"They what?" said Harry, Ron, and Hermione/ntogether./n/n"Yeah," said Neville, panting a little now, because the/npassage was climbing so steeply, "well, you can see/ntheir thinking. It had worked really well, kidnapping/nkids to force their relatives to behave, I s'pose it was/nonly a matter of time before they did it the other way/naround. Thing was," he faced them, and Harry was/nastonished to see that he was grinning, "they bit off a/nbit more than they could chew with Gran. Little old/nwitch living alone, they probably thought they didn't/nneed to send anyone particularly powerful. Anyway,"/nNeville laughed, "Dawlish is still in St. Mungo's and/nGran's on the run. She sent me a letter," he clapped a/nhand to the breast pocket of his robes, "telling me she/nwas proud of me, that I'm my parents' son, and to/nkeep it up."/n/n"Cool," said Ron./n/n"Yeah," said Neville happily. "Only thing was, once/nthey realized they had no hold over me, they decided/n/n/n/n/n/nHogwarts could do without me after all. I don't know/nwhether they were planning to kill me or send me to/nAzkaban; either way, I knew it was time to disappear."/n/n"But," said Ron, looking thoroughly confused, "aren't/n— aren't we heading straight back into Hogwarts?"/n/n" 'Course," said Neville. "You'll see. We're here."/n/nThey turned a corner and there ahead of them was/nthe end of the passage. Another short flight of steps/nled to a door just like the one hidden behind Ariana's/nportrait. Neville pushed it open and climbed through./nAs Harry followed, he heard Neville call out to unseen/npeople:/n/n"Look who it is! Didn't I tell you?"/n/nAs Harry emerged into the room beyond the passage,/nthere were several screams and yells: "HARRY!" "It's/nPotter, it's POTTER!" "Ron!" "Hermionel"/n/nHe had a confused impression of colored hangings, of/nlamps and many faces. The next moment, he, Ron,/nand Hermione were engulfed, hugged, pounded on the/nback, their hair ruffled, their hands shaken, by what/nseemed to be more than twenty people: They might/njust have won a Quidditch final./n/n"Okay, okay, calm down!" Neville called, and as the/ncrowd backed away, Harry was able to take in their/nsurroundings./n/nHe did not recognize the room at all. It was enormous,/nand looked rather like the interior of a particularly/nsumptuous tree house, or perhaps a gigantic ship's/ncabin. Multicolored hammocks were strung from the/nceiling and from a balcony that ran around the dark/nwood-paneled and windowless walls, which were/n/n/n/n/ncovered in bright tapestry hangings: Harry saw the/ngold Gryffindor lion, emblazoned on scarlet; the black/nbadger of Hufflepuff, set against yellow; and the/nbronze eagle of Ravenclaw, on blue. The silver and/ngreen of Slytherin alone were absent. There were/nbulging bookcases, a few broomsticks propped/nagainst the walls, and in the corner, a large wooden-/ncased wireless./n/n"Where are we?"/n/n"Room of Requirement, of course!" said Neville./n"Surpassed itself, hasn't it? The Carrows were/nchasing me, and I knew I had just one chance for a/nhideout: I managed to get through the door and this/nis what I found! Well, it wasn't exactly like this when I/narrived, it was a load smaller, there was only one/nhammock and just Gryffindor hangings. But it's/nexpanded as more and more of the D.A. have arrived."/n/n"And the Carrows can't get in?" asked Harry, looking/naround for the door./n/n"No," said Seamus Finnigan, whom Harry had not/nrecognized until he spoke: Seamus's face was bruised/nand puffy. "It's a proper hideout, as long as one of us/nstays in here, they can't get at us, the door won't/nopen. It's all down to Neville. He really gets this room./nYou've got to ask it for exactly what you need — like,/n/n'I don't want any Carrow supporters to be able to get/nin' — and it'll do it for you! You've just got to make/nsure you close the loopholes! Neville's the man!"/n/n"It's quite straightforward, really," said Neville/nmodestly. "I'd been in here about a day and a half,/nand getting really hungry, and wishing I could get/nsomething to eat, and that's when the passage to the/nHog's Head opened up. I went through it and met/nAberforth. He's been providing us with food, because/n/n/n/n/nfor some reason, that's the one thing the room doesn't/nreally do."/n/n/n/n"Yeah, well, food's one of the five exceptions to/nGamp's Law of Elemental Transfiguration," said Ron/nto general astonishment./n/n"So we've been hiding out here for nearly two weeks,"/nsaid Seamus, "and it just makes more hammocks/nevery time we need them, and it even sprouted a/npretty good bathroom once girls started turning up —/n/n/n/n" — and thought they'd quite like to wash, yes,"/nsupplied Lavender Brown, whom Harry had not/nnoticed until that point. Now that he looked around/nproperly, he recognized many familiar faces. Both/nPatil twins were there, as were Terry Boot, Ernie/nMacmillan, Anthony Goldstein, and Michael Corner./n/n"Tell us what you've been up to, though," said Ernie./n"There've been so many rumors, we've been trying to/nkeep up with you on Potterwatch." He pointed at the/nwireless. "You didn't break into Gringotts?"/n/n"They did!" said Neville. "And the dragon's true too!"/n/nThere was a smattering of applause and a few/nwhoops; Ron took a bow./n/n"What were you after?" asked Seamus eagerly./n/nBefore any of them could parry the question with one/nof their own, Harry felt a terrible, scorching pain in/nthe lightning scar. As he turned his back hastily on/nthe curious and delighted faces, the Room of/nRequirement vanished, and he was standing inside a/nruined stone shack, and the rotting floorboards were/nripped apart at his feet, a disinterred golden box lay/n/n/n/n/nopen and empty beside the hole, and Voldemort's/nscream of fury vibrated inside his head./n/nWith an enormous effort he pulled out of Voldemort's/nmind again, back to where he stood, swaying, in the/nRoom of Requirement, sweat pouring from his face/nand Ron holding him up./n/n"Are you all right, Harry?" Neville was saying. "Want/nto sit down? I expect you're tired, aren't — ?"/n/n"No," said Harry. He looked at Ron and Hermione,/ntrying to tell them without words that Voldemort had/njust discovered the loss of one of the other Horcruxes./nTime was running out fast: If Voldemort chose to visit/nHogwarts next, they would miss their chance./n/n"We need to get going," he said, and their expressions/ntold him that they understood./n/n"What are we going to do, then, Harry?" asked/nSeamus. "What's the plan?"/n/n"Plan?" repeated Harry. He was exercising all his/nwillpower to prevent himself succumbing again to/nVoldemort's rage: His scar was still burning. "Well,/nthere's something we — Ron, Hermione, and I — need/nto do, and then we'll get out of here."/n/nNobody was laughing or whooping anymore. Neville/nlooked confused./n/n"What d'you mean, 'get out of here'?"/n/n"We haven't come back to stay," said Harry, rubbing/nhis scar, trying to soothe the pain. "There's something/nimportant we need to do — "/n/n"What is it?"/n/n/n/n/n/n"I — I can't tell you."/n/n/n/nThere was a ripple of muttering at this: Neville's/nbrows contracted./n/n"Why can't you tell us? It's something to do with/nfighting You-Know-Who, right?"/n/n"Well, yeah — "/n/n"Then we'll help you."/n/nThe other members of Dumbledore's Army were/nnodding, some enthusiastically, others solemnly. A/ncouple of them rose from their chairs to demonstrate/ntheir willingness for immediate action./n/n"You don't understand." Harry seemed to have said/nthat a lot in the last few hours. "We — we can't tell/nyou. We've got to do it — alone."/n/n"Why?" asked Neville./n/n"Because ..." In his desperation to start looking for/nthe missing Horcrux, or at least to have a private/ndiscussion with Ron and Hermione about where they/nmight commence their search, Harry found it difficult/nto gather his thoughts. His scar was still searing./n"Dumbledore left the three of us a job," he said/ncarefully, "and we weren't supposed to tell — I mean,/nhe wanted us to do it, just the three of us."/n/n"We're his army," said Neville. "Dumbledore's Army./nWe were all in it together, we've been keeping it going/nwhile you three have been off on your own — "/n/n"It hasn't exactly been a picnic, mate," said Ron./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"I never said it had, but I don't see why you can't/ntrust us. Everyone in this room's been fighting and/nthey've been driven in here because the Carrows were/nhunting them down. Everyone in here's proven they're/nloyal to Dumbledore — loyal to you."/n/n"Look," Harry began, without knowing what he was/ngoing to say, but it did not matter: The tunnel door/nhad just opened behind him./n/n"We got your message, Neville! Hello you three, I/nthought you must be here!"/n/nIt was Luna and Dean. Seamus gave a great roar of/ndelight and ran to hug his best friend./n/n"Hi, everyone!" said Luna happily. "Oh, it's great to be/nback!"/n/n"Luna," said Harry distractedly, "what are you doing/nhere? How did you — ?"/n/n"I sent for her," said Neville, holding up the fake/nGalleon. "I promised her and Ginny that if you turned/nup I'd let them know. We all thought that if you came/nback, it would mean revolution. That we were going to/noverthrow Snape and the Carrows."/n/n"Of course that's what it means," said Luna brightly./n"Isn't it, Harry? We're going to fight them out of/nHogwarts?"/n/n"Listen," said Harry with a rising sense of panic, "I'm/nsorry, but that's not what we came back for. There's/nsomething we've got to do, and then — "/n/n"You're going to leave us in this mess?" demanded/nMichael Corner./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"No!" said Ron. "What we're doing will benefit/neveryone in the end, it's all about trying to get rid of/nYou-Know-Who — "/n/n/n/n"Then let us help!" said Neville angrily. "We want to be/na part of it!"/n/nThere was another noise behind them, and Harry/nturned. His heart seemed to fail: Ginny was now/nclimbing through the hole in the wall, closely followed/nby Fred, George, and Lee Jordan. Ginny gave Harry a/nradiant smile: He had forgotten, or had never fully/nappreciated, how beautiful she was, but he had never/nbeen less pleased to see her./n/n"Aberforth's getting a bit annoyed," said Fred, raising/nhis hand in answer to several cries of greeting. "He/nwants a kip, and his bar's turned into a railway/nstation."/n/nHarry's mouth fell open. Right behind Lee Jordan/ncame Harry's old girlfriend, Cho Chang. She smiled at/nhim./n/n"I got the message," she said, holding up her own fake/nGalleon, and she walked over to sit beside Michael/nCorner./n/n"So what's the plan, Harry?" said George./n/n"There isn't one," said Harry, still disoriented by the/nsudden appearance of all these people, unable to take/neverything in while his scar was still burning so/nfiercely./n/n"Just going to make it up as we go along, are we? My/nfavorite kind," said Fred./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"You've got to stop this!" Harry told Neville. "What did/nyou call them all back for? This is insane — "/n/n"We're fighting, aren't we?" said Dean, taking out his/nfake Galleon. "The message said Harry was back, and/nwe were going to fight! I'll have to get a wand, though/n/n/n/n"You haven't got a wand — ?" began Seamus./n/nRon turned suddenly to Harry./n/n"Why can't they help?"/n/n"What?"/n/n"They can help." He dropped his voice and said, so/nthat none of them could hear but Hermione, who/nstood between them, "We don't know where it is./nWe've got to find it fast. We don't have to tell them it's/na Horcrux."/n/nHarry looked from Ron to Hermione, who murmured,/n"I think Ron's right. We don't even know what we're/nlooking for, we need them." And when Harry looked/nunconvinced, "You don't have to do everything alone,/nHarry."/n/nHarry thought fast, his scar still prickling, his head/nthreatening to split again. Dumbledore had warned/nhim against telling anyone but Ron and Hermione/nabout the Horcruxes. Secrets and lies, that's how we/ngrew up, and Albus ...he was a natural. ... Was he/nturning into Dumbledore, keeping his secrets/nclutched to his chest, afraid to trust? But/nDumbledore had trusted Snape, and where had that/nled? To murder at the top of the highest tower .../n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"All right," he said quietly to the other two. "Okay," he/ncalled to the room at large, and all noise ceased: Fred/nand George, who had been cracking jokes for the/nbenefit of those nearest, fell silent, and all of them/nlooked alert, excited./n/n"There's something we need to find," Harry said./n"Something — something that'll help us overthrow/nYou-Know-Who. It's here at Hogwarts, but we don't/nknow where. It might have belonged to Ravenclaw./n/nHas anyone heard of an object like that? Has anyone/never come across something with her eagle on it, for/ninstance?"/n/nHe looked hopefully toward the little group of/nRavenclaws, to Padma, Michael, Terry, and Cho, but/nit was Luna who answered, perched on the arm of/nGinny's chair./n/n"Well, there's her lost diadem. I told you about it,/nremember, Harry? The lost diadem of Ravenclaw?/nDaddy's trying to duplicate it."/n/n"Yeah, but the lost diadem," said Michael Corner,/nrolling his eyes, "is lost, Luna. That's sort of the/npoint."/n/n"When was it lost?" asked Harry./n/n"Centuries ago, they say," said Cho, and Harry's heart/nsank. "Professor Flitwick says the diadem vanished/nwith Ravenclaw herself. People have looked, but," she/nappealed to her fellow Ravenclaws, "nobody's ever/nfound a trace of it, have they?"/n/nThey all shook their heads./n/n"Sorry, but what is a diadem?" asked Ron./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"It's a kind of crown," said Terry Boot. "Ravenclaw's/nwas supposed to have magical properties, enhance/nthe wisdom of the wearer."/n/n"Yes, Daddy's Wrackspurt siphons — "/n/nBut Harry cut across Luna./n/n"And none of you have ever seen anything that looks/nlike it?"/n/nThey all shook their heads again. Harry looked at Ron/nand Hermione and his own disappointment was/nmirrored back at him. An object that had been lost/nthis long, and apparently without trace, did not seem/nlike a good candidate for the Horcrux hidden in the/ncastle. ... Before he could formulate a new question,/nhowever, Cho spoke again./n/n"If you'd like to see what the diadem's supposed to/nlook like, I could take you up to our common room/nand show you, Harry? Ravenclaw's wearing it in her/nstatue."/n/nHarry's scar scorched again: For a moment the Room/nof Requirement swam before him, and he saw instead/nthe dark earth soaring beneath him and felt the great/nsnake wrapped around his shoulders. Voldemort was/nflying again, whether to the underground lake or here,/nto the castle, he did not know: Either way, there was/nhardly any time left./n/n"He's on the move," he said quietly to Ron and/nHermione. He glanced at Cho and then back at them./n"Listen, I know it's not much of a lead, but I'm going/nto go and look at this statue, at least find out what/nthe diadem looks like. Wait for me here and keep, you/nknow — the other one — safe."/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/nCho had got to her feet, but Ginny said rather/nfiercely, "No, Luna will take Harry, won't you, Luna?"/n/n"Oooh, yes, I'd like to," said Luna happily, and Cho/nsat down again, looking disappointed./n/n"How do we get out?" Harry asked Neville./n/n"Over here."/n/nHe led Harry and Luna to a corner, where a small/ncupboard opened onto a steep staircase./n/n"It comes out somewhere different every day, so/nthey've never been able to find it," he said. "Only/ntrouble is, we never know exactly where we're going to/nend up when we go out. Be careful, Harry, they're/nalways patrolling the corridors at night."/n/n"No problem," said Harry. "See you in a bit."/n/nHe and Luna hurried up the staircase, which was/nlong, lit by torches, and turned corners in unexpected/nplaces. At last they reached what appeared to be solid/nwall./n/n"Get under here," Harry told Luna, pulling out the/nInvisibility Cloak and throwing it over both of them./n/nHe gave the wall a little push./n/nIt melted away at his touch and they slipped outside:/nHarry glanced back and saw that it had resealed itself/nat once. They were standing in a dark corridor: Harry/npulled Luna back into the shadows, fumbled in the/npouch around his neck, and took out the Marauder's/nMap. Holding it close to his nose he searched, and/nlocated his and Luna's dots at last./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"We're up on the fifth floor," he whispered, watching/nFilch moving away from them, a corridor ahead./n"Come on, this way."/n/nThey crept off./n/nHarry had prowled the castle at night many times/nbefore, but never had his heart hammered this fast,/nnever had so much depended on his safe passage/nthrough the place. Through squares of moonlight/nupon the floor, past suits of armor whose helmets/ncreaked at the sound of their soft footsteps, around/ncorners beyond which who knew what lurked, Harry/nand Luna walked, checking the Marauder's Map/nwhenever light permitted, twice pausing to allow a/nghost to pass without drawing attention to/nthemselves. He expected to encounter an obstacle at/nany moment; his worst fear was Peeves, and he/nstrained his ears with every step to hear the first,/ntelltale signs of the poltergeist's approach./n/n"This way, Harry," breathed Luna, plucking his sleeve/nand pulling him toward a spiral staircase./n/nThey climbed in tight, dizzying circles; Harry had/nnever been up here before. At last they reached a/ndoor. There was no handle and no keyhole: nothing/nbut a plain expanse of aged wood, and a bronze/nknocker in the shape of an eagle./n/nLuna reached out a pale hand, which looked eerie/nfloating in midair, unconnected to arm or body. She/nknocked once, and in the silence it sounded to Harry/nlike a cannon blast. At once the beak of the eagle/nopened, but instead of a bird's call, a soft, musical/nvoice said, "Which came first, the phoenix or the/nflame?"/n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n"Hmm . . . What do you think, Harry?" said Luna,/nlooking thoughtful./n/n"What? Isn't there just a password?"/n/n"Oh no, you've got to answer a question," said Luna./n/n"What if you get it wrong?"/n/n"Well, you have to wait for somebody who gets it/nright," said Luna. "That way you learn, you see?"/n/n"Yeah ... Trouble is, we can't really afford to wait for/nanyone else, Luna."/n/n"No, I see what you mean," said Luna seriously. "Well/nthen, I think the answer is that a circle has no/nbeginning."/n/n"Well reasoned," said the voice, and the door swung/nopen./n/nThe deserted Ravenclaw common room was a wide,/ncircular room, airier than any Harry had ever seen at/nHogwarts. Graceful arched windows punctuated the/nwalls, which were hung with blue-and-bronze silks:/n/nBy day, the Ravenclaws would have a spectacular/nview of the surrounding mountains. The ceiling was/ndomed and painted with stars, which were echoed in/nthe midnight-blue carpet. There were tables, chairs,/nand bookcases, and in a niche opposite the door/nstood a tall statue of white marble./n/nHarry recognized Rowena Ravenclaw from the bust he/nhad seen at Luna's house. The statue stood beside a/ndoor that led, he guessed, to dormitories above. He/nstrode right up to the marble woman, and she seemed/nto look back at him with a quizzical half smile on her/nface, beautiful yet slightly intimidating. A delicate-/n/n/n/n/nlooking circlet had been reproduced in marble on top/nof her head. It was not unlike the tiara Fleur had/nworn at her wedding. There were tiny words etched/ninto it. Harry stepped out from under the Cloak and/nclimbed up onto Ravenclaw's plinth to read them./n/n" 'Wit beyond measure is man's greatest treasure.' "/n/n"Which makes you pretty skint, witless," said a/ncackling voice./n/nHarry whirled around, slipped off the plinth, and/nlanded on the floor. The sloping-shouldered figure of/nAlecto Carrow was standing before him, and even as/nHarry raised his wand, she pressed a stubby/nforefinger to the skull and snake branded on her/nforearm./n/n/n/n/n/n/n/n

title: The Sacking Of Severus Snape
text: /nThe moment her finger touched the Mark, Harry's/nscar burned savagely, the starry room vanished from/nsight, and he was standing upon an outcrop of rock/nbeneath a cliff, and the sea was washing around him/nand there was triumph in his heart — They have the/nboy./n/nA loud bang brought Harry back to where he stood:/nDisoriented, he raised his wand, but the witch before/nhim was already falling forward; she hit the ground so/nhard that the glass in the bookcases tinkled./n/n"I've never Stunned anyone except in our D.A./nlessons," said Luna, sounding mildly interested. "That/nwas noisier than I thought it would be."/n/nAnd sure enough, the ceiling had begun to tremble./nScurrying, echoing footsteps were growing louder/nfrom behind the door leading to the dormitories:/nLuna's spell had woken Ravenclaws sleeping above./n/n"Luna, where are you? I need to get under the Cloak!"/n/n/n/n/nLuna's feet appeared out of nowhere; he hurried to/nher side and she let the Cloak fall back over them as/nthe door opened and a stream of Ravenclaws, all in/ntheir nightclothes, flooded into the common room./nThere were gasps and cries of surprise as they saw/nAlecto lying there unconscious. Slowly they shuffled/nin around her, a savage beast that might wake at any/nmoment and attack them. Then one brave little first-/nyear darted up to her and prodded her backside with/nhis big toe./n/n"I think she might be dead!" he shouted with delight./n/n"Oh, look," whispered Luna happily, as the/nRavenclaws crowded in around Alecto. "They're/npleased!"/n/n"Yeah ... great ..."/n/nHarry closed his eyes, and as his scar throbbed he/nchose to sink again into Voldemort's mind. ... He was/nmoving along the tunnel into the first cave. ... He had/nchosen to make sure of the locket before coming . . ./nbut that would not take him long. . . ./n/nThere was a rap on the common room door and every/nRavenclaw froze. From the other side, Harry heard the/nsoft, musical voice that issued from the eagle door/nknocker: "Where do Vanished objects go?"/n/n"I dunno, do I? Shut it!" snarled an uncouth voice/nthat Harry knew was that of the Carrow brother,/nAmycus. "Alecto? Alecto? Are you there? Have you got/nhim? Open the door!"/n/nThe Ravenclaws were whispering amongst/nthemselves, terrified. Then, without warning, there/ncame a series of loud bangs, as though somebody was/nfiring a gun into the door./n/n/n/n/n/n"ALECTO\ If he comes, and we haven't got Potter —/nd'you want to go the same way as the Malfoys?/nANSWER ME!"
